News.title: Moment thug who hid guns used in chicken shop murder of schoolgirl is arrested while working out after stashing pistol
News.content:
Next

A REMORSELESS gangster involved in the 2010 chicken shop murder of a schoolgirl was back behind bars last night for stashing a gun in a lift shaft.

Cops matched Dwayne McIntosh-Wisdom’s DNA to the converted blank-firing pistol.



Police video footage showed him being arrested outside a gym close to his home in Hackney, East London, in September this year, where he had been working out.

Yesterday, the 32-year-old gang member admitted illegal possession of the firearm and ammunition when he appeared at Snaresbrook crown court via video-link from Thameside prison.



Judge Georgina Sharkey remanded McIntosh-Wisdom in custody ahead of sentence on a date to be fixed.

Dwayne McIntosh-Wisdom was 17 when he was jailed for a minimum 10-year tariff for hiding a sub-machine gun for older members of the London Fields gang.



Innocent 16-year-old Agnes Sina-Inakoju was shot in the throat when the deadly Agram 2000 weapon was used by killers on bikes used to spray rivals at the Hoxton Chicken and Pizza take-away in April 2010.

Her killers, Leon Dunkley and Mohammed Smoured, were each sentenced to 32-year minimum terms at the Old Bailey in 2011.



Fellow gang member McIntosh-Wisdom was convicted of assisting an offender by hiding the Croatian special forces sub-machine gun, which had been used in a spate of gang shootings.

McIntosh-Wisdom used the name “Fields” in his Facebook profile and had uploaded a picture of guns to his page.

His “misguided loyalty to the London Fields gang” led to him being involved in several fights while in custody, the Old Bailey heard.

Jailing him then, the judge told him: “You have not accepted, in terms of remorse, any responsibility for your behaviour.”

Yet following his release from jail he acquired a Retay S2022 blank-firing pistol which had been converted to fire live bullets.



The weapon was in a bag with ammo when it was found inside a lift shaft during routine maintenance at a property on New Kent Road, Southwark on 26 March 2025.

Police were called by the lift engineers and sharp-eyed officers noticed Dwayne McIntosh-Wisdom, 32, loitering nearby.

Recognising his suspicious behaviour and how close he was to the weapon, they detained and arrested him on suspicion of possession of a firearm.

He was released on bail but a forensic examination of the gun discovered McIntosh-Wisdom’s DNA on the trigger of the gun and the bag it was found in.

The gangster was located on Tuesday 15 September at a gym and he was arrested outside.



McIntosh-Wisdom admitted two charges of possessing a prohibited firearm and having ammunition without a firearm certificate.

He pleaded guilty to two more offences of possession of a firearm and ammunition while prohibited for life on both counts.

Met Detective Constable Claire McNulty said: “Officers identified McIntosh-Wisdom early in the investigation.

“But it took months of hard work and dedication before we could present irrefutable evidence that he had handled the gun.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Through forensic work, relentless investigations and fearless proactive interventions, we are taking the fight to those who cause serious violence, fear and intimidation across London.”



The conviction comes amid a Met’s crackdown on serious and violent crime with 676 firearms taken off the streets during 2025, 74 per cent more than the previous 12 months.

News.title: UK ‘Silicon Valley of VAPES’ where streets ‘stink of sweet smoke’ brace for PM’s e-cig crackdown – will it REALLY work?
News.content:
Next

BRITAIN’S so-called “Silicon Valley of Vapes” is bracing for a crackdown on the devices – with customers already swapping e-cigs for energy drinks like Red Bull.

Blackburn has been dubbed “the vape capital of the UK” with a survey finding 22.5 e-cig shops per 100,000 people and nine manufacturers based in the former industrial town.



Residents say while the streets may have once smelt of the smoke of industrial mills – now they stink of the sweet smell of flavoured vapes.

And they say they often see their roads cluttered with discarded boxes, fliers and tossed out vapes.



Trouble is brewing for the shops and factories that call the town home with a raft of new restrictions coming in on the devices.

The tough new rules are part of Labour’s efforts to clampdown on “unrecognisable” high streets and rogue operators.

Blackburn’s affinity with the vape industry – and the number of shops – saw it dubbed the “Silicon Valley of Vapes” by The Sunday Times.

Street cleaner Kevin Oates, 59, gave up smoking when his wife died of breast cancer, but started back up two years later when his mum died.



Kevin told The Sun: “I’ve been doing this job two years and I get to pick up more vape rubbish than anything else in the town centre.

“First you find the advert, then you find the wrapper, then the box and then the information leaflet, so much rubbish from just one product.”

Retired engineer Rob Sewell, 65, is aware of the vaping phenomenon as he chats to vape holding Emma Brownridge, 23, who started on e-cigs at school about nine years ago.

Emma said: “We all used to be behind the bushes and smoking – now for the last three years I am on the strawberry flavour vapes.”

Rob added: “Vaping is more popular than smoking. I’ve never vaped and gave up smoking 20 years ago.



“I live in Bamber Bridge and have seen a lot of discarded vapes both here in Blackburn and there – they are everywhere.”

Another pensioner, who didn’t wish to be named, added: “I don’t like the aroma of the vapes. In Blackburn that smell is everywhere and I don’t like it.”

The crackdown is coming after Blackburn’s council was told over half of the 107 schoolchildren surveyed in the town had used nicotine vapes.



And a quarter revealed they had used drug-laced vapes.

Forty-one per cent of the children surveyed said they had been given a vape by someone they knew.

Trading standards will also be handed new powers – and it comes as a new tax is slapped on vaping, as confirmed in yesterday’s Budget.

New rules in place from tomorrow include a total ban on selling vapes to anyone under the age of 18, regardless of whether the product contains nicotine.

It brings vapes – with estimates saying between 6 per cent of children aged between 11 and 17 puff on the devices – in line to booze and cigarettes.



The law will also change to ban giving away vaping or nicotine products for free, offering substantial discounts and giving away or selling coupons to promote the products.

Buying nicotine products on behalf of an under 18 will also be an offence.

During The Sun’s visit to Blackburn, we spoke to Lilly Huncoat, 18, who is studying health and social care, has been vaping with pals for eight years.



Lilly said: “I don’t know what got me into it, but everybody did it, so I did as well.”

Maddison Harvey, 21, also started out vaping at school as a teenager. Maddison said: “I started on e-cigs when I was about 14. I started vaping to stop smoking.

“Everyone at school did it. These days there are lots of kids still vaping and smoking.

“My two younger siblings don’t smoke or vape though.

“But when I was at school everyone did it and they had to start taking them off people.”



Another confirmed smoker Karen Duckworth, 41, said: “I’ve been smoking 30 years since I was 11.

“I don’t vape as my chest cannot handle the vapes – I have my cigarettes.

“I’ve tried them, but they all make me have a coughing fit.”

In Blackburn, half of 107 schoolchildren surveyed had used nicotine vapes and a quarter revealed they had used drug-laced vapes.

And 41 per cent of the children surveyed said they had been given a vape by someone they knew.



Vape shop owners are seriously worried about their future ahead of the law lockdown.

Blackburn market is dominated by vape shops with the sector employing 2,000 staff in the area.

At Allied E-Cig owner R Patel, 50, is concerned for his shop.



He said: ‘It is very scary times. Here we are at lunchtime and that’s supposed to be the busiest time of the day and nobody is about.”

He said: “When Covid hit we had to throw lots and lots of stock away, we don’t know if we will be here this time next year.

“Me and my wife work here for six days a week and then work the seventh day sorting stock.

“It’s the first time in my life that I’ve been worried about my future, I used to work in a call centre for British Telecom, but now I am confused as I don’t know where we are going.

“As it stands we work seven days a week and are just surviving.”



His fear was shared by the manager of Murrary E-Cigs who reckoned the ban on disposable vapes a couple of years ago kicked off a massive downturn in trade.

And meanwhile, opposite the Udat vape shop owner Hasib Patel, 65, says sales are on the decline.

And he said Red Bulls have become his most popular sale instead.

Hasib said: “I’ve had the shop for 23 years and we moved into vapes four years ago, but since the disposable ban came in I am selling less vapes.

“The Red Bull really is my best selling product now, I started vaping and back then vapes were selling good and cigarettes were still selling, but now both have declined a lot.”



Lancashire factories make millions of vapes every year, supplying the whole country and the world.

Those firms rake in half a billion pounds in annual sales and employ more than 2,000 people, from assembly line workers to chemists.

Phil Riley, the Labour leader of Blackburn with Darwen Borough Council, has praised an employment boost from “very reputable” local businesses at the “leading edge of the industry”.

But Burnham‘s new vape policy is feared to threaten the prosperity of the area’s vape industry.

Around 5.4million people in the UK smoke e-cigarettes – but there is ongoing concern children are taking up the habit.



Blackburn councillor Damian Talbot says the authorities are working to lower the number of children vaping.

He said: “As a local authority, our view is that vapes should only ever be used as a tool to quit smoking, as a short-term harm reduction support offer for adult smokers.

“We believe that those who have never smoked should not begin vaping.

“We believe that children and young people should not vape, that this is harmful and must be prevented and our approach focuses on providing support and education.”

Professor Abdul Razaq, Blackburn with Darwen’s Director of Public Health, said: “We will ensure that our position on vaping remains evidence-led, and also that it evolves to consider developments in national guidance, the Tobacco and Vapes Act 2026 legislation, together with local insights, offers of support and implementation of key measures to ensure a smoke-free generation.”



Blackburn is also home to e-liquid manufacturer Flavour Warehouse which turned over £161million last year and employs over 500 people.

Its chief executive, Simon Brierley, told The Sun that Blackburn’s successful vape firms “support hundreds of local jobs and generate investment”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He Said: “At a time when many towns are competing for high-quality employment and private sector investment, having ambitious businesses that manufacture, distribute and sell products nationally and internationally is a positive for our local economy.

“The sector reflects many of the strengths that have long defined East Lancashire, including entrepreneurship, innovation, logistics expertise and a strong trading tradition.”

News.title: Fury as UK council to remove ALL dog poo bins to save £160,000 in ‘unbelievable’ move
News.content:
Next

A UK council has scrapped all dog poo bins in a bid to cut £160,000 per year.

The decision has been branded as “unbelievable” and “disgusting”, with residents encouraged to chuck bags into their household bin.

Hillingdon Council in west London plans to remove all 700 of its public dog waste bins because they don’t believe the extra waste service is needed.



The service currently collects around 14.5 tonnes of dog waste every month, amounting to 174 tonnes per year – but the council now believe the arrangement is no longer necessary.



Now, residents in the borough have been encouraged to throw dog waste bins in regular waste bins, or to carry them home.

The council has also said it will place stickers reading “I can take dog waste too” on bins in parks and dog walking locations during the removal process.

Scrapping Hillingdon’s bins has a number of cost benefits to the council, with proposals suggesting it will save £160,000 per year, with £60,000 reserved to fund street cleaning.

A report written by the authority reads that the recommendations will “improve operational efficiency, reduce ongoing service

costs and make better use of the Council’s existing waste disposal infrastructure.”

Hillingdon Council also write in the report that there is a “possibility of an increase in dog fouling” but it could be managed with “clear communications” and “updated signage.”

Residents of the neighbouring Ruislip Residents’ Association have protested against the decision to scrap the bins, predicting that the removal process could begin in mid-November.

Members shared their concern online, saying: “We can also imagine bags of dog poo tied to bushes and shrubs along the walks where the bins used to be, until they look like a poo Christmas tree.”



“How will ordinary litter bins cope with an extra 174 tonnes of dog poo a year, when on many streets there isn’t one to cope?”, they continued.

Images posted by the group showed that that dog waste bins in the area were already full and spilling over, with no nearby waste bin to be found.

According to the Association, the council’s report refers to “an increase in dog fouling”, but it could be fixed with signs and stickrs.

Many Brits have been quick to criticise Hillingdon Council’s decision, calling it “unbelievable” and “disgusting”, questioning “what kind of stupidity is this?”

Hillingdon Council said: “From November, residents and visitors will be able to put dog waste bags in any public litter bins across Hillingdon – except those in children’s play areas – which is already common practice for many councils across the country, including our neighbouring boroughs of Ealing and Harrow.



“This will effectively double the number of bins where dog waste can disposed with more than 1,500 litter bins, making it even easier for dog walkers to get rid of their pets‘ waste, so it is difficult to see how this could present a substantial increase in the risk of the anti-social dumping of dog waste.

“Removing dedicated dog waste bins will help us reduce costs and unnecessary vehicle journeys as collections are currently undertaken by a contractor. Simplifying collections will give us greater control over service delivery and generate significant savings, with up to £60,000 being reinvested to increase frequency and bin provision where required to help keep our borough clean.”

News.title: Inside Andrew’s ‘annus horribilis’ a year on from losing royal titles – & why things could be about to get MUCH worse
News.content:
Next

FOR a man who cherished being called His Royal Highness, the loss of Andrew Mountbatten Windsor’s royal title a year ago appeared to be his lowest point.

But next year could be far worse than the annus horribilis the former prince has just experienced, according to two experts.





Over the past 12 months Andrew became a regular citizen, was thrown out of his home and faced the humiliation of being photographed cowering in the back of a car following his arrest on suspicion of misconduct in a public office.

Yet King Charles’ eldest brother might fall further from grace.

Not only is the 66-year-old former Duke of York under fire in the UK, the authorities on the other side of the Atlantic are pursuing him.

There is a determination in the US to get Andrew to answer all the questions law enforcement has about his relationship with the convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

If, as the pollsters predict, the Democrats win the midterm elections on Tuesday, they have vowed to hand unredacted Epstein files over to British detectives.

There are also fears that Andrew’s daughters Beatrice and Eugenie are distancing themselves from the toxic ex-Duke.

Andrew Lownie, author of the best-selling book Entitled about Andrew, tells The Sun: “He’s out of Royal Lodge, a lot of the staff have gone, I think his family is fracturing.

“They’ve lost touch with him to a certain extent.





“The guy’s lost everything, he’s lost his family, his home, his reputation.

“But what’s also worrying for Andrew is that after one bad year, he’s going to get probably a worse year.

“There’s more material likely to come out, particularly after the midterms.”

As the late Queen Elizbeth II’s reported “favourite son”, Andrew held onto his royal privileges long after he was tainted by his association with seedy moneyman Epstein.

It was back in 2010 that the then-monarch’s third born was photographed strolling through Central Park in New York with convicted sex offender Epstein.

Andrew insisted he was there to tell his old friend that he could no longer see him.

On top of that Andrew made an estimated £12million out of court settlement in 2022 with Virginia Giuffre, who alleged that Epstein had sex trafficked her to the then prince when she was aged just 17.

Andrew strongly denied the claims and maintained he did not know Virginia.

All attempts to hold onto his Royal titles crumbled last year when the Epstein files suggested Andrew had maintained a friendship with the disgraced financier long after his conviction in 2008 for soliciting a minor for prostitution.

King Charles’ office finally announced they were severing ties on October 30, 2025.



Buckingham Palace said: “His Majesty has today initiated a formal process to remove the Style, Titles and Honours of Prince Andrew.”

To add injury to insult Andrew was served notice to leave the Royal Lodge in Windsor.

The statement, though, did add: “These censures are deemed necessary, notwithstanding the fact that he continues to deny the allegations against him.”

Then, matters got worse.

In February this year Thames Valley police announced: “We are aware of reports about a woman said to have been taken to an address in Windsor in 2010 for sexual purposes.

“We are assessing the information in line with our established procedures.”

According to the alleged victim’s lawyers she was in her twenties at the time and went to Royal Lodge to meet Andrew. Andrew did not respond to requests for comment, but has always denied wrongdoing.

Another woman is said to have been given a tour of Buckingham Palace by the former Prince.



The Epstein files also revealed private jet logs, which showed Epstein had flown unidentified girls into the UK.

Former British prime minister Gordon Brown called on the Met Police to investigate the allegations.

Andrew was then arrested on the Sandringham estate in Norfolk in February in relation to a Thames Valley Police probe into misconduct in public office.

The Epstein files appeared to show that Andrew forwarded confidential government documents to Epstein in 2010 while serving at the UK’s Trade Envoy.

These could have given Epstein privileged information about lucrative investment opportunities.

Over the years, Epstein was remarkably generous towards Andrew and his former wife Sarah Ferguson in terms of his hospitality.

Andrew denies any wrongdoing and his lawyers successfully challenged the legitimacy of the warrant Thames Valley used to search his property in February.

Has the former globetrotting Trade Envoy truly faced the music, though?



It has been reported that he regularly has dinner with his friends at his Marsh Farm lodging in Sandringham, goes shooting on the Royal estate and rides his horse.

His sister Princess Anne and brother Prince Edward are also loyal.

The ex-Duke has not been seen in public with Eugenie, 36, or Beatrice, 38, since losing his royal titles.

Eugenie gave birth to Adelaide Elizabeth Annina Brooksbank in August. It is not known if Andrew has met Adelaide yet.

Additionally, he is no longer so close to his ex-wife Sarah Ferguson who was removed from various charity roles this year after her friendship with Epstein was revealed.

There has been talk of Andrew moving to the United Arab Emirates, where he has powerful connections.

That comfortable lifestyle might be upended if the Americans finally get their way.

Nigel Cawthorne, author of Virginia Giuffre: Epstein’s Masseuse Who Took Down the Rich and Prince Andrew: Epstein, Maxwell and the Palace explains: “If the Democrats take over the oversight committee, Andrew could be in all sorts of trouble.

“They’ve promised to give the unredacted documents to the police here.

“It was the release of the Epstein files that led to the UK police finally investigating him, but only half have been released so far.”



A lot hinges on the midterm elections in the US.

President Donald Trump and the Republican party have been reluctant to release all of the files.

They still hold the balance of power on the House Oversight Committee which determines what is made public.

Three million of the six million pages remain under wraps.

The Democrats are pushing for full transparency, with Congressman Suhas Subramanyam willing to help get more documents into the hands of British detectives.

Nigel explains: “If the Democrats are in charge of the Oversight Committee and do what they say they’re going to do, then it’s going to push over the edge.

“The police have got to investigate.”

If that wasn’t enough for the former Prince to contend with, there is the issue of Royal lineage.



He is still eighth in line to the throne and MPs have expressed a desire to remove any chance of Andrew ending up with the Crown on his head.

The former Trade Envoy also has to deal with ex-Goldman Sachs banker Selman Turk who has asked to call Andrew as a witness in a civil fraud trial.

All those advisers in the Royal household who hoped that removing the HRH from Mountbatten Windsor’s name would end the slew of negative headlines are going to be disappointed.

Until his association with Epstein has been fully investigated the questions will keep on coming.

Remarkably, though, Andrew Lownie thinks that the disgraced ex-prince still believes he can return to the Royal fold.

He concludes: “I think he still thinks he can come back. This guy is very delusional. It comes from the sense of entitlement.”

News.title: Businesswoman, 24, ‘shot dead by boyfriend, 62, moments after ending their 38-year age gap relationship’
News.content:
GUNNED DOWN Businesswoman, 24, ‘shot dead by boyfriend, 62, moments after ending their 38-year age gap relationship’







Next

A GLAM businesswoman was allegedly shot dead by her boyfriend, who was 38 years older than her, moments after dumping him.

Priscila Lacerda Custodio, 24, was gunned down following a furious row with cattle rancher João Roberto Bolelli, 62, at his Brazilian property.



The couple had been dating for just four months, but Priscila had reportedly endured death threats and accusations of cheating.

Her older lover had also allegedly hired people to spy on her and assaulted her just four days before the killing.



Terrified of Bolelli, Priscila asked her brother and a friend to accompany her to his ranch to return a pickup truck she had been using.

But tensions boiled over when the pair began arguing over the phone before she arrived.



Priscila told Bolelli she wanted nothing more to do with him, before he allegedly opened fire.

The 24-year-old was struck in the chest and arm during the horror attack on Tuesday evening, October 27.

Her terrified brother was also forced to flee when Bolelli allegedly turned the gun on him and chased him.

Priscila was rushed to hospital by her brother but tragically died from her injuries.



Her suspected killer fled the scene in a Toyota Hilux pickup truck, sparking a police manhunt.

The shooting unfolded at the entrance to a rural property off the Candido Portinari Highway in Rifaina, São Paulo State.

A court issued a warrant for Bolelli’s arrest the following day as detectives launched a femicide investigation.



Witnesses later revealed chilling details about the couple’s final confrontation.

According to police reports, the pair had also clashed over a mobile phone Bolelli had given Priscila.

He demanded she return the device, but she insisted he hand back her own phone first.

A friend told investigators that Bolelli had become increasingly suspicious of Priscila’s movements during their short-lived romance.

He allegedly grilled her about a trip to Sacramento, in neighbouring Minas Gerais State, accusing her of secretly meeting another man.



The rancher also reportedly warned Priscila that he would not allow her to return to her hometown of Perdizes.

Just four days before the fatal shooting, on October 23, Bolelli had allegedly assaulted the young businesswoman.

Her friend claimed she had personally seen the injuries and revealed that Priscila had also been threatened with being shot in the head.



The frightened woman was urged not to visit the ranch alone, while her brother told police she had sounded apprehensive when asking him to accompany her.

Priscila’s brutal death has left her loved ones devastated, with friends paying heartbreaking tributes to the ambitious young woman.

She worked in digital marketing and as a videographer, producing content for shops, weddings and other clients.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The 24-year-old had been studying photography and dreamed of buying her own apartment.

Psychologist Fabyana Oliveira, a friend and client, told local media: “Priscila was a wonderful person, full of dreams and plans. Full of life! A life that was cut short by a wicked man.”

News.title: Kim Jong-un ‘SELLING his own people online to Russian businesses to fund North Korea’s nuclear ambitions’
News.content:
RUTHLESS REGIME Kim Jong-un ‘SELLING his own people online to Russian businesses to fund North Korea’s nuclear ambitions’







Next

NORTH Koreans are being sold online to Russian businesses as part of a state sponsored forced labour programme, a report has found.

The twisted scheme allows Vladimir Putin to bolster his war machine with a brutally controlled workforce while Kim Jong-Un snatches their wages to fund his ballistic missile programme, it claims.



A bombshell investigation by the Global Rights Compliance (GRC) has exposed how the two states use the network to “bypass international sanctions” and fuel their military “aggression”.

GRC Legal Advisor Elise Luriot Prevost, who worked on the investigation, told The Sun: “Cooperation between the DPRK and Russia is only getting stronger.



“The DPRK is getting hard cash and fuel while Russia is getting workers to supplement its manpower shortages.”

The report follows a nine-month undercover investigation into KNDR.su, a broker network run by Moscow businessman Vladimir Sokolov.



The platform, which markets North Korean workers for sale, charges a commission of £900 to £1,350 per worker for a minimum of 50 workers.

GRC identified nine sites in Russia associated with North Korea through Sokolov’s network alone.



Elise said: “Both countries treat people as instruments of state power.

“But none of this is new. North Korea has exported forced labour for more than two decades.

“The same can be seen through Russia’s aggression in Ukraine and the high death toll of their own soldiers.

“It seems both countries are willing to sacrifice their own civilians for their military machines.”

Kim and his evil cronies have sent tens of thousands of workers overseas to replace Russians killed since the invasion of Ukraine in 2022.



By using student visas the scheme evades UN sanctions that ban formal labour contracts, the report found.

North Koreans are falsely enrolled at Russian colleges before being shipped abroad and placed at host companies.

Spies hide among work crews to keep a watchful eye on dissent, while workers have their passports confiscated, and any movement is restricted while in Russia.



In one  on the KNDR.su website, possible employers are assured that workers “won’t run away”.

Dylan Carter, Lead Investigator at Global Rights Compliance, said: “These workers do not come cheap, yet little, if any, of the money paid for their labour reaches them.

“Instead, it lines the pockets of the DPRK state.”

Russia granted more than 36,000 visas to North Koreans in 2025 – a fourfold increase from the previous year – of which 98 per cent were student visas.

After North Korea’s sixth nuclear test in 2017, a UN Security Council resolution put a blanket ban on the hiring of its workers overseas and mandated their return home.



But between 35,600 and 101,280 North Korean workers were based overseas in 2025.

This has generated up to an estimated £600million for Pyongyang which is channelled into its ballistic missile programme, according to the report.

The North Korean government is directly involved in the scheme, the report said.



As part of KNDR’s certification process, Russian companies must undergo an inspection visit from the North Korean embassy.

Sites publicised by Sokolov include KPP Ruskon, one of the largest producers of military rations based in Moscow Oblast.

North Korean officials were also documented visiting Agrisovgaz, a US sanctioned metalworking plant whose clients include sanctioned defence, aerospace, and naval enterprises.

Elise said: “Russia and North Korea are trading weapons, knowledge and notably battlefield testing of the weapons in Ukraine.

“North Korea will be able to use this knowledge on how the weapons actually work in the field.”



Since 2024, North Korea has sent more than ‌10,000 troops to fight alongside Russians in the Ukraine war as well as weapons to ‌replenish Moscow’s dwindling armoury.

The war has seen the two despots forging closer ties, with fears Putin’s missile and nuclear knowhow is being transferred to Pyongyang.

It comes as Volodymyr Zelensky warns that Putin is recruiting up to 50,000 North Korean men as he prepares to unleash his worst winter blitz on Kyiv yet.

The reach of Russia’s war economy is “deeply troubling”, Elise said, but the brazen approach is also “striking”.

“Sokolov posts factory visits on his social media and on his website, his operations director told us the arrangement exists to avoid labour law, and the network advertises 12-hour days as a selling point”, Elise explained.



Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, its compliance with the UN sanctions regime has collapsed.

Now facing debilitating labour shortages, Moscow has deepened its ties with Pyongyang.

Elise said: “Russia wants to keep its economy and war effort supplied while showing that UN sanctions can be ignored at little cost.



“This network shows two sanctioned states building a working arrangement outside the rules that constrain them.

“Every unpunished breach weakens the credibility of the sanctions regime and invites others to test it.

“The erosion of existing rules is already visible.”

The latest findings form part of a “consistent” picture of cooperation between Russia and North Korea through a student-visa “pipeline” to fund their military aims, Elise said.

It comes as North Korea has been accused of helping set up sinister camps full of snatched Ukrainian children while pocketing £9.7billion from Putin.



The UK recently sanctioned a chilling camp in North Korea after it was claimed Putin has been coughing up cash to ship off abducted youngsters under the guise of “re-education”.

The International Criminal Court has issued arrest warrants for Putin and his children’s commissioner, Maria Lvova-Belova, over the deportations back in March 2023.

South Korean intelligence estimates the despot has raked in almost £10bn from Putin’s war in Ukraine.

More than £448m of that also comes from “fees” Kim charges for his own soldiers to be sent to the frontlines to fight and die for Russia.

Putin paid the tyrant in hard cash, energy supplies and military technology.



In return, Moscow has received artillery shells, rockets, ballistic missiles, and thousands of troops.

The haul is huge for the hermit kingdom, with the United Nations estimating North Korea’s entire economy was worth just £12.8bn in 2024.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Russian businessman investigated in the report, Sokolov, has recently been sanctioned by the European Union.

The GRC said it approached Sokolov for comment but did not receive a response.

News.title: Met refers itself to police watchdog over ‘lost’ letter to Meghan Markle about dad’s child sex abuse claims
News.content:
Next

THE Met Police has said it has voluntarily referred itself to the police watchdog because it failed to pass on a letter detailing allegations against the Duchess of Sussex’s father to other law enforcement agencies.

The letter, alleging Thomas Markle Snr had sexually abused a child, was sent to cops in 2019 and then passed to Meghan’s office.



Meghan, 45, claimed she cut off all ties with her father after the letter was passed to her, soon after her wedding to Harry.

Thomas Markle Snr strongly denies all of the allegations, and has denounced the accusations as “sick lies.”



On Saturday, the Met confirmed it received a letter in early 2019 containing allegations about Markle Snr but the force admitted they did not share details of the letter with other law enforcement agencies.

The Met Police has now referred itself to the Independent Office for Police Conduct.

The Duchess of Sussex issued a statement saying the letter had been shared with her in 2018.

Her statement followed The Sun’s world exclusive story that award-winning former film lighting man Mr Markle is under investigation for allegedly stashing boxes of child abuse images.

She said the letter contained “troubling and disturbing” allegations and had been sent to the Met’s Royalty and Specialist Protection and “subsequently shared with me.”

Markle’s son sparked the investigation after finding a child abuse video on a phone among his father’s abandoned possessions.



Meg’s half-brother Thomas Jnr told The Sun he handed over four large boxes of items to cops last week — including a mass of unviewed material.

Cops the Philippines are currently investigating suspected child sex abuse images reportedly found at Thomas Markle Sr’s former home.

Markle Snr has admitted paying for sex in the south-east Asian country but denies ever possessing a hoard of such material.



Commander Adam Slonecki, who leads the Metropolitan Police’s Protection Command, said: “In January 2019, the Met received a letter addressed to our Protection Command, specifically the Fixated Threats Assessment Centre.

“The author of the letter suggested they were writing to raise concerns relating to the security of the Duchess of Sussex.

“While the letter did not actually contain any information specifically related to security matters, it did contain a number of claims about alleged offending outside the United Kingdom.

“The letter was assessed and subsequently passed to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex for their awareness.

“The details of the allegations in the letter were not shared with other law enforcement agencies.



“In recent days, the Met’s Directorate of Professional Standards has carried out an initial review into our actions following receipt of the letter in 2019.

“Following that review, a voluntary referral has been made to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) in respect of the decision not to inform other law enforcement agencies, and the decision to pass the letter to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex.

“In addition, it is our intention to make a number of referrals to relevant overseas law enforcement agencies in relation to the allegations contained within the letter.”



Window fitter Thomas Jnr became his father’s full-time carer after he suffered a stroke in 2022 and moved to Mexico to support him.

Markle Snr then moved to the Philippines in 2025 after suffering a series of strokes.

Thomas Jnr found the haul while 82-year-old Markle Snr was receiving medical treatment in the US.

It emerged the alleged stash of sick material included an image of Markle Snr having sex with a girl who appears underage.

Thomas Jnr has now told police further checks of computers, cameras, phone and DVDs unearthed “hundreds, if not thousands” of child abuse pictures and videos.



He said victims apparently no older than ten or 11 appeared in sex acts.

The Sun on Sunday reported how the Duchess of Sussex told her estranged father she knew he had abused young girls in a letter she sent him last year.

Meghan told Markle Snr it would be the last time he ever heard from her — and that she would never allow him to meet his grandchildren.

It is understood she accused him of sexually abusing children and said that the authorities were aware of his vile behaviour.

Meghan learned of allegations in 2019 but was given assurances these were being investigated. She was advised speaking out could jeopardise any potential legal case.

News.title: ‘Christmas cancelled’ as light switch-on is AXED in blow to UK town centre
News.content:
Next

A CHRISTMAS light switch-on in a historic market town has been axed in a blow to residents.

The council has pulled the festivities and admitted it was a “disappointing” decision for locals.

Councillors have confirmed the annual Christmas light switch-on on Kington, Herefordshire, has been cancelled.



They decided to pull the event after meeting the working party responsible for the town’s Christmas lights.



Officials said ongoing works at two buildings in the town, Market Hall and Coach House, raised concerns about putting up the display, reported County Times.

Kington Town Council said contractors found “unexpected issues”, forcing work to stop while they are resolved.

No completion date can currently be confirmed, the council added.

A spokesperson for the town council said: “Whilst this is extremely disappointing, both the town council and chamber of commerce feel that a substandard display would not be appropriate.”

The spokesperson added that “every effort” is being made to organise a Christmas event to replace the usual switch on and residents will be kept informed as soon as they have more details.

News of the cancellation sparked an angry response from residents in the town.

One person posted on Facebook: “Why wasn’t the work started earlier in the year?”



Another person wrote: “How sad.”

A third person added: “Christmas is cancelled.”

News.title: Spain train crash latest: Chilling audio from driver who 'can't start' before 69 killed
News.content:
Two trains ploughed into each other on the high-speed line between Madrid and Andalusia causing carriages to leave the tracks and roll down an embankment

Spain train crash latest: Chilling audio from driver who 'can't start' before 69 killed

Rescuers are using cranes to search the wreckage for people feared trapped after a devastating high-speed train crash in Spain killed at least 69 people.

Among those confirmed dead are former Spanish employment minister Fátima Báñez and 24-year-old athlete Julieta Gallego.

A total of 110 people were taken to hospitals in Castilla-La Mancha following the collision, with 60 since discharged and 50 still receiving treatment.

The crash involved Renfe and Iryo trains on the Madrid-Andalusia high-speed line shortly before 9am on Wednesday, with carriages thrown from the tracks and down an embankment.

Survivors have described “apocalyptic” scenes. One said wrecked carriages had been reduced to a “twisted mass of metal” and looked “as if a bomb had gone off”.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez visited the crash site and declared three days of national mourning, saying: “Today all of Spain is grieving.”

News.title: Man burnt while being kept as prisoner in own home and suffered 11 broken ribs
News.content:
Man burnt while being kept as prisoner in own home and suffered 11 broken ribs

Warren Davies launched a savage attack on Jason Leeder inside his own room, imprisoning him and breaking 11 of his ribs following a dispute

View Image Warren Davies has been jailed (Image: North Wales Police)

A man was kept prisoner in his own room, gagged, punched and had his arm burned with a lighter following a dispute that started over a text message.

‌



‌



The victim, Jason Leeder, had 11 of his ribs broken in the ordeal, which took place inside the room he occupied in shared accommodation in Wrexham, North Wales. A court heard that Warren Davies launched the savage attack on Mr Leeder on February 25 this year.

‌



Mr Leeder was in his room inside a dwelling on Watery Road when Davies arrived at the address to visit his mother who lived there. At around 1am, Davies knocked on the door of Mr Leeder and went inside to use the man's mobile phone as he didn't have one.

‌



Davies logged into his Facebook Messenger account and about 30 minutes later became angry, accusing Mr Leeder of messaging his partner. David Mainstone, prosecuting, said this was "something which he [Mr Leeder] had not done".

Mr Leeder retrieved his phone and messaged Davies' partner to say he was not the one using the device but Davies then locked the door and prevented his victim from leaving, North Wales Live reports. Davies forced a pair of boxer shorts into Mr Leeder's mouth and tried to gag him with a belt.

The victim resisted and Davies used a lighter to burn his arm and punched him to the ribs with both fists as Mr Leeder tried to escape. He fell to the floor and Davies continued to kick and knee him.

‌



"He threatened to torture him with pliers," said Mr Mainstone. "He was terrified at this point the defendant was going to kill him."

Mr Leeder ran down the stairs eventually but was followed by the attacker, who pushed him down the last few steps and forced him into his mother's room.

‌



Mr Leeder managed to escape and ran to Wrexham Maelor Hospital, where he was found to have 11 broken ribs, a split lip and a burn injury to his right arm. In a victim statement, Mr Leeder said he did not expect to be assaulted in his own home and thought he was going to be "tortured for hours".

He added he believed he was going to be killed and no longer felt safe. He was still in pain, struggling to breathe and sleep, and was anxious and scared.

‌



The defendant, 30 and of Watery Road, Wrexham, appeared in court via video link from prison and admitted grievous bodily harm and false imprisonment. The court heard Davies had 18 previous convictions for 48 offences, including common assault, actual bodily harm and assaulting a police officer.

Amy Edwards, defending, said Davies indicated an early guilty plea, had mental health problems and had a traumatic upbringing, with substance misuse issues. He has been trying to access rehabilitation help while on remand and was remorseful.

Article continues below

Sentencing Davies to three years and nine months in prison, Recorder John Philpotts said: "You threatened to torture him and kept him a prisoner in his own flat for a period, before he was able to escape."

Judge Philpotts also granted a restraining order preventing the defendant from approaching or contacting Mr Leeder until further order and ordered Davies to pay a victim surcharge.

News.title: Arsenal learn Max Dowman red card appeal verdict after controversial Fleetwood red card
News.content:
Arsenal learn Max Dowman red card appeal verdict after controversial Fleetwood red card

Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman was sent off after kicking out at Fleetwood midfielder Harrison Neal during the Gunners' defeat in the Carabao Cup fourth round on Tuesday

View 2 Images Max Dowman was given a straight red card against Fleetwood (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

Arsenal's appeal to overturn Max Dowman's red card against Fleetwood has been rejected, the FA have confirmed. Dowman, 16, will now serve a three-game suspension for violent conduct.

‌



‌



The winger reacted to a strong tackle from Harrison Neal by kicking out at the Fleetwood midfielder, and he was shown a straight red card by referee Michael Salisbury in the closing stages of Tuesday's Carabao Cup fourth-round tie. Fleetwood went on to win the game on penalties, booking their place in the quarter-finals for the first time in League Two club's history.

‌



Arsenal launched their appeal on Wednesday but their case has been dismissed. A statement from the FA read: "An independent Regulatory Commission has dismissed claims of both wrongful dismissal and excessive punishment for Max Dowman.

‌



"The Arsenal player was sent off during their EFL Cup game against Fleetwood Town on Tuesday 27 October and will be suspended for three matches. The Regulatory Commission's written reasons for its decisions will be published in due course."

News.title: Man 'kills disabled cousin over £250,000 inheritance by feeding him doughnut'
News.content:
Man 'kills disabled cousin over £250,000 inheritance by feeding him doughnut'

A man has been arrested on suspicion of killing his disabled cousin who could not eat solid food by feeding him a doughnut - he reportedly stood to inherit £250,000

View 2 Images The incident took place in Reggio Emilia, Italy (file) (Image: REDA/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

A man has been charged with killing his disabled cousin after allegedly feeding the man a doughnut despite knowing he could not swallow food due to a medical condition.

‌



‌



The 76-year-old man is now at the centre of a police investigation in the city of Reggio Emilia in Italy. He is suspected of killing his cousin, aged 74, over a £250,000 inheritance.

‌



The suspect is the legal guardian of his cousin, who died from suffocation at the care home where he lived on June 27, according to Italian broadcaster Tgcom24. The 74-year-old suffered from progressive dysphagia, a condition that prevented him from swallowing solids.

‌



View 2 Images The suspect is his cousin's legal guardian (file) (Image: WIKIPEDIA)

The Prosecutor's Office said the victim started having trouble breathing after ingesting a doughnut.

Despite the difficulties breathing, the victim’s cousin is said to have not alerted staff at the care home right away, instead bringing him a canned drink from a vending machine to help him wash the doughnut down.

‌



It wasn’t until after giving him the drink that the suspect called care home staff, telling them his cousin was unwell. He allegedly did not mention the fact that he had fed him solid food.

Paramedics rushed to the care home but sadly the man died of cardiac arrest caused by choking. Nurses at the care home called authorities after they found crumbs on the victim’s clothing.

‌



The Prosecutor's Office said there had been previous occasions where the suspect had tried to give solid food to his cousin, and he had tried before to sneak treats to the care home.

The suspect was also found to be one of the heirs to his cousin's assets, and had allegedly tried to tamper with statements given by family members to police.

Article continues below

He has since been charged with premeditation, abuse of duties in the role of a legal guardian, killing a disabled person, and impaired defence.

He is currently under house arrest.

News.title: OnlyFans rumour about our mate’s sexy new girlfriend
News.content:
Dear Coleen

I’m a woman in my 20s and I’m looking for some advice on whether I should tell a mate about his girlfriend’s past. He’s been seeing her for a few weeks and seems very keen but I’ve found out some things about her.

Basically, someone we know said she’d been on OnlyFans, although she doesn’t seem to do that any more. I’ve also heard that she has a wild dating history, dumping a long-term boyfriend out of the blue for a much older guy, who she dated for ages. We’re a close group of friends and she’s not like anyone else he’s ever been out with.

I don’t want to come across as being judgmental and small minded but I do worry that our friend is getting himself into something that might not be good for him. It’s all we talk about at the moment.

He’s a really lovely person and he’s been burned in the past so I’d feel terrible if it all went wrong and I hadn’t told him what I know. What do you think I should do?

‌



Coleen says

Honestly, I think you are coming across a bit judgy and small minded.

Firstly, your friend might know about his girlfriend’s internet and dating history and, secondly, I don’t think it’s anyone else’s business (even if it’s true). He’s a grown man and free to make his own choices and work out for himself whether this relationship is right for him or not.

You and your friends seem very worked up about this girl coming into the group and that says more about you than it does about her. Why not give her a chance and take the time to see who she is? Why not be welcoming? I’m sure your friend would appreciate that.

What he won’t appreciate is having these rumours repeated to him with a heavy dose of disapproval. So, if this friendship is important to you, I would keep quiet because I don’t think he would take it well and he’s more likely to shoot the messenger than dump his girlfriend and tell you how grateful he is that you shared the information.

If you’d found out she was cheating on him, that would be a different scenario, but to repeat rumours that she was on OnlyFans for a bit and dated an older guy just comes across as a bit spiteful.

News.title: I’ve fallen for an old friend but she doesn’t feel for me
News.content:
Dear Coleen

I’m a man in my thirties and when a good female friend was going through a difficult divorce, I offered her a place to stay until she got back on her feet. We’ve known each other for years and had a brief relationship in our early twenties.

She was grateful to have a room at mine and gradually friendship turned to something more and we started sleeping together but agreed to “no strings”. I suppose we were both lonely and it suited us both at the time.

Although I was OK with it being a casual thing, I’ve developed stronger feelings for her which I should probably have anticipated. The problem is, she admitted recently that she’s met a guy she likes and we need to stop sleeping together.

I know I should have seen this coming, but I didn’t want to see it and started to hope that this casual affair would turn into a proper commitment.

‌



I feel so down about the whole situation which is made even harder because we’re living together. I don’t want to ask her to leave, though, mostly because I don’t want her to go, but I also know she doesn’t have anywhere else to live. It’s a nightmare and the thought of her being with someone else is killing me.

How do I move on from this?

Coleen says

I’m sure you already know this, but the only way for you to move on is for her to move out.

It’s up to her to figure out her living arrangements. You have feelings for her and, as much as you don’t want her to go, you won’t be able to cope with her dating this guy and coming home to your house.

‌



While you didn’t promise each other anything more than friendship and sex, things have changed. You really care for her and want more, and that often happens in these friends-with-benefits situations. One person falls in love, while for the other it remainsjust sex with no emotional attachment and the relationship is a placeholder while they keep their options open and wait for someone else to come along.

Ensure Coleen's advice always appears at the top of your Google Search by making The Mirror a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as your Preferred Source in your Google search settings.

I’m not suggesting you kick her out with nowhere to go, but you need a plan and a timeframe, so she can start looking for somewhere else to live.

I’m hoping she realises it’s time to move on, too, but if she doesn’t, then you need to be honest and explain how you feel and why you’re asking her to leave.

‌



I know it’s hard to feel so vulnerable, but if she’s a good enough friend, she’ll understand and make it easy for you. Good luck.

Get all the latest advice from Britain's straightest-talking agony aunt Coleen Nolan here

Coleen’s words of wisdom

In order to make a fresh start, it’s important to make peace with the past. Accept that you can’t change what happened, but you can let go of regrets or blame and instead focus on the present.
