Sports.title: Tottenham receive major James Maddison injury update after star limped off against Chelsea following ACL return
Sports.content:
Next

JAMES MADDISON’S latest injury is not thought to be serious.

The Tottenham star, who has been beset with crock issues over the last 18 months, limped off in Saturday’s 2-0 win at Chelsea with a suspected groin issue.

It sparked fears of yet another setback for the luckless playmaker who has only recently returned from a long spell out with an anterior cruciate ligament injury.



But SunSport understands the latest problem is not severe, with sources close to the player describing it as fairly minor.



It remains to be seen whether Maddison will be fit enough or not to take part in Spurs’ hosting of Crystal Palace this weekend.

Roberto De Zerbi’s men have the chance to make it three wins in a row when they take on the Eagles in N17 in Saturday’s 5.30pm kick-off.

Maddison sparked the recent upturn in results when scoring on his return to the starting line-up with a wondergoal in the 3-1 victory over boyhood club Coventry 10 days ago.



His creativity in the No10 position has been sorely missed by Spurs over the last few seasons.

Maddison first damaged his medial ligament in the final weeks of the 2024-25 campaign, meaning he missed out on the Europa League semi-finals and final as Tottenham won the competition.

He then suffered his ACL in August 2025 during pre-season and has had a few niggles since returning at the back end of the last campaign.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Boss De Zerbi is set to give an update on Maddison’s fitness in Friday’s press conference ahead of the Palace match.



Other players who missed the Chelsea game through injury include defender Tosin Adarabioyo, Lucas Bergvall, Savio, Wilson Odobert and Xavi Simons.

Loanee Mykhailo Mudryk is also sidelined with an ankle injury picked up in training which De Zerbi described as “stupid” – though the Ukrainian would have been ineligible to face his parent club Chelsea anyway.

Sports.title: Ex-Chelsea star Marc Cucurella’s partner reveals she narrowly missed deadly train crash in Spain which killed 68 people
Sports.content:
Next

THE PARTNER of former Chelsea star Marc Cucurella has revealed how she narrowly avoided being one of the tragic victims of the Toledo train crash in Spain.

At least 68 people were killed and at least 100 more injured in a horrific high-speed train crash amid a failure to communicate about the obstruction from central command.



The tragedy has caused an outpouring of grief across the country and Europe, with several high-profile Spanish footballers also sharing their sympathies.

However, Claudia Rodriguez, the long-term girlfriend of Real Madrid defender Cucurella, shared an Instagram story revealing how she had been travelling to Malaga on the train behind the one involved in the fatal incident.



Taking to the platform, she explained she was “on the way to Malaga on the train behind” and expressed “support to the victims’ families and friends”.

In a longer follow-up story, she added: “Guys, I’m fine. My train wasn’t affected at all since there was plenty of distance between us and the train that had the accident.



“We simply had to turn around and head back to Madrid since it was on the same route.

“It made my stomach turn thinking that if it had happened later, it would have happened to my train, but honestly, that’s nothing compared to what the people who actually were on that train must have gone through.

“All my strength once again to those families.”

She also shared a post asking for blood donations in Madrid, where her family is now based following her boyfriend’s £52million transfer from Chelsea.



The Spanish Football Federation postponed 24 Copa del Rey matches in light of the tragedy which occurred.

A number of La Liga matches were also postponed.

The government also announced three days of national mourning.



It comes mere months after the country’s first fatal train crash this year which also involved one high-speed Renfe train hitting another stationary one from rail operator Iryo.

Claudia and Cucurella met in 2018 and have three children together, Mateo, Rio and Bella.

The pair were together in London for the Ballon d’Or ceremony – won by Harry Kane – ahead of Wednesday’s crash.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish donates £10,000 to dad of three fighting cancer as fans hail ‘one of the kindest footballers out there’
Sports.content:
Next

JACK GREALISH has been hailed as one of the kindest footballers out there after donating £10,000 to help a father-of-three battling aggressive cancer.

The Everton winger made the heartwarming gesture after learning about the plight of Toffees supporter Leon, 35, who has been given just one to three years to live.



Leon is battling an aggressive form of kidney cancer and his family have launched a fundraising campaign to help pay for the best possible treatment.

His partner Crystal Duffey set up a GoFundMe page in a desperate bid to give him more time with their three young sons, aged two, three and ten.



And Grealish, 31, wasted little time in stepping forward with a remarkable £10,000 donation after the appeal was shared on social media.

Everton-supporting DJ Anton Powers had highlighted the family’s heartbreaking situation on Instagram on Wednesday night.

He was left stunned when the former England international responded by digging deep into his pockets.

Powers wrote: “What an absolute gent Jack Grealish is.

“I put up an Insta story up late last night about a heartbreaking situation for a big Everton fan.

“And Jack goes on to donate to his fund. What a top guy.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The generous gesture sparked an outpouring of praise from football supporters, who hailed Grealish for his kindness.

One fan wrote: “Believe he makes a lot of charity donations like this, gent of the game. More players should follow.”

Another said: “In fairness Grealish has shown over the years that he’s class. Fair play.”

A third added: “Absolute top lad is Jack. You can tell he comes from good parents and wants to help where he can.

“Never advertises what he does either, it’s always others that tell his story of just what a good lad he is.”



Grealish has earned a reputation for his charitable gestures over the years, regularly helping families facing heartbreaking circumstances.

In 2021, he donated £5,000 to the family of a woman who died in a car accident.

Two years later, he gave another £5,000 towards the funeral costs of an Aston Villa supporter.

He also contributed £5,000 to help Birmingham City fan Dylan Lamb travel to America for a clinical trial as he battled blood cell cancer.



And last year, Grealish donated £1,000 towards funeral expenses in another fundraising appeal, as well as £1,400 to help a man seeking specialist cancer treatment.

The former Manchester City star returned to Everton for a second loan spell at the start of the season after injuries disrupted his first campaign at the club.

But his latest act of generosity has once again won him plenty of admirers away from the pitch.

Sports.title: Worst returns to old clubs EVER after Alonso’s Liverpool nightmare, with Ole’s Man Utd woe and Lampard’s Chelsea despair
Sports.content:
Next

RETURNING home after a holiday away can always feel strange.

For football managers returning to their former playing clubs, it can even be nightmarish.



Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso proved just that having witnessed ANOTHER Anfield defeat last night but with a whole new club.

Andoni Iraola’s side dumped the Blues out of the Carabao Cup as Wesley Fofana shot his penalty over the bar to see Liverpool win 5-3 on pens – after Cody Gakpo and Morgan Rogers cancelled each other out with a spot-kick apiece.



In 2024, the German boss had already grimaced at a 4-0 thrashing at his old stomping ground with Bayer Leverkusen.

But Alonso is not the first familiar face to fall victim to a warm welcome turning sour and he will not be the last.



SunSport looked back at the nightmarish returns for managers to their former clubs.

Vincent Kompany (Man City 6-0 Burnley, 2023)

Manchester City’s former skipper made his box office return to the Etihad with his promotion-chasing Burnley side.

But Erling Haaland was not planning to take it easy, especially given it was the FA Cup quarter-finals.

The Norway striker picked up a hat-trick as Pep Guardiola’s men put six past the Clarets to leave Kompany with a painful reminder of the damage City can deliver.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Frank Lampard (Chelsea 3-2 Derby, 2018)

Chelsea’s record goalscorer returned to Stamford Bridge in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup – only to watch his Derby side fall apart.

Own goals from Fikayo Tomori and Richard Keogh cancelled out the two goals that Derby managed to actually get into the opposition’s net.

Cesc Fabregas was the man of the hour who settled the four-goal confusion in the first-half.

Ole Gunnar Solskjaer (Man United 2-0 Cardiff, 2014)

United’s former super sub found himself back at Old Trafford leading Cardiff in a classic Premier League clash.



But the welcome was much warmer than the result after Robin van Persie and Ashley Young both scored on the night that Juan Mata made his Man Utd debut.



But on his return, nearly five years later, then-United caretaker boss Solskjaer thrashed Neil Warnock’s Bluebirds 5-1 on the road.

Xabi Alonso (Liverpool 4-0 Bayer Leverkusen, 2024)

Alonso brought his German champions to Anfield for a huge box office Champions League clash.

The 44-year-old was still a fan favourite following his part in Liverpool’s 2005 European triumph.



But the reunion turned sour after Luis Diaz scored a hat trick in the second-half.

And Gakpo joined in to send Leverkusen back to the Bundesliga with their tails between their legs.

Graham Potter (Brighton 4-1 Chelsea, 2022)

Graham Potter was handed a sensational snub after walking away from Brighton for a huge fee in September 2022 – even if he was not a player.

On his first trip back to the seaside Amex, Potter watched on as his Chelsea side went three down before half-time, including two own-goals.



Roberto De Zerbi celebrated his first Brighton win but it had to be after his predecessor’s unfortunate expense.

Pep Guardiola (Barcelona 3-0 Bayern Munich, 2015)

Everyone knew what Lionel Messi could do, but the question of how to stop him was another matter.

Pep Guardiola’s Bayern side held out until the 77th minute before Messi struck twice, famously leaving Jerome Boateng on the turf for his second.

And, of course, Neymar had to add a third in injury time.



Bayern fought back in the next leg of the Champions League semi-final but Neymar’s brace secured Barca progression – to eventually be crowned winners.

Pep Guardiola (Barcelona 4-0 Man City, 2016)

Different club but the same nightmare…

In true Messi fashion, the Argentine helped himself to a hat-trick on Guardiola’s return with Man City.

And to add to the drama, former Barcelona goalkeeper Claudio Bravo was sent for an early shower for handling outside his area.



But it was Neymar (again) who delivered the final blow for Pep.

Mikel Arteta (Everton 1-0 Arsenal, 2023)

Arteta returned to Goodison Park with Arsenal top of the Prem, only to find his old club thriving with a case of new manager fever.

James Tarkowski headed in the winner in Sean Dyche’s first game at the helm to hand the Gunners their second league defeat of the season in February.

Steven Gerrard (Liverpool 1-0 Aston Villa, 2021)

Anfield welcomed back its former captain… but Mohamed Salah wasn’t feeling quite so generous.



His second-half penalty condemned Steven Gerrard to defeat on his first return as rival manager, and only after Villa had spent more than an hour frustrating the hosts.

Kevin Keegan (Liverpool 4-3 Newcastle, 1996)

Kevin Keegan’s title-chasing Newcastle were forced to come from behind TWICE – only to still lose out at Anfield.

Stan Collymore delivered the injury time blow which saw the Liverpool hero slumped over the advertising boards in what became the decisive snap from the seven-goal classic.



Kenny Dalglish (Liverpool 2-1 Blackburn, 1995)

Blackburn’s Alan Shearer opened the scoring before John Barnes cancelled it out after half-time.

But it was Jamie Redknapp’s late free kick that threatened to turn Dalglish’s Anfield return into the cruellest of title day disasters.

The visitors were two points ahead of United, but thanks to the Red Devils’ tie at West Ham, Blackburn held onto a one point lead to secure the title.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Luckily for the Liverpool legend, United’s draw at West Ham meant Blackburn were champions anyway.

Sports.title: Emi Martinez ‘set to hand Chelsea miraculous injury boost with speedy recovery from broken jaw’ to re-bench Mike Penders
Sports.content:
Next

CHELSEA goalkeeper Emi Martinez could be set for a stunning early return from a broken jaw in a major boost for the Blues.

The Argentine World Cup winner has been sidelined since suffering the nasty injury during Chelsea‘s 2-0 victory over Everton on October 17.



Martinez, 34, was forced off following a collision with Toffees defender Jarrad Branthwaite at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

The former Aston Villa star subsequently underwent surgery and initially suggested he would be out for several weeks.



But according to The Athletic, there is growing optimism that Martinez could return sooner than originally anticipated.

It is also reported that the goalkeeper has been seeing a specialist about having a protective mask fitted in a bid to speed up his comeback.

However, it remains unclear exactly when he will be fit enough to return to action.

Martinez’s potential early comeback would be a welcome boost for Chelsea, who have endured a difficult spell without their first-choice goalkeeper.

Belgian youngster Mike Penders, 21, has stepped in between the sticks during the Argentine’s absence.

Penders replaced Martinez against Everton before making his first Premier League start in last weekend’s clash with Tottenham.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

However, it proved a difficult afternoon for the youngster as he was at fault for Spurs’ opening goal in a 2-0 defeat at Stamford Bridge.

The Belgian produced a much-improved performance against Liverpool in Wednesday’s Carabao Cup clash.

But his efforts were not enough to prevent Chelsea from crashing out of the competition following a penalty shootout defeat.

Martinez’s return could see Penders relegated to the bench once again as the Blues look to get their season back on track.

The Argentine only arrived at Stamford Bridge in August after completing a £7.5million move from Aston Villa.



He has made six appearances for Chelsea so far, keeping just one clean sheet — against Everton in the match in which he suffered his injury.

Chelsea are currently fifth in the Premier League after winning four of their opening eight matches.

They welcome Manchester United to Stamford Bridge on Saturday as they look to bounce back from their recent setbacks.

Sports.title: Carrick ready to 'move forward' with Fernandes as captain
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick says he is ready to "move forward" with Bruno Fernandes as Man Utd captain.

Carrick benched Fernandes for Sunday's 3-0 loss to Bournemouth after the midfielder spoke out about his manager's tactics in the Champions League defeat at Como last week.

Sky Sports News reported Carrick and Fernandes held clear-the-air talks on Tuesday.

On Sunday, Carrick said the decision to name Fernandes among the subs was for "football" reasons and he stood by that statement on Thursday in a press conference ahead of Saturday's Premier League trip to Chelsea.

"It was a decision for the game. That's it," said Carrick. "Bruno is fully committed to this football club. I've got no issues with that, we move forward.

"We're looking forward to the game now."

On whether Fernandes would continue as captain after Harry Maguire took the armband last weekend, Carrick said: "There's no decision to be made on that."

Carrick was then asked whether Fernandes was too emotional to be captain and gave his clear backing to the 32-year-old.

"He's the captain of our football club," said Carrick. "There are different personalities, different characteristics, different ways to lead. It all comes down to what happens on the football pitch and whether you win or not in the end.

"He cares deeply about this football club and the team and he's desperate to do well. We'll lead that together."

Carrick: I don't need assurances on my future

Carrick's future as Man Utd head coach has been in the spotlight since the defeat at home to Bournemouth extended the club's worst-ever start to a Premier League season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Manchester United’s match against Bournemouth in the Premier League.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox met at the club's Carrington training ground this week to discuss next steps but Carrick will continue to lead the team.

Despite the noise around his position, Carrick has insisted he doesn't require guarantees from the hierarchy about his long-term security.

"I don't need assurances from anyone," he said in Thursday's press conference. "I totally get the position, I get the job, the responsibility, I get what comes with that. I really don't need any assurances from anyone in that regard."

Carrick said his "main focus" has been preparing for Chelsea and he is not tuned in to criticism or questions about his future in the media.

"I don't see it," he said. "I only see the things I need to see.

"I don't look for it. It doesn't help. I've said it before, I care about what the supporters think. I care about how it feels in the stadium and them travelling to games - I care about what we give them and what they see.

"I genuinely don't take any notice of anything else. I know this job and I know what we need to be better. I don't need anyone else to tell me."

Asked if he was surprised to still be in his position, Carrick said: "No. I'm here to do my job. I'm here to do the best for the team. I'm desperate to make things better and improve things. I'm not surprised, no."

Analysis: Cool Carrick delivers message of togetherness

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Kaveh Solhekol reflects on Michael Carrick's press conference on Thursday and how the Manchester United boss dealt with questioning over his future and Bruno Fernandes being his captain.

Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol:

"He handled himself very well. He was very cool, he was very calm, he was very self-assured.

"The message he was trying to send out was: 'we at this club are going to stick together, I'm going to stick together with the players, the players are hurting, we accept performances and results haven't been good enough but we're working hard to turn things around'.

"I got the sense Carrick didn't want to talk too much about Fernandes. But we know he's had clear-the-air talks with Fernandes and it seems he will remain as captain.

"When it comes to handling the media, Carrick is the ultimate safe pair of hands because of his experience at the highest level being a player. He knows how things can be spun and blown up out of proportion.

"His message is always 'this is not about me, it's all about Man Utd, the club'."

Sports.title: McDermott: England face 'unique task' to progress and can't get distracted
Sports.content:
Brian McDermott has warned his England side not to chase the points as they look to keep their slim Rugby League World Cup hopes alive with a big win against Papua New Guinea.

England are up against it in their bid to make it through to the semi-finals after they lost 30-12 to Tonga in their opening game.

They must beat Papua New Guinea in their final pool game in Woollongong on Friday and then wait until Sunday, when they need Tonga to beat Samoa, upon whom England must also make up a 68-point deficit.

That means tries will be the order of the day against Papua New Guinea but McDermott, who saw his side beat France 82-0 in their second game, has called for patience.

"We've got a specific task this weekend. I think it'll be a stiffer test than it was against France," McDermott said at his Thursday press conference.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brian Carney discusses the core issues surrounding Rugby League in the UK and why the gap with Australia is getting larger.

"We once again find ourselves in another similar situation, very unique as well, that we don't just need to beat them, we need to be beat them convincingly.

"If we're going to go through, we need to score the points, but we can't get to the points first.

"We've got to get to the physicality first and we're going to manage a very physical team, a very dominant team.

"There's a discipline in that we don't start looking for things or searching for things outside of how we want to play.

"That was really impressive against France because we knew we had points in us and they weren't coming in that first 20 [minutes]. We didn't try to do anything different.

"Every team, and I've been involved in so many teams, where you're winning by a large margin and you either take your foot off the gas because we think it's job done or you start to overplay.

"But against France we stuck to the game model and just put it on rinse and repeat."

Image: McDermott has previously branded the Rugby League World Cup format 'harsh,' with his side up against it to progress

While England made hay against the French in Perth, McDermott knows Papua New Guinea represent a tougher task.

"They're well coached by Jason Demetriou, who's got a chunk of players who are playing in the British game as well," he said.

"So I think they are going to be really well co-ordinated."

What do England need to avoid historic early World Cup exit?

Quite simply, before Tonga face Samoa, England must beat Papua New Guinea and do it by a considerable margin.

Samoa's thumping 78-4 win over France in their tournament opener and a 64-6 victory over Papua New Guinea on Saturday leaves them with an impressive +132 point difference.

England beating France takes them to a +64 points difference, 68 points behind Samoa heading into the final round of fixtures. Another win Friday would lift them to four points and level with both Samoa and Tonga.

McDermott's side would then be left to wait 48 hours for the outcome of Tonga vs Samoa in Sydney. A Samoa win would guarantee England's elimination, while a Tonga victory would see the points difference decide second spot.

Image: England were thrashed by Tonga in their opening game at the 2026 Rugby League World Cup

England don't necessarily need to beat Papua New Guinea by 68 points or more, but a victory by that margin would mean any loss for Samoa would be enough to progress.

A smaller England win would see them need Samoa to lose by a bigger score, depending on England's final points difference.

The winner of the combined Groups B+C table would progress to the semi-finals to face the runner-up of Group A, a four-team league consisting of Australia, New Zealand, Fiji and the Cook Islands.

Havertz has been Mikel Arteta's first choice since returning from injury last season. The 27-year-old started and scored in the Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain in May and appeared to pick up where he left off in the new campaign.

After scoring in the Community Shield against Manchester City, Havertz added Premier League goals against Coventry and his former club Chelsea. Since then, though, he has played 561 minutes, more than nine hours, without finding the net in any competition.

Gyokeres finally broke his duck for the season in Tuesday's Carabao Cup penalty shoot-out loss to Fleetwood Town when he bundled in Arsenal's equaliser from close range. But it has been a struggle for him to even produce shots never mind goals.

Gyokeres has only mustered one shot, a header which looped harmlessly into the air against Nottingham Forest, in 148 Premier League minutes. The Sweden international hasn't registered any shots at all in his 160 minutes in the Champions League.

For the most part, the lack of goals from Arsenal's strikers hasn't mattered. They sit level on points with City at the top of the Premier League having won all but one of their eight games and have taken seven points from a possible nine in the Champions League.

But Arteta will be aware of just how tough it will be to continue their strong start to the season if they don't start to produce.

Nearly three months in, it is damning that Arsenal's defenders have scored more goals in all competitions than their strikers.

Sunday's meeting with Isak, a striker Arsenal coveted before his £125m move to Liverpool from Newcastle, is a reminder of what they lack. The club have built formidable resources in defence and midfield but still don't have a world-class goalscorer.

It is partly a result of how funds have been allocated.

The club have spent only £224.5m on forwards since Arteta's appointment, initially as head coach, in 2019 compared to £550.1m on midfielders and £350m on defenders.

Arsenal tried to address the issue in the summer. But after their unsuccessful pursuits of Vinicius Jr and Julian Alvarez, they opted to stick with what they had, hoping Havertz could stay fit and Gyokeres could build on a 21-goal first season at the club.

Havertz's loss of form may have something to do with the hamstring injury he suffered on Germany duty but he was the main culprit for Arsenal's wasteful display against Fleetwood on Tuesday, when he was unable to score from seven shots.

His failure to capitalise frustrated Arsenal fans but his efforts called to mind comments by Brentford owner Matthew Benham earlier this year on how he assesses strikers. "For a striker, getting in position is way more informative than finishing," he said.

Image: Arsenal's Kai Havertz celebrates his goal against Coventry on the opening day

Benham believes that generating a high volume of chances is the biggest indicator of future success for a striker. And that is one area in which Gyokeres, who only had three shots to Havertz's seven against Fleetwood, has struggled at Arsenal.

Gyokeres has failed to register a shot in eight Premier League starts. It is the second-highest total of any out-and-out striker since the start of last season, behind only Randal Kolo Muani, who spent last term fighting relegation while on loan at Spurs.

Gyokeres can of course point to a decent scoring record. His 14 Premier League goals last season helped Arsenal win the title.

But none of them came against opponents of Liverpool's quality, which is why Arteta may hesitate to start him on Sunday.

A comparison between Gyokeres and Havertz's last two Premier League starts against Liverpool illustrates the differences in what they offer against top opposition.

Gyokeres didn't register a shot in either of his, which came in last season's 1-0 loss in August and the 0-0 draw in January. He had a combined total of just 25 touches, only four of which came in Liverpool's box. He only made 11 passes and won three duels.

Havertz didn't score in either of his last two starts against Liverpool either, in the 2-2 draw in October 2024 and the 3-1 win in February of the same year. But he caused problems in both, registering five shots worth 1.22 xG and having 14 touches in the box.

He also contributed far more in general play, as is typical. Havertz had 80 touches - more than three times as many as Gyokeres. He made considerably more passes, created more chances, won a far higher number of duels and won possession more times too.

Havertz's ability to combine with team-mates, interchange positions and help construct attacks makes Arsenal far more fluid in the final third and helps to explain why their open-play threat has increased this season, even as their striker's goal drought continues.

Arteta could opt for another player up front on Sunday. Mikel Merino is an option after proving his value as a makeshift striker. But Havertz remains the most likely candidate given the breadth of what he brings. A first goal since September would be timely.

Araujo a Liverpool favourite

Ronald Araujo will face Arsenal on Sunday having produced another excellent performance for Liverpool in their Carabao Cup win over Chelsea. The summer signing's resolute defending helped his side through. He made 10 of the team's 15 clearances.

He was similarly effective in their 2-0 win over Brighton last weekend, drawing roars of approval from fans at Anfield with his crunching tackles. "When you see someone like Ronald making challenges, being aggressive at the right times, everyone responds and that energy can help the team going forward," said Virgil van Dijk.

Image: Ronald Araujo has made a big contribution defensively, despite only playing 496 of Liverpool's 720 Premier League minutes so far this season

Araujo played in his natural position at centre-back against Chelsea but has mostly been used by Andoni Iraola at right-back. The size of his contribution to Liverpool's defensive efforts, even in a relatively unfamiliar role, can be seen in the numbers.

Iraola has also noted his offensive improvement. Araujo scored in Liverpool's Champions League wins over LASK and Villarreal and would have had a third goal against Chelsea if not for a superb save from Mike Penders. It all adds up to a positive impression.

On Sunday, Liverpool vs Arsenal headlines the action, with kick-off at 4.30pm. The weekend's live coverage concludes on Monday Night Football, when Newcastle United take on Everton at 8pm.

Sports.title: WNBA Finals set to make history: Watch Game 6 live on Sky Sports
Sports.content:
WNBA Finals: Game 6 live on Sky Sports, Thursday at 4.30pm as Golden State Valkyries vs Atlanta Dream makes history

Game 6 of the WNBA Finals between Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream takes place live on Sky Sports on Thursday October 29 at 4.30pm

On Thursday, either the Golden State Valkyries will win a WNBA championship in just their second year of existence, live on Sky Sports, or the Atlanta Dream will force the first Game 7 in league history.

Amid scheduling drama, which has resulted in a 12.30pm tip off time in Atlanta - and 9.30am in San Francisco - the match is still a sell out and much anticipated.

"I'd like to see it be a national holiday for all WNBA championship games," Atlanta coach Karl Smesko said in jest this week.

"I hope everybody gets to see it, somehow. I know for some people, it's not realistic. They have jobs. They won't be able to make it. I'm disappointed for that, but I'm really hopeful that as many people can see the game as possible."

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

The game could have been played at Atlanta's 'usual' home court at the Gateway Center Arena on Thursday night. It would have been a great atmosphere, but nobody wanted the tiny crowd of 3,500 or so.

In the future, State Farm and its 17,000 capacity will become the full-time home of the Dream, which means potential WNBA Finals dates won't clash with Atlanta Hawks NBA games.

"It's better than, you know, having it at the YMCA that night in front of 75 people," the NBA's Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said. "They're doing what they've got to do."

The Valkyries, for their part, have some ideas on how fans can manage the early start time.

"Call in sick," guard Veronica Burton said. "I recommend it."

Forward Kiah Stokes added: "Don't y'all know how to fake a cough?"

The players have handled it with a sense of humour. So too has Smesko, with his tongue-in-cheek plea for a national holiday to be declared.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Continued growth in record-breaking year for WNBA

Game 6 will serve as either the last game, or the next-to-last game, in a season that the WNBA can point to as a sign of continued growth.

There were more games than ever, which meant that more people showed up than ever - around 3.8 million and counting this season, including playoffs.

The average number of fans per game will end up around 11,500, another record and up about 4.5 per cent over the previous season.

Las Vegas star A'ja Wilson won her record fifth MVP award. The league set records for points and three-pointers per game. A new star was born, with Minnesota's Olivia Miles the unanimous pick as rookie of the year.

Atlanta's Angel Reese was named defensive player of the year, while in Indiana, Kelsey Mitchell and Caitlin Clark scored more points than any WNBA backcourt ever in a season.

The playoffs too were unpredictable, and will end with a new champion crowned. But it's just a case of whether it will happen at Game 6 on Thursday?

Sports.title: Carrick keeps Fernandes as captain and says he needs no assurances on United future
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick has said he will not strip Bruno Fernandes of the Manchester United captaincy after dropping him for the defeat by Bournemouth and that he is not surprised to have kept his job as the head coach.

Carrick and Fernandes held talks this week after the Portuguese criticised the tactics in the loss to Como, resulting in the midfielder being an unused substitute on Sunday. Harry Maguire took the armband but will not retain it for Saturday’s game at Chelsea, with Carrick saying “there is no decision to be made” and praising Fernandes.

“He’s an important player for this group,” he said. “He has been and he will be. Between us, we’ve got to make a difference and we’ve got to push things in a good direction. He’s fully committed to this football club, he’s fully committed to making things better. It doesn’t change for me. He’s the one that’s kind of led the team so well for many a game and many a year, and he’ll continue to do that.”

Carrick’s future remains unclear but he has been given a chance to turn around United’s form. The hierarchy held talks over whether to stick with Carrick at the start of the week after eight games without a win, including a wait of more than two months for a Premier League victory. There is keen interest in Eddie Howe or Julian Nagelsmann as potential replacements.

“I don’t need any assurances from anyone,” Carrick said. “I totally get the position, I understand the job, I understand the responsibilities, I understand what comes with that.”

Asked whether he was surprised still to be in charge, Carrick said: “No, I am here to do my job. I am here to do the best for the team, and I am desperate to make us better and improve things, so I’m not surprised, no.”

The United supporters cheered Carrick off after the Bournemouth game, turning their anger on the players, who were booed at Old Trafford. “I care about what the supporters think,” Carrick said. “I care about what it feels like in the stadium, and them travelling for games, to come and see us and support us.

“I care about what we give them, and what we offer them, and what they see. I genuinely don’t take any notice of anything else. I know this job, I know what it brings, I know what we need to do really to be better. I don’t need anyone else to tell me anything else.”

Sports.title: Liverpool beat Chelsea as three more join penalty hall of shame | Football Daily
Sports.content:
FOFANA’S PENALTY GOES POSTAL

Football Daily isn’t suggesting standards at Chelsea have slipped in recent years, but the quality of their players who miss penalties in shootouts against Liverpool certainly appears to be on the slide. Before last night, footballing royalty such as Arjen Robben, Geremi, Tammy Abraham, César Azpilicueta, Mason Mount and even goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga had all missed from the spot in four consecutive post-match deciders against Liverpool across 19 years and four different competitions. On Wednesday, a flame-haired Argentinian irritant, a striker we’d never previously heard of before yesterday and a defensive liability whose boots increasingly look to have been welded on to the wrong feet each added their names to the roll of shame. Valentín Barco, Emanuel Emegha and Wesley Fofana, take a collective bow.

On a night when the two head coaches made a combined 11 changes to their starting lineups, it was Liverpool who advanced to the Fizzy Cup quarter-finals. Any remaining doubt that Liverpool would notch up yet another shootout win over Chelsea evaporated when Fofana’s penalty proved more of a threat to the windscreens of passing motorists on nearby Walton Breck Road than Giorgi Mamardashvili’s goal. “This is football, this is part of our job,” sighed Xabi Alonso, over the sound of screeching brakes and shattering glass. “We played with courage, the game was close with not many chances for both sides. It is a small setback because it is probably the least important competition for us.” Despite Alonso’s assessment of Fizzy Cup’s place in the domestic trophy pecking order being entirely correct, he has been accused of being disrespectful towards a competition that has previously staged its first round draw in a Morrisons supermarket and once seriously harboured notions of conducting a zero-gravity equivalent in outer space.

The Chelsea head coach is also accused of contemptuousness towards Estêvão, the young Brazilian tyro considered a certainty to start in the absence of Cole Palmer, but spent the evening looking increasingly forlorn on the bench. Despite repeated calls for the introduction of “Steve-oh!” from travelling Chelsea fans, Alonso elected not to use the 19-year-old, prompting rumours of some sort of rift. “I understand his situation and that he could be happier for sure,” he parped of a future superstar who has spent just 172 minutes on the pitch under his watch. “We have had some intense games and there will be moments for everything. I’m sure Estê will have his moment.”

As for Liverpool, progressing felt less like a triumph of tactical ingenuity and more like an unavoidable civic duty, on a par with renewing one’s car tax or desperately trying to get out of jury service. Their reward is a quarter-final tie at home to Bournemouth, setting up a potentially awkward reunion between Andoni Iraola and the club he left behind for bigger things. “Honestly, I was talking before the draw and I said: ‘The only team I don’t want is Bournemouth’,” he sighed. “For me, it’s special. They know me very well. They are playing very well lately, in a good moment but it is what it is.” On the bright side, with this being the lowly Fizzy Cup, he won’t have to pretend to be too upset when one of the two sides competing on four different fronts inevitably gets knocked out.

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Join Scott Murray from 7.45pm GMT for hot Carling Cup fourth-round updates from Everton 1-2 Newcastle and Sarah Rendell for Women’s Bigger Cup action from Manchester City 3-1 Paris Saint-Germain.

I want to thank the fans for their support, and I wish the squad, the management, staff, and the supporters the very best for the future” – James McClean and Derry City confirm they have reached a mutual agreement to terminate McClean’s contract with immediate effect. The forward had not played for the club since July.

Main after match conversation topics were how we’d shipped four goals in the second half, our new signing Gary Madine, and those people on the balconies of the new flats who watched the game for free. Sports.title: Rodman rule has been revised but the fight to keep stars in the NWSL goes on | Moving the Goalposts
Sports.content:
When Washington plays Chicago this Sunday in DC, “Rowdy Audi” will probably be full. It will also be full when the post-season starts, should they lock up their top-four position with a positive result on Decision Day. Equipped with an accessible stadium in a big city, a proud fanbase and a formidable roster rife with players qualifying for the High Impact Player (HIP) rule’s initial criteria (including Trinity Rodman, who gave the rule its moniker), the Spirit hold sway in the attendance charts.

But starting next season, everyone on the Spirit will qualify for the “Rodman Rule”. So will every player in NWSL. Announced Friday, NWSL settled a grievance with the league’s Players Association, who argued that the initial criteria violated federal labor law.

Admittedly, when the new policy arrived on the scene last winter, it appeared half-baked, a somewhat frantic attempt to keep Rodman from floating across the Atlantic and doing something terrible, like playing for Michele Kang’s London City Lionesses instead of Michele Kang’s Washington Spirit.

A rule was born to prevent that. It allocated added funds beyond the salary cap for players who met league-set criteria that clearly prioritized international name recognition in a global market. Qualifying players needed to meet one of eight categories including SportsPro Media’s top 150 Most Marketable Athletes (only Alessia Russo and Aitana Bonmatí placed in 2026, though 16 female football players did in 2025, including three in the NWSL at the time – Trinity Rodman, Sophia Wilson and Marta, in that order). It also included ESPN’s Top 50, the Guardian’s top 100, top minutes on the US national team, the Ballon d’Or’s 30-player list, or NWSL’s MVP and Best XI awards.

Some measure of umbrage followed, as invested onlookers argued for a simpler solution: just raise the salary cap. And perhaps they should, but keeping an American-style sports league competitive in a global football landscape is less straightforward. The looming spectre of Europe’s super-teams, who have attracted key members of the USWNT starting XI, is ever present, waiting to take Croix Bethune away for the right amount of money. No doubt, the NWSL’s appeal is evident in its expansion and growth, in the success of its spine of stateside stalwarts, in its rapidly expanding dedicated facilities, and in the international talents such as Esme Morgan or Ann-Katrin Berger that choose to sharpen their skills in the US.

However, the domestic sporting culture of the NWSL is somewhat at odds, in some ways a disadvantage, when it comes to maintaining its margins, with a stand-alone team structure in a parity-driven league, while competing for international glory with teams such as Chelsea, Lyon or Barcelona, who spend three times or more the amount that some NWSL teams do. While competing for status as the world’s go-to destination, for players and fans, glory hunting and name recognition do matter.

Just look at the Ballon d’Or: Barcelona’s women took all but one of the awards available to them, though Alexia Putellas, who collected her third main prize, now plays in London. That Putellas deserves her trophy is not in dispute, though the inequitable factors contributing to international accolades were manifest. Putellas starred for two super-teams: Barcelona and Spain. Ewa Pajor, Barcelona’s Polish striker, fell just short, perhaps edged out by only having one super-team to play for.

View image in fullscreen Alexia Putellas’ performances for two super-teams – Barcelona and Spain – offered a fine platform for her to win the Ballon d’Or again. Photograph: Tolga Akmen/EPA

Subtly, it seemed, the original criteria for the HIP rule flirted with the idea of fostering a super-team in the US. Prior to the update, there was no cap on the number of players who could access the extra million if the salary cap was already met. For a team such as Kang’s in Washington, the door felt open, possibly, to building a team even more ready to contend with the heavy spenders in Europe (including those also funded by Kang), and the international accolades that go with it. If a NWSL player lifted the NWSL trophy, helped win January’s inaugural Club World Cup, then performed well at the World Cup, could a second NWSL (active) player win the Ballon d’Or?

The structure of the HIP rule remains in place. Teams that have met 2027’s salary cap of $4.4m (£3.3m) in 2027 can spend an additional $1.257m (as reported by ESPN) on a player. The post-grievance difference is that teams can spend that additional sum on any player. Gone are the stipulations mandating adherence to that eight-criteria list of global recognition.

The change is a win for players that did not meet it, which includes elite players who fell short in previous seasons (such as Ashley Sanchez) or star players with long-lasting or recurring injuries (Catarina Macario). It gives the NWSL’s individual teams the autonomy to decide which players are worthy, based on whatever criteria they see fit. And, with a cap on the number of players that can access it, it gives cash-strapped teams the theoretical ability to rein in teams with already-stacked rosters.

But the spirit of NWSL’s original criteria has more merit than many suggest. The NWSL is responsible for securing overhead issues such as an improved media rights deal, marketing marquee names to broadcasters, ensuring the league is seen as the go-to destination before a World Cup and performing well in global cup competitions such as the Concacaf W Champions Cup (Mexico’s Club América prevailed in the most recent final) or the upcoming Club World Cup. With that in mind – plus the ever-pressing desire to keep USWNT players in the US – the original HIP criteria had its eye on awarding stardom as it’s seen in the global market.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Stardom is imprecise. It’s hard to measure, but impossible to miss. Rodman did not make the Ballon d’Or shortlist and is not leading the Golden Boot race. But Rodman and her closest national team peers (including “Triple Espresso” compadres Mallory Swanson and Wilson) are the presumed stars of the NWSL. Rodman, alongside Wilson (who clocked the Michael Jordan “shrug” celebration after scoring in the 2022 Championship final) have not just the skill but the personality flourishes reminiscent of Alex Morgan sipping the tea in Lyon.

The NWSL has yet to replicate the Morgan effect (think default attendance records and adoring away fans), but requiring that teams reward players with a certain je ne sais quoi in their international football fame was baked into the league’s original attempt at the HIP criteria.
