In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Jake Paul will make his boxing comeback on Christmas Eve in Dubai - just a year after suffering a double broken jaw in brutal defeat by Anthony Joshua
Sports.content:
Jake Paul will make his boxing comeback on Christmas Eve in Dubai - just a year after suffering a double broken jaw in brutal defeat by Anthony Joshua

Jake Paul has confirmed he will return to the boxing ring on Christmas Eve in Dubai, almost a year after suffering a double broken jaw in his defeat by Anthony Joshua.

The YouTuber turned boxer will headline a Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) event on December 24, marking his first professional fight in Dubai.

Paul's opponent is expected to be announced in the coming days, with the American already understood to have held talks with former UFC star Darren Till.

He has also been in discussions with former UFC heavyweight Alistair Overeem, although Paul is understood to want the Dutchman to lose a significant amount of weight before they could agree to fight.

MVP have yet to confirm who Paul will face as he prepares to return to action following the most damaging defeat of his professional career.

The 29-year-old was stopped by Joshua in the sixth round of their heavyweight showdown in Miami on December 19, 2025, after struggling to cope with the Briton's size, power and experience.

Jake Paul has confirmed he will return to the boxing ring on Christmas Eve in Dubai, almost a year after suffering a double broken jaw in his defeat by Anthony Joshua

Paul pictured fighting AJ at the Kaseya Center, Miami, Florida on December 19, 2025

Paul spent much of the early stages attempting to keep his distance from the former two-time unified heavyweight world champion, using his movement to evade Joshua's attacks.

But the contest began to turn decisively in the fifth round as Joshua increased the pressure, flooring Paul twice and leaving him struggling to cope with the relentless assault.

The American survived the round but was dropped again in the sixth before Joshua delivered the decisive blow, landing a powerful right hand that sent Paul to the canvas for a fourth time.

Paul failed to beat the referee's count, with the contest officially stopped at one minute and 31 seconds of the sixth round.

It marked the first knockout defeat of Paul's professional boxing career and his second loss overall, following his split-decision defeat by Tommy Fury in February 2023.

The damage extended well beyond the result. Paul confirmed immediately after the fight that he had suffered a double broken jaw, later sharing an X-ray on social media showing fractures in two places.

He subsequently had surgery to repair the injuries, with two titanium plates fitted and some teeth removed. Recovery did not go according to plan, with Paul having to go back under the knife for a second time.

The severity of the injury raised questions over how long Paul would be sidelined and whether he would return to the ring.

The YouTuber-turned-boxer pictured alongside his fiancee Jutta Leerdam (Olympic champion)

Paul's opponent is expected to be announced in the coming days, with the American already understood to have held talks with former UFC star Darren Till

But the American has now confirmed his comeback, with Dubai set to host another major event as he looks to rebuild his boxing career.

'I've spent years proving people wrong, taking risks, and pushing myself against opponents nobody thought I'd face,' Paul said.

'Nothing that's happened has changed my belief in myself or what I'm working toward.

'I'm hungrier than ever, and on Thursday, December 24, I'm returning to the ring in Dubai to start the next chapter of my journey.

'Dubai is a city that thinks big, breaks boundaries, and doesn't believe in limits. That's exactly the kind of place I want to make my comeback.

'We've got plenty of names on the list; let's see who signs the contract. Merry Christmas, Dubai. Santa Paul is coming to town, and somebody's getting knocked out.'

Paul, who boasts a professional record of 12 wins and two defeats, has become one of boxing's biggest commercial attractions since making his debut in 2020.

His November 2024 bout against Mike Tyson attracted a reported 125million global viewers, while his showdown with Joshua a year later drew 33m.

He has also been in discussions with former UFC heavyweight Alistair Overeem (above)

The announcement comes as MVP continues to expand its international presence, with the Dubai event being organised in cooperation with the Dubai Sports Council and the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism.

MVP co-founder and chief executive Nakisa Bidarian said Paul's return demonstrated his determination to continue competing after his injury against Joshua.

'Well he is back, and that tells you everything about the competitor Jake Paul is and how much he loves this sport,' Bidarian said.

'This is more than a fight. It's a global event in one of the world's great destination cities, on one of the most special nights of the year, when families everywhere are together and watching.

'We're finalising an opponent worthy of Jake's return and look forward to sharing more in the coming weeks.'

Till, who previously challenged for the UFC welterweight title, has increasingly explored opportunities outside mixed martial arts since leaving the UFC.

Overeem, meanwhile, enjoyed a lengthy career at the highest level of MMA and kickboxing, competing in promotions including the UFC, Strikeforce and K-1.

The 45-year-old Dutchman has not competed in professional MMA since 2021, when he was released by the UFC following his defeat by Alexander Volkov but has stated he's interested in pursing a boxing career.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury and wife Paris both break down in tears as they recount how he 'didn't want to live' in deep depression amid his alcohol and drug addiction in new Netflix documentary trailer
Sports.content:
A tearful Paris Fury has revealed how she was left 'scared' over husband Tyson's alarming health decline, with the heavyweight superstar opening up on his paralysing drink and drug addiction in a new documentary.

Tyson, 38, saw his life spiral out of control after reaching the pinnacle of boxing following his heavyweight title triumph over arch rival Wladimir Klitschko in 2015.

The Gypsy King, speaking in Netflix's new documentary Tyson Fury, confessed how he had lost his 'whole point of existence' after his win in Dusseldorf, leading to a crippling addiction to alcohol and cocaine.

In the documentary trailer, Tyson says: 'All I wanted to was beat Klitschko. It was an obsession for me.

'I'd achieved all my childhood dreams, but my whole point of existence had been taken away. I didn't want to live.'

Tyson and Paris Fury both broke down in tears as they recounted his troubling addiction past

Fury revealed how he had lost his whole point of existence after winning the heavyweight title

Fury fulfilled a career-long obsession after beating Wladimir Klitschko in 2015

Tyson's wife and childhood sweetheart Paris, could only watch on as her husband's life unravelled, and was emotional as she recounted the traumatising episode.

'Straight after [the Klitschko fight], Tyson said to me "this is as good as it is ever going to get". I didn't understand at the time what he meant,' she says.

'The Tyson I knew was gone and I was so scared.'

The documentary, which charts Tyson's incredible rise to heavyweight champion of the world, tells how he grew up surrounded by strong male figures - where discussing emotions was off limits.

'Growing up in my family, there was no emotion shown. They were all hard nuts. Like 50cent said: "Show no love, love will get you killed."'

Fury fought back from his addiction problems to make his boxing comeback in 2018, before triumphing over Deontay Wilder in a sensational heavyweight trilogy against the big-hitting American - where he won the WBC title.

The Gypsy King sought to unify the heavyweight division against the all-conquering Oleksandr Usyk, but twice fell short in a pair of thrilling contests against the Ukrainian.

Netflix cameras have documented the lives of the Fury family since 2023. The latest series centred on Fury's decision to come out of retirement, plus the family's move from Morecambe to the Isle of Wight.

The streaming giant will broadcast Fury's mega-fight against Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on December 11.

Sports.title: Professional boxer Edgar Berlanga arrested after striking baby mama on the head with a pistol in heated dispute
Sports.content:
Professional boxer Edgar Berlanga arrested after striking baby mama on the head with a pistol in heated dispute

Professional boxer Edgar Berlanga was arrested earlier this week for aggravated battery following a heated physical bust-up with the mother of his child.

Berlanga, who is signed to Dana White's Zuffa Boxing, was arrested and booked in Polk County, Florida, on one charge of battery and one charge of aggravated battery on Monday.

The fighter is alleged to have repeatedly slapped a woman before hitting her on the head with a gun, according to court documents obtained by the Daily Mail.

The alleged victim, the mother of Berlanga's son, told police that the pair became embroiled in a heated argument while the boxer was driving after leaving a gun range on October 18.

She claimed that the dispute turned physical when Berlanga began slapping her before reaching into the vehicle's cupholder and retrieving a pistol, according to police documents.

The boxer is then alleged to have struck the woman on the forehead with the magazine well of the gun.

Professional boxer Edgar Berlanga was arrested earlier this week for aggravated battery

The boxer is accused of hitting the mother of his child on the forehead with a pistol

He lost to Canelo Alvarez for the WBA, WBC and WBO super middleweight titles in 2024

The woman claimed she attempted to escape from the vehicle and flee only for Berlanga to grab her arm and pull her back into the car. She eventually managed to exit the vehicle and sought safety at a nearby 7-Eleven.

Police said they observed swelling and bruising on her face which corroborated her allegations. They also said that they noticed a rip in her shirt and bruising on her inner arm consistent with her claims that Berlanga grabbed her.

When asked by officers if the gun Berlanga struck her with was real, the woman confirmed that it was and that she had witnessed the boxer fire the gun multiple times at the range around 20 minutes earlier.

The police report stated that she was unsure if she wanted to press charges, however, Berlanga was still ultimately arrested as officers declared it a domestic violence case.

Berlanga was booked on felony aggravated battery and misdemeanor battery touch/strike. He made his first court appearance on Tuesday and bond was set at $16,000, per court records.

Berlanga is a top rising boxer with a 24-2 record with 19 KOs. He went up against Canelo Alvarez for the WBA, WBC and WBO super middleweight titles in September 2024 but lost by unanimous decision.

Earlier this year, he headlined an event at Madison Square Garden in New York City, where he delivered a KO loss to Steven Butler in the seventh round.

Sports.title: Teen fighting for life identified after Brisbane boxing night mass shooting - as event official speaks out
Sports.content:
Teen fighting for life identified after Brisbane boxing night mass shooting - as event official speaks out

Jimboomba woman Vana-Reese Schuster-Togiatau, 19, has been identified as the innocent bystander fighting for life after being shot in the head and neck outside a Queensland pub.

She remained in a critical and unstable condition at Princess Alexandra Hospital on Monday afternoon. Metro South Health confirmed the teenager is still fighting for life in the intensive care unit.

The teenager was active on social media just hours before the shooting. She and her partner were seen lip syncing to Justin Bieber's Daises in a video posted on Saturday afternoon.

Four people were wounded outside Fitzy's Loganholme, south of Brisbane, on Saturday night, while more than 100 spectators, including families with young children, attended the Logan City Titles boxing event.

Phil Austin, from the Australian National Boxing Federation Queensland, categorically rejected suggestions it was a bikie or organised crime attack targeting the boxing.

Austin was in the venue's foyer when the shots erupted.

'The wider community is questioning how can this happen in Logan?' Queensland Police Chief Superintendent Mel Adams said on Monday.

Jimboomba woman Vana-Reese Schuster-Togiatau remains critically injured after suffering gunshot wounds to her head and neck

Vision of bullet marks on a mirror after four people were shot outside Fitzy's Loganholme during a boxing event on Saturday night

Boxing official Phil Austin was in the foyer when shots erupted, with flying glass striking his arm

'That's a popular local pub, a well-respected institution. That location had children, teenagers, mums and dads at that sporting event.'

Taskforce Maxima is a specialist Queensland Police squad that investigates outlaw motorcycle gangs and serious organised crime.

It is assisting Logan CIB and State Crime Command, which are jointly leading the investigation into the Fitzy's Loganholme shooting.

But Austin told Daily Mail that speculation linking the boxing event to bikies and organised crime was 'people putting two and two together and getting five'.

'I haven't seen any reputed organised crime figures at a fight show in this country in years,' he said.

'Bikies used to go to events, but since the government changed their laws, you just don't see them.'

Austin said he did not recognise any of the victims and could not say whether they had been attending the boxing.

'I don't even know if they were there to watch the boxing,' he said.

Ms Schuster-Togiatau (above) remained in the intensive care unit on Monday afternoon

Austin rejected speculation linking the boxing event to bikies and organised crime

'There's more than just boxing happening at that pub.'

He said no fighters or trainers appeared to have been involved and challenged assumptions that the boxing event itself had been targeted.

'We just happened to be there,' he said.

'It could have been the flower arranging show. It's just the fact that we were there.

'We have no idea why what happened happened. The only thing that we know for sure is it's a tragedy.'

Austin said he had just finished seeing a fighter and left the room being used as the dressing rooms near the venue's front doors when the shooting began.

'I'm in the foyer. I've got maybe a couple of metres, and then there's just a series of shots very, very quickly,' he said.

'We're talking about five or six shots in that or less seconds.'

Police say shots were fired from a Mitsubishi's front passenger window near the venue's drop-off area

Two men wearing balaclavas and gloves were seen inside the vehicle, according to police

Ms Schuster-Togiatau (above) had shared a video lip syncing to a Justin Bieber song just hours before the shooting

Flying glass struck the back of his arm.

'I was wearing a long shirt. Nothing hurt, but it just sort of reinforced me like, okay … this is happening,' he said.

'Before I could sort of basically say to myself, 'Oh crap,' it's over.'

Austin saw a car with its lights on but did not see anyone get out.

'It was my impression that they were actually still in the car,' he said.

Police said a Mitsubishi approached the passenger drop-off area during an intermission and shots were fired from its front passenger window.

Two men wearing balaclavas and gloves were seen inside.

Austin went to alert his crew in the boxing hall at the rear of the venue, away from where the shots had been fired.

Three men aged 27, 37 and 38 remain in hospital with serious injuries but are improving, police said

The Mitsubishi was found burnt out at Waterford West shortly after the shooting

'Then people's reactions start to kick in, and there's a bit of pandemonium, really, a lot of very, very angry people,' he said.

'They used the boxing room, basically, like a safe haven for everybody.'

Patrons began leaving through the back as hotel staff and security marshalled the crowd.

Chief Superintendent Mel Adams said everyone who witnessed the violence would carry some trauma from the night.

'This could have been your family member,' she said.

'This was a random group of people at the front of a popular hotel that became victims.'

The three other victims, men aged 27, 37 and 38, all suffered gunshot wounds to their abdomens. The 38-year-old was also shot in the arm.

All three remained in serious conditions on Monday but were improving, Adams said.

Police have not confirmed whether the men knew one another.

Police believe the attack involved pre-planning but say it remains premature to speculate about gang or organised crime involvement.

The Mitsubishi was found burnt out at Waterford West shortly after the shooting.

CCTV from nearby homes showed its occupants being collected by another vehicle after the car was torched. Police believe one of those involved may have suffered burns or another injury.

A ute was also found burnt later that night, with investigators still examining whether it was connected.

Adams urged anyone who knew or suspected who was responsible to come forward.

'There will be people out there who know who did this or suspect who did this,' she said.

For Austin, who has a son the same age as the critically injured teenager, the shooting has hit particularly hard.

'I've got a son her age, so it's really, really hit home hard,' he said.

He offered the federation's support to the victims, their families and friends.

'This is an awful, awful time for everyone,' he said.

'Let's just hope this girl recovers. It's just awful.'

Sports.title: Conor Benn calls out Conor McGregor for lucrative crossover fight - as he looks to bounce back from brutal second-round knockdown by Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Conor Benn has called out Conor McGregor for a potential crossover fight, just weeks after suffering a devastating defeat by Ryan Garcia.

Benn was stopped in the second round of his world title challenge against Garcia in Las Vegas, with a brutal right hand sending the Briton crashing to the canvas before the American finished the job.

It was the first knockout defeat of Benn's professional career and left serious questions over what comes next for the 30-year-old.

But he appears to have an unexpected opponent in mind.

Benn took to social media to share a fight poster featuring himself and McGregor, accompanied by the caption: 'Benn vs McGregor coming soon, 2027'.

He added to the speculation by responding: 'Any day of the week.'

Conor Benn (pictured above) has called out Conor McGregor for a potential crossover fight, just weeks after suffering a devastating defeat by Ryan Garcia

Benn is understood to be interested in making the fight happen and is expected to explore potential terms with the Irishman.

Benn has previously been tipped to face McGregor in a lucrative crossover bout, with boxing legend Roy Jones Jr suggesting that the fight would make sense.

He said the crossover bout would be one of two major paydays for the Brit before he considers bringing his career to a close.

Jones also suggested such a contest could help Zuffa Boxing recoup its investment in Benn.

The prospect would offer Benn the chance to headline another major event without the pressure of a world title being on the line, while a fight against McGregor would attract an audience well beyond traditional boxing fans.

McGregor is one of the biggest names in combat sports, having become a global superstar during his time in the UFC before stepping into the boxing ring to face Floyd Mayweather in 2017.

The Irishman is also coming off a difficult period of his own, having suffered a fresh setback on his return to the Octagon against Max Holloway.

A fight with Benn would undoubtedly attract huge attention, although there is no indication yet that the pair are close to agreeing a deal.

Roy Jones Jr has said such a contest could help Zuffa Boxing recoup its investment in Benn

Benn's call-out comes after a brutal night in Las Vegas, where his hopes of becoming a world champion were ended in devastating fashion.

The British fighter had talked up his chances of upsetting Garcia, but the American's speed and power proved too much.

Garcia caught Benn with a vicious right hand in the second round, dropping him heavily to the canvas. Benn managed to get back to his feet, but Garcia immediately went on the attack again, forcing referee Thomas Taylor to step in after just one minute and 25 seconds of the round.

It was a crushing result for Benn, who had worked his way back into contention following his two-fight rivalry with Chris Eubank Jr.

Benn lost their first encounter by decision in April 2025 before getting his revenge with a points victory in November.

He subsequently returned to welterweight to challenge Garcia for the WBC title, but the American proved a step too far on the night.

The defeat also raised fresh questions about Benn's future at 147lbs, with making the weight having been a talking point in the build-up.

After the fight, Benn admitted he was unsure what came next and spoke about the sacrifices his boxing career had demanded of his family.

Benn was beaten inside two rounds by Ryan Garcia in their welterweight championship fight

It was the first knockout defeat of Benn's professional career and left serious questions over what comes next for the 30-year-old

He made it clear that spending time with his children was his immediate priority, leaving his next move uncertain.

A lucrative showdown with McGregor would offer a very different route back into the spotlight from another world title challenge.

McGregor, meanwhile, has endured his own difficult return to competition.

The former two-weight UFC champion had been out of action since breaking his leg during his trilogy fight with Dustin Poirier in July 2021.

His long-awaited comeback against Holloway was supposed to mark the start of a new chapter, but things quickly went wrong.

McGregor injured his knee after attempting a jumping kick in the opening seconds of the fight. Unable to continue, he was forced to withdraw after just 69 seconds, handing Holloway the victory.

The result was a frustrating setback for the Irishman, whose return had generated enormous interest among UFC fans.

McGregor subsequently announced plans to undergo surgery, leaving his immediate and long-term future uncertain once again.

McGregor's long-awaited comeback ended in disaster at UFC 329 in Las Vegas (above)

The Irishman blew his knee out after throwing a kick within the first seconds of the bout

At 38, he remains one of the most recognisable figures in combat sports, but another comeback will depend on his recovery and whether he can return to full fitness.

A boxing match with Benn would be a different proposition from another UFC appearance, though it would still require McGregor to make a significant commitment to training and preparation.

McGregor is no stranger to a crossover fight.

His most famous venture outside MMA came in August 2017, when he faced Floyd Mayweather in one of the most heavily promoted boxing matches of all time.

McGregor had never competed in a professional boxing bout before, but that did little to dampen interest in the contest.

The pair embarked on an extraordinary promotional tour, trading insults in front of huge crowds as the fight became a global spectacle.

McGregor made a competitive start, but Mayweather quickly took control before stopping him in the 10th round.

Mayweather improved his professional boxing record to 50-0, while McGregor returned to the UFC having secured a huge payday and further cemented his status as one of sport's biggest commercial attractions.

Sports.title: Boxing world champion Adrien Broner back in hot water as video shows him being handcuffed and hauled into police car in Beverly Hills
Sports.content:
Adrien Broner, the troubled former boxing champion once seen as the future of the sport, had another run-in with police over the weekend in Beverly Hills.

Now more than two years removed from his last fight, the 37-year-old Broner was among a group of men recording content on the streets of Beverly Hills for the social media platform, Kick, when local police arrived.

Viral footage from the incident shows the group recording what appears to be a music video involving both Broner and his fellow content creator, Deen The Great.

A separate clip shows Broner with his arms raised and walking backwards towards a pair of officers, who ultimately placed him in handcuffs. Broner is seen trying to poke fun at the situation by doing a funny walk for the officers' benefit, but they did not seem amused.

'Broner was detained during a traffic stop as part of an investigation into a large street gathering in a residential area,' Beverly Hills police told TMZ in a statement. 'He was released from the scene and a citation was not issued.'

The Daily Mail has sought further information from Beverly Hills police.

Adrien Broner dancing while getting put in handcuffs by the police 💀 pic.twitter.com/h9SZlIYfdM — Happy Punch (@HappyPunch) October 26, 2026

Viral footage shows the group recording what appears to be a music video involving both Broner (center, open gray sweatshirt) and his fellow content creator, DeenTheGreat

A separate clip shows Broner with his arms raised and walking backwards towards a pair of officers, who ultimately placed him in handcuffs on the streets of Beverly Hills

Adrien Broner and Deen The Great attend the Internet Ball on August 19, 2026

Broner is currently among several defendants being sued in Los Angeles County over allegations of sexual battery, battery and assault.

'Plaintiff alleges that Broner repeatedly pressured Plaintiff for sexual activity after repeated refusals, attempted to isolate Plaintiff, repeatedly pressured Plaintiff while intoxicated, attempted unwanted physical contact, publicly humiliated Plaintiff, and made false sexual statements about Plaintiff to a livestream audience,' read the complaint, obtained by The Daily Mail.

Broner has denied any wrongdoing in the case.

Previously, in September of 2025, Broner was kicked off rapper Cam'ron's popular podcast after ignoring the host's warnings to stop flirting with his on-air co-host.

Sporting a greying beard and speaking in an increasingly raspy voice, Broner repeatedly interrupted the interview to make passes at Treasure 'Stat Baby' Wilson, who co-hosts It Is What It Is with Cam'ron and Ma$e.

Adrien Broner and Deen The great attend Sold Out Saturdays on August 15, 2026 in Atlanta

Adrien Broner punches Gavin Rees during their WBC Lightweight Title fight at Atlantic City Boardwalk Hall in 2013. Broner won the WBO Super Featherweight title at just 22 in 2011

At one point, Broner responded to a question about boxing's welterweight division by telling Wilson: 'Stat, I love you.'

Things ultimately boiled over during a discussion about Sunday's NFL action when Broner appeared to stop himself from making another comment about Wilson: 'I can't talk… You told me to stop.'

Cam'ron took the moment to end his interview with Broner.

'Hey, we going to have to ask you to go, my n*****,' Cam'ron said before pulling a stack of cash out of a small bag to give to his guest.

'I don't have no problems with you, but I'm gonna pay you for your time,' the rapper said, adding: 'You can't violate, bro.' Cam'ron went on to explain that Wilson's boyfriend was on set.

A native of Cincinnati who won the WBO Super Featherweight title at just 22 in 2011, Broner enjoyed a meteoric rise in the boxing world before his career was derailed by a series of arrests, upset defeats and mental health issues.

Sports.title: Aussie boxing legend Jeff Fenech hospitalised as he faces fresh new health battle: 'He's always a fighter'
Sports.content:
Aussie boxing legend Jeff Fenech hospitalised as he faces fresh new health battle: 'He's always a fighter'

Australian boxing legend Jeff Fenech has been hospitalised with heart problems, with his NRL star son-in-law Bradman Best revealing the family’s concern ahead of his Kangaroos debut.

The four-weight world champion, 62, was admitted to Strathfield Private Hospital around 10 days ago after suffering severe fatigue, breathing difficulties and feeling unwell.

Fenech has since had a blood clot removed from his wrist and undergone tests to investigate whether a potentially life-threatening staph infection has returned.

A recurrence has not been confirmed.

Best, who has a baby daughter with Fenech’s daughter Kayla, disclosed the hospital stay while discussing the boxing great’s influence on his career.

The Newcastle centre is preparing to make his Australian Test debut against Fiji on Sunday, but took time to acknowledge Fenech’s health battle.

Jeff Fenech, 62, has been hospitalised after suffering heart problems, fatigue and breathing difficulties

Bradman Best paid tribute to his father-in-law ahead of his Australian Test debut

Fenech has reportedly had a blood clot removed from his wrist and undergone tests for a possible recurrence of a serious infection

‘Jeff has been massive for me, I just want to give a quick shout-out to him,’ Best said.

‘He’s actually in hospital at the moment.

‘I’m thinking of him. He’s tough, he’s always a fighter.’

Best said Fenech had become an invaluable source of advice as he worked towards representing Australia.

‘Jeff has done a lot for me in my career,’ he said.

‘I was visiting him last week and he’s always giving me tips on what to do and how to be better.

‘It’s special having a father-in-law like that who’s a four-time world champion.

‘He’s an icon in Australia and it’s special having a bond like that with him.’

Tim Tszyu’s preparations for his world-title clash with Erislandy Lara have been disrupted by his trainer’s hospitalisation

Fenech became one of Australia’s greatest boxers, winning world titles across four weight divisions during a career that earned him the nickname ‘The Marrickville Mauler’

Asked whether Fenech’s condition was serious, Best remained hopeful.

‘Yeah, he will be right. He’s always a fighter. He’s been in there with a few heart problems and stuff, but he’ll be good.’

The hospitalisation has also interrupted Tim Tszyu’s preparations for his planned WBA middleweight world-title clash with Erislandy Lara.

Fenech became Tszyu’s head trainer in July, helping guide him to a unanimous decision victory over American star Errol Spence Jr.

Tszyu credited the veteran trainer with helping inspire that result, which set up his pursuit of a world championship in a second weight division.

With Fenech sidelined, fellow trainer Basil Nassis has taken charge of Tszyu’s work in the gym.

The Lara bout is expected to take place in Australia in November or December, according to the reports.

Fenech hopes to recover in time to be involved, although the Telegraph reported he is unlikely to perform padwork during the build-up.

The latest scare follows two major heart operations.

In October 2019, Fenech underwent emergency open-heart surgery in Thailand while preparing Jack Brubaker for a fight against Tszyu.

He needed another six-hour open-heart operation in 2024 during a serious infection.

Sports.title: British boxing has a world beater in the ascendancy. Daniel Dubois is starting to look like a monster - and he's ready for Oleksandr Usyk, Anthony Joshua, Tyson Fury or anyone else, writes JEFF POWELL MBE
Sports.content:
'Bring him on,' roared Daniel Dubois when asked if he would like a third fight against the greatest boxer of his generation who has beaten him twice.

Oleksandr Usyk, who is in a state of limbo somewhere between vacating all the heavyweight tiles and semi-retirement, is a genius so may not fall readily into the trap baited on the banks of the Thames in the dark hours of this Sunday morning.

Ukraine's war hero will have watched Dubois annihilate the gallant Fabio Wardley and recognised that Dynamite Daniel is no longer the callow youth he wiped the canvas with a couple of times during his reign as the undisputed world champion.

Promoter Frank Warren is not given to understatement but when he said 'Daniel has matured now' he was only scratching the surface of the transformation.

It may be a stretch to compare Dubois with the once terrifying Sonny Liston but to those rivals wearing the other belts he needs if he is to become undisputed then he is starting to look like a monster.

'I want them all,' said WBO champion Dubois. He was referring to the winner between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua in December, who will thereby hold a WBA title, as well as IBF and WBC champions Filip Hrgovic and Ajit Kabayel.

Daniel Dubois knocks down Fabio Wardley during his annihilation on Saturday night

Dubois has declared himself ready to fight anyone in the heavyweight division

Their availability, especially that of AJ or the Gypsy King, will be determined no doubt by there being many more millions in the Aladdin's Cave from which Saudi Arabia has helped finance the welcome flux of mega-fights of late.

If so then Warren is promising a 2027 bursting with monthly heavyweight spectaculars as lustily anticipated as Dubois' second demolition of Wardley . At the rapid conclusion of which another packed O2 crowd was switching its allegiance from a love affair with Fabio's romanticised emergence from white collar boxing to realisation that Britain has a world beater in the ascendancy.

One who may be growing, also, into more of a box office star than the monosyllabic Liston ever was. If his accurate bravura prediction of a 'bash and smash' slaughter of Wardley and his most jovial media conference yet which followed are anything to go by.

Having nursed his confidence in the Dubois family cocoon Daniel now has a mansion of his own to live in and a selection of race cars to drive. No more Mister Shy Guy but none the less likeable for that.

The transition to full manhood was rounded off over the two fights with Wardley. This included recovery from two early knockdowns in the first Fight Of The Year battle to a brutal 11th round stoppage victory.

And now the onslaught triggered by a staggering right hand blow only 17 seconds after the first bell which imposed an eight count on the ropes. Followed by an overwhelming TKO in round two. Wham, bam and thank you man. No criticism this time of a delay in calling it off. In flew the white towel, in jumped referee Steve Gray.

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua fight each other in December - and Dubois wants the winner

There has been some nagging at the edge of Dubois' triumph. Suggestions that Wardley came back too soon after the second-half beating in May. But if five-and-a-half months is not sufficient time to recover then how long would be? The immortal Joe Louis used to fight once a month, for heaven's sake.

Wardley, honest man that he is, blamed himself. Having lived to fight another day he vows to do better enough to launch a comeback campaign for another world title. Meanwhile Dubois, at 29 last month, heads for the stratosphere as champion of the next generation of heavyweight boxing.

As the new monster of the prize-ring? It took The Greatest Of All Time to stop the Liston beast In his awesome tracks. Might Usyk be the Muhammad Ali in waiting for Dubois? Maybe. Perhaps not since he is the older legend now. It would be fascinating finding out.

The tombstone on Sonny Liston's grave in Las Vegas describes him simply as A MAN. Frank Warren is right about Dubois becoming exactly that.

Sports.title: Antonelli skips F1 Mexico GP media day due to illness
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli won’t attend Formula 1’s Mexico Grand Prix on Thursday due to feeling unwell, the Mercedes team has revealed.

A spokesperson for the Anglo-German outfit told media that the championship leader was “feeling under the weather” due to a “viral illness” he has been recovering from, with the FIA therefore excusing him from today’s media activities.

“We expect him to be back tomorrow,” the statement continued.

Antonelli is on the brink of a maiden F1 title, which would make him the youngest world champion as he would beat Sebastian Vettel’s 2010 record by over three years. All he needs on Sunday is ninth place, or for neither George Russell nor Lewis Hamilton to win.

Read Also: Formula 1 The maths behind Antonelli becoming F1 world champion at Mexico GP

The 20-year-old Italian won’t be the only driver to skip media day, with Valtteri Bottas also calling in sick; Cadillac notified media that the Finn was “unwell”.

“The team has taken the decision to allow him a day of rest, to support his recovery,” the statement read.

“This is a precautionary measure and does not currently affect his participation in the remainder of the race weekend. We will continue to monitor the situation and provide updates if necessary.”

Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac Racing Photo by: James Sutton / LAT Images via Getty Images

Who will step up if necessary?

Albeit unlikely, there is a chance of a reserve driver being called up for either racer.

At Mercedes, that would be 2023 Formula 2 runner-up Frederik Vesti, who has never competed in a grand prix but is scheduled to make his seventh career Free Practice 1 outing this weekend in George Russell’s car.

As far as Cadillac is concerned, Zhou Guanyu is the team’s reserve driver, so the seven-time points scorer would make his F1 return after he wound up his three-year stint with Alfa Romeo/Sauber at the end of the 2024 campaign.

Sports.title: Why Ricciardo would consider a comeback at Le Mans
Sports.content:
Last month marked two years since Daniel Ricciardo’s last motor race to this day, as the eight-time grand prix winner regretfully, discreetly bowed out of Formula 1 – but is his career over?

Ricciardo admits it likely is, having come to terms with the way his F1 stint ended – “I’m not 100% there, but I’m 90%,” he said of his quest of closure – but he might still be interested in further opportunities, as long as they don’t require a season-long commitment.

“A year ago, I would have said, ‘I will never put a helmet on again, I’m done, that’s it’,” Ricciardo told the Beyond The Grid podcast. “But there is something there where I’m like, it would be nice to finish a racing career a bit more on my terms; to do something that, when I take the helmet off, I’m smiling and happy. Maybe that’s the last bit of closure I need.

“The thought of doing a full championship still doesn’t really sound that exciting. Probably a one-off, like a one-off Le Mans.

“F1 is so selfish – in a necessary way. Yes, you have team-mates, but that’s your first opponent and all that. I think to share a car with other drivers and to actually have real team-mates to share data and help out, I think it would be – especially now, at this point where that insane fire and whatever ruthlessness, that has faded to a degree. I think I’ll just enjoy it. It would be the form of driving and kind of companionship that I would really enjoy, and I think it would make me smile and feel good about the art of competition again.”

Daniel Ricciardo, McLaren Photo by: Clive Mason / Getty Images

Ricciardo explained he never enjoyed driving all that much and mostly revelled in competition, though his last few years in F1 dampened his enthusiasm. Le Mans could be a new way to find fulfillment, but the Australian – who hasn’t been training the way he used to – is cautious about that prospect.

“Do I need to open the box again? I don’t know,” Ricciardo pondered. “That’s why I haven’t rushed into making a decision on anything, because, again, I want to make sure I’m not doing it for ego or for some fairy-tale ending. It has to be because it’s right inside me and I really want to do it, and it’s not to please others.

“I’m not going to lie, there’s a part of me which would love to do it for all the people that cared and supported and loved me over the years and also hated the way it ended. So, yes, there is certainly a part of me which feels for the fans, but it has obviously to be for me and my reasons first and foremost.

“That’s the hard part – would it open the box? I don’t think it will; as I said, I’m much more at peace with everything, but then, who am I kidding? Would I go to Le Mans just to go and compete and just be happy to be there, or would I go there to try and win?

“As much as I want to say, ‘Oh, just be happy, just soaking in the experience’, we all know once the helmet’s on it’s different. I can’t deny that I would want to go and do it properly. And that’s maybe something I need to understand as well – is my heart in it?”

A Ricciardo-Verstappen-Vettel trio?

Sebastian Vettel tests the Porsche 963 Photo by: Porsche Motorsport

When it comes to the drivers Ricciardo would dream of sharing that companionship with, other Red Bull icons come up.

“I don’t want to put pressure on him, but obviously Max [Verstappen] is a name that would be high on the list. We talked about Red Bull obviously in 2018, and what if, and what if; I was trying to get back at the team at the end of my career, so maybe that’s a way that we could give the people what they want,” Ricciardo chuckled.

Verstappen has openly expressed interest in Le Mans for the future, and interviewer Tom Clarkson suggested the pair could be joined by Sebastian Vettel, who tested Porsche’s Hypercar challenger in 2024 but is yet to enter the French classic.

“Well, butter my butt and call me a biscuit!” Ricciardo exclaimed.

“There’s no denying that he still is extremely fast and would be fast in anything. I fricking love Seb, so that could be a nice little Red Bull reunion of sorts.”

Sports.title: Cadillac 'honoured' to have Perez as special 300th race celebration planned for Mexico GP
Sports.content:
General Motors president Mark Reuss has praised Cadillac Formula 1 driver Sergio Perez ahead of his 300th race in the series, insisting it is "an honour" to have the Mexican on side.

Perez will become just the seventh driver in F1 history to reach the milestone - joining Rubens Barrichello, Fernando Alonso, Jenson Button, Lewis Hamilton, Kimi Raikkonen and Michael Schumacher - and will celebrate the achievement in front of his adoring home support at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez in Mexico City.

As part of the occasion, Perez has taken to the streets for a demonstration run along the Paseo de la Reforma. He will also visit General Motors staff in the city before taking to the track in the MAC-26. Cadillac has also announced a renewed contract with the Mexican through to 2029.

Read Also: Formula 1 Why Sergio Perez shows vote of confidence in Cadillac despite mixed 2026 debut

Asked about the celebrations when speaking at the Autosport Business Exchange New York, Reuss said: "It's a big deal.

"It'll be Checo's 300th, really proud to have him driving for our team, and he's given us so much feedback, and expertise on someone who's run the tracks - and [Valtteri] Bottas - both giving us real feedback around the car, the track, and what the differences are and how to build the models, and how to get those simulations right as we move through and experience our first season.

"This is a big deal for him. It's also a big deal for General Motors. Our Mexico headquarters is in Mexico City, so he's going to speak to our dealers, he's going to speak to our employees, and I can't wait to go and be part of that with him, and all of his fans.

"He's just a great person, who he is as a person; because he's not only a wonderful driver, a wonderful representative for Cadillac and General Motors and Formula 1, but he's just a really good person.

Mark Reuss, ABX Photo by: Bryan Bedder / Getty Images

"It's an honour to have him."

Perez and Bottas joined Cadillac for its maiden F1 season this term, bringing race-winning experience to the GM brand as it made its first steps into the pinnacle of single-seater racing.

And while the season has been far from smooth sailing, which was to be expected for a new team built from zero, Reuss has been impressed with the character shown by both drivers.

"They're very different," he revealed. "Any driver in any series is always, if they're really good, very different.

"In that professionalism and precision, whatever series it is, whether it's endurance, Formula 1, off-road, trucks, I don't care what it is, you can see it in the champions, and they strive to do the best, the very best they can every race and if they don't, if something happens - you can't win every race, no one can win every race - when they have a day that is unfortunate or mistakes were made, they move on from that race, and perfect their craft, whether it's with the car, or themselves or their physicality, or whatever that is.

"They drive for that perfection, and both of these gentlemen do that, and they really understand what it takes and the process. I'm very, very happy that they're patient with us to be honest.

"That takes a special person, and both of those guys have it."

Sports.title: F1 publishes first Social Impact Report; key student scholarship renewed
Sports.content:
Formula 1 has published its first sport-wide Social Impact Report, with over half a million young people across the world having benefited from F1 programmes last year.

In initiatives designed to educate, inspire and open pathways into the sport in 2025, youngsters from across 71 countries were able to take a step closer to F1.

F1 has also renewed its now-established Engineering Scholarship programme, which was founded in 2021, for three academic years, promising more than £2.4 million in funding. The initiative helps relieve students who would otherwise face key barriers to higher education, including financial and accessibility obstacles. 48 students have already been supported by the programme.

Full tuition fees and living costs will be covered for ten new scholars each year between 2026/27 and 2028/29 at the University of Strathclyde, Imperial College London, the University of Cambridge, the University of Oxford and MUNER in Italy.

Social impact of F1 revealed in new report

For the first time, the contributions of F1, governing body the FIA, all 10 teams and 24 race promoters during the 2025 season have been collated in one report, working to the recommendations of The Hamilton Commission, which was launched by seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton and the Royal Engineering Academy in 2021.

Among the key points in the report, standout successes include:

• 500,000+ young people given access to the sport through education, STEM and inspiration programmes globally • 100% of Diversity and Inclusion Charter signatories delivering social impact programmes • 1,000+ skills and talent development opportunities spotlighting motorsport and related industries • 29,000+ schools compete annually in the STEM Racing global education initiative • 700+ schools across the UK, South Africa, India and Brazil participated in the British Council’s Learning Sectors education programme • 2,500+ young people participating in activities delivered at Formula 1 events • 50+ wishes granted through Formula 1's partnership with Make-A-Wish • 140 young people attended F1 Academy workshops

STEM Racing World Final 2026 Singapore Photo by: STEM Racing

“Formula 1 has an extraordinary power to inspire, and we want everyone to believe there is a place for them in our sport," said F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali.

"We are turning our commitments into action, working across motorsport to break down barriers and widen access for future generations. We are proud of the progress made and grateful for the collective efforts of Lewis Hamilton, the Hamilton Commission, the FIA, our teams, race promoters, partners and the many organisations helping to create lasting change.

"By renewing the Formula 1 Engineering Scholarship for a further three academic years and investing in young people and communities, we will open more doors, nurture talent and inspire the next generation to believe that a future in Formula 1 is within their reach."

FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem added: “Motorsport has the power to transform lives and we have a responsibility to ensure its benefits reach beyond the racetrack.

"This report demonstrates the strength of collaboration across our community in reaching more than 500,000 young people worldwide.

“Together, we are breaking down barriers, developing future talent and creating new pathways into our sport. I welcome the continued investment in education and scholarships as we work to make motorsport more accessible and deliver a lasting legacy.”

Sports.title: The unusual Aston Martin, Honda and Red Bull Powertrains rumours put into perspective
Sports.content:
One of the most remarkable moments on Sunday in Austin did not take place on the track itself, but rather in the Formula 1 paddock after the US Grand Prix. During the usual post-race media sessions, both Aston Martin and Red Bull’s representatives were asked about a subject that had very little to do with the race at the Circuit of the Americas – quite the opposite, in fact.

Both Aston Martin's chief trackside officer Mike Krack and Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies were asked whether they could rule out a potential partnership between the two brands in the future. It seems rather extraordinary, and both men understandably looked surprised when that question randomly came up during their media rounds, which is why the matter requires some context.

It all goes back to a BBC article and a somewhat unfortunate interpretation of it. In the regular Q&A column of F1 correspondent Andrew Benson, he was asked whether customer teams might be interested in the Red Bull Ford power unit, given that it appears to be more than competitive in its first year.

The answer made it abundantly clear that no F1 team is currently looking for a power unit and then rightly highlighted something that is widely known in the paddock: the shock at Aston Martin, particularly for team owner Lawrence Stroll, when it became apparent earlier this year just how far behind Honda was on the power unit side at the start of F1’s new era.

That understandably led to some initial doubts and considerations, although the decision was made to remain fully committed to Honda – something the BBC article also correctly emphasised. The only speculative element that left the door slightly open was the possibility that those doubts could resurface if Honda fails to make the expected step forward in, let’s say, 2027 or 2028.

As so often happens in F1 and today's media landscape, the story subsequently took on a life of its own and became a bigger talking point than it should have been, according to several insiders. It is a self-fulfilling prophecy: something automatically becomes a topic, rightly or wrongly, if enough people in the F1 paddock are asked about it, which in turn generates coverage. It is a snowball effect, making it crucial to put such stories into perspective.

The Aston Martin perspective: Abandoning works deal potential would be extremely premature

Both Krack and Mekies were asked on Sunday evening whether they could deny that talks were taking place between Aston Martin and Red Bull Powertrains, with the implication of that question naturally going considerably further than anything suggested in the original BBC article. Krack was quick to reaffirm Aston Martin's long-term commitment to Honda.

Shintaro Orihara, Honda Racing Corporation Trackside General Manager and Chief Engineer Photo by: Alex Bierens de Haan / LAT Images via Getty Images

“I can only say we have a long-term partner, which is Honda, that by the way has done its 500th race this weekend. And I think we will be together also when we win our first race together”, the Aston Martin representative said.

It is important to point out that the current partnership and works deal offer enormous potential in theory. Yes, it is true that Honda is nowhere near the desired level yet, but the Japanese manufacturer has previously demonstrated that it can turn a difficult situation around – just think of its false start with McLaren, which eventually led to multiple world titles with Red Bull.

This ties in with Adrian Newey's comments during the FIA press conference in Austin. When asked about alleged motivation problems during the difficult years at Red Bull, he implicitly pointed to a crucial difference between the team's engine partner at the time, Renault, and its current relationship with Honda.

“As a chassis designer, if the PU manufacturer has a bad year, that happens, and you accept it. But if the PU manufacturer has a bad year and doesn’t appear to have any intention of trying to address the problem, that’s altogether a different matter, and that’s quite bleak at that point.

“That’s the situation that unfortunately we faced in 2014. And as it turned out, that situation didn’t really change with that supplier until we changed to Honda in 2019. So, you can imagine my pain and frustration at that time.”

With Honda, however, the situation is very different. The Japanese manufacturer is acutely aware of the current shortcomings and is pulling out all the stops to turn the situation around, something Newey also highlighted.

“At Honda, there’s a lot of energy and projects on the way now that perhaps are in their early stages of development, but we see a lot of promise from those.”

Adrian Newey, Aston Martin Racing Photo by: Alex Bierens de Haan / LAT Images via Getty Images

That says something about Honda's determination, but also about the potential that still exists in the longer term. Aston Martin deliberately opted for a works deal, as it marks the next step in the team's evolution.

Not only does it offer a much better opportunity to shape the partnership than would be possible as a customer team, it also brings the potential benefits of integrating the power unit more effectively into the chassis and helping each other – something both Newey and Honda have identified as a crucial priority for 2027. Both brands still fully recognise that potential, which makes abandoning a works deal highly unlikely and, moreover, an extremely short-term approach – something of a knee-jerk reaction.

The Red Bull perspective: Not yet ready to supply a customer team

All of this explains why, from Aston Martin's perspective, it would make perfect sense to continue down the current path, give it time and eventually reap the rewards of this works partnership.

And then, of course, there is Red Bull's side of the story. Yes, its own powertrains project in collaboration with Ford has made a considerably better start than many thought possible, but according to Mekies, that does not automatically mean the company is ready to take the step towards supplying customer teams.

“Look, we got a lot of unwanted, positive publicity about the performance of our engine and that certainly came with attention from a lot of teams”, Mekies smiled, referring to the FIA’s ADUO ranking and not receiving a development token.

“Are we having any serious conversations with anyone to supply another team? No, we don't feel we are ready for that. Is it set in stone for the next five years? No, because I don't know what's going to happen in the next five years.

“But for sure for us, there is enough work on our side to improve the power unit, to improve its integrations in the car, and to get at the level of the best competitors before we can consider being able to supply one more team on top of Racing Bulls. So nothing will change in the next year or so.”

Laurent Mekies, Red Bull Racing Team Principal Photo by: Jayce Illman / Getty Images

One of the main reasons for a manufacturer to supply engines to a customer team is to gather more data, which can benefit development. It is one of the factors that may be hampering Honda, given that it supplies just one team and was able to collect very little data during winter testing and the opening races because of all the reliability problems.

For Red Bull, however, that is not an immediate incentive to take on a customer team, as it already has one in the form of its sister team Racing Bulls. The Milton Keynes-based manufacturer already supplies two teams and therefore has four cars from which to gather data.

All of this means that, from both Aston Martin's and Red Bull's perspectives, such a partnership is certainly not an obvious option at present. It is crucial to view the recent speculation in that light – in other words, in the right context. It is understandable that much will depend on Honda's development over the coming years, but for now, this is another example of something that frequently characterises the F1 paddock and today's media landscape: a storm in a teacup.

Sports.title: FIA announces new partnership to help drive future F1 regulations
Sports.content:
The FIA has announced a wide-ranging partnership with Amazon Web Services as it aims to upgrade its digital capabilities.

AWS will join as its Official AI and Cloud Computing Partner, as the governing body will use AWS's suite of AI tools to improve its capability to produce future technical regulations.

The FIA also runs its aerodynamic simulations on AWS’s High Performance Computing technology, allowing it to conduct air flow tests in the virtual world without having to build physical parts, speeding up the process and reducing the costs involved.

This partnership also expands the digital licensing platform the governing body uses to simplify tasks like licence administration, which should make it easier for national sporting authorities to run their events and for officials to sign up. That digital platform, first trialled in Canada and Sri Lanka, will now be rolled out across more countries.

Sepang race start Photo by: Srinivasa Krishnan

The AWS integration forms part of the FIA’s wider digital transformation, as president Mohammed Ben Sulayem explained. "Technology is changing every part of our sport, and the FIA must lead that change. Our new partnership with AWS will support everything from the cars of the future to the grassroots clubs where so many careers begin.

"By bringing world-class cloud and AI technology into the heart of the FIA, we can make it simpler for drivers, officials and volunteers to take part, help our Member Clubs work more efficiently, and move closer to our ambition of doubling global motor sport participation."

AWS is already an existing partner of F1 management, having joined in 2018 as its innovation technology partner. Among other services, AWS tools process telemetry data for broadcast use, powering live strategy predictions.

Sports.title: Mercedes has a Russell-sized problem and it is sharing responsibility
Sports.content:
George Russell's form hit a new low at the United States Grand Prix, despite glimmers of progress in the Formula 1 grands prix shortly before then. In Austin, the Mercedes driver qualified over four tenths behind team-mate Kimi Antonelli, slumping to an eighth-placed finish on Sunday while the 20-year-old took another step to the world title with a ninth win of 2026.

There were some mitigating circumstances behind Russell's P8, as a five-second penalty on lap one dropped him behind McLaren's Oscar Piastri. Permanently, as it would transpire. But Mercedes boss Toto Wolff pointed out afterwards that that "doesn't make any difference to the underlying problem that we need to solve”.

It came despite a slight upturn in form following the summer break, like his Baku win, before the Russell-sized problems grew worse and worse heading into Texas. Other than a strong performance in Singapore sprint qualifying, taking second before crashing from the lead, he hasn't qualified higher than sixth - or higher than Antonelli - since Mercedes introduced its major Malaysia upgrade. Though, of course, he was on course for third at Sepang until a late engine failure.

Nevertheless, Russell isn’t having the best of times with the new package and looked bereft of ideas as to why things aren't clicking for him. But the prevailing theory is that the new-look W17, while demonstrably faster at its peak, has a much narrower performance window. Whether a matter of driving style or adaptation, when the car isn't in that sweet spot, Russell appears to be all at sea.

"George just struggled so much," Wolff said. "I believe this is because the operational window of the car is so difficult. In Q2 he was there and thereabouts. Q3 didn't work. He said: 'That goes on me.'

“In the race, I don't know, we got stuck behind Piastri, which looks a bit unfair. Why he didn't get past is [because they have] the same engine, it's the same electric charging and deployment."

Russell and Wolff in Montreal Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

Russell summed up his race as "six good laps, 50 bad laps", but was otherwise at a loss for words to explain his unravelling performances. "I want to understand why the pace was so bad in the first stint,” he said, now with a 123-point gap to Antonelli. “The penalty was a bit ridiculous as well, but that was least of my worries after such a bad weekend.

"The potential is there, but the window is narrow. I mean, we saw it in Malaysia. I think he [Antonelli] was quickest in FP3 and then we qualified fourth and eighth. And then this weekend we were both up there in Q2, and then I was nowhere in Q3 and nowhere [in the race].

"He obviously was exceptionally competitive, and there are signs that the window is very small. I hope that's an explanation for my lack of pace today, but I need to dig deep with my team because it's difficult to understand when you're so far off.”

Asked if he feels he has gone backwards in recent weeks, Russell said: "A little bit, a little bit. So, I don't have the answers right now and I need to give it 24 hours to think clearly!"

Russell had already thrown the kitchen sink at adapting his driving style to the 2026 cars, a process which started after winning the Melbourne opener from pole, having had few answers to Antonelli's run of five consecutive wins - even if the Briton encountered some misfortune.

That means his problems are unlikely to be solved over the five remaining races of this year, so Mercedes is banking on its 2027 car being more suited to both drivers, or to Russell at least unlocking fresh ways to exploit it.

Russell was the heavy title favourite when he won from pole in Australia Photo by: Joe Portlock / Getty Images

Wolff was adamant Russell would be able to brush off the disappointment of being usurped by a much younger and less experienced team-mate. The Austrian insisted the 28-year-old still has what it takes to mount his own title challenge based on the way he rose through the ranks - taking back-to-back GP3 and F2 crowns - fared against Lewis Hamilton during their time together, and proved competitive in 2025 when the car wasn't.

"George is a champion and has won in every category. I think he merits to be put in the group of the very best ones. We saw that last year,” said Wolff, explaining that Mercedes shares the responsibility of solving Russell's puzzle.

"This year we see this variability in results. When we land the car in the way that suits him, he's absolutely fast. But when it drops out of that operational window, he struggles more than maybe Kimi - and that is on us.

"We just have to work it out with him, how there can be such a difference in driving, in performance, because George is not half a second or three tenths slower than Kimi. That's just absolutely not the case.

"So, what is it that he doesn't like? What is it that we need to do in terms of modifying the car, setting it up in a different way for him to go fast? Because it's all there, the intelligence, the ability, the determination."

Sports.title: The role Friday practice played in Hamilton failing to achieve a podium at the US GP
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has explained the reasons why the podium narrowly eluded him in Formula 1’s United States Grand Prix.

The Ferrari driver started from fifth on the grid and jumped Isack Hadjar for fourth at lights out, despite being the only driver on used (soft) tyres for the opening stint.

But Hamilton lost 0.277s per lap to team-mate Charles Leclerc during that stint, as well as 0.422s to Max Verstappen, with the pair on new soft tyres. Those few seconds corresponded to the time the Briton was missing to beat Verstappen to third at the end of the Austin race – and perhaps surpass Leclerc for second.

The main reason for that early lack of pace, according to the seven-time world champion, was his suboptimal set-up in the opening stint – the consequence of pursuing wrong avenues in free practice.

“I was lacking pace in the first two stints, basically. I just couldn't turn the car,” Hamilton said.

“Ultimately, it all kind of started on Friday. Wrong set-up really for FP1 and went the wrong direction in FP2, reverted back and got to a better place in FP3.

“But there's a subtle difference between Charles’ and my car, basically, just in the race. It's just to do mostly with flap, how much wing you put in, and I think we've just been under-hitting it – continuously under-hitting it for some reason.

“When you do the laps of the grid, it feels like the car is good. And then as soon as the race starts, it's just massive washout and understeer. I couldn't do anything about it, so they just pulled away. I lost those eight seconds, and that was really why I didn't get that [third] position in the end.”

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Brett Farmer / LAT Images via Getty Images

He added: “Through the pitstops, I added four clicks [of front wing angle], the next pitstop I added another four clicks, and even then, I'm still another four clicks too short. And it's crazy to be 12 clicks down. We really need to look at how we get into that point.

“But I think it would have been a bit different if we had started with it in FP2, where you did the long run. That's where Charles got the experience on that set-up, and I didn't get the long run on it.

“So, as I said, I got a bit on the back foot, but lots of positives to take from it. The team did a really great job with pitstops and the strategy, and we obviously had a decent pace today, particularly the last stint. If I had that in the first two, we would have for sure been on the podium.”

Hamilton’s struggle was compounded by his tyre choice; he did switch to the hard compound for the last stint instead of another set of mediums as initially planned, but the harm had been done.

“I chose to have two medium tyres because they didn't think the hard tyre was going to be any good,” he explained. “In hindsight, two hard tyres would have been the better one – the hard tyre was the best tyre.

“And then it meant I started on a used soft which, from used to new, is two seconds of race time. And it affects the start as well compared to others that are all new. All the cars ahead are new, but I had a really good start, nearly got to third place, but Charles got the outside and I didn't get to capitalise on that.”

Hamilton was also hindered by the late virtual safety car intervention to recover Valtteri Bottas’ stricken Cadillac. His fresher tyres meant he was catching Verstappen by nearly one second per lap, but the neutralisation thwarted his recovery.

When asked if things might have been different without the VSC, Hamilton replied: “Probably I would have had a little bit of a battle with Max, maybe the last couple of laps. Yeah, that would have been awesome. But, as I said, I think it was all a result of the first two stints where I just lost so much ground. I can't be giving up that time in the future.

“I really feel like I'm happy with how I drove. It just took two whole stints to try and get this car to turn. And then once it started to turn in the third stint, I was back on pace with the guys ahead. But it's a big gap to close. It's eight, nine seconds or whatever it was to the car ahead, and those guys were obviously very quick. So, I’ve just got to work on not losing that.”

Leclerc still chasing victory

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Photo by: James Sutton / LAT Images via Getty Images

Meanwhile, Leclerc took Ferrari’s third-consecutive podium finish but was disappointed to end up 13 seconds adrift of race winner Kimi Antonelli.

“I enjoyed it,” the Monegasque commented. “The start was fun, then later on with Lando [Norris] and Max again was quite fun. So, it's one of those races where you're not getting too bored inside the cockpit and there's something to play for.

“I even thought the victory was possible at one point when I saw Kimi going for the one-stop. Based on our numbers, he would start to struggle a bit more towards the end of the race. He never really struggled towards the end of the race, but, yeah, it's been a fun race. A shame just that we came short of winning.”

Ferrari is now on a nine-round winless streak and despite recent encouraging signs, Leclerc is unsure he can turn his pace into victory soon.

“Whether I can convert that into a win is a bit difficult to predict, because it's such fine margins, and it also depends on what the upgrade plans of the others are in upcoming races,” he said.

“But the feeling with the car is getting better and better. These cars are very specific and unique, and I feel like, over the last two or three races, I've unlocked something again in terms of driving, and particularly set-up with my driving. Just both together, we've taken a step forward, and I just feel much more comfortable with the car.

“So I hope that this will result in a win soon. Whether it's in Singapore or here in Austin, we were quite close, so I'm confident that we'll have a shot to win a race before the end of the season.”

Sports.title: Perez performs Cadillac show run in Mexico City – in a car from F1: The Movie | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Sergio Perez performed a show run in his home country ahead of this weekend’s Mexican Grand Prix.

The Cadillac driver took to the streets of Mexico City along the Paseo de la Reforma. Over 100,000 fans were estimated to have attended the event.

The event promoters billed this as Perez’s fourth appearance in a Formula 1 car on the streets of his home country. However it appears Perez was not in fact driving a real F1 car.

Teams ordinarily use older cars to conduct show runs and ‘Testing of Previous Cars’. As this is Cadillac’s first season in F1 they have no such cars available.

The team therefore used one of the cars used to film “F1: The Movie”. These cars were based on Formula 2 chassis – the filmmakers purchased six for this purpose – and used bodywork modified by the Mercedes F1 team.

Cadillac yesterday confirmed Perez will continue to drive for them until at least 2029. He will make his 300th start in his home race at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez this weekend.

“Being able to celebrate my 300th grand prix here is extraordinary,” said Perez. “A lot had to happen for this to become a reality, and being able to share this moment with everyone who has supported me, in such an iconic place as Reforma, makes it incredibly special to me. Thank you to Cadillac and everyone who made this possible.”

Sports.title: Fans “pay a bit less attention” to Formula 1 as calendar gets longer – Sainz | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Carlos Sainz Jnr suspects the growing size of the Formula 1 calendar may not be helping to make the sport more popular.

F1 has increased the number of rounds to 24, though only 23 are scheduled to happen this year due to the cancellation of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix. The number could fall further if either of the final two rounds are cancelled.

If the final rounds go ahead as planned, F1 will hold nine events in just eleven weeks. Sainz says he would have enjoyed more regular races when he was younger but suspects it may have become a turn-off for some fans.

“I think if I were a fan, I would love it because the more F1 I can watch on TV, the better,” he said. “I remember when I was a kid and there were only 16 races in the calendar, or 18. I used to miss Formula 1 [because it was not on] for a lot of weekends.

“But we also need to consider as a sport if that’s something that maybe is also counterproductive. Sometimes you need to miss the sport to get people engaged. When you get so many races in a row, people or the sport can maybe feel a bit like a league, like the Premier League rather than the Champions League. So maybe you pay a bit less attention to the matches or to the races in this case.

“So, it’s more a philosophy for the sport to consider whether you want to keep having so many races in a row.”

However Sainz, a director of the Grand Prix Drivers’ Association, is also concerned about the effect F1’s long calendar has on the teams’ staff.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“More important than that, I think as the GPDA, we’ve been told more or less that 24 races, 25 races is the limit of the championship that they’re willing to go for. I don’t know if that will be the case, the more offers there are to keep increasing venues. But I think that is the limit.

“I think it’s more about the members of the team that are going to spend only three or four days at home, or five days at home every month. And it’s the people in the teams that get the tougher end rather than the drivers. I think we are in a more privileged position in that sense.

“So, let’s see. I have the motivation to do however many races we need to do. I have the will to race. I love racing. But it is true that this end of the triple header, with three triple headers in a row, is going to be tough for the body, tough for the people, tough for the mind.”

Sports.title: F1 newcomers Tsolov, Mini and Slater among eight drivers to run in practice on Friday | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Eight teams will give practice outings to inexperienced drivers at this weekend’s Mexican Grand Prix.

Three of them – Red Bull junior driver Nikola Tsolov, Alpine’s Gabriele Mini and Audi’s Freddie Slater – will make their debuts in an official F1 test session. Tsolov will drive for Red Bull’s second F1 team, Racing Bulls.

Teams must give four opportunities to inexperienced drivers – two in each of their cars – in first practice sessions over the course of the year.

Among the others driving this weekend is Luke Browning. Williams has entered him for a fifth session this year after he completed no laps when he appeared for them at the Circuit de Catalunya.

Also in action this weekend are Leonardo Fornaroli and Jak Crawford, making their fourth appearances for McLaren and Aston Martin respectively. McLaren recently confirmed Fornaroli, the 2025 Formula 2 champion, will drive for its new WEC Hypercar team.

Ayumu Iwasa will also make his fourth appearance this year, and third for Red Bull. He has also previously driven for Racing Bulls. Ryo Hirakawa will appear for the third time in a Haas this season.

More than half the teams will have completed their obligation to run drivers on four occasions after next week’s Brazilian Grand Prix. Unlike in previous years, none of the remaining rounds are sprint events, meaning they theoretically have more opportunities to run their junior drivers. But with doubt continuing to hang over whether the final races in the Middle East will go ahead, teams appear to be ensuring they do not fail to fulfil their practice quotas should they be cancelled.

Sports.title: New contract to keep Perez racing for Cadillac until at least 2029 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Cadillac has announced a new contract with Sergio Perez, days before he starts his 300th grand prix at home in Mexico.

Perez will remain at the team until at least 2029 under his new, long-term deal.

He joined the F1 newcomers last year ahead of their debut this season.

“Building a competitive team in F1 is a long-term journey, and securing Checo’s talent and leadership gives us the continuity and commitment we need to build on the strong foundation established in our first year,” said CEO Dan Towriss. “Together, we are focused on the next phase of our journey, pushing the team forward and making progress up the grid.”

Cadillac is yet to confirm the identity of Perez’s team mate for next year. The team are yet to score a point, Perez having achieved a best finish of 14th, current team mate Valtteri Bottas 13th.

“Building a Formula 1 team from the ground up takes time, relentless work and patience, but the progress we are making together is incredibly rewarding,” said Perez. “There is still a lot of work ahead of us and I am fully committed for the next three years.”

Perez has experienced disappointment with multi-year contracts before. In 2019 he agreed a three-year deal to stay at Lawrence Stroll’s Racing Point team, before it became Aston Martin. However Stroll dropped Perez at the end of the following season and replaced him with Sebastian Vettel.

During his fourth year at Red Bull the team extended his contract by two years, then dropped him at the end of the season. He sat out the 2025 campaign before returning to F1 with Cadillac.
