Sports.title: Antonelli’s coronation, Mexico’s optional turn one and more Mexican GP talking points | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The world championship outcome may be a foregone conclusion but there are plenty of other talking points of note at this weekend’s Mexican Grand Prix.

All over bar the shouting

There could hardly be less doubt over the destination of this year’s world drivers’ championship. Yes, theoretically there are still three drivers in the hunt, but the two who aren’t Andrea Kimi Antonelli realistically need him not to score in the next four consecutive races to still be in with a shot come the final round.

On top of that, consider that at least one of the remaining rounds might not go ahead anyway. In which case even this flimsy conjecture is moot, and the championship is already Antonelli’s.

But if, as seems almost certain, he does win the title this weekend, what a venue to do it at. If the remodelled Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez has one thing going for it, it’s the joyous theatre of F1 fever which greets drivers in the stadium at the end of the race.

Optional turn one

The opening trio of corners on the Mexico City track has been a trouble spot since Hermann Tilke’s designers reworked the layout for the race’s return in 2015. The tight corner configuration and generous run-off area make it easy for drivers to abuse track limits at this point on the track.

Last year’s start was a particularly egregious example as multiple drivers arguably benefitted from cutting the corner. Max Verstappen’s approach to it gave every indication he never intended to stay within the track’s boundaries.

Will race control take note and put stricter measures in place? There was little sign this was a priority in Austin last weekend, where track limits have long been a problem.

Debutants Slater and Mini join the rookies

At least two drivers will make their debuts in an F1 practice session this weekend. Audi’s promising rookie Freddie Slater, who finished second in Formula 3 this year, will take over Gabriel Bortoleto’s car for first practice. Alpine’s Gabriele Mini will be in Franco Colapinto’s car.

Several of the regular practice session drivers will also appear: Frederik Vesti at Mercedes, Luke Browning at Williams and Ryo Hirakawa at Haas. Some teams are yet to confirm their plans.

Mexico versus Lawson

Liam Lawson was at the centre of a bizarre incident last year when he had the misfortune to encounter two marshals on track. Incredibly, Mexico’s automobile club accused the blameless driver of being responsible for the oversight.

The FIA later made it clear Lawson had done nothing wrong. Hopefully there is no repeat of either administrative slip-up this year.

Perez hits 300

Last year’s Mexican Grand Prix was the first without a home driver since the event returned to the calendar. But Sergio Perez is back on the grid this year and will mark his 300th start in front of his home crowd.

Expect the usual huge cheers for the Guadalajaran. However the hope of a points finish looks as remote as ever. Indeed, the combination of high cooling demands and several heavy braking points could aggravate one of Cadillac’s most obvious weaknesses.

Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster Reveals Shakur Stevenson Vanished After Ring Stunt
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson gathered all the buzz for a potential O’Shaquie Foster bout without stepping into the ring. By stepping through the ropes following Foster’s win over Raymond Ford in May, Stevenson ignited major public anticipation. Yet Foster reveals his team pushed for the bout, waited, and met total silence.

That recent past demands a sharper look at Stevenson’s latest words. Foster just took down Emanuel Navarrete, and Stevenson quickly voiced fresh interest. Boxing enthusiasts ought to pause before celebrating, keeping Foster’s prior experience in mind.

“We kept asking. We didn’t hear nothing. We didn’t hear nothing,” Foster said on the Ariel Helwani show. “We held out for a little bit. We didn’t hear nothing. Tyrone didn’t hear nothing.”

Foster explained that talks never progressed to discussing weight classes. He expressed total readiness to step up to lightweight or junior welterweight, clearing away a major hurdle for a 130-pound titleholder looking upward.

“We didn’t even get that far, but I didn’t care,” Foster noted. “Like, I honestly didn’t care whether it was 135, 140. Either one. It didn’t matter to me.”

It looked like pure clout chasing from Shakur, plain and simple. Walking into another man’s spotlight right after a hard-earned victory creates the illusion that you want the fight next. Fans get excited, the broadcast cameras lock onto you, and you get all the free publicity without taking an ounce of risk. Then, the second Foster’s camp actually reached out to make the fight happen, Shakur vanished into thin air. Total silence.

Once Foster beat Navarrete, Stevenson offered public compliments along with a fresh challenge.

“Hell of a fighter. He will never give me my credit, but I’ll be real tonight. He showed his level,” Stevenson stated in a social post read on air. “That’s a challenge that would get me out of bed. Let’s do it whenever he’s ready. I’ll be here after his undisputed run.”

That is what makes Stevenson’s latest comment after Foster beat Navarrete look so empty. Saying he will fight Foster “whenever he’s ready” completely flips the reality of what happened. Foster was ready months ago, even offering to jump up in weight to make it effortless for Stevenson. Shakur was the one who went missing.

For now, Foster’s sights remain locked on unifying all four belts at 130 pounds. Chasing undisputed status puts Foster in control rather than hanging on Shakur’s schedule. Foster can hunt the remaining belt while Stevenson figures out whether his online comments translate into real business.

Sports.title: David Benavidez Gives PBC More Years Without Becoming A Star
Sports.content:
David Benavidez is locking in more of his prime with PBC, even though his run with the outfit has not turned him into a household name. He has collected belts in three divisions. Casual fans still have little reason to tune in, and facing Michal Cieslak on December 5 will not change that.

Benavidez turns thirty next year. He burned through his twenties chasing Canelo Alvarez. Then he cleared out of light heavyweight without ever facing Dmitry Bivol or Artur Beterbiev. Now he sits at cruiserweight, stacking belts while marquee opponents remain out of reach.

“I’ve always wanted to stay with PBC. I feel like what we’ve built, obviously PBC is PBC before I got there, but the work I’ve put in for this promotional company, I’m not going to get that anywhere else,” Benavidez told FightHubTV. “I feel comfortable with Luis De Cubas. I feel comfortable with Al Haymon. This is my family. I’m one of the pillars that helps PBC stand.”

He sounds like someone trapped by sunk costs. Pouring years into a promotional stable is no reason to surrender the rest of his career. If mainstream fame is the actual target, he needs to look honestly at what loyalty has given him.

He has put on solid bouts. Caleb Plant provided genuine heat. Demetrius Andrade came undefeated. David Morrell was a dangerous test. Gilberto Ramirez offered the chance to pick up cruiserweight hardware. The resume is legitimate.

The box office numbers tell a different story. Reports put the Morrell clash at 150,000 to 160,000 pay-per-view buys. The Andrade fight reportedly landed around 60,000 buys. Those figures are not official numbers, but they prove he has not developed into an elite pay-per-view draw.

Canelo was the matchup that could have launched him into superstardom. It never happened, even with both fighters under the PBC umbrella. Canelo walked his own road, while Benavidez paid the bill in wasted time. Sharing a promotional banner provided zero leverage to force the biggest draw into the ring.

Bivol chose his own path too, giving up the WBC belt rather than facing Benavidez in 2025. Promoters cannot force anyone to sign. Yet Benavidez is the one creeping toward thirty without those career-defining names on his record.

Cieslak brings another strap to the table, but offers zero buzz for American fans. Winning might give Benavidez three cruiserweight titles, yet leave him completely invisible to general sports culture. That is the exact loop he must break.

Launching DB Promotions once his deal with Sampson Lewkowicz wraps up gives him real leverage. Sticking with PBC feels familiar, but familiarity seems to be his main motivation for staying put.

Benavidez has shown he can win titles with this team. He has not shown he can become a crossover sensation with them. Betting the remainder of his peak on this same routine is risky. He needs Jai Opetaia or another opponent people will actually pay to watch. Cieslak is just another belt while the real clock keeps ticking.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Documentary Launches on Netflix Ahead of Joshua Fight
Sports.content:
Netflix releases TYSON FURY on November 27, tracing the heavyweight’s rise through boxing and examining his personal struggles before he faces Anthony Joshua on December 11.

Lucy Wilcox directs the feature-length documentary. Fury, his wife Paris and father John give interviews alongside previously unseen footage from his life and career.

Tyson Fury’s Career and Family Life

The film follows Fury from childhood into the heavyweight ranks, revisiting the victories and setbacks that shaped his career. His family contributes its accounts of the experiences behind those performances.

Mental health, addiction and the loss of a child are among the subjects covered. The documentary also examines Fury’s views on masculinity, his family relationships and the support he has relied on throughout his career.

Paris and John bring their perspectives to a film that explores the personal pressures accompanying Fury’s success in the ring.

Fury vs Joshua: December 11 Date and Netflix Broadcast

Fury and Joshua step into opposite corners on Friday, December 11, 2026, at Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales. Netflix will broadcast their first professional meeting globally to all members at no additional cost.

The remaining bouts have yet to be announced.

At their September 30 press conference, Fury spoke about the years spent waiting to get Joshua into the ring.

“I’m looking forward to the challenge. It’s been 10 years in the making,” Fury said.

“The rise has been phenomenal from both fighters. We’ve both had our ups and downs. Finally, we arrive at this moment.”

Fury also praised his British rival: “He’s been a role model and a poster boy for British boxing for years.”

Joshua welcomed the occasion and said their exchanges would drive him through extra rounds in the gym.

“I feel fresh. I feel very excited about this opportunity to work again,” Joshua said.

Sports.title: Jake Paul Ends Retirement Doubts With December 24 Dubai Fight
Sports.content:
MVP chief Nakisa Bidarian addresses questions over Paul’s boxing future following the Anthony Joshua injury, with a Christmas Eve comeback confirmed.

Jake Paul will fight again after the broken jaw he suffered against Anthony Joshua raised doubts about his boxing future. MVP has confirmed a December 24, 2026, comeback in Dubai, and promoter Nakisa Bidarian says Paul’s decision answers those who questioned his desire to return.

The opponent remains unconfirmed.

Bidarian put the injury and its aftermath at the centre of his comments about Paul’s first fight back.

“Twelve months ago he suffered a double broken jaw against a two-time heavyweight world champion and since then many have doubted his desire or need to return to boxing,” the MVP co-founder and CEO said.

“Well he is back, and that tells you everything about the competitor Jake Paul is and how much he loves this sport.”

Paul Answers With a Christmas Eve Comeback

Paul heads into his return with a 12-2 record and seven knockouts. His December 2025 meeting with Joshua preceded the year-long absence that will end when he headlines MVP’s card in the United Arab Emirates.

He has committed to another fight.

“I’m hungrier than ever, and on Thursday, December 24, I’m returning to the ring in Dubai to start the next chapter of my journey,” Paul said.

The comeback will also take Paul into a new location for his professional career. He has never contested a professional bout in Dubai, which will host the event through MVP’s cooperation agreement with the Dubai Sports Council and Dubai’s Department of Economy and Tourism.

MVP has not yet named the opponent, venue or broadcaster. The promotion plans to release further details over the coming weeks, with no weight division or scheduled distance specified in the October 29 announcement.

Paul began his professional career in 2020. His headline appearances have since included Mike Tyson in November 2024 and Joshua the following December, with the latter leaving him facing a lengthy spell outside the ring.

Bidarian described the decision to resume fighting as evidence of Paul’s commitment to boxing. Paul, meanwhile, closed his comeback statement with a prediction for whoever signs to face him.

“Merry Christmas, Dubai. Santa Paul is coming to town, and somebody’s getting knocked out.”

Sports.title: David Benavidez Ready To Put Oleksandr Usyk First
Sports.content:
David Benavidez is risking his shot at Oleksandr Usyk by messing around with Jai Opetaia or Artur Beterbiev beforehand. Jumping straight up to heavyweight makes total sense, especially since he already sounds open to flipping the script.

Talking about skipping straight to Usyk sounds a whole lot less like fearless ambition and a whole lot more like self-preservation.

Benavidez knows that the road running through Jai Opetaia and Artur Beterbiev is not a tune-up run. It is an absolute danger. If he actually believed he could steamroll both men, he would happily take their scalps, build an undeniable mountain of momentum, and walk into a showdown with Usyk as a massive multi-division attraction.

Bypassing them exposes the reality: he knows the risk of getting derailed before cashing that mega check is sky-high.

“If they want me to go up … I don’t give a f***,” Benavidez stated in the interview. “I want to fight. I want to fight the best people. And if I got to go up there and fight for the lineal belt with no belts, I’ll do that … I just want to fight the best in the world. I want my respect, and I’m going to get it one way or another,” said Benavidez to Fight Hub TV about moving up to heavyweight to face Usyk.

That sounds like someone ready to sign for Usyk the moment pen meets paper. He never locked himself into clearing out Opetaia or Beterbiev before taking that leap.

If he takes an L against either one, the Usyk lottery ticket instantly turns to dust. Usyk is not going to look twice at a defeated Benavidez trying to pick up the pieces, not when he can command massive money elsewhere.

Opetaia has the exact southpaw movement, discipline, and sharp counterpunching to turn Benavidez into a frustrated stalker swinging at fresh air while eating clean leather all night. Beterbiev brings brutal inside violence and technical craft that makes trading in the pocket pure trouble.

Both matchups carry a high probability of stripping Benavidez of his spotless record and shredding his market value.

Benavidez already wasted years chasing Canelo Alvarez, only to come away empty-handed. Now that he is finally free from that waste of time, he ought to recognize the danger of waiting around for the stars to align.

Usyk is clearly the legacy crown he wants.

“Usyk has more accolades than Canelo, in my opinion,” Benavidez noted. “Once I beat him, there’s no denying me my spot in the history of boxing.”

Admitting he would train “like I’m scared for my life” shows he respects the mountain in front of him. Taking Usyk immediately carries risk, but it locks down the biggest prize while Benavidez’s zero remains intact.

Sports.title: Chrisean Rock vs Morgan Victory In Smack Fighting Championships Main Event
Sports.content:
While some of the elite level boxers continue to disappoint their fans with overpricing themselves, and dehydration clauses, a new wave of combat sport is scooping up the casual fans, and some of the traditional boxing fans.

On Friday night November 20th reality TV star turned boxer Chrisean Rock will face Morgan Victory. The action is set to take place at Harrah’s Philadelphia Casino, and it will air live on Triller TV.

This event is unique because of the unconventional format. For this collection of contests, half of the card is boxing, and the other half of the event card will be smack fighting matches.

Unlike traditional boxing, smack fighting is an open-hand fast pace type of bout. The fighters use custom designed gloves that are made for open hand strikes.

The architect of the Smack Fighting Championships is the CEO Damon Feldman. The Broomall, Pennsylvania native is a former boxer who had a record of (9-0, 4 KOs).

Unfortunately, his professional boxing career was derailed due to injury. Now Feldman has put together an event that is both unique and entertaining.

Chrisean Rock (1-0, 1 KO) has dedicated herself to the sweet science, and she plans to take another successful step in her boxing journey. Her opponent Morgan Victory was also victorious in her boxing debut and she’s ready to play the role of the spoiler.

The night of November 20th promises to be a groundbreaking night of entertainment. Naughty By Nature rapper Treach, and two-division boxing world champion Danny “Swift” Garcia will be the guest hosts for the event.

Sports.title: Will Golden Boy Pay Shakur Stevenson’s Price?
Sports.content:
Oscar De La Hoya is making a play to sign Shakur Stevenson, but his pitch reveals Golden Boy’s real priority: staging a William Zepeda rematch. While De La Hoya sees big business in a second meeting, he has yet to outline what he would actually put on the table to secure Stevenson’s signature.

“I would love to promote a Shakur Stevenson. He’s arguably the best fighter pound-for-pound in the world. Who doesn’t want to promote him? I know what to do with him,” De La Hoya said to the media.

De La Hoya is either dreaming or running a pure promotional bluff, because the economics make zero sense.

If Dana White and Zuffa walked away from Shakur over demands of 15 million per outing, there is no world where Golden Boy can satisfy that appetite. Golden Boy operates on a standard broadcast model with DAZN. To justify a 15 to 20 million guarantee, a fighter has to generate massive pay-per-view buys, fill a football stadium, or carry commercial sponsorships at an astronomical level.

Shakur does none of that.

His pure boxing skill is undeniable, but his safety-first style has never translated into commercial box office power. Casual fans simply refuse to pay premium pay-per-view prices to watch twelve rounds of tactical potshotting and resetting. If Golden Boy put Shakur on pay-per-view against anyone other than a megastar like Gervonta Davis, the buy rate would be catastrophic. Even a rematch with William Zepeda is nowhere near big enough to cover those kinds of purses.

So what is Oscar actually doing? Most likely, De La Hoya is using Shakur’s free agency to generate free press and build up Zepeda’s profile. By publicly offering to sign Shakur and insisting Zepeda is the man who pushed him to the brink, Oscar gets the benefit of elite association without having to cut the check.

“What excites me is that who gave Shakur his toughest fight? William Zepeda, who’s getting better, who is becoming a complete fighter,” De La Hoya claimed. “So will we see that fight happen again? I would love to see it because Zepeda right now is a punching machine that now has the wit, the experience, the power, and the punch output is through the roof.”

If Oscar truly believes he can deliver 15 million purses on DAZN pay-per-view with Shakur at the top of the bill, he is setting Golden Boy up to take a massive financial bath. In reality, once real contract numbers replace public soundbites, the gap between what Shakur expects and what Golden Boy can afford will stop any deal dead in its tracks.

Money talks, yet De La Hoya skipped the finances entirely. He talked up his promotional track record, but stopped short of floating purse guarantees, a schedule, or a debut matchup.

Shakur benefits from having another major player chasing him openly. Golden Boy gets to chase a generational star while building buzz around Zepeda. De La Hoya put his cards on the table. Now, Golden Boy needs to back up the talk with a genuine contract offer.

Sports.title: Vergil Ortiz Jr. Scrambles To Sell Shot Keith Thurman
Sports.content:
Vergil Ortiz Jr. wants everyone to treat Keith Thurman like a live dog ahead of their December 5 matchup, yet cracked wise about Sebastian Fundora’s towering reach along the trail. Joking around will not scrub away the harsh reality of that loss. Thurman looked completely spent against Fundora, leaving Ortiz to convince paying customers that a victory here actually counts for something meaningful.

Here lies the messy reality of selling this event. Ortiz must puff up Thurman because blasting out a shot fighter earns him zero credit.

“People are overlooking Thurman because he got stopped by a world champion who can tie his shoes standing up,” Ortiz remarked during promotional duties.

Fundora’s freakish height definitely created problems. The sixth-round stoppage proved Thurman lacked answers once his punches fell short. He absorbed steady damage with zero response.

His prior appearance, a third-round stoppage over Brock Jarvis, provided a highlight reel against soft opposition. It never proved the former unified champion could still hang with the division’s best, which made the harsh lesson against Fundora predictable.

The sport leans on this familiar strategy. Promoters match a surging contender against a faded name coasting on reputation. The veteran cashes a check on past glory, and the rising star gets a marquee notch on his resume. Fans see right through it.

“I just want to be in exciting fights. That’s the point of boxing. I want to be remembered as a guy who never said no to a fight,” Ortiz stated.

Taking every challenge is commendable, but that attitude fails to justify Thurman as pay-per-view headliner material. Crowds clamoring for clashes with Jaron Ennis or Fundora get handed a guy Fundora already battered into submission.

“I don’t go in with the mentality to get someone out right away. I’ll feel him out and download information. Obviously I’m familiar with Thurman, but we’re not gonna take anyone lightly,” Ortiz explained.

Ortiz walks right into a classic situation. Score a swift knockout, and critics declare Thurman washed up. Grind out a distance win, and people will point out Fundora did the job much faster.

Thurman desperately needed an honest tune-up to give this clash real credibility. Without that foundation, Ortiz is left doing all the heavy lifting at the podium.

Ghana News.title: Ashanti Regional GJA secures land waiver for proposed press centre
Ghana News.content:
The Ashanti Regional Branch of the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) has secured a waiver on land allocated by Asantehene Otumfuo Osei Tutu II for the proposed Ashanti Press Centre, marking a significant milestone in efforts to establish a permanent office for journalists in the region.

Chairman of the association, Kofi Adu Domfeh, announced at the Ashanti Media Excellence Awards 2026, where he called on corporate institutions, development partners, philanthropists and individuals to support the next phase of the project.

Mr. Domfeh described the proposed centre as more than a physical structure, indicating it would serve as a hub for professional training, collaboration, media development and the advancement of journalism in the region.

He expressed profound gratitude to Otumfuo Osei Tutu II for the gesture and acknowledged Access Bank Ghana and Fidelity Bank Ghana for providing seed capital to support the project's take-off.

However, he noted that additional resources would be required to move the project from planning to construction.

He therefore appealed for financial contributions, building materials, technical expertise and other forms of practical assistance to help realise the vision.

“The Ashanti Press Centre must become our collective legacy. We invite you to be part of it,” he said.

The chairman's appeal comes at a time when the media landscape is undergoing rapid transformation, driven by digital platforms, artificial intelligence and growing concerns about misinformation and declining public trust.

The proposed Ashanti Press Centre is expected to provide a dedicated institutional space to support journalists and strengthen the media profession in the region.

Beyond serving as a physical base for the Association, the project is intended to create opportunities for professional development, collaboration and improved journalistic practice.

Credibility remains journalism's greatest asset

Additionally, Mr. Domfeh highlighted the importance of credibility, ethical conduct and accountability in journalism.

He observed that artificial intelligence was creating new opportunities for research, production and storytelling, while also making it easier to generate fake images, fabricate audio, manipulate videos and circulate misinformation.

In such an environment, he argued, credibility would remain the defining difference between professional journalism and the growing volume of online content.

“AI can generate content, but journalists must provide verification, context, judgement and accountability,” he said.

He urged journalists to embrace technological innovation without compromising accuracy, ethics or the public interest.

The GJA Chairman also stressed the importance of credible journalism in addressing challenges confronting communities in the region, including illegal mining, environmental degradation, unemployment, public health concerns and governance deficits.

He called on journalists to investigate critical issues, ask difficult questions, amplify neglected voices and hold those in positions of authority accountable.

Ghana News.title: Asene farmers demand compensation for farms destroyed by Accra-Kumasi expressway
Ghana News.content:
More than 200 farmers at Akyem Asene, near Oda in the Eastern Region, have appealed to the government to pay them adequate compensation for their farms and plantations destroyed to make way for the construction of the new Accra-Kumasi expressway.

The affected properties include cocoa farms, food crop farms and oil palm plantations, which the farmers say were their main sources of livelihood.

The farmers, some of whom wore red pieces of cloth around their heads, necks and arms, staged a demonstration through some principal streets of Asene before gathering at the Asene durbar ground to address the media.

Leaders of the affected farmers, including Kofi Koranteng Sarpong, Yaw Peprah, Da Costa Asamoah and Yaw Ampomah Asiedu, took turns to describe the economic hardships they have endured since their farms were destroyed more than eight months ago.

They said the loss of their farms had made it difficult to meet their daily needs and pay the school fees of their children in tertiary institutions.

Mr Asamoah said he had struggled financially since his eight-acre cocoa farm was destroyed in February 2026. He said the farm had previously earned him an average annual income of about GH¢40,000.

Mr Koranteng Sarpong, meanwhile, expressed concern that the farms of more than 20 affected farmers, including his own, had not been measured by surveyors to determine the extent of the damage and the compensation due to them.

When contacted by the Daily Graphic, the Head of the Ghana Highway Authority (GHA) survey team for the project, Samuel Tieku, confirmed that some of the destroyed farms had not been measured to assess the extent of the damage.

He explained that the original width of the expressway was 120 metres but had been increased to 150 metres, a change that had affected additional farmers.

Ghana News.title: Divided by Party, United in Suffering: Ghana’s dilemma of blind partisan loyalty
Ghana News.content:
There is something deeply troubling about the way politics has come to occupy Ghana’s public space. Every morning, from television and radio programmes to conversations in taxis, offices and homes, we encounter the same political theatre.

The government of the day says one thing, the opposition holds press conference to say another, their supporters then rush to defend, accuse and counter-accuse one another over who has mismanaged the country more.

And somewhere in the middle of all this noise is the ordinary citizen, struggling with unemployment, rising living costs, inadequate public services and the daily uncertainty of making ends meet.

The concern is not simply that Ghana is politically divided. It is that partisan loyalty increasingly shapes our understanding of right and wrong, our tolerance for poor governance and our willingness to demand accountability from those entrusted with public office.

This is where I juxtapose Karl Marx’s famous description of religion as the “opium of the masses” to offer an interesting lens through which to examine Ghanaian partisan politics.

Marx, the German philosopher and economist, used opium as a metaphor for something that provides comfort amid suffering while potentially distracting people from the conditions responsible for that suffering. The argument was not merely that religion was harmful, but that it could through its teachings make suffering more bearable without necessarily changing its underlying causes.

A similar argument can be made about partisan politics and the particular version of democracy we practice here in Ghana.

It is no doubt that political parties (the NDC and the NPP) are essential to representative democracy. They represent competing ideas, offer alternatives to voters, mobilise citizens and create opportunities for peaceful changes in government. But there is an issue when political loyalty consistently interferes with independent judgement.

In Ghana, partisan identification provides many people with a sense of belonging, identity and emotional reassurance. It gives supporters a political community and the feeling that their preferred party represents their interests. But when that attachment becomes unconditional, it can numb their response to wrongdoing.

Imagine a scenario where a former or serving government official is facing allegations of corruption, mismanagement or questionable conduct. Party communicators and supporters rush to defend the individual, question the credibility of the investigating institutions or redirect attention to the conduct of a previous or opposing administration.

An allegation involving a member of one party quickly becomes an opportunity for the other to revisit controversies from its own time in office. The familiar questions follow; Who started the problem? Which government borrowed more? Which administration built more roads? Who was more corrupt?

I mean, these are legitimate questions in a functioning democracy. Historical context matters, and governments should be assessed against their predecessors where appropriate. However, comparisons should clarify responsibility, not erase it. The fact that a previous government committed similar mistakes does not absolve the current government. Likewise, criticism of an incumbent administration should not automatically become a defence of its predecessor.

A country cannot make meaningful progress if every demand for accountability is met with a counter-accusation.

The Ghanaian political scene also interestingly operates through the psychology of the divide trap. This is the tendency for citizens to become so invested in political groups that the success or failure of their side influences how they interpret reality.

When political identity becomes deeply embedded in one’s sense of self, criticism the party can feel like criticism of one’s own community or identity.

This creates an “us versus them” mentality.

When our side succeeds, we celebrate it as evidence of competence. When the opposing side succeeds, we search for reasons to diminish its achievements. When our party faces allegations of wrongdoing, we demand evidence and caution. When the opposing party faces similar allegations, we demand immediate punishment.

The same action can therefore be interpreted differently depending on who performs it.

This is the divide trap, reinforced by partisan motivated reasoning. People tend to accept information that confirms their political beliefs while dismissing information that challenges them. Over time, the question becomes less about whether something is true and more about whether it benefits their political side.

Instead of political parties being accountable to citizens, citizens begin to feel accountable to political parties.

Instead of asking, “Is this government doing the right thing?” we ask, “What will this mean for our party?”

Instead of asking whether an allegation is credible, we ask who is being accused. Rather than asking how the country can improve, we focus on how our side can defeat the other in the next election.

That is where partisan politics begins to resemble a drug to which we have become addicted.

Political arguments become emotionally satisfying while the material problems generating our frustrations remain unresolved.

A young person struggling to find employment may spend hours defending a political party online. A family facing rising living costs may spend an evening arguing about which government is responsible. A citizen frustrated by poor public services may defend an official simply because that official belongs to the party they support.

The irony is difficult to ignore. We can be fiercely committed to defending political leaders while complaining about the very conditions their decisions, or those of their predecessors, helped create.

One of the most troubling consequences of the divide trap is the transformation of accountability into a political weapon.

An investigation involving political opponents is celebrated as evidence that the rule of law is working. A similar investigation involving political allies is described as persecution, witch-hunting or political victimisation.

Political influence can exist within investigations, and not every allegation proves wrongdoing. Due process, credible evidence and the presumption of innocence are fundamental principles of justice.

But these principles must apply consistently, regardless of political affiliation.

If we believe in due process, we must believe in it when our opponents and our allies are investigated. If we believe corruption should be punished, we must demand accountability regardless of the political colours of those involved. If public officials should be held accountable, we cannot suspend that principle whenever an official belongs to our preferred party.

Otherwise, we are not defending principles. We are defending our side.

Public officials are not private representatives of party supporters. They exercise public authority and use public resources. Their primary obligation is to the Ghanaian people and the laws of the Republic, not to political parties.

Political disagreement is a natural and necessary part of democracy. But democracy should be more than a competition between two political camps.

A government initiative should not automatically be considered good because our party introduced it, nor should it automatically be condemned because the opposing party introduced it. Policies must be judged on their merits, politicians on their conduct, institutions on their performance and governments on whether their decisions improve people’s lives.

Yet political discussion increasingly seems less concerned with these judgements and more concerned with winning arguments for one’s preferred party.

From morning radio programmes to television discussions and social media, we debate who said what, who insulted whom, which party is responsible and which administration performed worse. Then tomorrow, we begin again.

Meanwhile, the unemployed graduate remains unemployed. The struggling farmer continues to face production challenges. Families confronting rising costs continue to struggle, while citizens waiting for better healthcare, education, roads and public services continue to wait.

The political argument has been won, but the problem remains.

The contradiction becomes even clearer when a party moves from opposition into government. While in opposition, its supporters demand transparency, accountability, respect for the rule of law and freedom of expression. Yet when that same party assumes power, some of those demands suddenly lose their urgency.

The standards used to criticise political opponents are not always applied to political allies. This inconsistency undermines the very democratic principles citizens claim to defend.

The problem is not that citizens support political parties. They have every right to believe that one party offers better policies, leadership or vision. The distinction is in whether that support remains open to evidence, criticism and reconsideration.

There is a difference between political loyalty and political blindness. There is a difference between defending a policy because one believes it is right and defending it simply because one’s party introduced it. There is also a difference between challenging an allegation because the evidence is inadequate and dismissing it because the accused belongs to one’s political camp.

Democracy requires the former, not the latter.

Breaking out of the divide trap does not mean abandoning our political parties. It means putting them in their proper place.

Parties exist to serve democracy. Democracy does not exist to serve political parties.

Our allegiance to Ghana must therefore be greater than our allegiance to any political party. We should be able to admit when our party is wrong, acknowledge when an opposing party introduces a good policy and criticise our preferred government without being accused of working for the opposition.

Equally, praising an opposing government should not amount to a betrayal of our political identity. These are not signs of political weakness. They are signs of democratic maturity.

The responsibility also extends to the media and political actors. Radio and television discussions should create room for evidence-based debate, meaningful policy analysis and scrutiny of all political parties. Political communicators must recognise that defending a party does not require defending every action taken by its members.

Journalists and media platforms must also avoid turning political conflict into entertainment simply because confrontation attracts attention. Citizens deserve discussions that help them understand policies, assess performance and hold public officials accountable, not endless exchanges that deepen political divisions without addressing national problems.

Citizens, too, must play their part. We cannot continuously complain about bad governance while rewarding those in realm of affairs with unconditional loyalty. We cannot demand accountability from the government we oppose and excuse the government we support.

Our political consciousness should be measured not by how fiercely we defend the NDC or the NPP, but by how consistently we demand honesty, transparency and accountability from whoever holds political power.

Regardless of who occupies the presidency, certain questions should remain central to our political conversations.

Are young Ghanaians finding meaningful employment? Can families afford a decent standard of living? Can citizens trust public institutions? Can public officials be held accountable? Can the country move beyond the familiar cycle of promises, disappointments, blame and political retaliation?

These are questions that should unite us. Yet the divide trap encourages us to see those on the other side of the political divide as enemies rather than fellow citizens who may be experiencing the same frustrations.

The NDC supporter and the NPP supporter may disagree passionately because of party identity, yet both may be struggling with the same economic pressures. Both may have children seeking employment. Both may complain about the same roads, schools, hospitals and public services.

Their political identities divide them, but their lived realities often unite them.

If we fail to recognise this, we risk becoming participants in a political cycle that continually demands our emotional loyalty while offering too little in return.

I’m not saying Ghanaians should stop caring about politics. But can we care about politics without allowing politics to control our judgement.

Can we support a party without surrendering our conscience? Can we oppose a government without romanticising its predecessor? Can we demand accountability from our own side with the same energy with which we demand it from the other?

And can we recognise that the greatest victory in a democracy is not the triumph of one political party over another, but the triumph of citizens over bad governance?

Until we do, partisan politics risks remaining “the opium of the us” keeping us emotionally occupied, politically divided and perpetually arguing while the deeper problems of our society remain largely untouched.

The question, therefore, is not simply, “Whose side are you on?” It is, “Whose interests are being served?”

Ghana News.title: Prisons Council explores legal aid for inmates over challenges with appeals
Ghana News.content:
The Chairman of the Ghana Prisons Service Council, Apostle Ing. Alexander Nana Yaw Kumi-Larbi, has disclosed plans to explore legal assistance for inmates, following concerns over difficulties in accessing court proceedings and securing legal representation for appeals.

He made the disclosure during a familiarisation visit to the Ankaful Prison Complex in the Central Region, where inmates appealed for support in navigating legal processes.

Apostle Kumi-Larbi said he was in discussions with more than 100 lawyers who are members of The Church of Pentecost to explore ways of providing legal support to inmates.

The visit involved a tour of the various prison establishments and engagements with officers and inmates on welfare, rehabilitation, and operational challenges.

During the interaction, inmates expressed gratitude to President John Mahama for the recent presidential amnesty but highlighted difficulties in obtaining court proceedings needed to pursue appeals and accessing legal assistance.

Drawing inspiration from the biblical story of Joseph, the Council Chairman encouraged the inmates to remain hopeful and focused on building a better future. He also prayed for both officers and inmates.

The delegation visited the prison infirmaries, where Prof. Ernest Yorke, President of the Ghana Medical Association and a member of the Prisons Service Council, offered recommendations on managing available healthcare resources.

Prof. Yorke also assured the delegation of his commitment to exploring avenues for additional support to improve healthcare delivery within the facilities.

Ghana News.title: Ghanaian neuroscientist honoured at Millennium Excellence Awards USA for Alzheimer’s blood test discovery
Ghana News.content:
Thomas Karikari, associate professor of psychiatry and clinical and translational science at the University of Pittsburgh’s School of Medicine in the United States, was a proud recipient of the Excellence in Scientific Research award at the recent Millennium Excellence Awards ceremony in Washington, DC, under the royal patronage of Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, the Asantehene.

When young Dr. Thomas Karikari entered his laboratory in Sweden years ago for his research program, one question lingered on his mind: “Why don’t we have a good blood test kit for Alzheimer’s dementia?”

This was a question that not only developed into a hypothesis for research, but one that was ready to transform biomedical research in neuroscience and enhance medical care for people living with the condition.

Many scientists had attempted in their might to understand how the disease could be easily tested without an invasive procedure, but failed at it.

Dr. Karikari was nearly discouraged in his quest for answers.

“I was told you don’t talk about it. Companies have spent millions; they couldn’t do it. People have spent years, but they couldn’t do it. So, just shut up,” he recounted.

But, burning with the desire, the neuroscientist was poised to develop his question into a groundbreaking practical solution to testing the neurological disorder with blood samples.

‘And I set out to do it as my side project. I wasn’t even doing it as my main project because no one believed it would work,” he noted.

For decades, diagnosing Alzheimer’s required invasive procedures such as spinal taps or expensive brain scans. These tests are often inaccessible in many regions of the world, especially in low-resource communities.

Dr. Karikari’s experience with limited diagnostic capacity in Ghana fueled the need for a solution. So, when he was headhunted to lead a clinical research program in diagnostic medicine at the University of Pittsburgh in the United States of America (USA), he was bent on dedicating most of his career to developing, improving, and validating the clinical performance of blood tests that could simplify Alzheimer’s diagnosis.

After grueling years and sleepless nights at the lab, he finally found a means to detect the disease.

Dr. Karikari has about 300 publications to his name. He has published multiple seminal works in leading medical journals describing major innovations in high-performance blood tests for the neurological disorder.

He also holds several patents and pending patents to that effect. Last year, Dr. Karikari was recognized by Clarivate as among the top 1% of scientists worldwide. The high-impact journal Nature also named him as a Rising Star in Ageing research, an accolade that was bestowed on only three investigators.

These accomplishments have earned Dr. Karikari global respect and recognition as a leading figure in biomedical research. His achievements were celebrated at the just-ended Millennium Excellence Awards USA, spearheaded by the Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II.

“I am so proud that today I have made that contribution. A contribution that would change the face of how we treat diseases for a long time. This is just a stepping stone,” he gladly noted.

Dr. Thomas Karikari's groundbreaking research has led to the development of multiple blood tests for Alzheimer's disease and other forms of dementia.

In his acceptance speech, Dr. Karikari further noted that two new blood tests for Alzheimer’s disease have been approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

This adds to two already approved by the authority over the last two years.

Dr. Karikari’s mission is beyond scientific discovery—he wants diagnostics to reach everyone, including people in places like his home village of Manfo.

He says a parcel of land has been acquired back home in his late mother’s hometown of Achinakrom near Ejisu in the Ashanti region to continue with the groundbreaking scientific discoveries in Ghana. He is poised to establish a research center to help advance biomedical research on the continent.

“Everything we do must get back to our people,” he said.

Ghana News.title: Mahama appoints 15 officers of the Ghana Prisons Service
Ghana News.content:
President John Mahama has appointed 15 officers of the Ghana Prisons Service, elevating seven Deputy Directors of Prisons to Directors of Prisons and eight Assistant Directors of Prisons to Deputy Directors of Prisons.

In a statement issued on Thursday, October 29, it said the appointments, which took effect on July 1, 2026, were made in accordance with Article 207 of the 1992 Constitution, on the advice of the Prisons Service Council.

The seven officers appointed to the rank of Director of Prisons are Abraham Nii Moi Allotey, David Ofosu Addo, Thompson Otsyokpo, Edward Ashun, Joseph Asabre, Alfred Moses Cudjoe and Samuel Fiifi Dontoh.

Mr Allotey is the Western Regional Commander and Officer-in-Charge of Sekondi Central Prison, while Mr Ofosu Addo serves as Head of Government Business at Prisons Headquarters.

Mr Otsyokpo is the Bono-Ahafo Regional Commander and Officer-in-Charge of Sunyani Central Prison. Mr Ashun serves as Greater Accra Regional Commander and Commanding Officer at Prisons Headquarters, while Mr Asabre is the Central Regional Commander and Officer-in-Charge of Ankaful Maximum Security Prison.

Mr Cudjoe serves as General Staff Officer at Prisons Headquarters, while Mr Dontoh is Head of Procurement at the headquarters.

The eight officers appointed from Assistant Directors of Prisons to Deputy Directors of Prisons are Joseph Aggrey-Graham, Gandaa Bekanuo Zunuo, Aaron Agbenyegah Agbo, Michael Osei Akoto, Forson Odei, Naja Daniel Donkor, Nasom Kwabena Bawah and Matilda Nyampong.

The Ghana Prisons Service congratulated the officers and wished them success as they take on their new responsibilities.

The Service reaffirmed its commitment to professionalism, discipline and effective leadership, as well as its mandate of ensuring the safe custody, welfare, reformation and rehabilitation of prisoners.

Ghana News.title: Minerals Commission defends termination of Northern Ashanti Mines’ mineral rights over $8.3m debt
Ghana News.content:
The Minerals Commission has defended its decision to terminate the mineral rights of Northern Ashanti Mines Limited, formerly Owere Mines, insisting that the company persistently failed to meet its statutory financial obligations despite several opportunities to settle its debts.

According to the Commission, the company accumulated approximately US$8.33 million in unpaid Annual Mineral Right (AMR) fees on its mining leases as of April 2025, alongside US$49,928 owed on prospecting licences.

Addressing a press conference, the Commission rejected allegations by Northern Ashanti Mines that the termination was carried out in bad faith, maintaining that the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources acted within his legal authority.

The Commission explained that Owere Mines acquired a mining lease covering 595 cadastral blocks in January 2010 but subsequently failed to fulfil its annual payment obligations under Section 24 of the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703).

It disclosed that the company had accumulated more than US$4 million in outstanding fees by May 2020, prompting the issuance of a notice to remedy the breach.

Following the takeover of the company by BCM Investments, management proposed settling the debt in four instalments. However, the Commission said the company failed to honour the arrangement despite being given additional opportunities.

By October 2022, the outstanding debt had risen to US$5.59 million, increasing to US$6.18 million by December of the same year.

The Commission indicated that further notices issued in April 2025 revealed that the company's indebtedness had reached US$8.33 million in mining lease fees, excluding outstanding prospecting licence fees.

Consequently, on April 7, 2026, the Commission recommended the termination of the company's mineral rights to the Lands Minister, citing persistent non-payment.

The Minister subsequently approved the issuance of the termination notice.

Responding to the company's challenge to the debt figures, the Commission insisted that its records showed Northern Ashanti Mines had paid only US$300,000 in two instalments, contrary to the company's claim of having paid US$1 million.

"For a company that claims to have spent US$200,000,000 on the mine, what prevented it from paying the US$8,000,000 owed to the people of Ghana?" the Commission questioned.

It further criticised the company's decision to pursue legal action against the Lands Minister, the Minerals Commission and the Attorney-General while simultaneously seeking public dialogue over the matter.

The Commission maintained that the company should allow the courts to determine the dispute rather than engage in what it described as litigation through the media.

It stressed that the termination of the mineral rights meant the affected concessions had reverted to the State, without cancelling the company's outstanding financial liabilities.

The Commission consequently announced its intention to pursue the recovery of all outstanding payments owed by Northern Ashanti Mines.

It also emphasised the State's responsibility to protect the affected mining assets from encroachment and other illegal activities, citing Section 70 of Act 703.

The Commission reaffirmed that due process had been followed throughout the termination proceedings and insisted that no mining company, whether locally or foreign-owned, would be permitted to disregard its statutory obligations.

"No one is above the law in this country. If you flout the laws, there are sanctions, and those sanctions will apply," the Commission stated.

It reiterated its commitment to enforcing Ghana's mining laws without fear or favour, stressing that the country's mineral resources belong to the people and must be managed in accordance with the law.

Ghana News.title: Women domestic workers earn 48% of other employees’ wages – ILO
Ghana News.content:
Women employed as domestic workers worldwide earn an average of 48% of the monthly wages of other employees, highlighting persistent gender-based inequalities in the sector, according to the International Labour Organisation (ILO).

In its latest report, The State of Domestic Work in 2025: 15 Years After Convention No. 189, the ILO said women account for 77.2% of domestic workers globally and are disproportionately concentrated in cleaning and direct-care occupations.

The report found that male domestic workers earn an average of 65.8% of the monthly wages of other employees, compared with 48% for their female counterparts.

The figures underscore the persistent wage disparities affecting women in a sector that provides essential household services, including cleaning, cooking and caring for children, older persons and people with disabilities.

The ILO estimates that 80 million people aged 15 and above are employed as domestic workers worldwide, up from 75.6 million in 2019.

However, 66.5 million of these workers, representing 83.1% of the global domestic workforce, remain in informal employment, often without effective labour and social protection.

The organisation said domestic workers earn an average of 53.3% of the monthly wages of other employees, while those in informal employment earn just 48.7%.

The report also found that 35.2% of domestic workers work at least 49 hours per week, with 14.6% working 60 hours or more.

The ILO has called for stronger implementation of its Domestic Workers Convention, 2011 (No. 189), and Recommendation No. 201 to improve wages, expand social protection, strengthen working-time safeguards and ensure decent working conditions.

It also urged governments and other stakeholders to strengthen labour-law enforcement, promote social dialogue and collective bargaining, and invest in decent care jobs.

Patrick Belser, Chief of the ILO’s Informal Work Branch, said progress in some countries showed that change was possible, but more needed to be done to address informality and the widening wage gap.

“We cannot claim to value care while undervaluing the people who provide it,” he said, calling for the rights outlined in the convention to be translated into effective protection for domestic workers.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
