World.title: France football chief backs Real Madrid’s Mbappe after China apology
World.content:
Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe should be allowed to move on after apology to China, says French football federation chief.

French Football Federation ‌chief Philippe Diallo said Kylian Mbappe should be allowed to move on ⁠amid controversy over ⁠the France captain referring to former Chinese leader Mao Zedong as a dictator because the player has apologised and intended no offence.

Mbappe’s club ⁠Real Madrid and La Liga have also apologised following the remarks, while the league’s president Javier Tebas set up a crisis unit and met Chinese ambassador to Spain, Yao Jing, ⁠on Wednesday as Spanish football sought to contain the fallout.

The backlash highlights the risks for athletes and brands in the lucrative Chinese market, where satire about Mao, modern China’s founding leader who governed the country from 1949 until his death in 1976, remains ‌a social taboo.

Chinese state media outlet China Daily said Mbappe’s remark had “triggered a backlash among his Chinese fans, threatened his lucrative commercial relationships and offered a sharp reminder of the limits of celebrity influence”.

China’s state-owned broadcaster Migu is not showing Real Madrid’s game at Racing Santander on Sunday, and Chinese brands including dairy companies Mengniu and Shanghai Milkground Food Tech, as well as Eastroc Beverage, have ceased all cooperation with Mbappe.

Diallo expressed hope the issue would soon be ⁠resolved.

“It is a controversy which, ultimately, should not, I hope, last because Kylian has very well explained the context in which this intervention took place. He has apologised,” Diallo was quoted as saying ⁠by French newspaper Ouest-France on Thursday.



“I believe we should now leave it at that so that he can continue his ⁠season in the best possible conditions.”

The controversy stems from ⁠a long-running joke surrounding 27-year-old Mbappe’s influence at club level.

In a video on a French podcast that has since been taken down, Mbappe is heard discussing a meme in which his face had been ‌photoshopped onto that of “some guy”, adding: “I think he’s a Chinese dictator.”

Fans have previously created memes superimposing Mbappe’s face on images of military and political leaders to suggest ‌he ‌has the power to influence decisions at the teams he plays for. Mbappe has been nicknamed “the dictator” in the European press.

A spokesman for China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the government is taking Mbappe’s apology “seriously”.

World.title: European Central Bank President Lagarde to step down early
World.content:
Christine Lagarde will leave the post in February, nine months before the end of her eight-year term.

European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde will step down months before her term ends, kicking off a race to succeed her against a turbulent backdrop in the eurozone.

Lagarde announced on Thursday that she will leave the post on February 7, about nine months before the scheduled end of her eight-year term. She said in a filmed statement posted on X that she was leaving “with a sense of good work done and an ECB that is fit for the future”.

The move gives European Union leaders time to choose her successor before April’s French presidential election, which polls have suggested far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is favoured to win.

The timing could allow current European Council members, including French President Emmanuel Macron, to take part in appointing Lagarde’s successor before France’s vote.

Macron, who is not allowed to run again, thanked Lagarde in a post on X for “the determined action she led at the head of the European Central Bank” during “a period marked by numerous crises”.

“The transition at the head of the ECB must now be prepared in an orderly and balanced manner with our European partners,” the leader of the eurozone’s second-largest economy added.

However, Markus Ferber, a German member of the European Parliament, warned: “If the impression arises that such a departure is timed around national elections, it damages trust in an institution that must stand above any domestic political calculation.”

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, leader of the eurozone’s largest economy, said Lagarde had led the bank “with great aplomb during challenging times”, and European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen thanked Lagarde “for everything you have done for Europe and the euro”.



French Finance Minister Roland Lescure praised her tenure. “Christine Lagarde has been an exceptional President of the ECB. As Europe navigated through crises and difficult times, she brilliantly modernised and strengthened the institution,” he posted on social media.

Marcel Fratzscher, president of the German Institute for Economic Research, told the Reuters news agency the early exit gives governments “an opportunity to appoint a successor who will safeguard European values and protect the ECB’s independence”.

Markets appeared unfazed. “Our view is that institutional behaviour is likely to outlast Lagarde and be quite similar, whoever takes over,” Simon Dangoor, head of fixed income macro investing at Goldman Sachs told Reuters.

Lagarde, appointed in October 2019, steered the bank through the COVID-19 pandemic, Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine and the United States-Israel war on Iran.

The ECB faced criticism for responding too slowly to the 2022 inflation surge, caused by post-pandemic supply chain bottlenecks and the war on Ukraine. Inflation is currently running at almost double the bank’s 2 percent target amid worries over France’s public finances.

A former French finance minister and head of the International Monetary Fund, Lagarde arrived in Frankfurt in 2019 as the first ECB chief with no formal economics training or central banking experience, prompting some market participants to warn of a “credibility risk”.

In March 2020 as the pandemic shook sovereign debt markets, she said the bank was not there to narrow the gap between Italian and German borrowing costs. She went on to show that political diplomacy could steer a central bank through historic shocks.

Sources told the AFP news agency that leaving early would give Lagarde “greater freedom to express her views”. She has hinted she could campaign in the French presidential race, saying a European voice was needed in the debate.

World.title: Manchester United’s Carrick backs Fernandes and is expected to face Chelsea
World.content:
Michael Carrick will manage Man Utd at Chelsea on Saturday despite sacking rumours, and says team captain Bruno Fernandes will return.

Share Manchester United’s Carrick backs Fernandes and is expected to face Chelsea on social media

Manchester United manager Michael Carrick, under pressure after a woeful run of results, said on Thursday that he was “here to do my job”, insisting he needed “no assurances” over his future at Old Trafford.

Carrick also said he was unsurprised to still be in charge and gave his backing to United captain Bruno Fernandes.

Portugal midfielder Fernandes was left on the bench for last week’s loss at home to Bournemouth following his criticism of Carrick’s tactics in a 4-1 thrashing by Como.

“He’s the one that’s kind of led the team so well for many a game and many a year, and he’ll continue to do that,” Carrick told reporters on Thursday.

Carrick’s position has been the subject of intense speculation after a miserable run of eight football games without a win.

Sunday’s 3-0 humbling loss at home to Bournemouth left the English giants one point above the Premier League relegation zone.

The 20-time English champions have won just two of 12 matches in all competitions this season, with a return of seven points from eight league games representing their worst start to a league season in 40 years.

Carrick was widely expected to be sacked this week, but he remains in charge after a show of support from the club’s hierarchy.

Speaking ahead of Saturday’s match away to Chelsea, the former United and England midfielder was in a defiant mood.

Asked if he was still surprised to be in post, Carrick said: “No, I am here to do the best for the team, and I am desperate to make us better and improve things, so I’m not surprised, no.”



Carrick “doesn’t need assurances” from Manchester United, he said.

Carrick was equally adamant he did not require public backing from the United hierarchy.

“I don’t need assurances from anyone,” he said. “I totally get the position, I get the job, the responsibility, I get what comes with that.”

Questioned on Fernandes’s position, Carrick said leaving him on the bench against Bournemouth was a “decision for the game”.

“That’s it. Bruno is fully committed to this football club. I’ve got no issues with that; we move forward. We’re looking forward to the game at the weekend now.”

Carrick appears to have the backing of the United faithful, being warmly applauded by fans as he made his way down the tunnel following the defeat by Bournemouth.

Moments later, a chorus of boos erupted as the players left the pitch, as supporters made clear where they think the blame lies for United’s poor performances.

Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after inspiring a revival as caretaker boss that saw United finish third in the Premier League and return to the Champions League after struggling under manager Ruben Amorim.

But results have been so bad this season that former United captain Gary Neville, who played alongside Carrick at Old Trafford, said on Thursday that “sometimes a manager needs sacking for their own good”.

Carrick, however, was adamant he would not walk away from his job, saying: “I’ve said it before, I care about what the supporters think. I care about what we give them, and what we offer them, and what they see.

“I know this job, I know what it brings, I know what we need to do really to be better. I don’t need anyone else to tell me anything else.”

This season’s drastic decline is an all-too-familiar story for United supporters, who last witnessed a Premier League title triumph 13 years ago under Alex Ferguson.

But Carrick insisted his much-criticised players felt the sting of poor results every bit as much as the fans.

“The boys are hungry,” he said. “We’re hurting because we haven’t won enough football games. But there is an intensity, an edge, a hunger to do better.”

World.title: Israel’s anti-Qatar campaign bleeds into elections
World.content:
As Israel awaits the final results of its highly contested elections, some political figures have sought to drag Qatar into the fray with claims of voting interference – an accusation Doha rejects.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party and media outlets associated with it have, without evidence, accused Qatar of sending money to Arab parties in Israel for get-out-the-vote drives.

Qatar’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesman on Thursday categorically denied the allegations of interference or funding of any activities aimed at influencing the election results.

“We reject the accusations made by certain Israeli politicians and their contacts in the media, who have launched yet another disinformation campaign aiming to drag Qatar into Israeli political disputes following this week’s elections,” Majed al-Ansari said in a post on X.

The unsubstantiated Israeli claims, which the spokesperson described as “ridiculous and dangerous in equal measure”, are the latest in a long-running campaign against Qatar.

Netanyahu has previously boasted about attacking Qatar in September 2025 during Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza while Israeli influence experts and political advisers also worked on a secret campaign targeting Qatar in the weeks after the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attacks on southern Israel.

“[Some Israeli politicians] accuse Qatar of buying off Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli political left and now, in this latest campaign, the Arab vote. If these claims were to be believed, Qatar would apparently own all of Israel,” al-Ansari said.



Partial results indicated that Netanyahu’s bloc would not secure a majority in the Knesset in Tuesday’s parliamentary elections. Those results showed the two Arab lists securing a record number of seats in the new parliament, but the main parties have rejected the idea of partnering with them.

Despite the latest claims, Dean Livine, the acting director for Israel’s Central Elections Committee, has rejected allegations of foreign interference in the elections. “The Knesset elections were conducted lawfully. The integrity of the elections at polling stations was rigorously safeguarded,” he wrote in a letter to an MP and fellow committee member.

“The repeated invocation of Qatar in Israeli electoral rhetoric reveals an excessive obsession with our country among certain Israeli political and media figures,” al-Ansari said, adding that Qatar should “not be used as a scapegoat for the political failures of certain Israeli politicians”.

The Foreign Ministry spokesman said some Israeli politicians, instead of shifting attention onto Qatar, “would be better off focusing on their own voters, improving people’s everyday lives, and undoing the damage they’ve created in the region”.

He reiterated that Qatar has “no involvement” in Israel’s political or electoral competition.

“These are internal Israeli matters in which we do not interfere, and we will not accept any attempt to draw Qatar into its domestic political disputes.”

Qatar is a key mediator in the conflict between Israel and the Palestinians and played a central role in talks to halt Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.

Doha is also leading mediation efforts between Washington and Tehran to end the United States-Israel war on Iran.

Al-Ansari said the latest accusations would not distract Doha from its “important role as a mediator, our diplomatic and humanitarian efforts, our support for the Palestinian people, or our commitment to a just and comprehensive peace and regional stability.”

World.title: Spanish long jumper Julieta Gallego among victims of deadly train collision
World.content:
Julieta Gallego, who competed for Madrid-based AD Sprint, among those killed in train crash in Spain.

The Royal Spanish Athletics Federation expressed its condolences following the death of 24-year-old long jumper Julieta Gallego, who was among the victims of the train collision in Spain’s Toledo province that killed at least 68 people.

“The Spanish athletics family joins in the grief over the passing of Julieta Gallego, athlete of AD Sprint, in the train accident that occurred in Urda (Toledo),” the federation (RFEA) said in a statement on Thursday on X, offering its support to her family, friends and club teammates.

Gallego competed for Madrid-based AD Sprint and was a regular participant in Spain’s club championships. Her long jump personal best was 5.90 metres (19.4 feet), set in Antequera in 2023.

“There are blows that strike at the very heart of the athletics family. Today, the sport mourns the passing of Julieta, a life ahead of her that has been unjustly extinguished,” RFEA president Raul Chapado told Spanish newspaper ABC.

Two high-speed trains collided on Wednesday in the second deadly accident in less than a year on the line connecting Madrid to southern Andalusia.

At least 68 people were killed in the crash and about 80 were injured, 50 of them seriously and 15 critically, said Emiliano Garcia-Page, president of the Castilla-La Mancha regional government.

The most seriously injured people were taken to hospitals in the region and in Madrid, the capital. Others were assessed at a sports hall near the crash site, where emergency teams sorted them by the severity of their injuries before sending them home or to hospital.



Survivors treated near the scene had head wounds, facial swelling and bloodied clothing, and many were dazed, according to local media reports.

World.title: Israeli strikes hit Gaza as Health Ministry urges Rafah opening
World.content:
At least two people have been killed in the latest Israeli attacks on Gaza, as the Ministry of Health in the strip calls for the Rafah crossing to be opened to allow sick and wounded Palestinians to leave for treatment.

Israeli attacks across Gaza continue at a “very high pace” on Thursday, with drone strikes hitting the centre and north of the territory over the past few hours, according to Al Jazeera’s Ashraf Abu Amra.

Reporting from Deir el-Balah, Abu Amra said an Israeli drone fired two missiles in quick succession at a civilian car in the middle of the Maghazi refugee camp in central Gaza, killing two Palestinians and wounding others.

The wounded were taken to Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital, where they were rushed into operating theatres or admitted to intensive care. One is in critical condition.

“The strike was sudden and came without prior warning,” Abu Amra said, noting that Israeli aircraft are flying at low altitude across all areas of the strip.

Earlier, an Israeli strike in Jabalia, in northern Gaza, wounded a Palestinian who was taken to al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City.

Abu Amra said attacks were escalating east of Jabalia in the Halawa camp, one of the largest displacement camps in the north, where Israeli forces stationed along the edges of the so-called “Yellow Line” have begun firing directly at tents sheltering displaced families.

Israeli strikes in east Gaza City

In eastern Gaza City, explosions have been heard in the Shujayea, Tuffah and Zeitoun neighbourhoods as a result of Israeli artillery shelling. Israeli forces are also carrying out large-scale demolitions in areas under their control behind the “Yellow Line”, including east of Deir el-Balah, Khan Younis and Gaza City, and in Beit Lahiya in the north, destroying homes and what remains of local infrastructure.



On Thursday morning, four Palestinians were buried at Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis after being killed in an Israeli drone strike in the al-Mawasi area of Rafah, near the Rafah and Karem Abu Salem (Kerem Shalom) crossings.

Abu Amra said the victims were civilian employees of the Ministry of Economy who monitor aid trucks entering through Karem Abu Salem.

More than 30 others were wounded in the attack, according to Al Jazeera’s Moath al-Kahlout. Tens of thousands of displaced Palestinians live in tents in al-Mawasi, which Israel had previously designated a “safe zone”.

Al-Kahlout also reported that 11 people, including women and children, were wounded when Israeli artillery struck a house east of Gaza City, citing emergency services.

Gaza’s Health Ministry said on Thursday that six Palestinians had been killed and 38 wounded over the previous 24 hours.

The violence came as the ministry renewed its call for the Rafah crossing to be opened so that sick and wounded Palestinians can leave the territory for treatment.

In a statement, the ministry said 21,468 patients and wounded people need to travel for care outside Gaza, including 6,430 identified as priority cases.

It blamed repeated border closures and what it described as deliberate delays in evacuation procedures for worsening patients’ conditions, saying dozens had died while waiting for permission to leave and the health of thousands more had seriously deteriorated.

Since February, 3,056 patients and wounded people have been evacuated for treatment abroad, the ministry said, 2,614 through Rafah, which connects Gaza with Egypt, and 442 through the Karem Abu Salem crossing with Israel.

World.title: As US midterms approach, farmers decide what to plant and how to vote
World.content:
Share As US midterms approach, farmers decide what to plant and how to vote on social media

When Paul McKinney, a farmer in northeast Arkansas, thinks of his son’s childhood, he remembers a small boy playing in vast fields.

To a child, a flooded rice field is “like a giant, 40-acre swimming pool”, he said.

Rice has been a staple on McKinney’s farm for four generations. Next year, however, the family plans to plant much less. Instead, they will focus on soya, a crop that is cheaper to produce.

Like farmers across the United States, McKinney is making tough decisions this year in response to higher fuel and fertiliser costs, which have skyrocketed since the start of the war on Iran.

This week, farmers also face tough choices at the polls. Democrats are expected to make gains in the midterm elections, as voters react to high prices economy-wide by switching parties or staying home.

Observers are watching farm country closely. Texas and Kansas could send Democrats to the Senate for the first time in decades. In the House of Representatives, two majority-rural districts, Wisconsin’s Third and North Carolina First, could become tipping points for Democratic control.

Still, many of the country’s most rural areas, like Arkansas, are also its most safely Republican.

That leaves an uphill battle for Democrat Hallie Shoffner, who quit farming last year to challenge Republican Senator Tom Cotton in a campaign squarely focused on rising costs.

How high costs hurt farmers

Even before the US-Israel war on Iran, high input costs were straining farmers, said Ryan Loy, an extension economist for the University of Arkansas’ Division of Agriculture.



Loy pointed to a trade war with China that began in 2018, the ongoing war in Ukraine and disruptions related to the 2025 tariffs as factors driving up input costs and disrupting markets. A drought across the US heartland, made worse by climate change, has added to the strain.

Farmers across the country are working to adapt. In Arkansas, many farmers skipped rice in favour of soya. Soya is “the least input-intensive crop, and perhaps can break even or have the shallowest loss”, Loy said.

Now Arkansas, usually the country’s top rice producer, has its lowest rice acreage since the 1970s. Many farmers hoped 2026 would bring economic recovery so they could return to rice.

Then, the war on Iran hit. With the Strait of Hormuz blocked, fertiliser costs jumped just as farmers were fertilising during the spring planting season.

Loy tracked the increase in a sample budget that he maintains for Arkansas row crop farmers. “Urea fertiliser specifically peaked about 39 percent over our budgeted amount,” Loy said. Diesel costs came in about 72 percent more than budget averaged across the planting, growing and harvesting seasons, Loy found.

Those changes represent a significant economic hit. “For our state alone, it’s an additional cost of about $343m,” Loy said.

Last week, US President Donald Trump announced an $8bn fuel relief programme for farmers, following $12bn in tariff-related aid in 2025. If the fuel relief payment were divided equally between the 50 states, it would cover less than half of the extra costs that Loy estimates Arkansas’ farmers paid this year.

McKinney, a member of the Arkansas Farm Bureau, said the announcement was welcome. Still, he hoped for longer-term solutions that would prevent “this constant battle for survival”.

For many farms, survival is indeed getting harder. Farm bankruptcies for the first three quarters of 2026 were up 19 percent compared to this time last year, according to a recent analysis by the University of Arkansas’ National Agricultural Law Center. They were up 73 percent compared to 2024.

‘We can’t keep doing this’

McKinney’s son, who grew up playing in muddy rice fields, now helps his dad farm their 24,000 acres. So does McKinney’s nephew, who this year is driving a combine.

“As has been done for us, we would love to be able to hand that down to the next generation,” said McKinney. “But you also have to think about what is going to be best for them.”

McKinney questions how long farming will provide a sustainable living. “It’s some heavy things to think about,” McKinney said.



For Shoffner, a sixth-generation Arkansas farmer, that reckoning came last year.

Higher costs, lower crop prices and the uncertainty of trade wars and tariffs “made the numbers stop working” for their 2,000-acre farm operation, Shoffner told Al Jazeera.

“I know what it feels like to work hard, make every adjustment you can, and still have to sit down with your family and say, ‘We can’t keep doing this,’” Shoffner said.

To protect her parents’ land and retirement, Shoffner closed the family’s farm. That “heartbreaking” decision helped spur her Senate run.

“I decided that if I can’t farm, I will fight,” Shoffner said.

If elected, Shoffner wants to end the war on Iran, build trade policies farmers “can actually plan around”, invest in local processing and distribution, and pass a robust Farm Bill — strategies she hopes will help farmers and rural economies more broadly.

“If we want rural communities to have a future, the people producing our food have to be able to make a living doing it.”

Cotton did not respond to a request for comment.

How will farmers vote?

Economic pain may not change farmers’ votes, however, in Arkansas or nationwide. Michael Shepherd, a political scientist at the University of Michigan, said many farmers, like many rural voters, are committed Republicans.

Committed voters tend to view the economy through a partisan lens, according to Shepherd. “Their political behaviours, their voting choices, things like that, are not particularly responsive to changes in the agricultural economy,” he said.

Some polling this year, however, did suggest the potential for movement. A poll by the Farm Journal in April found that 35 percent of farmers who “usually” vote Republican and 15 percent who “always” vote Republican were still considering how they would vote.

And September polling from Purdue showed that, for the first time this term, a majority of farmers surveyed think the country is “on the wrong track”.

Even if farmers are swayable, of course, Shoffner still may not be the one to sway them: her campaign has been far outspent by Cotton’s, an established lawmaker who has received funding from interest groups like AIPAC and leaders at companies like Anthropic and Palantir.

“If one side has a massive war chest, and the other side has very limited resources, then that game of tug of war can be won much easier than it should be,” Shepherd said.

And even if farmers do change their votes, they may not decide elections.

McKinney, who is now farming one of the Shoffner family’s former fields, said farmers represent a shrinking percentage of rural voters — their strength now is in organising, not numbers.

Still, even where candidates like Shoffner don’t win, their campaigns might signal to funders that similar races may be competitive in the future or help Democrats win down-ballot seats.

In Arkansas’ second congressional district, for example, the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee is betting on Democrat Chris Jones. It’s a long-shot campaign, but across the country, at least some long-shot candidates are expected to win.



“All indications are that this is gonna be one of the biggest shifts away from the president’s party that we’ve observed,” Shepherd said.

World.title: Israel’s opposition may not be able to form a government, but it still could control Parliament.
World.content:
For decades, Israel’s Arab parties have been relegated to the margins of Israeli political life, often sitting on the sidelines while Jewish parties assembled a governing coalition in Parliament and picked a prime minister.

Heading into Israel’s pivotal election on Tuesday, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned his supporters that the Arabs were “trying to steal the election,” though electoral officials said there were no reports of widespread irregularities. He repeatedly invoked the specter of Arab voters to galvanize his right-wing base, vowing to keep them out of power.

Mr. Netanyahu’s leading rival, Gadi Eisenkot, largely declined to answer whether he would partner with Arab parties if necessary to topple the Netanyahu government, though he said none met his conditions as potential allies.

But record turnout by supporters of the Arab parties looks to deliver them their largest vote totals in generations, possibly since Israel’s establishment 78 years ago.

Now, the Arab minority represents a political reality that cannot be ignored.

Turnout in the Arab community, which represents about 20 percent of Israeli citizens, appears to have translated into a stunning windfall of parliamentary seats — potentially as many as 19 combined between the two leading parties, Raam and the Joint List alliance. The Arab parties have 10 seats in the outgoing Parliament.

Israel’s future could turn in part on whether Mr. Eisenkot decides to take the political risks of partnering with them. Without their support, Mr. Eisenkot and his alliance will almost certainly fall short of the 61-seat majority required in the 120-seat Parliament to form a new government and end Mr. Netanyahu’s hold on power. Mr. Netanyahu’s alliance also looks to fall short of 61 seats.

Many Israeli Jews have long objected to building a governing coalition that relies on Arab party backing for a majority. Some say a Jewish state should be ruled exclusively by Jews. Some cite national security reasons, questioning whether Arab leaders who see themselves as part of the wider Palestinian people can be entrusted with crucial matters of state.

Those objections became even more acute after the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attacks on Israel and the subsequent rightward shift in Israeli politics. Both Raam and some members of the Joint List condemned the assault, although they have also been highly critical of how Israel has conducted its war against Hamas in Gaza.

The Arab parties for many years were themselves reluctant to join governments that oversaw the Israeli occupation of the West Bank and Gaza. And turnout among Arab citizens has traditionally been lower than Jewish turnout, reflecting doubts about their ability to influence national decision-making.

Raam, a socially conservative party with roots in Islamist politics, has achieved some acceptance in Israel’s mainstream by putting less emphasis on the cause of Palestinian statehood. But the Joint List, an alliance of three smaller parties that includes a joint Jewish-Arab leftist faction and a Palestinian nationalist faction, is seen as more antagonistic toward Zionism.

Initial election results show that the Joint List will be the significantly larger of the two in Parliament.

“Netanyahu knows that without the Arab parties, there’s no majority to unseat him. That’s why he incites against us,” said Yousef Jabareen, the leader of the Joint List alliance in an interview. “The opposition should reject that incitement.”

He added: “The ball is now in Eisenkot’s court. Whoever wants to remove Netanyahu and change his policies — we are ready to cooperate to topple his government.”

Political analysts say the Joint List would be more likely to support Eisenkot from outside the governing coalition, for instance by agreeing to block any no-confidence votes. There is some precedent for this: In the 1990s, then Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin relied on Arab lawmakers to prevent the collapse of his own minority government.

Arab citizens, some of whom identify themselves as Palestinians with Israeli passports, experience a tension that can cut to the heart of daily life. Unlike Palestinians in the West Bank — who live under Israeli military rule — they have the right to vote, and some have held high office, including on the country’s Supreme Court.

But they largely live in separate cities and towns from Jewish Israelis and retain tight familial and historical bonds with Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza. Many view themselves as second-class citizens in the Jewish state, saying they face discrimination in housing as well as neglect in receiving public services.

Before this year, the largest electoral success recorded by Arab parties was in 2020, when they secured 15 seats. And the first — and so far, only — time an independent Arab party joined the Israeli governing coalition was in 2021, when Mansour Abbas, the leader of Raam, joined Mr. Netanyahu’s rivals to unseat him in favor of a short-lived government.

Mr. Abbas has since worked to make his party more acceptable to Israeli Jews. He has recognized Israel’s Jewish character as a fact of life and publicly considered integrating Arabs into the country’s mandatory national service, in particular community service.

In a bold move during the election campaign, he named Jewish lawmaker Yoav Segalovitz — a former senior police officer and centrist Zionist — as the number two on the Raam candidate list.

But if exit polls and initial results are correct, Raam’s support would not be enough to give Mr. Eisenkot’s bloc a parliamentary majority. He would also have to rely on the Joint List to topple Mr. Netanyahu. While political analysts say that Mr. Eisenkot might be willing to bring Raam onboard, he would struggle to keep his bloc with him if he made common cause with the Joint List, even if he wanted to, because this could provoke too much political blowback from many Jewish voters.

“There’s a shift in Arab politics, an attempt to get closer to the Jewish Zionist mainstream. It’s just that the other side is not willing to do so,” said Thair Abu Rass, an expert on Israel’s Arab politics. “There’s no partner on the Jewish side to create an alternative reality.”

World.title: The crash comes months after a fatal accident involving the same train operators.
World.content:
Pinned

A high-speed passenger train rear-ended another in Spain on Wednesday morning near the central city of Toledo, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens more, officials said, in one of the deadliest train crashes in Spanish history.

The accident happened after traffic control operators told a high-speed train to continue its journey when another train was stopped farther along the tracks, Spain’s transportation minister, Óscar Puente, said. He called the operators’ instruction “inexplicable.”

The deadly crash was the second this year involving the same two rail operators; the first, in January, killed 46 people. The latest accident, and its timing months after the previous crash, was likely to deepen doubts about the security of Spain’s once-vaunted rail system.

In Spanish news reports, passengers described an awful impact that tossed people from a dining car, broke limbs and piled passengers atop one another. People crawled out of windows and others were carried by fellow passengers into a nearby field on makeshift stretchers. Local workers, who had heard the crash, rushed to help and guide survivors to safety.

The crash came about a month ahead of national election in Spain, and it had the potential to become an issue in an already bitter campaign about the competence of the left-wing government of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez.

Spain’s rail authority, the Adif, said the trains involved were a “Renfe train and another from the Iryo company,” both covering the route between Madrid, the capital, and the southern city of Seville. Renfe is the national rail provider.

Mr. Sánchez visited the scene of the crash, saying that Spanish rail’s security systems clearly needed to be reinforced. “If there has been negligence, it will come to light,” he said. “If there have been failures in the safety system, we will respond with the utmost firmness.” He declared three days of official mourning.

The conservative opposition leader, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, voiced his own concern.

“I am very concerned about the information we are receiving regarding another train accident,” he wrote on social media soon after the crash. “The priority now is to assist the victims and support their families. My full support goes to the emergency teams working on the ground.” His Popular Party canceled all its campaign events around the country.

Here’s what else to know:

Survivor speaks: A passenger on one of the trains described a routine trip, a sudden jolt and an effort to tend to the dead and injured. Read more ›

An earlier deadly crash: In January, a northbound Iryo train derailed, two of its cars falling onto the opposite track, and a southbound Renfe train slammed into the carriages seconds later. An official report on what caused that lethal accident has not been released, but preliminary investigations pointed to a broken rail as the likely cause.

A detailed account: In a news conference, Spain’s transportation minister described the events that he said preceded Wednesday’s crash. Read more ›

José Bautista contributed reporting from the scene of the crash.

But if exit polls and initial results are correct, Raam’s support would not be enough to give Mr. Eisenkot’s bloc a parliamentary majority. He would also have to rely on the Joint List to topple Mr. Netanyahu. While political analysts say that Mr. Eisenkot might be willing to bring Raam onboard, he would struggle to keep his bloc with him if he made common cause with the Joint List, even if he wanted to, because this could provoke too much political blowback from many Jewish voters.

“There’s a shift in Arab politics, an attempt to get closer to the Jewish Zionist mainstream. It’s just that the other side is not willing to do so,” said Thair Abu Rass, an expert on Israel’s Arab politics. “There’s no partner on the Jewish side to create an alternative reality.”

World.title: Audio reveals exchanges between control centre and drivers before deadly Spain train crash
World.content:
Audio recordings published in Spanish media reveal conversations between train drivers and a railway control centre in the minutes leading up to a deadly train crash that killed at least 69 people and injured dozens.

Officials are investigating the cause of the disaster, which occurred when a train travelling from Madrid to Seville barrelled into a stationary train on Wednesday morning.

Three audio recordings between the control centre in Madrid and two train drivers appear to show that one high-speed train was given clearance to move even though another some 25km (15 miles) up ahead had stalled.

Prime Minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez, who travelled to the area of the crash, said authorities were working "day and night" to "get to the bottom of every last detail of this tragedy".

The release of the recordings comes as Spain begins three days of national mourning for one of the worst rail disasters in Europe's modern history.

One train, run by state-owned operator Renfe, had 397 passengers on board. Ahead of it on the same line was a train run by private operator Iryo, with 147 passengers.

A reported issue with the automatic signalling system - a computer failure - had forced all trains to halt on the affected stretch.

But later the Renfe train was ordered to proceed in "error", according to Spain's transport minister.

World.title: Russian drone attack on Ukrainian train station kills at least 14, officials say
World.content:
At least 14 people have been killed after a Russian jet-powered drone hit a crowded platform at the main railway station in the central Ukrainian city of Dnipro, local officials have said.

Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha said at least 14 others were wounded in the attack, including an 11-year-old boy.

Ukraine's state railway operator, Ukrzaliznytsia, said a passenger train headed for the southern city of Zaporizhzhia was at one of the platforms in Dnipro when the drone hit.

Russia's military has not publicly commented. It has repeatedly hit Ukraine's large railway network, but Moscow denies deliberately targeting civilians.

In Dnipro, an elevated threat level was announced ahead of Thursday's strike, according to the railway operator chief, Oleksandr Pertsovsky.

"But unfortunately there were still a large number of people on the platform" when the drone struck, he said.

Dnipro Mayor Borys Filatov said the incident was a tragedy, adding that a drone hit an electric civilian train.

Pictures from the Ukrainian rescue services show a large hole in a platform that is strewn with blurred-out bodies, near a blast-damaged train with smashed windows.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said "the Russians used a drone to attack a platform where a regular commuter train and a regular passenger train were standing."

He called for further US, European and G7 sanctions on Russia and repeated his criticism of a controversial deal that was struck earlier this month between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, which eased some sanctions on Moscow, allowing the US to import Russian diesel.

Elsewhere in Ukraine, two girls aged 15 were killed in a Russian missile attack on the centre of Chernihiv city, in the north of the country, regional head Vyacheslav Chaus said. At least 25 others, including four children, were injured, he added.

A day of mourning has been declared for Chernihiv and Dnipro on Friday.

In the city of Kremenchuk, in the central Poltava region, three people were killed and 28 injured in a Russian drone attack that hit residential buildings and a school, regional head Vitaliy Diakivnych said.

World.title: Flávio Bolsonaro calls himself 'leader of Brazil' after election loss
World.content:
Bolsonaro starts his letter, which he posted on his X account, saying "I address the Brazilian people and the international community as the leader of Brazil".

However, he had posted a previous version, that was later deleted, in which he wrote: "I address the Brazilian people and the international community as the rightful president of Brazil."

Both versions repeat the allegation that Bolsonaro first made on election night, that an extension of polling hours on Sunday had benefited his rival.

In the letter, he says it was "an electoral fraud unfolding before my eyes".

The extension was requested by both Lula's and Bolsonaro's campaign teams, and the head of Brazil's electoral authority has said that the vote proceeded normally and in full accordance with the country's laws and constitution.

An analysis of election data conducted by BBC Brazil and BBC Verify has also found that only around 34,000 people voted during the extended hours - far lower than the 4.4 million votes that separated Lula from Bolsonaro.

In his letter, Bolsonaro also addresses his departure from Brazil - which caused confusion after he disappeared for more than 24 hours.

It later emerged that he had gone across the land border to Argentina, and from there flew on to Florida, following a brief refuelling stop in Ecuador.

World.title: Philippine police obtain warrant to search Thomas Markle's devices
World.content:
Philippine police have obtained a warrant to examine devices seized from the former home of Thomas Markle, father of the Duchess of Sussex.

Earlier this month, it was reported that hundreds of images of child sexual abuse allegedly belonging to Thomas Markle Sr, 82, had been found at the property in the Philippines.

Four boxes of material, including computers, phones, hard drives and old videotapes, were handed to police by Meghan's half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr, last week. However, officers in Cebu needed a court warrant before they could examine the items.

Thomas Markle Sr, who is now in the US, has strongly denied the allegations made by his son, describing them as "sick lies".

Cebu Regional Prosecutor Graeme Elmido told the BBC that Thomas Markle Jr was "adamant" that the case should be investigated, and that he felt his father "has to answer for it".

Last week, the Sun on Sunday reported that Thomas Markle Sr's ex-wife, Roslyn Loveless, had sent a letter to the Metropolitan Police about the 2019 allegations, which was shared with the Duke and Duchess of Sussex at the time.

Loveless, who has since died, is the mother of Meghan's two half-siblings. She divorced Thomas Markle Sr. in 1975, before he married the duchess's mother.

World.title: Rock collapse kills two in Turkey's Cappadocia, local media reports
World.content:
At least two people have been killed and five injured after a rock formation collapsed at a tourist site in Turkey's historical region of Cappadocia, local media is reporting.

One of the rock spires, which are known as fairy chimneys, reportedly disintegrated at the popular open-air museum in the central town of GÃ¶reme.

NevÅehir provincial Governor HÃ¼seyin KÃ¶k said the victims' bodies had been recovered from under the rubble, but the justice minister warned there could be "other potential victims" still trapped.

The cause of Thursday's incident was not immediately known, however local media reported the collapse could have been triggered by heavy rain.

Turkish media reported that the collapse happened near the entrance to the museum - a Unesco World Heritage site - at about 15:15 local time (12:15 GMT).

In a later post on social media, Justice Minister AkÄ±n GÃ¼rlek said that "according to initial assessments, two individuals have lost their lives in the incident, and five others have been injured".

He added that a search and rescue operation was continuing at the site.

The Cappadocia region attracts tourists from around the world, who want to see the ancient fairy chimneys - tall, cone-shaped rock formations that are created by volcanic activity.

World.title: EU chief lays out vision for new Canada partnership at Montreal summit
World.content:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has laid out her vision for what an "associate membership" status for Canada to the EU would look like as officials gather in Montreal to discuss closer ties.

It is "a partnership that comes close to membership than anything we have done before," she said on Thursday's remarks at the two-day Canada-EU summit.

She added it is a type of relationship that would be open "only to our closest partners outside of Europe who are ready to open a new frontier together."

It includes close alignment on governance and policies, and partnering in research and innovation.

For decades, Canada-EU summits took place without much fanfare - but that's not the case for this year's meeting in the Canadian city.

Thursday and Friday's summit is being closely watched for details on how Canada and the European bloc deepen their ties.

Von der Leyen first proposed "opening the door" to Canada last month for what she called an "associate membership" - a status that does not currently exist.

The overture came after Prime Minister Carney addressed the European Parliament in Strasbourg, telling EU lawmakers that Canada and Europe were "stronger together" in the face of "geopolitical rupture".

Carney and many EU member states welcome closer ties, but not all are on board with what to call this new relationship.

Some, like Germany, are questioning the "associate member" term, fearing that Canada is getting preferential treatment ahead of other nations who also want in.

According to reports by multiple news outlets, Germany and other nations successfully lobbied to remove mention of the title in a draft statement ahead of the summit, opting instead for softer language that references an "ever closer association".

Germany's ambassador to Canada, Matthias LÃ¼ttenberg, told CTV News on Tuesday that some member states were "a little surprised" by von der Leyen's announcement last month.

While there is broad support for closer ties, the concept of "associate membership" is something that is not clearly understood as it pertains to Canada, he said.

"Germany has been using the term of associate membership for something completely different, which is the relationship of the EU to Ukraine and potentially Moldova", he said, both of which have been trying to join the bloc for many years.

Despite some opposition, von der Leyen has continued to use the term has not addressed the disagreement over the term.

World.title: Netanyahu's bloc leading Israel election but short of majority, partial results show
World.content:
The two Arab parties - the United Arab List and the Joint List - are set to almost double their representation because of a surge in turnout among Arab Israelis, who account for about a fifth of the population and often describe themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel.

Mahdi Kabaha, who lives in a village near Haifa and campaigned to get out the Arab vote, described the result as "historic".

"Arab citizens came out and said clearly: we want a real say in this country," he said.

The head of the Joint List, Yousef Jabareen, told the BBC that Arab voters had been motivated in part by the opportunity to remove far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir from office, whom he accused of racism and "provocation against our community".

Ben-Gvir, the leader of the Jewish Power party, has called for the annexation of the occupied West Bank, Jewish settlement of Gaza, and the "voluntary emigration" of Palestinians. Several Western countries have imposed sanctions on him for incitement against Palestinians.

United Arab List leader Mansour Abbas, who served in a short-lived governing coalition formed after the 2021 elections, said on Tuesday night that he hoped "the numbers will work out and we, the Change Bloc and the UAL, can ensure that there are 61 Knesset seats".

The leader of the left-wing Democrats party, Yair Golan, told his partners in Eisenkot's bloc that there was an "opportunity to form a change government in partnership" with the Arab parties and replace Netanyahu's coalition.

"We have no future here if we don't stop being afraid. And if we don't put an end to racism," he wrote on X.

Eisenkot has previously raised objections or attached conditions to that kind of alliance, including recognising Israel as Jewish and democratic, and Hamas as a terrorist organisation that must be destroyed. The right-wing parties in his bloc, meanwhile, have flatly rejected it.

"The opposition parties cannot dictate any conditions," Jabareen said. "If the opposition in Israel are willing to afford real and substantive change, and an alternative for the dangerous, extreme-right-wing government... they will have to negotiate with us."

Netanyahu's Likud party has accused the Arab parties of "stealing" the election.

It complained to the Central Elections Committee (CEC) on Wednesday that they had resorted to "bribery, threats, violence, fraud and the use of prohibited software to encourage voters", without providing any evidence. The CEC said it would examine the allegations as part of a comprehensive post-election review.

On Thursday, CEC chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg instructed the Shin Bet domestic security service to investigate what he described as "serious suspicions" regarding "improper influence through foreign funding by external actors operating against Israeli interests".

He gave no further details, but the Haaretz newspaper cited a source as saying the committee had been presented with a claim that the Gulf state of Qatar had provided funding aimed at increasing voter turnout in Arab communities.

"This is an attack on democracy aimed at enabling foreign control of the Knesset, the Islamization of Israel, and the removal of the right-wing government," Likud said.

But Balad chairman Sami Abu Shehadeh, who is part of the Joint List, dismissed the allegation, saying: "The losing side is constructing a racist blood libel and calling on the security agencies to use force in order to overturn the election results."

Qatar's foreign ministry spokesman, Majed al-Ansari, denied that it had interfered in Israeli elections or funded any activities intended to influence their outcome. "The accusations are ridiculous and dangerous in equal measure," he warned.

World.title: Record number of purges as Xi emphasises 'party discipline' at China political gathering
World.content:
Sixteen of the 33 members expelled are from the military, according to a communique issued on Thursday, which marked the end of the four-day closed-door gathering held at a hotel in Beijing.

It's unclear what specific charges these members face beyond "serious disciplinary and legal violations". Such broad allegations have become routine under Xi's anti-corruption campaign.

It has now become "an effort to consolidate and maintain authority", says Chong Ja Ian, a non-resident scholar with Carnegie China.

"In this case, the campaign will continue and expand depending on how secure Xi feels rather than any real issue with corruption."

In its statement, the party said it has "squarely confronted the grim reality that party leadership had at times weakened or hollowed out" and that it will continue to "enforce strict party self-governance, including turning the knife inwards to... curb disorder".

The latest expulsions bring the total number of members removed under Xi's third term to a record 51, up from 35 and five in his first and second terms respectively.

Beyond the plenum, China's top anti-corruption watchdog reported that 680,000 people across the party apparatus have been disciplined in the first nine months of this year.

This is also the first time in Xi's 14 years of leadership that plenum attendance fell below 300. The current Central Committee started its term in 2022 with more than 370 members.

Observers argue that Xi views corruption not just as graft but also ideological impurity and, crucially, disloyalty.

In January, he warned against "two-faced cadres" who profess political loyalty but defy orders and act in their self-interest.

World.title: Bandits Attack: Reps seek security, humanitarian intervention in Taraba
World.content:
The House of Representatives has called for urgent security and humanitarian interventions following a deadly bandit attack on Binnari community in Karim Lamido Local Government Area of Taraba State, which reportedly left between 57 and 60 people dead.

The lawmakers also urged the federal government to complete the abandoned Wase-Karim Lamido road project to improve security operations and enable the rapid deployment of security personnel to affected communities.

The resolutions followed a motion of urgent public importance moved by Mohammed Audu (APC, Taraba) during Thursday’s plenary.

Presenting the motion, Mr Audu said the attack occurred on 23 October when traders and residents gathered at the community market.

He said the attackers opened fire, killing 10 people at the scene, while the ensuing panic caused several people to jump into a river, bringing the reported death toll to between 57 and 60.

According to the lawmaker, the attackers allegedly came from forested areas in Plateau State, including Dutsen Zaki in Wase Local Government Area, Kukawa in Kanam Local Government Area and areas around the Yankari Game Reserve and Gwana Mountain in Alkaleri Local Government Area of Bauchi State.

He said these areas shared boundaries with communities in Karim Lamido, making improved road access and coordinated security operations necessary to prevent further attacks.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Audu described the incident as unprecedented in its scale in Karim Lamido, adding that the affected communities had suffered considerably because of the lack of access roads.

“This type of deadly attack has never taken place in Karim Lamido Local Government; the people of Karim Lamido have suffered a lot. No access road leading to all these areas,” he said.

He also reported another attack on 26 October in neighbouring Gomben Dela community, where the assailants allegedly looted food items and seized vehicles. No deaths were reported in the second incident.

The lawmaker asked the House to observe a minute of silence for those killed in Binnari and neighbouring villages.

He further urged the federal government to strengthen intelligence sharing among security agencies in Taraba, Plateau and Bauchi states to prevent a recurrence.

Mr Audu also called on the North-East Development Commission (NEDC), the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), the National Commission for Refugees, Migrants and Internally Displaced Persons and other humanitarian agencies to provide relief materials to affected communities.

He listed building materials, food, blankets, mattresses and mats among the items needed to support survivors and affected families.

The motion also commended the Taraba State Governor, security commanders and other security agencies for their response to the attack.

Lawmakers question response to recurring attacks

Contributing to the debate, the Minority Leader, Fred Agbedi, expressed concern over the recurring attacks on communities across the country, questioning whether the government was doing enough to protect lives and property.

He said the House had repeatedly been confronted with reports of killings and destruction of property, often followed by motions and minutes of silence.

“I remember that in 2016, on this same floor, I rose to say that the life of a Nigerian is just now worth a one-minute silence,” Mr Agbedi said.

He acknowledged the efforts of security personnel but argued that the scale of the attacks demanded a stronger response, particularly through the deployment of modern technology.

According to him, attackers often invade communities, carry out killings and leave before security agencies respond.

“The situation where criminals will go to a community, attack the community, and there is no response. They finish. They will leave, and then we start reacting. It’s like medicine after death,” he said.

Mr Agbedi questioned whether the country had adequately deployed technological tools to identify attackers and trace their movements.

He also raised concerns about the funding and implementation of security budgets, urging relevant House committees to move beyond resolutions and take practical steps to improve national security.

He said lawmakers serving on security-related committees had a responsibility to work closely with security agencies and ensure that the necessary measures were implemented to protect Nigerians.

Another Taraba lawmaker, Jaafaru Yakubu, said the state and neighbouring areas had experienced coordinated criminal activities, including banditry and kidnapping.

Mr Yakubu said the Binnari attack was followed by another assault in which the attackers allegedly took food items and destroyed facilities belonging to the federal government.

Kalu defends Tinubu administration’s security record

Presiding over the plenary, Deputy Speaker Benjamin Kalu acknowledged the concerns raised by Mr Agbedi but defended the federal government’s efforts to tackle insecurity.

Mr Kalu said the House’s resolutions had contributed to measures taken by the government and that the legislature should not be seen as merely holding sessions without achieving results.

He cited figures he attributed to government reports, including more than 13,000 terrorists reportedly killed in the preceding year and an 81 per cent reduction in violent deaths since 2023.

He also said more than 124,000 fighters and their family members had surrendered since 2023, while over 104,000 people had been processed through the Safe Corridor programme in collaboration with the Multinational Joint Task Force.

The deputy speaker further said the number of local government areas under insurgent control had declined from 17 in 2022 to six, citing data from 2025.

On weapons recovery, he said more than 19,000 illegal weapons had been destroyed.

Mr Kalu also highlighted an increase in security spending, saying the allocation rose from ₦2.98 trillion in 2023 to ₦3.25 trillion in 2024, ₦4.91 trillion in 2025 and ₦5.4 trillion in 2026.

He added that the government had recruited 30,000 additional police personnel and expanded electronic policing initiatives.

The deputy speaker said the figures demonstrated that the government was acting on the legislature’s interventions and that security operations were producing results.

He maintained that the minute of silence was intended to honour victims, while the government continued efforts to reduce insecurity.

“Your resolutions here, your motions here, do not end only with one minute silence. The one-minute silence is to honor those who have lost their life, but the number is shrinking by the day because the government is deliberate in making sure that the issue of insecurity is reduced, and we must give kudos to whom kudos is due. This administration has been doing tremendously well,” he said.

Motion referred to committees

The House subsequently adopted the motion through a voice vote and observed a minute of silence in honour of those killed in the attacks.

Mr Kalu referred the matter to the House Committees on the North-East Development Commission, Works and NEMA for further legislative action.

The referral to the works committee is expected to facilitate consideration of the abandoned Wase-Karim Lamido road project, which the lawmakers said would improve access for security personnel responding to emergencies.

The committees are expected to pursue the House’s resolutions on road access, emergency response and assistance to communities affected by the attacks.

World.title: FGN’s CREDICORP showcases consumer credit access for over 1,000 Abians, pilots SPARK
World.content:
The Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation (CREDICORP) concluded its CREDICORP for All – Abia State Edition beneficiary showcase at the Prime Time Event Centre, Aba, Abia State, in Nigeria’s South East, highlighting affordable credit opportunities for over 1,000 Abians. The event brought together beneficiaries, participating financial institutions, local vendors and government representatives to demonstrate how consumer credit can improve everyday livelihoods.

At the showcase, market women and traders participated in live credit-access activities, while young Nigerians engaged with YouthCred and transport operators were showcased as beneficiaries of credit-backed tricycles. Together, the activities put real people and the practical value of consumer credit at the centre of the event.

A major highlight was the pilot of SPARK, a first-of-its-kind USSD-based entry-level credit product, designed to enable Nigerians, particularly first-time borrowers, to access credit and begin building their formal credit histories. By establishing repayment records through responsible borrowing, beneficiaries can progressively improve their credit profiles and create pathways to greater financial opportunities.

The product, which simplifies credit access through basic mobile phones without requiring smartphones or internet connectivity, is expected to become more widely available to Nigerians before the end of 2026.

The showcase also featured locally assembled tricycles made available on credit through CREDICORP’s S.C.A.L.E. (Securing Consumer Access for Local Enterprises) initiative. The programme connects consumers with Nigerian manufacturers and vendors through affordable credit, supporting local production, enterprise development and job creation.

YouthCred also featured at the event, connecting eligible young Nigerians, including serving NYSC corps members, with affordable credit opportunities intended to support their financial journeys and responsible borrowing habits.

Representing the Executive Governor of Abia State, Dr Alex Otti, Mr Chinenye Mba-Uzoukwu, Chief Principal to the Governor, welcomed the initiative and highlighted the steps taken by the Abia State Government to create an environment in which responsible consumer credit and enterprise can thrive.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Under Governor Alex Otti’s leadership, Abia State is putting the conditions in place for businesses to grow, investments to flourish and responsible credit to reach more of our people. By strengthening the enabling environment for enterprise, we are making it easier for initiatives such as CREDICORP to support traders, young people and hardworking families across the state.”

The Managing Director of MOFI and Board Member, CREDICORP, Dr Armstrong Ume Takang, described the showcase as an example of translating Federal Government policy into practical economic opportunities for Nigerians.

“The Federal Government’s consumer credit initiative reflects President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s commitment to building an economy where more Nigerians can access the tools and opportunities needed to improve their lives. Through CREDICORP, we are seeing how well-structured public investment can stimulate enterprise, support local manufacturers and deliver measurable economic impact directly to citizens.”

Speaking on CREDICORP’s expanding national footprint, Managing Director/CEO Uzoma Nwagba emphasised that the Corporation’s mission is to take consumer credit beyond financial institutions and into the hands of everyday Nigerians.

“Consumer credit should not be a privilege reserved for a few. It should be an opportunity available to every working Nigerian. Today in Aba, Abia State, in Nigeria’s South East, we are demonstrating what that means in practical terms: credit for market women, a financial head start for young people, productive assets for transport operators, and with SPARK, asimple way for Nigerians to begin building their credit histories. This is how we make credit work for the people.”

The Abia showcase builds on CREDICORP’s engagements across Lagos, Abuja, Ondo, Osun, Ogun, Rivers and Adamawa, reflecting the Corporation’s growing nationwide reach.

Since commencing operations, CREDICORP has enabled over ₦53.5 billion in consumer credit for more than 351,000 Nigerians, with women representing approximately 59 percent of beneficiaries.

Established under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’sadministration, CREDICORP is advancing the Federal Government’s objective of expanding consumer credit access to at least 50 percent of working Nigerians by 2030.

From market women accessing credit to young Nigerians beginning their financial journeys, and transport operators acquiring income-generating assets, the Abia showcase demonstrated how consumer credit can move beyond policy into practical opportunities that improve everyday lives.

CREDICORP for All. Credit for Every Nigerian.

For more information, visit here.

World.title: Kaduna deputy gov swears in three commissioners, 18 special advisers
World.content:
The Deputy Governor of Kaduna State, Dr Hadiza Balarabe, has counseled political appointees to serve the administration faithfully and act without fear or favor. She reminded them of the import of taking the Oath of Allegiance and Oath of Office, as prescribed by the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution.

Balarabe made this known after swearing-in three Commissioners, the Deputy Chief of Staff Administration and Counselor of Infrastructure, as well as 18 Special Advisers on Thursday.

According to her, the oath of allegiance and oath of office are not mere words because ‘’they bind you before God and the people of Kaduna State, to serve faithfully.’’

She said the administration of oath is a moment of trust, a call to service, and a solemn reminder that leadership is not a privilege to be enjoyed, but a responsibility to be carried with humility, integrity, courage, and an unwavering commitment to the people.

‘’Your appointments reflect the confidence His Excellency has placed in your abilities, experience, judgment, and capacity to contribute meaningfully to the development of our dear state,’’ she added.

The deputy governor urged the appointees ‘’to receive this confidence not merely as recognition of your past achievements, but as a challenge to accomplish even greater things in the service of our people.’’

Justifying the timing of the appointments in the middle of an election season, she maintained that ‘’elections have their calendar, but the needs of our people do not wait for it.’’

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to her, Governor Uba Sani is focused on delivering on his promises to the people of Kaduna State, irrespective of party or ethno-religious affiliations.

The governor’s objective is to build a peaceful, prosperous, inclusive Kaduna State where no community is left behind, she stated.

‘’Since May 2023, Kaduna State has been steadily transformed. Communities once divided by conflict are reconciling under the Kaduna Peace Model; farmlands are reopening and markets are alive.

‘’More than 500 schools closed by insecurity have been reopened, and over 300,000 out-of-school children returned to class in 2025 alone, ‘’ she added.

Balarabe further said that hundreds of classrooms have been built while more have been renovated, and tens of thousands of teachers trained.

In the health sector, she said that 255 primary healthcare centres have been upgraded to level two, adding that ‘’our general hospitals are being improved.’’

Balarabe further said that about 160 road projects, covering some 1,335 kilometres, are opening up all 23 local government areas and that “the light rail and bus rapid transit projects point to the Kaduna of tomorrow.’’

She enjoined the newly sworn in appointees to go to their various duty posts and be the bridge between the government and the grassroots.

‘’Let your performance be the argument that convinces the skeptical and the proof that justifies the trust of the supportive,” she stressed.

The three commissioners that were sworn in are Hon Benjamin Dalhat Solomon Kure(Sports Development), Hon Amina Akilu Dalhat (Special Duties I) and Abdullahi Garba Abbas (Special Duties II) as well as 18 special advisers.

At the same event, Dr Haliru Musa Soba and Balarabe Muhammad Bello were sworn in as Deputy Chief of Staff(Administration) and Counsellor Infrastructure respectively.

World.title: How I paid money into ex-CCT chairman’s wife’s account, covered his children’s school fees – Contractor
World.content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) opened its corruption case against former Code of Conduct Tribunal (CCT) chairman Danladi Umar with its first prosecuton witness at the FCT High Court in Abuja on Thursday.

Oluwatayo Solomon, owner of JTF Global Links Limited and Portal Realities, testified on he bankrolled Mr Umar’s children’s school fees at the Baze University in Abuja and transferred money into his wife’s account after the CCT paid him for the contract awarded to him.

He said he received a call to pay N6 million into the bank account of Zulaihatu Umar, Mr Umar’s wife, barely two days after he was paid by the tribunal.

According to the witness, a deputy director at the CCT at the time, Akinola Akonju, called him concerning the “request” and forwarded the account details to which the payment would be made.

“Mrs Umar also called me about the payment. The money was paid from the Portal Realities Limited Wema Bank account into her account,” the witness said.

On 9 July, the EFCC arraigned Mr Umar before the FCT High Court in Abuja on charges of receiving gratification involving about N15.6 million from CCT’s contractors between 2021 and 2024.

Mr Umar, whose tenure spanned July 2011 to November 2024, allegedly received financial inducements from contractors via deposits into his wife’s bank account and through the settlement of his children’s school fees at Baze University, Abuja.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The anti-corruption agency alleged that Kurchmives International Limited, a subcontractor under the contract awarded by the CCT to Momanaf Global Ventures Limited for the painting of the tribunal’s headquarters, sent N5 million to his wife, Zulaihatu Umar’s Zenith Bank account on 5 October 2021.

It also alleged that Portal Realities Limited, a sister company of JTF Global Links Limited, a company awarded the contract for the digitalisation of CCT’s management records, sent N6 million to Mrs Umar’s account on 25 January 2024.

The prosecution also stated in the charges that Portal Realities Limited paid over N4 million for Mr Umar’s children, Faiza and Yakubu, at Baze University.

These transactions, according to the prosecution, constituted acts of corruption, involving a public officer using his office or position to gratify or confer any corrupt or unfair advantage upon himself or any relation or associate criminalised under section 19 of the Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act, 2000.

‘How I paid ex-CCT chair’s children’s school fees’

Mr Solomon, the first prosecution witness, explained how he made payments for the school fees of Mr Umar’s children.

The witness said Mr Akonju called him in October 2021 that Mr Umar asked that he be informed to pay the school fees of two of his children in Baze University, Abuja.

“I paid about N2 million for Yakubu Umar Danladi from the Portal Realities Limited account in Jaiz Bank to Baze University. I also paid school fees on behalf of Faiza Umar Danladi,” from the same account.

Led in evidence by EFCC’s lawyer Christopher Mshelia, the witness presented the documents regarding the contract awarded by the CCT, chaired at the time by Mr Umar, to his company, JTF Global Links Limited.

Cross-examination

Under cross-examination by defence lawyer Edward Sunday, Mr Solomon confirmed that he had known Mr Umar for more than ten years.

He also acknowledged that he knew Mr Umar’s wife and children and could be considered as family friends.

Responding to the defence lawyer’s suggestion that the N6 million paid into Mrs Umar’s account could be considered a loan, Mr Solomon said, “There was no reason to give her a loan because I did not have that discussion with her.”

He also confirmed that he did not disclose.

He acknowledged a transfer of N3 million from Mrs Umar into his business account with Zenith Bank on 16 February 2024 but confirmed the transaction was omitted from his statement to the EFCC.

On how he was asked to pay for Mr Umar’s school fees, Mr Solomon said he received the directive from Mr Akonji, the CCT official, but never cross-checked with Mr Umar.

“Based on the relationship I have with him and the beneficiaries sent to me are the people I am familiar with,” the prosecution witness said.

He also disclosed that Portal Realities Limited, through which he paid the fees, was not awarded any contract by the CCT.

Witness answers questions on relationship with Umar, qualification

Earlier, Mr Solomon told the court that CCT awarded a contract to JTF Global Links Limited on 22 September 2021, after submitting the company’s profile to the tribunal.

Responding to the defence lawyer’s suggestion under cross-examination that he asked to be awarded the contract, Mr Solomon said, “Based on my relationship with Mr Umar, he asked me to meet Mr Akonji, whom I submitted my company profile to. Mr Akonji called me on the 18th (no month stated) to come for a financial bid.”

The witness, who said he is registered and has all the necessary documents “for bidding according to the laws of Nigeria,” maintained that the documents he submitted for the CCT contract confirmed that “I am qualified to be awarded the contract,” pushing back a suggestion that he won the contract based on his relationship with Mr Umar.

He said he could not list other entities who bidded for the contract because, according to him, he was “not part of the tenders board.”

He also told the court that Mr Akonji served as the current procurement director for the CCT.

The witness said, before the CCT contract, he had executed contracts for the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), the Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission (RMAFC), and Katsina State Government.

Defence lawyer, who described some of Mr Solomon’s claims as an afterthought, sought to confront him with his extrajudicial statement.

But he could not proceed with that line of cross-examination after it was realised that there was no certified true copy of the witness’ extrajudicial statement in court.

The judge, Peter Kekemeke, then adjourned the matter until 20 January 2027 for the prosecution to furnish the defence with the certified true copy of the statement.

Section 19 of the Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act, 2000, under which Mr Umar was charged criminalises the act of public officers who use their office to confer undue advantage on themselves, friends or family.

The offence attracts seven years’ imprisonment upon conviction.

But Mr Umar denied all the allegations.

World.title: Nigeria reviews national security strategy to address terrorism, cyber threats, misinformation
World.content:
The Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) has inaugurated a committee to review Nigeria’s National Security Strategy (NSS) 2019 and develop a new framework to address emerging security threats, including terrorism, banditry, kidnapping, misinformation, and cybercrime, among others.

The 33-member committee is chaired by Sarkin Bello, a retired Nigerian Army major general, who is deputised by Emeka Onumajuru, also a retired major general.

The National Security Adviser (NSA), Nuhu Ribadu, inaugurated the committee on Thursday, 29th October. The committee is expected to submit its final draft of the NSS 2026 to the NSA by 27 November.

Represented by the committee’s chairperson, Mr Ribadu said the review was necessary because Nigeria’s domestic, regional and global security environments had changed significantly since 2019.

He added that the new strategy would serve as an overarching framework for coordinating national security, resilience and sustainable development.

The NSA said the strategy must reflect current realities, anticipate future disruptions and support the government’s national objectives under President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, particularly in human security, economic transformation and national cohesion.

“Nigeria demands a strategy that is realistic and implementable,” he said, urging committee members to work with resource institutions and relevant stakeholders to produce a comprehensive and actionable document.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He assured the committee that ONSA would provide the administrative, technical and logistical support required to complete the assignment.

Mr Onumajuru said the country’s changing security environment required a thorough reassessment of its strategic priorities.

He said conventional security threats, including terrorism, insurgency and banditry, had become intertwined with non-kinetic challenges such as cyber threats, economic instability, food insecurity and climate change.

“The National Security Strategy 2026 must be an inclusive, forward-looking and highly actionable blueprint,” he said.

Mr Onumajuru said the committee would work with its secretariat and consult resource institutions, private-sector leaders and traditional rulers to develop a comprehensive strategy.

He said the committee’s composition, which includes representatives of the armed forces, intelligence agencies, government ministries, civil society and academia, would help ensure a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach to national security.

He urged members to begin work immediately, stressing the need for rigorous analysis, professional integrity and constructive engagement to meet the submission deadline.

“Together, we will deliver a strategy that firmly safeguards the sovereignty, unity and future prosperity of the Federal Republic of Nigeria,” he said.

World.title: AGFUND to expand development initiatives in Africa, seeks Nigerian partners — Saudi Prince
World.content:
The Chairman of Arab Gulf Programme for Development (AGFUND), Prince Abdulaziz bin Talal bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, says the fund is seeking partnerships with governments, local organisations and non-governmental organisations (NGOs) to expand its development initiatives across Africa, including Nigeria.

The Saudi Arabia Prince made the remarks on Wednesday during a press conference with journalists in Armenia.
