When PREMIUM TIMES asked what specific investments or programmes is AGFUND willing to prioritise in Nigeria to support young entrepreneurs, smallholder farmers and community-led development, and how can Nigeria access this support, the Saudi Arabian Prince said the organisation is looking to work with local partners to identify development challenges in different African countries and develop solutions tailored to their needs.

The AGFUND Chairman also disclosed the organisation’s development priorities, including efforts to tackle unemployment by supporting small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), entrepreneurs and financial inclusion initiatives.

Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country, continues to grapple with the unemployment challenge, amid government efforts to create sufficient employment opportunities for its growing population, particularly young people entering the labour market to address the soaring rate of young talents leaving the country, which is commonly known as “japa” in the Nigerian parlance.

According to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), Nigeria’s official unemployment rate is pegged within the range of 4.3 to 4.9 per cent. Although under the older NBS methodology used prior to 2023, the reported unemployment rate was much higher, it was about 33.3 per cent in late 2020. A vast majority of the Nigerian workforce operates in the informal sector, with the informal employment rate estimated at roughly 92.8 per cent.

On Wednesday, a Nigerian climate technology and agritech startup, D-Olivette Labs, emerged as one of four winners of the 2025 Prince Talal International Prize for Human Development, receiving $200,000 for its clean-energy innovation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Addressing unemployment

In his response to PREMIUM TIMES reporter’s question, Prince Abdulaziz bin Talal bin Abdulaziz Al Saud explained that the organisation is seeking to help address unemployment by supporting entrepreneurs rather than relying on governments to absorb an increasing number of graduates into public-sector employment.

“When we talk about unemployment, you know, most of these countries, some of them are our countries as well, whoever graduates is always looking for a government position,” the representative said.

“Government position, they would say it’s much safer, it’s much secure, etc., but we want to stay away from these government positions because government will reach a day where they don’t have any more positions for new employees.”

The representative said AGFUND was exploring ways to help small businesses and entrepreneurs grow, including through financial inclusion banks that provide microloans and share knowledge with beneficiaries.

“So, I think our part of what we’re doing is we’re trying to help SMEs. We’re trying to help entrepreneurs,” the representative said.

The initiative, the representative explained, is intended to help low-income individuals establish businesses, expand their activities and eventually employ other people.

“So, these poor people, whoever they are, wherever they are, tomorrow they will become employers. They will have employees. And this is the effect that we want,” the representative said.

Microfinance and local partnerships

The AGFUND Chair said its approach builds on a mission that began in 2006–2007 and is now being expanded further into Africa.

The organisation’s representative said AGFUND was established to support development initiatives that other funding institutions might not prioritise.

The prince cited the organisation’s work on financial inclusion and microfinance banks, linked to the late Prince Talal, the founder of AGFUND, and Professor Muhammad Yunus of Bangladesh’s Grameen Bank.

He said the organisation was now seeking partnerships with government institutions and NGOs to identify specific needs and develop interventions that could help communities become economically self-reliant.

According to the him, expanding these initiatives would require an understanding of the differences in culture, regulations and development priorities across African countries.

The representative also cautioned against focusing exclusively on large-scale projects, arguing that smaller pilot initiatives could provide a more practical route to sustainable development.

“Sometimes we’re looking for the big projects, the mega-projects, the giga-projects. How many projects we’ve seen in the region have not succeeded? How many projects we’ve seen in Africa, for example, they have not succeeded?” the representative said.

“The aspirations are very big and the dreams are very big, but sometimes you need a pilot project.”

The representative said AGFUND tests initiatives on a smaller scale before expanding successful projects, with adjustments to reflect the circumstances of different regions.

Africa’s development challenges

Additionally, Prince Abdulaziz also highlighted the varying economic and social challenges confronting African countries, including instability, economic difficulties and declining global funding for development.

The representative said these challenges made it necessary for African countries to build on existing institutions and development platforms rather than continually creating new ones.

Referring to the African Union’s Agenda 2063, the representative said the continent was entering a new phase of its long-term development vision and needed to align existing efforts to address persistent problems such as unemployment.

“How can we align ourselves with whatever already exists? Why do we need to always create new platforms, find new solutions? No, the solutions are there. The platforms are there,” the representative said.

“All we need to do is just realign to stop having unemployment, if we can.”

AGFUND’s proposed expansion could create opportunities for Nigerian development organisations, government agencies and NGOs to explore partnerships aimed at improving access to finance and supporting entrepreneurship.

However, the organisation did not specify the amount of funding it plans to commit to Nigeria, the number of beneficiaries it expects to reach or a timeline for implementing new initiatives in the country.

World.title: Enugu govt, Humatrix partner to create 100,000 jobs through BPO
World.content:
The Enugu State Government and Humatrix Limited have signed a partnership agreement to establish a Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) hub in the state. The long-term target is to create over 100,000 jobs for young people and positioning Enugu as a leading destination for digital services in Nigeria and Africa.

The agreement, signed at Government House, Enugu, marks the implementation phase of the initiative, which aligns with Governor Peter Mbah’s economic diversification agenda, human capital development policy and drive to attract private investment.

Speaking at the ceremony, Director of Humatrix Limited, Dr Dakuku Peterside, said the company chose Enugu after assessing its investment climate, policy consistency and the state government’s commitment to economic transformation.

He said, “It was very easy for us to choose Enugu. Enugu is investing, and there is consistency. Most importantly, we have a supportive environment. These are core things any business would request to scale.”

Peterside disclosed that the company would commence operations with a 750-seat BPO centre, expand to over 2,000 seats within the first year and target 100,000 jobs within five years.

He explained that the initiative would go beyond direct employment by equipping young people with industry-relevant digital and technological skills, connecting them to employment opportunities and attracting global companies seeking skilled talent.

According to him, the state government had already provided a building for the take-off of the project, while recruitment and training opportunities would be opened to interested Enugu youths.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Peterside commended the government’s rigorous negotiation process, describing the diligence and thoroughness demonstrated by its multi-agency team as evidence of the seriousness with which Enugu approaches investment partnerships.

Also speaking, the Special Adviser to the Governor on MSME and Digital Economy, Mr Arinze Chilo-Offiah, said the partnership represented a significant step towards actualising the governor’s vision of growing Enugu’s economy from $4.4 billion to $30 billion.

He explained that the Enugu Talent City Initiative was designed to position the state as a leading digital services and outsourcing hub in Nigeria and Africa, attracting global companies, creating employment and enabling young people to work for international clients from Enugu.

The special adviser further disclosed that the state’s long-term ambition was to develop an outsourcing ecosystem with up to 300,000 seats by 2031, building on the initial 750-seat BPO centre and expanding opportunities for digitally skilled youths.

In his remarks, Governor Mbah said the partnership was consistent with his administration’s commitment to ensuring that young people could acquire relevant skills, secure rewarding employment and build their futures in Enugu rather than leave the state in search of opportunities.

The Governor disclosed that over 33 per cent of the state’s expenditure was dedicated to human capital development, reflecting his administration’s emphasis on education, skills acquisition and workforce preparation.

He stressed that developing talent must go hand in hand with attracting companies capable of employing that talent, noting that private capital would be critical to achieving the state’s economic growth ambitions.

Mbah also reiterated his administration’s ambition to scale the digital economy through the proposed Talent City and Digital Industrial Park, expressing confidence that the infrastructure could support growth beyond the 100,000-job target set by Humatrix.

“We want the ‘japa’ where we can stay in Enugu and serve companies across the world, anywhere in the world,” the Governor said, describing the initiative as an opportunity for young people to earn globally competitive incomes while living in their home state.

He also signals the administration’s determination to connect investments in education with industries that can translate knowledge and skills into productive employment.

World.title: Nigeria’s Excise Stamp Policy: Setback for tax reform? By James Z Mayokun
World.content:
Nigeria’s tax reform programme was built around an important economic imperative: create a more coherent tax administration system, improve compliance, strengthen public revenue and make it easier for businesses to operate within the law. However, the introduction of the Nigeria Customs Service’s Excise Stamp Regulations, 2026, raises a difficult question about whether government agencies are working towards the same objective or inadvertently recreating the administrative complexity that reform is intended to remove.

The regulations, which took effect on 20 January 2026, establish a framework for physical or electronic authentication stamps and the tracking of excisable products, including alcohol, tobacco and sugar-sweetened beverages. Its stated objectives include improving product traceability, curbing counterfeiting, strengthening accountability and reducing revenue leakage. While these are legitimate responsibilities of the state, the desirability of an objective does not automatically validate every mechanism selected to achieve it.

The critical question is whether the new regime delivers additional enforcement benefits that justify its financial and operational costs. Until the government can demonstrate that value, imposing the system across affected industries risks undermining the broader objectives of tax reform. The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN) has already raised concerns about the proposed stamp system, warning that it could impose what its Director-General, Segun Ajayi-Kadir, described as a hidden compliance tax on industry.

The association argued that the additional burden could erode the gains of the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, create production bottlenecks and disproportionately affect smaller manufacturers. It urged the government to improve existing digital infrastructure instead of introducing another compliance layer. The objection deserves more than a routine dismissal as resistance to regulation. Businesses must comply with applicable laws and pay legitimate taxes. But they are also entitled to expect that regulations will be proportionate, predictable and designed with a clear understanding of their cumulative effects.

A mandatory compliance process can impose costs even when it is not formally classified as a tax. Manufacturers may need additional equipment, technology integration, staff training, product-handling procedures and administrative capacity. Where the process interferes with production-line operations, costs may extend to downtime, inventory management and distribution.

These expenses matter because manufacturers do not operate in isolation from the rest of the economy. They must manage energy, transport, financing, raw-material and labour costs. Every additional obligation competes with other uses of scarce capital, including investment in equipment, expansion, productivity and employment.

The government must therefore distinguish between a charge that produces measurable public value and an expense that merely adds another layer to an already demanding compliance environment.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

What does the law actually say?

The Nigeria Tax Act 2025 includes provisions on stamp duties for dutiable instruments and recognises methods such as tax stamps, electronic or digital tagging and electronic receipts. The regulations cite the Nigeria Customs Service Act 2023 as its enabling authority. A definitive conclusion about legal inconsistency would require a detailed examination of the relevant statutes, regulations and the scope of the Customs Service’s powers.

That qualification does not weaken the economic case for reviewing the policy. A regulation can be legally authorised and still be poorly designed, unnecessarily expensive or inconsistent with the wider direction of government policy. The issue is whether the stamp regime advances the tax system’s overall efficiency. If one agency seeks to simplify compliance while another introduces requirements that overlap with existing reporting infrastructure, the government must explain how the different measures fit together.

Policy coherence is especially important when the federal government is asking businesses to adjust to major fiscal changes. Investors need confidence that regulatory requirements will not multiply unpredictably and that government agencies will coordinate their systems rather than impose separate demands on the same companies.

The government already has a starting point for improving excise administration. In September 2025, the Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation reported that the Customs Service completed the pilot phase of its Automated Excise Register System (ERS), with live operations commencing at three facilities: British American Tobacco Nigeria in Oyo State, International Tobacco Company in Kwara State and Leaf Tobacco & Commodities Nigeria in Kaduna State.

The report said the system was designed to record production figures, compute excise duties and generate statutory reports, reducing reliance on manual documentation. It also reported a 75 per cent efficiency score during user acceptance testing at British American Tobacco Nigeria. That figure relates to the reported testing exercise; it should not be interpreted as proof that the system can perform every product-authentication function contemplated by the later stamp regulations.

The ERS and e-invoicing may not perform identical functions to a product-level stamp. That is precisely why a technical audit is needed. The authorities should compare the capabilities of the existing systems against the functions required under the new regime, identify any genuine gaps and estimate the cost of closing them.

If the problem is poor data exchange, the solution may be interoperability. If the problem is inadequate inspections, it may be better risk profiling and enforcement. If the problem is counterfeit products entering the market, targeted authentication and intelligence-led operations may be more appropriate than a blanket requirement that affects all compliant producers. Introducing another system without first answering these questions risks confusing administrative activity with actual improvement.

The hidden economic cost

The stamp regime may also place a disproportionate burden on small and medium-sized industries. Large manufacturers generally have greater capacity to invest in equipment, technology and specialised compliance teams. Smaller firms may have limited capital and narrower margins, making fixed implementation expenses more difficult to absorb.

The resulting pressure could affect investment, hiring and production decisions. Manufacturers may absorb some costs, pass some to customers or reduce other expenditure. The precise effect will vary, but government should not assume that mandatory compliance is economically neutral.

Nor should it assume that higher compliance costs necessarily produce higher net revenue. If firms reduce output or consumers switch towards untaxed products, the government could collect more from one mechanism while losing revenue elsewhere. Only a transparent assessment can establish the likely net effect. The government should measure additional revenue against implementation costs, changes in formal production, compliance expenditure, enforcement outcomes and possible shifts in consumer demand. Without that evidence, claims of fiscal benefit remain incomplete.

Nigeria should not abandon the fight against illicit trade. It should make that fight more effective. But it must not confuse the need for stronger enforcement with the necessity of one particular technology or administrative arrangement. The government should suspend implementation of the hybrid excise stamp regime pending an independent technical, legal and economic review. That review should establish the system’s additional value, assess its compatibility with existing platforms, quantify the burden on businesses of different sizes and recommend the least costly effective alternative.

The Customs Service should also publish measurable objectives and a transparent framework for evaluating any future system. Where a physical component is genuinely necessary, its use should be justified by evidence and limited to circumstances in which it delivers a clear advantage.

Nigeria’s tax reforms should not be weakened by regulatory duplication. The government must demonstrate that the excise stamp regime improves enforcement sufficiently to justify its costs. Until it does, suspension is the prudent course. Tax administration should make compliance simpler, revenue collection more effective and industry more competitive—not leave businesses wondering whether one reform will be undone by another obligation.

World.title: 2027: David Mark urges ECOWAS to warn FG, INEC against poll crisis
World.content:
David Mark

By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – The National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Senator David Mark, has urged the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) to warn the Federal Government and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) against actions that could trigger a crisis over the 2027 general elections.

Mark made the appeal in Abuja on Thursday when he received an ECOWAS delegation on a pre-election fact-finding mission, stressing that the credibility of Nigeria’s elections was critical to peace and stability across West Africa.

According to a statement by the ADC National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the party said it had raised concerns over INEC’s preparedness, alleged government control of state institutions, including the judiciary, and threats of violence it attributed to the ruling party.

Mark said credible elections were essential to preventing electoral conflict.

“The best way to prevent conflict, especially in relation to elections, is to ensure that it is free, fair and transparent,” he was quoted as saying.

He urged ECOWAS to join the ADC in pressing Nigerian authorities to ensure a credible electoral process.

Mark said, “We in the ADC have committed ourselves to the highest standards of peaceful conducts before, during and after the elections. But we need ECOWAS to join us in insisting on a credible election now.

“This is why you must tell the Federal Government and the INEC that they must not do anything that could plunge Nigeria into needless crisis. This must form a part of your early warning signals.”

The Head of Mission and former Vice-President of Sierra Leone, Mr Victor Bockarie Foh, said the delegation would report the ADC’s concerns, alongside those of other stakeholders, to the regional body.

Foh said the mission was assessing Nigeria’s preparedness for the elections and the political atmosphere ahead of the polls, stressing that peace and stability in Nigeria were important to the entire West African region.

Other members of the delegation included Francess Piage Alghali, ECOWAS Commissioner for Political Affairs, Peace and Security; Julius Fofanah Sandy, representing the ECOWAS Permanent Representatives’ Committee; and Segrine Mamadou, Head of the Electoral Assistance Division.

World.title: Billing disputes: LASCOPA recovers N26.2m refund for Ikeja Electric customers
World.content:
.Resolves 528 cases

By Olasunkanmi Akoni

Lagos State Consumer Protection Agency (LASCOPA) has resolved 528 complaints against Ikeja Electric Distribution Company (IKEDC) and secured credit adjustments and refunds totalling N26,243,758.75 for affected consumers between January and September 2026.

The General Manager, LASCOPA Afolabi Solebo, Esq., revealed this on Thursday.

Solebo explained that 556 complaints were received against Ikeja Electric during the nine months, with 528 resolved and 28 ongoing, representing about a 95 per cent resolution rate.

He reaffirmed the agency’s commitment to promoting fairness, accountability, transparency and improved service delivery in the electricity distribution sector.

According to Solebo, the agency facilitated refunds and credit adjustments worth N26.2m, underscoring the importance of regulatory intervention and mediation in securing redress for consumers.

Head of Complaints and Mediation Department, Mr Yusuf Musiliu, said the agency receives and analyses complaints through online and offline channels, while stakeholders’ parley provides a platform for Ikeja Electric officials and affected consumers to discuss grievances and reach amicable resolution.

Musiliu therefore urged aggrieved consumers to follow established procedures rather than resorting to self-help, advising them to submit relevant documents, including electricity bills, payment receipts and other evidence when filing complaints for timely investigation.

He disclosed that LASCOPA’s stakeholders’ parley with Ikeja Electric holds on the last Thursday of every month, providing a regular platform for consumers to present unresolved complaints and engage directly with the distribution company.

Musiliu encouraged consumers to promptly report billing disputes, estimated billing, overbilling, electricity supply issues and other unfair practices.

The agency reiterated its commitment to protecting consumers and promoting accountability in line with Lagos State Consumer Protection Law 2025 (as amended), urging residents to contact the agency through the toll-free helpline 080 0005 2726 on weekdays or email [email protected] to report complaints.

World.title: Borno community to Tinubu, Zulum: Bring our 78 children home
World.content:
By Luminous Jannamike & Kehinde Folarin

ABUJA – The Margi community in Borno State has urged President Bola Tinubu and Governor Babagana Zulum to intensify efforts to rescue 78 schoolchildren and a teacher abducted from Mussa and Lassa communities in Askira/Uba Local Government Area.

The community said the victims’ continued captivity had plunged their families into anguish, urging the authorities to step up rescue efforts and provide regular updates on their whereabouts.

Briefing journalists in Abuja on Thursday, the community’s Secretary, Malla Gadzama, said 43 pupils were abducted from Mussa on May 15, 2026, while 35 students and a teacher were taken from a secondary school in Lassa on June 26 as they prepared for national examinations.

“Our message is simple and clear: our children must not be forgotten,” Gadzama said.

He called on Tinubu to mobilise the necessary security and intelligence resources and ensure effective coordination among security agencies.

“Mr President, these children are Nigerians. Their lives matter,” he added.

Gadzama also urged Zulum to make the rescue a priority and establish a reliable channel for keeping affected families informed without compromising security operations.

“Development must also be measured by the safety of our children and the well-being of their families. Infrastructure cannot compensate for the continuing anguish of parents whose children remain in captivity,” he said.

The community appealed to Senator Ali Ndume and other elected representatives from Askira/Uba to use their positions to sustain pressure on the authorities. It also called for better security around vulnerable schools and medical, psychological and educational support for the victims upon their return.

Citing Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Constitution, which identifies the security and welfare of the people as the primary purpose of government, Gadzama said the authorities must fulfil their constitutional responsibility.

“We are not asking for favour from government. We are just asking the government to fulfil its primary responsibility to the people,” he said.

The community urged Tinubu, Zulum and security agencies to sustain rescue efforts until the children and their teacher were safely reunited with their families.

“Bring Mussa schoolchildren, Lassa schoolchildren and their teachers safely home. That is our demand,” Gadzama said.

World.title: ‘No country developed in less than 30 years’, Kashifu defends Tinubu
World.content:
.As TMS unveils new platform

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: Director General of the National Information Technology Development Agency NITDA, Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi, has defended the reforms of President Bola Tinubu, saying no country has developed in less than 30 years.

Kashifu, who is also Chairman, Board of Trustees and National Coordinator of the Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation (TMS), spoke on Thursday in Abuja at the group’s inaugural training workshop.

“No country in the world developed in less than 30 years. The fastest developed country is South Korea. It took 30 years. To develop, you need the right policies first. That is the foundation Mr President is laying. Then you build on it to get investors,” he said.

The programme, themed ‘Empowering Every Nigerian to be Heard’, also saw the Movement launch its official website, http://tmsnigeria.ng, where citizens can engage and verify information.

The event was convened to educate citizens on the Renewed Hope Agenda and to give Nigerians a platform to contribute ideas on how to move the country forward.

Kashifu said the thrust of the reforms is a change in what government spends its money on.

“We spend most of our resources trying to subsidise consumption. When President Bola Ahmed Tinubu came on board, he looked at it: Is it consumption we should subsidise, or production, innovation, and investment? That is what the reforms are all about,” he said.

According to him, the President built the Renewed Hope Agenda around eight priority areas. They are reforming the economy for sustained growth; strengthening national security; boosting agriculture for food security; unlocking energy and natural resources; enhancing infrastructure and transportation; focusing on health, education and social investment; accelerating diversification through industrialisation, digitalisation and creative industry; and improving governance through efficient service delivery.

The NITDA chief pointed to the integration of digital skills into formal education, the introduction of Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) by the Ministry of Education, and the Student Loan scheme, which he said ensures no Nigerian is left behind because of economic circumstances.

He added that NITDA is promoting digital literacy through Digital Literacy for All, the training of over 19,000 National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) champions in markets and motor parks, and the Three Million Tech Talent programme, which prepares young Nigerians to work remotely for global companies.

Kashifu said the reforms are already attracting investors, citing the Dangote Refinery, a $1 billion data centre investment by a South African firm announced this week, and JP Morgan’s decision to open operations in Nigeria.

“Reform is a journey; it is not a one-off event. The essence of this movement is to enlighten Nigerians on these reforms, so that Nigerians can understand what is in it for them. You are the ultimate beneficiary,” he said.

He urged participants at the roundtable to propose ideas on how to sustain the reforms and to state what government needs to do more, including inputs for the approved National Youth Conference.

A member of the TMS Board of Trustees, Olujonwo Obasanjo, said the Movement was set up to close the information gap between government and citizens and to showcase progress being recorded through projects across the country.

He described the creation of regional development commissions by President Tinubu, and his commitment to local government autonomy affirmed by the Supreme Court, as deliberate steps to fast-track inclusive development and bring governance closer to the people.

“Nigeria’s development challenge has never been lack of ideas, but policy discontinuity. There is the need for sustained, uninterrupted reforms to consolidate gains, drive economic growth and ensure that ongoing investments translate into lasting prosperity,” Obasanjo stated.

The Director-General of TMS, Marcel Ngogbehei, said the workshop was conceived to empower and educate ordinary Nigerians and give them a credible platform to be heard on national issues.

He explained that the training combined civic education with practical engagement, including role-play sessions in which participants set public expectations of governance against what the Tinubu administration is already implementing.

Ngogbehei acknowledged that reforms come with initial pains, but maintained that continuity is critical to attracting long-term investment and ensuring the benefits eventually reach every household.

He urged Nigerians to move beyond rhetoric and demand substance from political actors. “Instead of following rhetoric, we should encourage Nigerians to ask the opposition a simple question: What alternative are you offering that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is not already doing?” he said.

World.title: 2027: Tinubu’s daughter mobilises market women, launches Iyaloja movement
World.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu’s daughter and Iyaloja-General of Nigeria, Dr Mujidat Folasade Tinubu-Ojo, has launched the Iyaloja General Movement (IGM) to mobilise market women and other grassroots voters for her father’s re-election in 2027.

The movement, inaugurated on Thursday at Eagle Square, Abuja, comprises mainly market women from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, with structures reportedly established across the country’s 774 local government areas and various electoral wards.

The group pledged to mobilise 10 million votes for Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general election.

Speaking at the inauguration, Tinubu-Ojo said the movement would sensitise market leaders, traders and members of the informal sector about the forthcoming elections and encourage them to support candidates they consider capable of providing effective leadership.

She said the group had coordinators and other officials at the state, local government and ward levels to drive its mobilisation efforts.

According to her, market women and other informal-sector operators constitute an important voting bloc because of their presence in communities across the country.

“What we are putting together as market leaders is to encourage our people and sensitise them on the next election — on which direction they should follow — so that they will not derail. And to inaugurate my own movement, the Iyaloja General Movement,” she said.

Tinubu-Ojo urged voters to consider the direction of the country under the current administration, warning against electing candidates whose policies, in her view, could reverse the gains she attributed to the Tinubu administration.

She expressed support for the President’s economic policies, acknowledging that they had imposed hardships on Nigerians but arguing that the expected long-term benefits justified the difficulties.

“President Tinubu has done well. He has policies that will enhance the country and make our country boom again. We know what he has been doing,” she said.

“What he is doing right now is like a pregnant woman going through labour. We are labouring now. Almost all Nigerians are feeling what he is doing now. The policies are painful, but the end result will justify the means.”

The Iyaloja-General also defended the removal of the petrol subsidy, saying the additional revenue available to the three tiers of government had helped them execute projects and meet financial obligations, including the payment of workers’ salaries.

She urged voters not to support a candidate who had promised to restore the subsidy, arguing that the revenue generated following its removal had enabled governments to undertake infrastructure projects.

“We don’t want any person who will drive us back. If we vote somebody else now, that person will come with his own ideas. Somebody has said he is going to return the fuel subsidy, and we can see the impact of the fuel subsidy removal in the states,” she said.

“We can see what the three tiers of government are doing. Workers are getting their salaries paid on time, and infrastructure is in place.”

Tinubu-Ojo said the movement would work to sustain support for the President by engaging market associations and grassroots communities ahead of the election.

World.title: ICPC arraigns PFIPC’s Adeyemi afresh on 22 counts
World.content:
The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) on Thursday arraigned Adeniyi Adeyemi afresh on 22 counts of alleged forgery, impersonation and related offences before an FCT High Court in Abuja over his purported role as director-general of the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council (PFIPC).

Adeyemi pleaded not guilty to all the counts.

The fresh arraignment followed the striking out of an earlier eight-count charge against him by a Federal High Court in Abuja on October 12, after the Federal Government sought to terminate the proceedings following a review by the Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF).

Rotimi Oyedepo, Director of Public Prosecutions of the Federation, had told the court that the review established that the alleged offences fell within the jurisdiction of the FCT High Court rather than the Federal High Court, where the police initially filed the charge.

The prosecution subsequently filed the fresh charge before the FCT High Court.

Forgery, impersonation allegations

In the new charge, the ICPC accused Adeyemi of forging a letter dated March 8, 2024, purportedly signed by Femi Gbajabiamila, Chief of Staff to the President, appointing him director-general of the PFIPC.

The commission alleged that Adeyemi used forged documents to present the purported council as a legitimate government institution and gain access to government facilities and official processes.

Other counts accuse him of forging an executive order purportedly establishing the council and a legislative instrument bearing the titles of the Presidential Economic Advisory Council and PFIPC.

The ICPC also alleged that he forged a document addressed to the Accountant-General of the Federation seeking approval for the purported agency to operate within the government’s financial reporting structure.

Another allegation concerns documents purportedly submitted to the National Information Technology Development Agency to obtain a domain name for the council.

The commission further accused Adeyemi of using forged documents presented to the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy to seek more than N27 billion for the establishment of the purported agency and N3.8 billion for personnel costs.

In separate counts, the ICPC alleged that Adeyemi gave N210,000 to Aminu Abdullahi, an assistant chief technical officer in the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, to facilitate the allocation of office space without official authorisation.

He was also accused of giving N300,000 to Ogaba Harry, an officer in the Office of the Chief Economic Adviser to the President, to facilitate the release of a Prado sport utility vehicle and a Land Cruiser.

The commission further alleged that Adeyemi obtained N20 million from Oyekunle Gbenga, managing director of Divine Dopacy Nigeria Limited, under the pretence of a project facilitation loan for a purported N2.8 billion contract to furnish and renovate the official residence of the PFIPC director-general.

The alleged offences reportedly occurred between 2024 and 2026 and are punishable under relevant provisions of the Penal Code, the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Fraud Related Offences Act, and the Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act.

Adeyemi has denied the allegations. He has separately alleged that Gbajabiamila collected N400 million through a proxy in connection with the appointment letter. The allegation against Gbajabiamila remains a claim by Adeyemi and is not established by the charges outlined in court.

Court orders written bail application

After Adeyemi entered his plea, ICPC counsel, Fatima Bardi, asked the court to fix a date for the commencement of trial.

Defence counsel, Ibrahim Angulu, made an oral application for bail, but the presiding judge, Halilu Yusuf, directed him to file a formal written application.

Angulu agreed but urged the court to schedule an early hearing, citing his client’s prolonged detention and health concerns.

He told the court that Adeyemi had spent 155 days in detention and had a medical report from the police clinic where he received treatment. The judge adjourned the case until November 9 for trial and possible hearing of the bail application.

World.title: Publish details of N30bn East-West road approval, Ugolor tells Umahi
World.content:
Minister of Works, Davide Umahi.

By Adesina Wahab

An activist and publisher of The Common Good Letter, Rev. David Ugolor, has challenged the Minister of Works, Dave Umahi, to publish details of the Federal Government’s approval of N30 billion for remedial works on the East-West Road.

Ugolor said making the details public would promote transparency and accountability in the use of public funds, while enabling communities, motorists and civil society organisations to monitor the project’s implementation.

In an open letter to the minister, he welcomed the announcement that the Federal Executive Council approved the N30 billion for repairs to deteriorated sections of the road at its meeting on October 28, 2026.

He, however, said the announcement should be followed by clear information on the scope of work, contractors, funding arrangements and completion timelines.

“An approval is one stage of delivery. Nigerians also need to know what work has been authorised, who will execute it, how it will be financed and when it will be completed,” Ugolor said.

He called on the ministry to identify all sections of the road covered by the approval, including the states, communities, kilometre points and length of each intervention.

He specifically asked whether the package included the damaged Kira section in Rivers State and other locations recently affected by flooding.

Ugolor also urged the ministry to publish the engineering scope, bill of quantities and completion standards, clarifying whether the funds would cover temporary repairs, permanent reconstruction, drainage improvements, bridges, culverts or road elevation.

On procurement, he asked Umahi to disclose the contractors and supervising consultants, as well as whether the interventions involved new contracts, variations to existing contracts or other delivery arrangements.

He further requested details of the procurement process, relevant approvals and applicable clearances from the Bureau of Public Procurement.

The activist also sought clarification on the source of funding, asking the ministry to distinguish between the amount approved, funds released, payments made to contractors and sums certified against completed work, including the dates of each transaction.

Ugolor called for an explanation of how the N30 billion approval related to existing East-West Road contracts and the previously announced reconstruction of approximately 400 kilometres between Edo and Cross River states.

He urged the ministry to publish a consolidated schedule showing the boundaries, costs and responsibilities of the different interventions to prevent overlaps or uncertainty over project delivery.

On road safety and durability, Ugolor called for the publication of relevant drainage, flood-risk and geotechnical assessments.

He said the ministry should explain how the designs would address water flow, road elevation and the safety of neighbouring communities, including consultation and compensation arrangements where applicable.

The publisher also asked the ministry to disclose when contractors had been or would be mobilised, the expected completion dates, measurable project milestones, traffic management arrangements and the officials responsible for monitoring progress.

Ugolor urged relevant committees of the National Assembly to scrutinise the approval and track the expenditure through to the completion of the work.

He also called on state governments, host communities, transport associations and civil society organisations to seek access to project information to enable them to monitor implementation.

“The Common Good Letter supports urgent repairs and a transparent, adequately funded programme for the wider East-West Road,” he said.

He urged Umahi to provide a consolidated public explanation accompanied by the approval, procurement, funding and implementation records.

“Public money must deliver safe roads, measurable progress and lasting relief,” Ugolor added.

World.title: Ondo approves state burial for Fasoranti
World.content:
By Dayo Johnson, Akure

Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, has set up a committee to organise a state burial for the late Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, who died at the age of 100.

According to a statement issued in Akure by the governor’s Chief Press Secretary, Prince Ebenezer Adeniyan, the committee will work with the Fasoranti family and the leadership of Afenifere to organise a befitting burial for the elder statesman.

The committee is chaired by the state Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Dr Kayode Ajulo, SAN, while Apostle Eniola Olushola will serve as secretary.

Other members are Hon. Gbenga Fasua, Mr Gbenga Atiba, Mrs Kosemani Kolawole, Rt. Hon. Bakkita Bello, Hon. Idowu Otetubi, Erelu Modupe Martins, Mr George Asonja, Esq., Mr Muyiwa Ogunyemi, Hon. Stephen Abitogun and Mr Adetunji Gbenga.

Adeniyan said the state government decided to honour Fasoranti with a state burial in recognition of his contributions to Ondo State, Yorubaland and Nigeria.

He said Aiyedatiwa believed the late Afenifere leader deserved to be celebrated for his life of service, wisdom and selfless leadership.

The governor also reaffirmed the government’s commitment to ensuring that the burial reflects Fasoranti’s contributions to society.

The committee is expected to coordinate the arrangements in consultation with the family and Afenifere leadership to ensure a dignified farewell for the late nationalist.

World.title: Stretford Hill Executes Structural, MEP Works for Canary Points Headquarters
World.content:
Stretford Hill Limited has executed the structural and mechanical, electrical and plumbing (MEP) works for Canary Points Headquarters, a five-storey commercial building in Lekki, Lagos, commissioned on October 27.

The commissioning ceremony was attended by Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr Kadri Obafemi Hamzat; Chairman of Canary Point Holdings, Kayode Lambo; the company’s Group Managing Director, Idris Ibrahim; and other government officials, business leaders and industry stakeholders.

As the main contractor for the structural and MEP works, Stretford Hill handled the building’s structural construction from foundation to roof slab, as well as the installation of its mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems. Other aspects of the development, including interior finishing, were undertaken by specialist contractors, alongside the contributions of consultants and other project stakeholders.

Speaking on the project, Stretford Hill’s Chief Executive Officer, Engr. Lakunle Runsewe, said the successful execution of commercial developments depended on engineering precision, coordination and collaboration among project teams.

“On a project like this, the structural elements and building services must work together to ensure the building functions as an integrated facility. Achieving that requires careful planning, effective coordination and consistent attention to quality,” he said.

“At Stretford Hill Limited, we remain committed to demonstrating the capabilities of indigenous construction expertise through sound engineering, professional accountability and the consistent delivery of quality work.”

The commissioning adds to the portfolio of commercial developments delivered with the involvement of indigenous construction firms.

World.title: Alternativa Film Festival Opens 2027 Entries, Expands to Africa
World.content:
Vanessa Obioha

Alternativa Film Festival has opened submissions for its 2027 edition, marking its first expansion to Africa, with $120,000 in prize money across seven award categories.

The announcement was made on Thursday at MIP Africa, as the festival, founded and supported by global mobility company inDrive, invited filmmakers from Africa, Asia and Latin America to submit feature films for the competition.

Short film submissions, however, are restricted to African filmmakers, reflecting the continent’s status as the festival’s focus region for 2027. All entries must have been completed after January 1, 2026.

Three of the seven awards are reserved for African filmmakers: the $20,000 Focus Award and two Short Film Awards worth $10,000 each. African filmmakers are also eligible for the remaining categories.

Directors whose films are selected for the competition will be invited to attend the festival and awards ceremony, with travel and accommodation covered by the organisers.

Scheduled for late 2027, the festival’s host country, city and exact dates are yet to be announced. Submissions are free and close on March 1, 2027.

Alternativa champions impact-driven cinema from the Global South, a region home to roughly five-sixths of the world’s population but which remains underrepresented on screen.

Its expansion into Africa comes as the initiative broadens its efforts to improve the reach of films from the region. Earlier this year, it launched Alternativa Distribution, a non-profit model designed to reinvest in filmmakers and local film industries.

The distribution arm offers upfront minimum guarantees for non-theatrical rights, funds subtitling and dubbing, and shares revenue after recovering direct distribution costs.

“Exceptional filmmaking can come from anywhere, but access to international audiences is still hindered by a deeply unequal system,” said Arsen Tomsky, founder and chief executive officer of inDrive. “Alternativa Distribution was created to challenge that imbalance.”

Its catalogue includes Nepal’s ‘Elephants in the Fog,’ the country’s 2027 Oscar submission and winner of the Un Certain Regard Jury Prize at Cannes in 2026; ‘No Good Men,’ Afghanistan’s co-production and the opening film of the 2026 Berlin International Film Festival; Malaysia’s ‘Lost Land,’ which won the Orizzonti Special Jury Prize at the 2025 Venice Film Festival; and Tunisia’s ‘Four Daughters,’ a 2024 Oscar nominee.

Films selected for the 2027 festival may also be considered for inclusion in the distribution catalogue.

Alternativa began its festival journey in Almaty, Kazakhstan, in 2023, before moving to Yogyakarta, Indonesia, in 2024, and Medellín, Colombia, in 2026. The itinerant festival moves to a new region with each edition.

The Medellín edition received 1,831 submissions from 55 countries, attracting 11,000 attendees, 107 international guests and more than 60 partners, making it the festival’s largest edition to date.

“With each edition, Alternativa Film Festival grows,” said Liza Surganova, head of Alternativa. “Not only in reach and scale, but also in the connections it creates and the opportunities it opens up for filmmakers.”

She said the African edition would build on the festival’s previous achievements while introducing new initiatives for its community.

“Africa is home to an extraordinary diversity of cultures, perspectives, and cinematic voices, and we believe this new chapter will deepen our understanding of what transformative cinema can be and help us forge valuable new connections,” she added.

The 2027 programme will feature public screenings, discussions and other events exploring the social issues addressed in selected films. An awards ceremony will recognise films that combine artistic excellence with the potential to drive social change.

The festival will also hold Industry Days, a professional programme that connects filmmakers, producers, industry experts and social impact leaders from across the Global South.

Elise Shick, a Malaysian producer of ‘Lost Land,’ which won the Nativa Award at the 2026 edition, said the festival had helped foster international collaboration.

“Here, we have already formed a co-production project involving nine countries. We hope to screen it as the opening film of the next Alternativa Film Festival in Africa,” she said.

The festival is open to fiction, documentary, animation and hybrid films across all genres. Eligibility requirements, the list of qualifying countries and details of the award categories are available on the festival’s official website.

World.title: Alleged Cyberbullying: Sowore Seeks Adjournment, Trial Resumes November 3
World.content:
The trial of the presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), Omoyele Sowore, over alleged cyberbullying was stalled on Thursday at the Federal High Court in Abuja following his absence and a letter seeking an adjournment.

At the mention of the case, prosecuting counsel, Akinlolu Kehinde (SAN), noted that the defendant was absent from court.

Defence counsel, T. O. Etonyeaku, who said she was holding the brief of Sowore’s lead counsel, Adeyinka Olumide-Fusika (SAN), told the court that the politician was in Ekiti State for his presidential campaigns.

Etonyeaku subsequently prayed the court for a stand-down to enable another senior lawyer, who was earlier in court before the commencement of proceedings, to arrive and conduct the defence.

However, the presiding judge, Justice Mohammed Umar, drew the attention of both lawyers to a letter written to the court by Sowore and asked Kehinde whether he was aware of it.

The prosecution counsel denied being copied on the letter, arguing that it was wrong for an accused person represented by a lawyer to bypass counsel and write directly to the court without copying the other party.

He added that since there was no evidence that Sowore had discontinued the services of his lawyer, Olumide-Fusika, he ought not to have written personally to the court.

Kehinde, however, conceded to an adjournment in the interest of justice.

The prosecuting lawyer also noted that the defence was yet to respond to the written address he filed, as ordered by the court, on the issue of whether he could be subpoenaed to testify as a defence witness.

Justice Umar subsequently adjourned the case until November 3 for the adoption of addresses and continuation of the defence.

Sowore is being prosecuted by the Department of State Services (DSS) over posts he published on X, formerly Twitter, and Facebook in August 2025, in which he described President Bola Tinubu as a “criminal” and accused him of lying about the level of corruption in the country.

World.title: Tinubu Departs For Makkah, To Pray For Nation’s Peace, Stability
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu on Thursday afternoon departed the nation’s capital, Abuja for Makkah, Saudi Arabia, to perform Umrah pilgrimage.

During the exercise also known as lesser Hajj, Tinubu will offer prayers for Nigeria’s peace, national unity, stability and sustained development.

The president’s plane, Nigeria Air Force 1, took off from the presidential wing of the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, at approximately 2:20 p.m, after a brief departure ceremony attended by state governors and some top government officials who were on ground to see him off.

Ahead of his departure, the Saudi Arabian Ambassador to Nigeria, Yousef Bin Mohammed Al-Balawi, presented the president with a Bisht, a traditional Arabian ceremonial cloak, on behalf of the Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia.

Also on ground at the airport to see the president off were Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume; Kwara State Governor, Abdulrahman Abdulrazaq; his Yobe and Borno States counterparts, Mai Mala Buni; and Babagana Zulum respectively.

Others were Governors of Kaduna, Uba Sani; Jigawa, Umar Namadi; Ahmad Aliyu Sokoto; Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF) and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi; Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate; and the member representing Ikorodu Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Hon Babajimi Benson.

The Nigerian Ambassador to Mexico, Honduras, Guatemala and Nicaragua, Ambassador Reno Omokri, and Director of Protocol at the Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Ibrahim Sule Dan Agundi, also attended the departure ceremony.

Presidential spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, had on Wednesday confirmed the planned journey via a statement issued indicating that President Tinubu was due back in Nigeria next week upon completion of the religious exercise.

Tinubu’s visit will provide him an opportunity for spiritual reflection and devotion, while he undertakes the religious rites associated with Umrah and seeking divine guidance and blessings for Nigerians.

World.title: Borno Parents Seek Tinubu’s Intervention As 78 Children, Teacher Remain in Captivity
World.content:
Amina Hassan in Abuja

Parents of Margi community in Askira/Uba Local Government Area of Borno State have appealed to President Bola Tinubu to intensify efforts to secure the release of 78 schoolchildren and a teacher abducted from Mussa and Lassa communities in separate incidents.

Speaking at a press briefing in Abuja on Thursday, the Chairman of the Margi community, Malla Gadzama, said 42 children were abducted from Mussa on May 15, 2026, while 36 children and a teacher were taken from Lassa on June 29, during the period of the National Examinations Council (NECO) examinations.

The community said the victims had remained in captivity for months despite repeated appeals to the government and other relevant authorities.

Another community member, Frank Kudla, said the abductors had communicated with the government but had not contacted the victims’ families directly.

He noted that the community understood that the government was the only party aware of the kidnappers’ demands, leaving the families without direct information about the situation.

“We asked the government to resolve quickly so that our children can be released,” he said.

Kudla added that the families had received assurances from the Borno State Government that the children would be returned, but they were still awaiting their release months later.

Gadzama said the community had previously held press conferences in Maiduguri and at the National Assembly to draw attention to the abductions, but the efforts had yet to secure the victims’ freedom.

The community’s secretary, Gambo Kadiri, expressed concern that President Tinubu might not have been fully briefed about the situation, although the community could not establish whether the president had received information about the incidents.

Kadiri said the community had also written to the National Security Adviser (NSA) but had yet to receive a response. He called on the relevant authorities to treat the matter with urgency and sustain efforts to secure the victims’ release.

Kudla said attempts to secure an audience with the Senate President and other National Assembly authorities had also been unsuccessful, prompting the community to hold another press briefing to draw attention to the matter.

The community said it might consider a procession to the National Assembly to press lawmakers to engage the Presidency and security agencies over the continued captivity of the children and their teacher.

The community called for coordinated rescue efforts involving federal and state authorities, as well as regular communication with the affected families without compromising the safety of the victims.

It also urged the government to establish a designated liaison arrangement through which families could receive verified information and raise concerns about the situation.

The community called for psychosocial and welfare support for the affected families, alongside medical care, rehabilitation and educational assistance for the children upon their return. It further urged the authorities to strengthen security around vulnerable schools and communities to prevent future abductions.

Appealing to civil society organisations, religious and traditional leaders, professional associations, women’s and youth groups, and the media, the community urged sustained public attention to the victims’ plight.

It also cautioned journalists against publishing information that could endanger the children or compromise rescue efforts.

World.title: Former SGF Boss Mustapha Calls for Review of Public Servants’ Salary Structure to Tackle Corruption
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

Former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Boss Mustapha, has called for a review of the salary structure of public servants in Nigeria to reflect current economic realities, address the rising cost of living and correct abnormal disparities in the remuneration of Permanent Secretaries, Directors, Ministers, Directors-General and other heads of government agencies.

He emphasised the need for a fair and sustainable remuneration system that would improve workers’ welfare, boost morale, help tackle corruption within the service and enhance productivity across the public service.

Mustapha made the call while delivering the keynote address at the Colloquium and Unveiling of the Council of Retired Federal Permanent Secretaries and Heads of the Civil Service of the Federation (CORFEPS) Journal on Public Policy and Governance at the Rotunda, Tafawa Balewa House, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Abuja.

The event, which marked the beginning of CORFEPS Week 2026, was themed “Navigating the Headwinds of Governance: Centrality of the Civil Service”.

Mustapha said the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission, in collaboration with the Federal Civil Service and the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, must address the disparities in public sector remuneration.

“The National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission has an important role in remuneration options. I sometimes feel a little bit embarrassed when I see budget estimates that come out of successive governments over and over, and they are running into trillions of naira and the people that are supposed to manage those trillions of naira earn peanuts,” he said.

He questioned the rationale behind entrusting public servants with enormous responsibilities without adequately remunerating them, describing the situation in which some agency heads earn more than Ministers and Permanent Secretaries combined as abnormal.

Citing Singapore’s remuneration structure, he noted that its Prime Minister earned $2.6 million annually, compared with the $400,000 earned by the US President, Donald Trump. He attributed Singapore’s leadership structure to its rigorous recruitment process, which draws many leaders from the civil service.

In a goodwill message, the Chairman of the Federal Civil Service Commission, Prof. Tunji Olaopa, supported Mustapha’s position, stressing that policies could only be as effective as the workforce responsible for implementing them.

“Professionalising the civil service is therefore not rhetoric. It involves deep talent management reforms and investment in capacity development, training and retraining,” he said.

Olaopa noted that retaining talented personnel remained a major challenge despite the service’s ability to attract highly capable individuals. He disclosed that he had discussed the issue with the Salaries and Wages Commission, adding that ongoing deliberations could help advance civil service reforms.

Declaring the colloquium open, Vice-President Kashim Shettima, represented by the Special Adviser to the President on Power Infrastructure in the Office of the Vice-President, Sadiq Wanka, described the civil service as central to national development and the state’s ability to fulfil its obligations to citizens.

He said the Renewed Hope Agenda reflected the administration’s response to Nigeria’s economic and social challenges, adding that the government had shifted its focus from the number of policies announced and committees inaugurated to whether public interventions solved problems and improved lives.

He cited compulsory ministerial deliverables coordinated by the Central Delivery Coordinating Unit (CDCU) and ministerial briefings as mechanisms for assessing government performance.

“We are committed to providing positive answers to everyday questions that the average Nigerians want answer to, such as, Are services reaching the people for whom they are intended? Are public funds generating value? Are decisions timely and evidence-informed? Can citizens see and trust the results?” he asked.

The Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, Mr Olumuyiwa Enitan Abel, said the colloquium provided a platform for intellectual engagement, professional reflection and the exchange of ideas on strengthening governance and repositioning the civil service for greater effectiveness.

He stressed that effective governance depended on the civil service’s ability to provide objective advice, implement policies efficiently and remain accountable to citizens.

Earlier, the National Chairman of CORFEPS, Alhaji Yayale Ahmed, said the council was established to enable retired Permanent Secretaries and former Heads of the Civil Service to contribute their experience, professional knowledge and institutional memory to national development.

“Our retirement from formal office does not diminish our commitment to Nigeria. Rather, it provides an opportunity to reflect on our collective experience, draw lessons from our service and offer constructive advice on matters of public policy and administration. This commitment is captured in our motto: ‘Continuing Patriotic Service’,” he said.

Ahmed added that CORFEPS continued to organise policy dialogues, seminars and conferences, conduct research and provide advice on matters of national importance.

“We believe that those who have served the nation at the highest levels of public administration have a responsibility to make their accumulated knowledge available to succeeding generations,” he said.

World.title: FG Honours Miden Systems Chair, Usoro, for Corporate Governance
World.content:
Kasim Sumaina in Abuja

The federal government has honoured the Executive Chairman of Miden Systems Limited, Dr. Brendan Innocent Usoro, with the Excellence in Corporate Governance and Business Integrity Award for his commitment to ethical leadership, transparency and responsible business practices.

Usoro received the award yesterday at the Nigerian Press Council (NPC) National Summit on Curbing Fake News and Misinformation in the Nigerian Media Space, held in Abuja.

Speaking at the event, he warned that fake news and misinformation posed serious threats to national security, democratic stability, business confidence and peaceful coexistence, particularly as Nigeria approaches the 2027 general elections.

He expressed concern over the growing misuse of artificial intelligence to produce fabricated audio recordings, manipulate videos and spread misleading information.

According to him, misinformation has become a tool for damaging reputations, undermining businesses and creating social tension.

“People use false information to de-market their political opponents, competitors’ products and services, as well as create tension in the polity,” he said.

He urged Nigerians to verify information before sharing it, recommending independent fact-checking organisations such as Dubawa. He also called for improved training for journalists, wider access to verification tools and stronger collaboration among government agencies, media organisations and technology companies.

He stressed, however, that efforts to combat misinformation must not undermine press freedom, freedom of expression or legitimate criticism.

Speaking on Miden Systems, Usoro said the company was established in 1997 and had grown from providing safety and equipment maintenance services into a diversified business covering marine services, logistics, facility upgrades and management.

He attributed the company’s growth to quality service delivery and strong client relationships, reaffirming its commitment to ethical conduct, transparency and integrity.

Earlier, the Executive Secretary and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Press Council, Dr. Dili Ezughah, said the summit was organised to strengthen responsible journalism and equip media professionals to tackle misinformation ahead of the 2027 elections.

The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa, represented by his Special Adviser on Intelligence, Musa Likita, described fake news as a threat to national security and democratic governance, urging collective action to prevent the spread of false information.

Similarly, the Minister of Information and National Orientation, Alhaji Mohammed Idris, represented by Dr. Haruna Suleiman, called for stronger editorial oversight, accurate reporting and improved media literacy.

Other award recipients included Nasarawa State Governor, Abdullahi Sule; General Christopher Musa; Mohammed Idris; Senator Emmanuel Bwacha; Barrister Obioma Success Akagburuonye; and Dr. Yakubu Barde, Federal Commissioner for Salaries, Income and Wages.

The summit ended with a call for stronger cooperation among government institutions, media organisations, businesses and citizens to combat misinformation, protect press freedom and strengthen public trust.

The summit brought together media practitioners, government officials, corporate executives and other stakeholders to discuss strategies for combating misinformation and promoting responsible journalism.

World.title: Benue Security Crisis Has Gained Global Attention, Says Showunmi
World.content:
*Says Tinubu has improved security situation in Nigeria

George Okoh in Makurdi

Otunba Segun Showunmi, Convener of The Alternative Movement, says Benue has attracted serious attention from American leaders over insecurity and the suffering of its people.

Showunmi made this known at the movement’s town hall meeting in Benue, themed “Bridging the Divide, Building Trust Through Shared Purpose”.on Wednesday

He said he had visited the United States Congress three times and engaged with its leadership on issues concerning the state.

According to him, discussions among American leaders have increasingly focused on the security challenges and humanitarian concerns affecting Benue.

Showunmi urged political leaders and residents to unite ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that internal divisions could undermine the state’s interests.

He said Benue and other states in the North-Central region should position themselves to contribute meaningfully to the country’s leadership, noting that political power was not permanently restricted to particular regions.

The convener urged residents to mobilise voters ahead of the elections, saying Benue had more than 3.05 million registered voters capable of influencing national political outcomes.

He also commended President Bola Tinubu’s administration for infrastructure development in Benue, particularly road projects across the state’s three senatorial districts.

Showunmi said some roads that had remained neglected for years were now receiving attention under the current administration.

He further said the Federal Government was strengthening security arrangements, including the deployment of military formations, to address security challenges in the state.

Also speaking, Mr Edwin Adai, Benue Coordinator of The Alternative Movement, called on Gov. Hyacinth Alia and Sen. George Akume to embrace dialogue and reconciliation to prevent political tensions from escalating into violence ahead of the 2027 elections.

Adai warned that prolonged political disagreements could result in avoidable loss of lives if leaders failed to prioritise peace and the welfare of residents.

He urged the two leaders to put aside their differences and work together to address insecurity, unemployment, education, agriculture and economic development.

According to him, the interests of Benue residents should take precedence over personal ambitions and political rivalries.

Adai cited former Senate Presidents David Mark and Iyorchia Ayu, alongside Akume, as examples of political leaders who had demonstrated that disagreements could be resolved through dialogue.

He also expressed concern over the involvement of some youths in cultism, internet fraud and other criminal activities.

He called for improved education, vocational training, mentorship, access to capital and employment opportunities to help young people pursue legitimate livelihoods.

Adai urged political leaders to desist from recruiting or manipulating youths for violence, stressing the need to channel their energy into education, enterprise, agriculture and innovation.

He said farmers, traders, entrepreneurs, women and vulnerable households needed peace, security, accessible healthcare, quality education and economic opportunities to improve their living conditions.

World.title: Peter Ndlovu makes winning start as a head coach
World.content:
Mamelodi Sundowns legend Peter Ndlovu made an encouraging start to life as Scottland FC’s interim head coach after guiding the Zimbabwean champions to a 1-0 victory over CAPS United on Thursday.

Emmanuel Jalai scored the decisive goal in the sixth minute as Scottland secured maximum points in Harare, giving Ndlovu an immediate boost following his promotion from team manager to head coach.

The result offers a positive beginning for the former Zimbabwe Warriors captain, who has been tasked with guiding the ambitious club through the remainder of the 2026 season.



Peter Ndlovu gets off to a winning start

Ndlovu stepped into the hot seat following Norman Mapeza’s departure after Scottland’s disappointing exit from the CAF Champions League.

The former Mamelodi Sundowns team manager was handed the responsibility of steadying the team and keeping its domestic ambitions alive.

His first assignment against CAPS United was a significant test, with Scottland needing points to maintain pressure on Castle Lager Premier Soccer League leaders Hardrock FC.

Jalai’s early strike proved enough to settle the contest, allowing Ndlovu to begin his tenure with a victory rather than the setback that could have increased the pressure on the club.

Although one result is not enough to establish whether Ndlovu can sustain a title challenge, the win provides a timely confidence boost for the new coach and his players.

Peter Ndlovu takes over after Mapeza’s exit

Scottland parted ways with Mapeza following the club’s elimination from the continental competition, where they surrendered a two-goal first-leg advantage against Angola’s Petro de Luanda before losing 3-2 on aggregate.



The coaching change also brought an overhaul of the technical team, leaving Ndlovu with the responsibility of helping restore stability.

According to The Herald, Ndlovu will be assisted by Danger Fourpence, who was promoted from the club’s academy.

Veteran forward Knowledge Musona has also taken on a player-assistant coach role.

a big task ahead

Despite his limited experience as a senior head coach, Ndlovu holds a CAF A Coaching Licence, providing a foundation for his transition from administration to the technical area.

His stature in Zimbabwean football and previous experience at Mamelodi Sundowns give him valuable experience within the professional game.

However, leading a team from the touchline presents a different challenge from managing its off-field operations.

Scottland, owned by businessman Scott Sakupwanya, have invested heavily in building a competitive squad and will expect results from their new interim coach.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs boss hints at the coach’s work hours
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs head coach Fernando Da Cruz has been facing the heat after an underwhelming start. According to Motaung, the Frenchman is a top-level and hard-working coach who requires time.

Speaking on Marawa Sports Worldwide, Motaung expressed satisfaction with the coach’s work, praising his authority in the dressing room, tactical preparation and professionalism.

“I’m happy,” said Motaung.

KAIZER CHIEFS BOSS LAUDS FERNANDO DA CRUZ’S PROFESSIONALISM

Motaung made it clear that Amakhosi have confidence in their coach’s leadership, insisting that the dressing room is under control.



“My coach owns the change room, controls the change room. If you hear how people are fired in other clubs or whatever, we’re not in a circus game…”

Motaung also pointed to the team’s tactical structure and preparation as evidence of the quality within the technical setup.

“And look at the structure of the team, look at how he prepares the team, look at technical aspects of the team, it’s high level. But the only thing is patience and time, doesn’t happen overnight like I say, there’s injuries that happened.



Since arriving at Amakhosi, Da Cruz remains unbeaten in eight Betway Premiership league games, though these include three wins and five draws. His side crashed out of the CAF Confederation Cup preliminary qualifiers.

His defensive setup, performances and team selections have been slammed by fans, pundits and club legends.

“What I think without dwelling into it, this is a high level coach that we’ve got, technical staff professional, high level,” Motaung continued in his defence.



‘THESE COACHES LEAVE AT 5 O’CLOCK, 6 O’CLOCK’

Motaung also highlighted the hours the technical staff put into their work at the club’s training facilities, contrasting their commitment with what he described as the working habits of some local coaches.

“I can tell you about local coaches who come in at 9 o’clock, 11 o’clock at the village. We’ve got a facility there that’s got Sports Science, it’s got everything. These coaches leave at 5 o’clock, 6 o’clock, working on that, planning and looking at everything.”

His comments underline the club’s emphasis on preparation, tactical analysis and the use of its training infrastructure.

World.title: Da Cruz on why Kaizer Chiefs are confident ahead of Soweto Derby
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs come into the Soweto Derby high in confidence following their 3-0 win over TS Galaxy midweek.

Amakhosi coach Fernando Da Cruz felt a win on Tuesday lifted the spirit of the team heading into the derby weekend.

It will be the first time the French coach faces Orlando Pirates.



“It’s the most important game in South Africa. Sold out in six hours, one of the best games in Africa,” Da Cruz said.

“It divides the country. It’s a good moment for South African football.”

The Kaizer Chiefs coach praised Bucs coach Abdeslam Ouaddou for the work he’s done at Pirates since taking over in 2025.

“I’m good. We worked well this week with the team, we are confident. But we know it’s a difficult game against a good team, a big team.

“I have congratulate Abdes for the job since his arrival at Orlando Pirates. But we are ready for the game.”

Kaizer Chiefs high in confidence

A win for Amakhosi will revive their title ambitions but defeat will all but end their hopes of winning the Betway Premiership this season.



Da Cruz though feels his team should be confident from midweek win against Galaxy.

“We come to the game with a lot of confidence – when you score three goals and don’t concede you’ve got a lot of confidence,” the Kaizer Chiefs coach added.

“But we always want to improve the team, even when we win. So we must keep this confidence when we go to the derby.”
