World.title: Local elections 2026: Here’s how many ballot papers need your X
World.content:
South Africans heading to the polls on Wednesday, 4 November, will receive either two or three ballot papers. Image: IEC

South Africans heading to the polls on Wednesday, 4 November, will receive either two or three ballot papers in the 2026 Local Government Elections, depending on where they are registered to vote.

The Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) has explained that voters in metropolitan municipalities will receive two ballot papers, while those in local municipalities outside the country’s eight metros will receive three.

Each ballot paper represents a separate choice, meaning voters must make one clear cross (X) on every ballot they receive if they wish to cast a vote in each contest.



READ | Elections 2026: What is a spoilt vote? Here are 7 examples [photos]

Why do some voters get two ballots and others three?

The number of ballot papers depends on the municipality in which a voter is registered.

Voters in metropolitan municipalities receive two ballot papers:

Ward ballot: To choose a candidate to represent their ward on the metropolitan council.

To choose a candidate to represent their ward on the metropolitan council. Proportional representation (PR) ballot: To choose a political party for representation on the metropolitan council.

Voters in local municipalities outside metropolitan areas receive three ballot papers:

Ward ballot: To choose a ward councillor.

To choose a ward councillor. Local council PR ballot: To choose a political party for representation on the local municipal council.

To choose a political party for representation on the local municipal council. District council PR ballot: To choose a political party for representation on the district municipal council.

The third ballot is used in areas where voters elect representatives to both a local municipal council and a district municipal council.

READ | Here’s how many registered voters are in your province



How many crosses must you make?

The basic rule is simple: one ballot paper, one cross.

If you receive two ballot papers, you can make two crosses. If you receive three, you can make three crosses.

On each ballot, place one clear X in the box next to your chosen candidate or political party. Do not mark more than one option on the same ballot, sign it, write your name on it or add unnecessary marks, as these could result in a spoilt vote.

You also do not have to vote for the same political party on every ballot. Your ward candidate choice can differ from your party choice on the proportional representation ballots. Each ballot is counted separately.

What happens if you make a mistake?

If you mark a ballot incorrectly, do not put it into the ballot box.

Instead, approach the presiding officer and ask for a replacement ballot paper. The incorrect ballot can then be cancelled before a new one is issued.

Once a ballot paper has been placed in the ballot box, it cannot be removed.

What should voters remember on election day?

Before leaving for the voting station, make sure you know where you are registered and have an accepted identity document.

At the station, election officials will verify your registration details and issue the appropriate number of ballot papers.

World.title: ‘Feeders of many’: Why South Africans say the SASSA old-age grant increase matters at home
World.content:
For many South African families, the SASSA old-age grant does far more than support one elderly person.

That was the message from commenters responding to The South African’s report on a push to raise the Older Persons Grant to R3 000 a month.

Grandparents hold households together WITH SASSA GRANTS

On The South African’s Facebook page, Maureen Ntwendala said grandparents play a central role in keeping families fed. “That will be great, grandfather and grandmother are the feeders of many,” she wrote.



Her comment reflects a reality in many homes across the country, where pensioners use their grants to buy groceries, pay school costs and support unemployed adult children and grandchildren.

When one grant must stretch across several people, even a modest increase can affect what lands on the table each month.

‘Will make a big difference’

Sylvia Seeligsohn said a higher grant would ease pressure on households. “R3500 will make a big difference,” she wrote, suggesting an amount slightly above the figure under discussion.



Harold Toll kept his hopes simple. “I’ll appreciate it if the pension fund can be able to rise,” he wrote.

His comment drew a reply from another user, as grant recipients shared how rising food, transport and electricity costs continue to eat into their monthly payments.

Hope beyond politics

Not everyone is placing their trust in government.



Amina Pietersen wrote: “Leave everything in the almighty God hands, he will come through for us.”

What happens next

The proposed increase has not been approved. Grant increases are usually announced by the Minister of Finance in the Budget Speech each February and take effect from April.

Until then, grant recipients will continue to receive their monthly payments at current rates. Pensioners should rely only on official SASSA channels for confirmed grant amounts and payment dates.

World.title: Dricus du Plessis calls for action over horror farm attack
World.content:
Dricus du Plessis has supported a call for action after a horror farm attack in the North West. Images via X

Dricus du Plessis has reposted a message calling for action after the gruesome farm attack on North West farm owner Donovan Marx this week.

Marx was shot and stabbed and had both his ears cut off during the horrific ordeal that took place on Wednesday, 28 October.

The 50-year-old is currently recovering at his home.



DRICUS DU PLESSIS CALLS FOR ACTION AFTER HORROR FARM ATTACK

On his Instagram Stories, Dricus du Plessis reposted several videos and posts about the farm owner, Donovan Marx, who was attacked and tortured on his property located between Potchefstroom and Ventersdorp on Wednesday, 28 October.

Marx was shot in the back of the head, stabbed in one of his legs, and had both his ears cut off by his attackers. One of his farm workers was also tied up during the attack.

His attackers drove off in Marx’s red van. The 50-ear-old was rushed to the Mediclinic in Potchefstroom where h received treatment.



Marx’s community and loved ones are also offering a R4 000 reward for information leading to the arrest and conviction of the suspects.

In a social media post, Ian Cameron, the Chairperson of Parliament’s Portfolio Committee on Police, called for farm attacks to be recognised as violent crimes

He shared: “North West SAPS must prioritise Donovan’s case, support experienced detectives with forensic and intelligence capacity, and keep the family informed.



He added: “Beyond this investigation, rural safety requires properly equipped police officers who can reach the people they are responsible for protecting”.

‘I WANT PEOPLE TO SEE WHAT IS HAPPENING IN SOUTH AFRICA’

At his UFC debut win against Markus Perez in October 2020, Dricus du Plessis spoke publicly about his concerns over farm attacks.



He said during a press conference: “We have farm murders that are really taking the whole country by storm. It’s something unbelievable.”

“People are getting murdered daily, and I almost feel like, because it’s Africa, a lot of the world doesn’t see it, and nobody in the world really knows what’s going on there.”

Dricus vowed to use his status to draw attention to attacks.



He continued: “I’ve just got this opportunity on a bigger stage to say ‘let’s stop the farm murders’, and I want people to see what’s happening in South Africa.”

Dricus du Plessis has also used his platform to openly criticise President Cyril Ramaphosa as being “corrupt” and “taking all the money”.

World.title: South Africa’s GDP R324 billion bigger than ANYONE knew
World.content:
South Africa’s economy is significantly larger than previously measured, following a major revision by Statistics South Africa. Image: Wikimedia Commons

South Africa’s economy is significantly larger than previously measured, following a major revision by Statistics South Africa (Stats SA) that has increased the country’s estimated gross domestic product (GDP) by 4.9% for 2022.

The revised figures reflect changes to how the agency measures economic activity, including improved data sources, updated industry weightings and better estimates of activity in the informal and illegal economy.

Stats SA reported that South Africa’s GDP at current prices stood at R7 trillion in 2022, compared with the previous estimate of R6.7 trillion.



The agency’s comprehensive rebasing and benchmarking exercise also revised the estimated size of the economy in 2025 upwards by 5.3%, from R7.642 trillion to R8.044 trillion.

The revisions do not mean that South Africa suddenly produced more goods and services. Instead, they provide an updated estimate of economic activity that was already taking place.

Illegal mining contributes to revised GDP figures

Mining recorded the largest increase in its contribution to the economy following the revision, with its weighting increasing by 12.5%.

Stats SA attributed this primarily to improved coverage of illegal mining, an activity that has expanded amid rising gold prices.

The agency has also incorporated additional estimates of previously undermeasured economic activity, including illegal gambling and e-hailing services.

The non-observed economy – which includes informal, illicit and illegal activities that are not fully captured through conventional data collection – accounted for 8.7% of South Africa’s total economic activity in 2022.



That represents R551 billion, compared with a previously estimated share of 7.3%.

Stats SA has progressively expanded its measurement of this part of the economy over successive benchmarking exercises. Earlier additions included informal traders, shebeens, informal recycling and subsistence agriculture.

Finance sector sees a major revision

Finance, real estate and business services recorded the second-largest increase in industry weighting, rising by 9.1%.

At the 2022 base year, the revised GDP estimate was R324 billion higher than the previous estimate.

The finance industry contributed R127 billion of that increase, largely because of a methodological change in how Stats SA measures rent for owner-occupied homes.

Trade and mining each contributed a further R61 billion to the upward revision.

On the expenditure side, household consumption was the largest contributor to the revised estimate. Stats SA attributed this to the inclusion of data from its Income and Expenditure Survey, alongside improved measurement of owner-occupied rent and the non-observed economy.

Why has Stats SA changed its GDP calculations?

National statistical agencies periodically update their methods to reflect changes in how economies operate.

Stats SA said rebasing and benchmarking exercises are typically conducted every five years in line with international best practice.

The latest exercise changes the base year used to calculate GDP in volume terms from 2015 to 2022. It also incorporates new and updated information from Stats SA surveys and other sources, alongside methodological improvements.

The purpose is to provide a more accurate picture of the economy’s size and structure.

The revised figures show that some sectors account for a larger share of economic activity than previously estimated, while the improved measurement of the non-observed economy provides a more comprehensive view of activity outside conventional reporting systems.

What does the revised GDP mean for South Africans?

The upward revision provides a more complete statistical picture of South Africa’s economy, but it does not automatically mean that households are wealthier or that living standards have improved.

GDP measures economic production, not how income is distributed among households or whether individuals have experienced an improvement in their financial circumstances.

The revised figures also do not, by themselves, indicate that economic growth has accelerated. They reflect changes in the measurement and estimation of economic activity.

Stats SA’s updated national accounts will allow policymakers, businesses and researchers to work with a revised picture of the country’s economic structure.

The agency has published further details of the exercise in its report on the benchmarked and rebased estimates of gross domestic product for 2026.

World.title: Nations Championship: What the Springboks need from France and Ireland
World.content:
The Springboks must beat France and Ireland to keep pace in the Nations Championship. Image: Springbok Rugby website.

The Springboks’ Nations Championship campaign resumes in around a week.

South Africa are set to face Italy in Turin, with their trophy ambitions on the line.

Here’s why Rounds 5 and 6 could matter more for Rassie Erasmus and the team.



2026 Nations Championship: Where things stand

The Springboks are first on the Southern Hemisphere table, according to the Nations Championship website.

New Zealand are second and are the only other unbeaten team in the competition.

The two giants are level, but South Africa leads thanks to a massive 30-point difference.

However, they are all too aware that a single bad result opens the door for the All Blacks.

On the Northern Hemisphere table, France are top with 2 wins from 3 games.

Scotland have been impressive to hold on to second place and are a single point behind.



England and Ireland, placed third and fourth, remain within closing distance.

Like South Africa, France are one poor game away from losing their lead.

Matches ahead for the Springboks and All Blacks

The Nations Championship fixture page highlights each team’s path to the final round.

The Springboks visit Stade de France on 13 November to meet Les Bleus.

A week later, on 21 November, they face the Dublin Arena and Ireland.

By comparison, New Zealand have a slightly easier path to the final, on paper.

They take on Scotland on 7 November, but this is not likely to be a walkover.

Next up for the All Blacks is Wales on 14 November, at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

Their final fixture could be the decider as England wait at Twickenham Stadium on 21 November.

World.title: SA looks beyond US as AGOA uncertainty mounts
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Government has announced South Africa is prepared for any outcome as it awaits a US decision on its eligibility for AGOA trade benefits in 2027.



Trade, Industry and Competition Minister Parks Tau said engagements with Washington DC aimed at stabilising trade and investment relations will continue.



He said new markets have also opened for South African exports.



"If the United States' concerns remain, South Africa will have 60 days to address them before any action, full or partial, could take effect," Tau said.



"We will continue to engage the U.S. to stabilise trade and investment relations.



"Companies on both sides need a normalised trade environment because of existing value chains in key sectors. So colleagues, we are ready whatever the decision."



Tau added that South Africa was implementing its Cabinet-approved industrial development strategy and diversifying export markets across Africa, India, Saudi Arabia, the European Union, the United Kingdom, ASEAN, Mercosur and China.



He also highlighted progress in trade negotiations with the EU to protect hybrid and electric vehicle exports, an interim arrangement for steel, and new market opportunities for South African citrus, avocados, grapes and apples.

World.title: State must prove link to incitement - Mpofu tells court in Zuma-Sambudla case
World.content:
DURBAN - Advocate Dali Mpofu is demanding that the state prove someone actually broke the law because of Duduzile Zuma-Sambudla’s social media posts during the July 2021 riots.

Mpofu said without that link, the state doesn't have a case.

Zuma-Sambudla, who is accused of incitement to commit terrorism and public violence linked to the July 2021 unrest, is on trial in the Durban High Court.

"Was there any connection or link between whatever she did and the looters? Or anyone else that was that way inclined? The answer was that no. I think he came to the research. I do not believe the state case is that she is the cause of those unrests. But I believe the state case is that the incitement was through social media. So that is where their case is built.

"The point I'm making, my lord, is that whether it was through social media or a megaphone or whatever, it doesn't matter. There must still be an 'incitee'. That's the point, really. You cannot have incitement .That's the crux of this case," Mpofu said.

World.title: Two dead in rock spire collapse at tourist site in Turkey's Cappadocia
World.content:
CAPPADOCIA - A landslide triggered by heavy rainfall caused a rock spire to collapse in Turkey's UNESCO World Heritage-listed Cappadocia region on Thursday, killing at least two people, officials said.

Turkey's Cappadocia region, a magnet for tourists from around the world, is home to cone-shaped rock formations known as "fairy chimneys", created by ancient volcanic activity.

"According to initial findings, two people were killed and five others injured in the incident," Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said on X.

"Search and rescue teams are continuing intensive, coordinated operations to locate any other victims who may be trapped under the debris," he said.

The incident occurred at 3:15 pm local time (1215 GMT) when a landslide triggered a rockfall in the town of Goreme near the open-air museum, local governor Huseyin Kok said.

The area was closed to the public following the collapse, according to reports.

Eyewitnesses reported hearing a loud noise as the rock spire near an open car parking lot fell.

Television footage showed heavy machinery digging through the rubble as rescue teams gather at the site in an effort to recover people trapped beneath the debris.

"Our search and rescue operations at the scene are ongoing. The government is continuing its efforts at the scene with all available resources," Kok said.

Turkey's culture and tourism ministry has launched restoration work in the region to help preserve the fragile rock formations from climate-related damage, natural erosion and human activity.

In 2024, another rockfall was reported in Cappadocia, although no deaths or injuries were recorded.

The Cappadocia region, a major tourist attraction known for its rock-carved underground cities and early Christian churches, is also famed for hot-air ballooning, a thriving industry that sees dozens of balloons take to the skies on clear mornings.

But concerns have been raised about safety following a series of accidents.

World.title: Voices of Change | Protecting Children Beyond The Hospital: Prof Anrie le Roux On The SCAN Programme | 29 October 2026
World.content:
A Medical System Must Know How To Act When An Injury Does Not Add Up

A hospital emergency unit can heal a fractured bone, treat a burn, or mend a physical wound. But in cases of suspected child maltreatment, treating the body is only part of the responsibility. The more difficult and consequential question is what is happening in the child's life outside the hospital walls.

In South Africa, where child abuse and neglect remain deeply prevalent, recognizing the signs requires looking far beyond immediate medical symptoms. It demands a systematic and multi-disciplinary approach that bridges medicine, forensic practice, and child law.

The Space Between Suspicion And Certainty

For specialized child-protection teams, such as the SCAN (Suspected Child Abuse and Neglect) programme at Chris Hani Baragwanath Academic Hospital, clinical assessment begins with a rigorous standard of caution.

When a child presents with injuries, such as a skull fracture or unexplained bruising, caregivers often offer explanations. However, clinical evaluation tests whether the stated mechanism of injury aligns with the child's developmental stage and physical reality. A three-month-old infant who cannot yet sit or crawl cannot sustain certain impact injuries through accidental bumps.

Bridging the gap between suspicion and certainty requires ruling out alternative medical explanations while methodically investigating red flags. Because medical professionals are designated as mandatory reporters by law, recognizing these inconsistencies carries profound legal and ethical obligations. Failing to report suspected abuse not only leaves a vulnerable child unprotected but exposes clinicians to legal liability, including fines and imprisonment.

The Risk Of Fragmented Care

The danger of a fragmented healthcare system is stark. When hospitals focus solely on physical treatment without engaging multidisciplinary support, children can slip through the cracks. Tragic cases underscore how vulnerable a child remains if returned to an unsafe environment without proper statutory oversight and long-term psychosocial tracking.

Effective child protection cannot operate in silos. Paediatrics identifies the physical and behavioural red flags, such as sudden withdrawal, bedwetting, or unexplained developmental regression. Forensic medicine handles investigative medical examinations, while social development services and statutory authorities exercise the legal powers required to remove or place children safely. Furthermore, allied health professionals, including psychologists, speech therapists, and occupational therapists, play an essential long-term role in helping children cope with trauma and rebuild their lives.

Beyond Survival: Building Systems That Allow Children To Thrive

The ultimate objective of specialized child-protection programmes extends beyond acute medical recovery. It is to ensure that children not only survive trauma but are given the support, safety, and stability needed to grow into healthy, functional adults.

Expanding dedicated resources, strengthening training for healthcare workers across all levels of experience, and ensuring continuous intersectoral collaboration remain critical steps for South African healthcare. Protecting a child often begins with someone noticing, asking one more question, and refusing to let uncertainty become inaction, because early intervention can fundamentally change what happens next.

References

· Chris Hani Baragwanath Academic Hospital. SCAN Programme overview.

· Surgeons for Little Lives. SCAN Program institutional partnership.

· South African Children's Act and Mandatory Reporting Regulations.

· World Health Organization. Child Maltreatment Guidelines.

World.title: 'Cat' Matlala's fraud case postponed to next year
World.content:
PRETORIA - Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala will return to court on 11 February 2027 in his property fraud case.

Matlala and his co-accused appeared in the Pretoria Magistrate's Court, where the matter postponed for the finalisation of financial investigations.



Matlala, his wife Tsakane, his sister Claudette Masethe and Gift Makofane face charges of fraud, forgery and uttering.

The State has alleged they falsified documents in January 2025 to secure a R95,000-a-month lease for a Waterkloof property.



Matlala also faces a charge of contravening the Identification Act, linked to an allegedly forged Eswatini ID.



He abandoned his bail bid, while his co-accused are on R20,000 bail each.
