World.title: Accusations over De la Espriella’s narco ties “lack conclusive or solid evidence,” says Colombia’s justice minister
World.content:
Colombia’s Justice Minister, Ivan Cancino, downplayed the evidence of ties between President Abelardo de la Espriella and drug traffickers that was displayed in Congress by opposition Senator Ivan Cepeda.

In a video, Cancino said that “political oversight is a fundamental tool of our democracy. However, it cannot become an arena for launching accusations without proving and substantiating them.”

The justice minister admitted that the pieces of evidence provided to Congress “may seem serious,” but “lack conclusive or solid evidence, as well as any support that could jeopardize the innocence and the presumption of innocence of our president.”

It is not just about displaying organizational charts, deeds from over a decade ago, and business transactions to construct a narrative that supports neither judicial decisions nor the documentary, testimonial, circumstantial, or expert backing required for these types of accusations. Ivan Cancino

Cancino accused the opposition of remaining “silent regarding the grave scandals involving corruption, drug trafficking, and even alleged sexual abuse, as well as fiscal irresponsibility and possible links to criminal organizations that surrounded the previous government. ”

The justice minister was forced to come out after Cepeda showed Congress evidence of De la Espriella’s business ties with multiple convicted drug traffickers and announced criminal complaints against the president.

De la Espriella’s law firm rose to prominence during the demobilization of paramilitary organization AUC with whom he created a foundation that sought to justify the paramilitary violence that terrorized much of Colombia in the 1990’s and 2000s.

Once the ties between the AUC and elected politicians became known, the president ended up defending many of the “parapoliticians” in court.

According to Cepeda, De la Espriella plays a key role in a “revolving door” system that could end up benefiting the very drug traffickers and corrupt politicians that have paid the president for his legal defense in the past.

World.title: Colombia’s opposition announces criminal charges against De la Espriella over ties to drug traffickers
World.content:
Colombia’s opposition leader, senator Ian Cepeda, accused President Abelardo de la Espriella of leading an agrarian counter-reform designed to benefit land-owning clans and convicted drug traffickers.

During a congressional debate, Cepeda claimed that De la Espriella put allies of drug traffickers and paramilitaries in charge of key state institutions responsible for land distribution and asset forfeiture.

The president and his appointees are part of a revolving door system of people who, before being appointed to government positions, defended the interests of drug traffickers and paramilitaries associated with De la Espriella and his businesses, according to the opposition leader.

For example, the president put Diana Patrica Bravo, a former prosecutor and partner at his law firm De la Espriella Lawyers, in charge of The Society of Special Assets (SAE), which controls assets that were seized from drug traffickers.

The leader of the leftist Historic Pact party showed financial statements of one of De la Espriella’s companies, Dominio De la Espriella, that would prove that in between 38% and 40% of its capital deposits came from the family and corporate network of Hugues Rodríguez, a.k.a. Comandante Barbie, a former paramilitary financier who was charged with drug trafficking in the US.

The SAE would control more than 130 properties of Comandante Barbie.

De la Espriella family construction firm, Cosenza S.A.S., made property purchases in the city of Monteria directly with individuals under investigation for money laundering and illicit enrichment, according to Cepeda.

The president’s ex-wife, Yoly Beatriz Illidge, was appointed Superintendent of Notaries, making her “directly responsible for inspecting and monitoring all land entries and records issued by restitution judges throughout the country,” according to Cepeda.

De la Espriella is an associate of drug traffickers, owns assets purchased from drug traffickers, and defends drug traffickers from within the national government. Senator Ivan Cepeda

Last but not least, Agriculture Minister Indalecio Dangond “arrived at this post to execute an agrarian counter-reform at the service of paramilitary land-grabbers, foreign capital, and agro-industrial partners” while blocking investments for small farmers and displacement victims, the opposition leader stated.

Cepeda vowed that he would give the dossier to the United States Department of Justcie and to “Congressmen of the Democratic Party, given that mister De la Espriella is a US citizen.”

The opposition leader additionally promised to file criminal charges against the president and his agriculture minister in Colombia.

World.title: Colombia’s government claims Petro exploited 48 women as president
World.content:
The administration chief of Colombia’s President Abelardo De la Espriella told Congress that former President Gustavo Petro hired at least 48 women who were “trapped and exploited” for presidential parties.

During a hearing, DAPRE director Carlos Andres Rios claimed that Petro had 48 women “working in the Presidency, who were unfortunately exploited through temporary work contracts.”

We’re going to prove this to the Colombian people: how, unfortunately, the Casa de Nariño was set up, organized, and designed not for governing, but for partying there every day, bringing women there and engaging in behavior we should not be engaging in—behavior that sets a bad example. DAPRE director Carlos Andres Rios

“Forty-eight women are already speaking with us about how, through a contract and an OPS, they were trapped and exploited in order to be with President Petro,” said Rios.

Former DAPRE director Angie Rodriguez, who was sacked by Petro in July, doubled down on her successor’s allegations and asked the former president to prove that the president managed a network of women, including child transvestites.

Were there transvestite children there? Answer me, Mr. President. Were there transvestite children there? I am asking you a question, and I have every right to ask it. Were there? And if there weren’t, uh… prove that what I am saying is a lie. Angie Rodriguez

Last but not least, far-right magazine Semana published an interview with a woman identified as Deicy Jimenez, who claimed she as hired by Petro after meeting him on an adult website.

Jimenez even told Semana’s former presidential candidate Vicky Davila she trafficked drugs for the former president when he was senator.

VD: What happened on the day you say you transported drugs for Petro? DJ: Yes, I was traveling, and he asked me as a favor to bring him some drugs. VD: Were you outside of Bogotá? DJ: Yes. VD: How do you recall that favor Petro asked of you? DJ: He asked me as the favor to bring him some drugs. VD: Did you buy them? DJ: Yes, I bought them somewhere. He gave me money. VD: Did he give it to you in cash or deposit it for you? DJ: In cash. VD: How much money? DJ: Three million pesos. VD: What kind of drugs did you buy? DJ: Cocaine. VD: Where did you buy it? DJ: I bought it from some people. I can’t say (publicly) their names or the location. VD: Is it a gang? DJ: Yes. VD: Did he know you were going to buy the drugs from that gang? DJ: Yes. VD: At that time, was he a senator or the president? DJ: A senator. VD: How did you bring that drug in? DJ: I brought it through the airport. VD: You mean, on a plane? DJ: Yeah. VD: Did you get on a plane with Petro’s drugs? DJ: Yes. VD: How were the drugs packaged? DJ: In bags. VD: Like individual doses? DJ: Yes. VD: And where did you hide the drugs? DJ: In my suitcase.

In a response, Petro denied having hired women for sex and claimed that the far-right attack were the result of authorities’ failure to sustain corruption allegations.

World.title: “Brazil and Colombia need each other,” says De la Espriella
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella recognized the election victory of his Brazilian counterpart Luiz Ignacio Lula, who defeated far-right candidate Flavio Bolsonaro on Sunday.

In a post on social media platform X, the Colombian President said that “in the Colombian presidential campaign, President Lula openly supported Ivan Cepeda, and I won. In the Brazilian campaign, I supported Bolsonaro, and Lula won.”

“Neither does Lula decide for Colombians, nor do I decide for Brazilians. THE PEOPLE DECIDE! And when the people speak at the polls, their will is respected because it is sacred,” the president added.

Lula and I have major and profound political and ideological differences, but we agree on one fundamental point: Brazil and Colombia need each other. No other consideration can take precedence over the interests of our nations. Colombia and Brazil are sister nations, facing enormous shared challenges and opportunities.

President Abelardo de la Espriella

De la Espriella stressed that “we have much to do and much work to carry out for the benefit of our peoples” an ought to “fight against narco-terrorism and illegal mining, the protection of the Amazon, and the well-being of our citizens.”

Lula was the first leftist candidate and critic of US President Donald Trump to win an election, triggering celebrations among leftists throughout the continent.

De la Espriella, a US citizen, has been among the most fanatic among Trump supporter in trying to align his domestic policies to US foreign policy.

World.title: De la Espriella sacks interior minister after Congress bungles Colombia’s 2027 budget
World.content:
Colombia President Abelardo de la Espriella sacked Interior Minister Rodrigo Lara hours after Congress found a procedural flaw in the passed 2027 budget, which makes the law invalid.

In a post on social media platform X, De la Espriella briefly thanked Lara and announced he would be replaced by the ambassador to the Organization of American States, Alejandro Ordoñez.

The news surprised the interior minister, who suddenly left a congressional debate on a law to facilitate the demobilization of illegal armed groups after receiving a message on his phone.

Lara was apparently held responsible for the blunder of Congress, whose two houses approved the 2027 budget but with conflicting versions of an article on financial risk-coverage mechanisms for the Ministry of Finance.

By the time the error was detected, the budget debate had passed its October 20 deadline, forcing De la Espriella to issue a decree that would convert an older version of the budget bill into law.

The interior minister was the administration’s primary political liaison responsible for managing legislative procedure and whip operations in Congress.

Lara’s job was already under pressure after he failed to convince Congress to cede its presidency to the president’s candidate.

While Ordoñez returns from Washington, Justice Minister Ivan Cancino will assume the role of interior minister.

The incoming interior minister is an ultra conservative Catholic with ties to the Society of St. Pius X, which considers the modernizing reforms of the Catholic Church heresies and errors, and was declared in a schism with the church in June.

In Colombian politics and particularly among the opposition, Ordoñez is mainly remembered as the inspector general who illegally removed former President Gustavo Petro from his post as mayor of Bogota in 2013.

Petro was ultimately reinstated and would become president of the country in 2022.

World.title: Colombia’s Congress approves De la Espriella’s 2027 budget
World.content:
Colombia’s Congress agreed to increase the government’s 2027 budget despite promises by President Abelardo de la Espriella to reduce public spending.

Next year’s budget will be COP634.9 trillion, almost $204 billion, which is 16% more than last year’s budget and 10% higher than the proposal made by former President Gustavo Petro.

According to Finance Minister Miguel Gomez, the budget seeks to bring the State’s finances in line with reality.

The budget was approved in both the Senate and the House of Representatives with the support of De la Espriella’s government coalition.

The Historic Pact, the only leftist opposition party, rejected the budget and boycotted the vote.

On behalf of the national government, I would like to thank you all for your work over the past few months in passing the budget. I would also like to thank the opposition for the strength with which they defended their views. The message that Congress has sent today regarding the government’s economic policy is very important. It is the first step toward putting the country’s economy back on track toward growth, fiscal responsibility, and addressing the nation’s needs. Finance Minister Miguel Gomez

The budget seeks to reimpose the neoliberal model that had been abandoned by Petro and reduce public debt.

According to Green Party representative Jaime Raul Salamanca, who opposed the budget, funding for free higher education was cut in half from COP800 billion ($254 million) to COP400 billion (127 million).

“This cut raises concerns about its potential impact on the continuity and scope of this policy, which has enabled thousands of young people to enroll in public institutions of higher education,” said Salamanca.

The budget also cut the budget for the war crimes tribunal JEP, which could endanger the future of the peace process with the FARC and is opposed by the government.

World.title: De la Espriella announces “open, resolute, and patriotic struggle against wokeism”
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella announced an “open, resolute, and patriotic struggle against wokeism” as part of his “cultural counterrevolution.”

During a visit to the Culture Ministry, De la Espriella described wokeism as “an ideological paradigm that aims to transform moral, cultural, and social foundations in the West, perverting values, family tradition, and national identity.”

According to the president, Culture Minister Paola Holguin was a general in the “cultural counterrevolution.”

Culture has an enormous capacity to shape society, and that is why the State has a moral, inescapable, and political duty to prevent cultural spaces from being taken over by social communism, which is atheist and an enemy to the fundamental values upon which the nation of Colombia is built. This is where that cultural counterrevolution will begin. President Abelardo de la Espriella

De la Espriella said that Holguin, the daughter of a reported money launderer, would lead the “Culture War” against the “extreme left,” which has “permeated all parts of society, particularly the cultural and academic spheres.”

I want to be clear about this: we are going to wage an open, resolute, and patriotic struggle against wokeism, which is nothing more than an ideological movement that aims to transform the moral, cultural, and social foundations of the West, corrupting values, family tradition, and national identity. President Abelardo de la Espriella

Earlier in the day, the National Museum removed all references to members of the exterminated Patriotic Union party, slain guerrilla leader and presidential candidate Carlos Pizarro, and the struggle for the rights of Colombia’s LGBT+ community.

References to Colombia’s former guerrilla movements was “terrorism apology, which is “exactly what we have come to confront” in an attempt to “recover pride for Colombian culture.”

Atheists, the Pizarro family and gay rights activists rejected the president’s attempts to remove them from mainstream culture.

World.title: Colombia’s first lady promises transparency over earthquake donations
World.content:
Colombia’s first lady, Ana Lucia Pineda, vowed to reveal how much money she collected and spent in response to the August 10 earthquake that affected hundreds of thousands of people.

Amid mounting public pressure about where the money had gone, Pineda went on the morning program of public television channel Nuestro Caribe to promise that her foundation, Luz y Sonrisas, will take its finances public on Friday.

Carrying a white folder, the wife of President Abelardo de la Espriella stressed that “in the foundation’s accounts rest all, absolutely all of the monies from the donations we received during the ‘Colombia One Single Heart’ campaign” that was announced on August 12.

“A lie is not going to tear down the truth of who I am or what I represent, or how my children recognize me,” said Pineda.

Luz y Sonrisas was one of three NGO’s that were promoted by the De la Espriella government to collect contributions for victims of the earthquake.

Pineda’s foundation was the only one that could receive contributions from abroad.

Earlier in the week, news program Noticias Uno revealed that her foundation that was founded on July 7 lacked the tax exemption that would allow it to accept donations, a process that usually takes months.

In a press statement, tax office DIAN subsequently said that it had granted the tax exemption to the first lady and that she could legally accept financial contributions.

Pineda did not say how much money she had received, but said that she stopped supporting the initial relief efforts “because the humanitarian aid was sufficient, it was huge.”

The first lady vowed she had saved the donations for the reconstruction phase “because I have also taken the initiative to build and return to the victims a house that is durable for the families who lost everything.”

World.title: The IMF urges Argentina to “stay the course” despite doubts over growth and country risk
World.content:
The IMF urges Argentina to “stay the course” despite doubts over growth and country risk

29th Thursday, October 2026 - 16:26 UTC Full article

On Tuesday, IMF staff and the Argentine authorities reached agreement on the third review of the Extended Fund Facility programme, which would allow a disbursement of about US$900 million

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Thursday urged Argentina’s government to stick with its economic programme as the best way to reduce country risk, and set out four measures to turn the gains of stabilisation into growth and jobs, at a time when the press is warning of a possible technical recession.

“Our best advice for Argentina to continue reducing its country risk is to continue with its strong policy implementation, that is, to keep implementing the programme as it has been doing,” IMF spokeswoman Julie Kozack told her press briefing in Washington. She added that accumulating net international reserves and strengthening the external position are “really fundamental” to that end. “Our overall message on Argentina is really to stay the course with strong policies while broadening the benefits,” she said.

Asked about the possibility of the economy recording two consecutive quarters of contraction, Kozack said the Fund and the government agreed on “the importance of expanding the gains of stabilisation into stronger growth and job creation”. She listed four agreed measures: deepening capital and mortgage markets to widen access to financing; improving labour market flexibility to support private-sector employment; advancing recently awarded infrastructure concessions; and facilitating strategic investment under the Incentive Regime for Large Investments (RIGI), where approved projects already exceed US$76 billion, according to the Fund.

On Tuesday, IMF staff and the Argentine authorities reached agreement on the third review of the Extended Fund Facility programme, which would allow a disbursement of about US$900 million. Kozack said the board could consider it in early December. The Fund said the programme “continues to deliver impressive results, despite a more complex global environment”: net reserves exceeded the June target by about US$4 billion, the Central Bank bought nearly US$16 billion this year and the Treasury raised more than US$5 billion in local markets. The government, backed by official creditors, also secured US$3.2 billion in guaranteed international bank financing and is working on a further US$1 billion before year-end.

The agreement keeps the target of a primary surplus of 1.4% of GDP for 2026 and a similar effort in 2027, along with the exchange rate band regime. In October, the IMF cut its 2026 growth forecast for Argentina from 3.5% to 2.1%.

World.title: Falklands unveil 2026-2030 Islands Plan, with a sovereign wealth fund for energy revenues
World.content:
Falklands unveil 2026-2030 Islands Plan, with a sovereign wealth fund for energy revenues

29th Thursday, October 2026 - 14:49 UTC Full article

Under the first priority, the Plan aims to create the conditions for the economy to grow and diversify “while also ensuring effective regulation of industries”

The Falkland Islands Legislative Assembly on Thursday published the Islands Plan 2026-2030, the programme of government for the current Assembly, which provides for a sovereign wealth fund so that energy sector revenues benefit future generations and acknowledges that the government faces some of the largest projects in its history, with a capital programme of more than £300 million. Executive Council formally adopted the Plan on October 27.

The document, signed by the eight Members of the Legislative Assembly — Stacy Bragger, Lewis Clifton, Dean Dent, Jack Ford, Michael Goss, Dot Gould, Cheryl Roberts and Roger Spink — is built around a single vision: “a strong, secure and sustainable future for the Falkland Islands”. From it flow three priorities: providing strategic and proactive stewardship for the long-term prosperity of the Islands, building a sustainable and diversified economy for the future, and enabling a healthy, capable and prosperous community “with a strong sense of identity”.

An unprecedented capital programme

In the foreword, Members note that the Assembly has inherited “a substantial programme of work”: a capital programme of more than £300 million covering a new port, energy projects, improved waste management, housing and the development of land for release. These, together with the future of telecommunications and “the regulation of a developing hydrocarbons industry”, are “among the largest undertakings the Falkland Islands Government has ever embarked upon”.

The authors acknowledge the limits facing a small government. Each project “demands significant time, money, and expertise, and there is a limit to how much a government of our size can carry at once, and to what we can afford while living within our means”. Members have therefore chosen not to set a fixed four-year delivery plan: priorities will be set on a rolling 12-month basis “so that timeframes stay realistic and resources go where they are needed most”.

First-year priorities

For the first twelve months, the Assembly sets six priorities: progressing the Sovereign Wealth Fund for energy sector revenues; speeding up the release of housing plots and the building of government homes; delivering the next phase of the wind farm; introducing modernised anti-discrimination legislation; updating education law, including support for children with additional needs; and reviewing the Permanent Residence Permit system.

A tracking document setting out actions, owners and milestones will be brought to Executive Council, and a public version will be published “so the community can follow progress and hold the Assembly to account”.

Economy, energy and resilience

Under the first priority, the Plan aims to create the conditions for the economy to grow and diversify “while also ensuring effective regulation of industries”, review the National Infrastructure Plan and ensure delivery of the new port, energy projects, waste management and the healthcare and education estates. It also includes strengthening “national resilience” against evolving risks through intelligence-led risk management, modern technology, cross-government coordination and “international partnerships”, and a new framework for telecommunications.

On the economy, the government pledges to help local businesses meet the demands “of the new energy sector and other emerging sectors”, to work with partners on additional flight connectivity, and to review the Tourism Development Strategy, the tax system, aspects of the immigration system and health and social care provision. It also plans an inward investment strategy setting out “a clear framework for acceptable international investment” and national branding for the Islands’ economic, tourism and public diplomacy activities.

Identity and a voice in the world

The third priority covers housing, equalities, education and health, and mechanisms to monitor the social and economic effects of growth. It includes developing a set of “Falkland Islands Values” to communicate “our British values and our unique identity as Falkland Islanders, at home and abroad”, and a commitment to make “the voice of the Falkland Islands heard around the world” through public diplomacy and support for national sports teams, promoting “our right to self-determination”.

“By taking these bold steps, we are securing the right of Falkland Islanders to determine their own future,” the foreword concludes. The back cover reproduces a plaque bearing the words of then British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher on April 3, 1982: “They are few in number but they have the right to live in peace, to choose their own way of life and to determine their own allegiance.”

The Plan is published as development of the Sea Lion oil field north of the archipelago advances, the revenues from which would feed the future sovereign wealth fund. Argentina, which claims sovereignty over the islands, has imposed sanctions on companies linked to the project and asked the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea to halt it; the hearing will take place in Hamburg on November 10 and 11. The document does not mention Argentina.

Islands Plan 2026-2030 by MercoPress

World.title: UK Government aims to spend 3% of GDP on defense by 2030, Chancellor says, but not everyone's convinced
World.content:
UK Government aims to spend 3% of GDP on defense by 2030, Chancellor says, but not everyone's convinced

29th Thursday, October 2026 - 08:42 UTC Full article

Former Defense Secretary Dan Jarvis sets out Defense Investment Plan to MPs

The UK Government will aim to spend 3% of economic output on defense by 2030, and will plot a course for the target at next year's spending review, Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey has said. Work is underway to reach the target – and Britain's promise to NATO to spend 3.5% of GDP on defense by 2035 – in a “fiscally sustainable way”, the Chancellor said, indicating that raising defense spending further could in part come from making cuts elsewhere.

Mr. Healey's target of 3% by 2030 would fulfil a threshold he thought would be missed under Sir Keir Starmer's premiership, which sparked his resignation as defense secretary in June this year.

The announcement was welcomed by Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte, Defense Secretary Wes Streeting and the author of the Strategic Defense Review (SDR), Lord Robertson of Port Ellen.

Meanwhile, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch criticized his announcement as a “plan to have a plan”.

As he delivered his first Budget, the Chancellor told the Commons: “This year, our defense budget is £14bn higher than it was in the Conservatives’ last year of government.

”At the spending review next year, I confirm that I will set out the details of how we will meet our Nato commitment to spend 3.5% of GDP on defense by 2035, with a target date for 3% in 2030.And today I am getting work underway to get there in a fiscally sustainable way.“

Reaching the 3% target by the end of the decade is estimated by the Office for Budget Responsibility to cost an extra £17.3bn in 2029-30.

And Mr Healey hinted that reaching the commitment could come at the cost of spending elsewhere, telling MPs: ”That will include looking hard at public spending, as I have done to fund the Defense Investment Plan (DIP) today.But I am also determined to use more innovative financing, alongside the private sector and our international allies.“

Defense will rise to a 2.7% share of the economy by 2027 Mr Healey also committed at the Budget to ”fully funding“ a £4.7bn black hole in the Defense Investment Plan, left over by Sir Keir Starmer. The £4.7bn shortfall will be funded ”through reprioritization of capital budgets“, according to the published Budget document.

Departments across Government will be asked to reduce their capital budgets by 1% between 2027-28 and 2029-30 to raise some £3bn. The remaining £1.7bn shortfall will be made up from an “unallocated contingency in the Treasury’s capital reserve”.

The DIP, one of Sir Keir's final major announcements as prime minister, promised an extra £15bn of funding for the UK defense sector but only committed £10.3bn to it, leaving the rest for Mr. Healey to find. The extra cash means that government spending on defense will rise to a 2.7% share of the economy by 2027.

Responding to the Budget, Tory leader Kemi Badenoch said Mr Healey had not met his pledge and was making troops unsafe.

Mrs Badenoch said: ”He should have set out a plan for 3% today. So, now he is the man who is increasing risk to personnel on operations; he is the man who is making our country less safe; he has failed his own test. This is on him and no-one will ever forget. If he had any decency he would resign again today.“

She added: ”What he's done is he’s given himself a bit of breathing space until next year. Instead, what we have is a plan to have a plan. I bet (Vladimir) Putin's really scared now.“

Budget reaction in the defense world One of the SDR authors and former Nato secretary general Lord Robertson of Port Ellen said: ”John Healey is acting in the national interest – and has done exactly what he said was needed for defense in his resignation letter, by setting a head-mark for 3% in 2030.

“I am strongly in favor of innovative ways of financing defense – and this is a credible route to get more into UK defense. Today’s announcements strengthen UK leadership in NATO once again.”

Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey pressed the Government to push for a “European rearmament bank” which he said would “bring our allies together behind a shared vision of defence investment to protect our continent from Putin”.

Former defense secretary and Scots Guards officer Sir Ben Wallace was quick to criticize the Budget, highlighting the way he said it would affect people like Mr Healey's own son, who is a member of the Army Reserve.

Sir Ben posted on X: ”The MOD faces a real term cut to day-to-day spending of nearly 0.5% (RDEL) in 27/28.That's money we spend on training, ammunition, maintenance and operations. So the Chancellor's son in the reserves will have even less training and ammo.“

His comments were echoed by Afghanistan veteran Mike Martin, who said: ”The Chancellor has handed another year to Putin by deferring decisions to increase defense spending in today's Budget.

“The Government says we should prepare for war with Russia in three years, but is totally comfortable wasting one of those years standing still as it defers increasing defense spending until the next Spending Review.

”By then it will be 18 months since the Chancellor resigned as defense secretary over the Government's failure to reach 3% of GDP.”

Mr Healey also announced plans that will see the Government work with private and international finance. A defense finance taskforce is being set up ahead of next year’s spending review. (Forces.net by Sian Grzeszczyk Melbourne).

World.title: IMF expects Brazil to become the 8th largest economy in the 2027 ranking
World.content:
IMF expects Brazil to become the 8th largest economy in the 2027 ranking

29th Thursday, October 2026 - 08:33 UTC Full article

Brazil in 2026 figures as the tenth largest global economy

Brazil is expected to return to eighth place in the global GDP ranking for 2027, overtaking Russia and Italy, according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and its World Economic Outlook report, released this month.

IMF points out that Brazil’s GDP, which measures the value of goods and services produced in the country, is expected to reach US$2.80 trillion next year. This year Brazil is expected to finish in tenth place. A trillion in 12 zeros.

Likewise for 2027, United States is expected to remain the world’s largest economy, followed by China, Germany, India, UK. Follows the IMF top ranking for next year,

1. United States: US$ 34.44 trillion

2. China: US$ 22.94 trillion

3. Germany: US$ 5.66 trillion

4. India: US$ 4.52 trillion

5. United Kingdom: US$ 4.49 trillion

6. Japan: US$ 4.47 trillion

7. France: US$ 3.65 trillion

8. Brazil: US$ 2.80 trillion

9. Italy: US$ 2.77 trillion

10. Russia: US$ 2.68 trillion

11. Canada US$ 2.63 trillion

According to the IMF’s projections, Brazil is expected to maintain that position through 2031, the final year covered by the forecast. Brazil’s highest position in the global GDP rankings was seventh, a ranking it held in 1995 and from 2010 through 2014.

The rising star. One of the highlights of the IMF’s forecast is India, which is expected to jump from sixth to fourth place, overtaking the United Kingdom and Japan. By 2031, India is projected to move into third place, ahead of Germany.

The United States and China are expected to retain the top two positions, in that order, through 2031.

World.title: Bolsonaro’s exit via Argentina further strains relations between Milei and Lula
World.content:
Bolsonaro’s exit via Argentina further strains relations between Milei and Lula

29th Thursday, October 2026 - 01:30 UTC Full article

Presidential spokesman Adrián Ravier said the government had “taken note of the result” of the Brazilian election but ruled out an official statement

Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro’s transit through Argentina, after he left Brazil despite a court ban and flew to Miami from Puerto Iguazú following his election defeat, has opened a new front in the strained relationship between the governments of Javier Milei and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, while the Casa Rosada maintains its refusal to congratulate the Brazilian president on his re-election.

Argentina’s National Migration Directorate confirmed that Bolsonaro, his wife and two daughters entered the country via the Tancredo Neves international bridge in Misiones province at 10.50 p.m. on Tuesday, with valid documents and “without any legal impediment”. About 40 minutes later they boarded a private plane belonging to Argentine company Baires Fly, which stopped in Guayaquil before reaching Miami. Brazilian Supreme Court Judge Alexandre de Moraes had ordered the senator to surrender his passports and barred him from leaving the country as part of an investigation into alleged money laundering. Bolsonaro will lose his parliamentary immunity in January when his term ends.

Presidential spokesman Adrián Ravier said the government had “taken note of the result” of the Brazilian election but ruled out an official statement, arguing that Lula did not congratulate Milei when he was elected in 2023. According to the newspaper Ámbito, Lula congratulated “the elected authorities” at the time, without naming Milei.

Bolsonaro’s departure fuelled suspicion in Argentina. According to La Nación, presidential adviser Santiago Caputo was in Misiones when the plane took off; the government has not commented on that report. Sources in the Misiones provincial government distanced themselves and said that if there had been an irregular operation by the migration agency or the Airport Security Police, it was up to the national government to explain. Opposition lawmakers filed a formal request for information in the Chamber of Deputies. In the letter he released from Miami, Bolsonaro thanked Milei for “his courage, his sense of justice and legality”, without specifying what he meant.

Bilateral relations are at one of their lowest points. Milei backed Bolsonaro during the campaign and called Lula a “thief” and a “jailbird”, prompting Brazil to recall its ambassador in Buenos Aires for consultations in July. Brazil is Argentina’s main trading partner.

The episode coincided with another Argentine government decision pointing in the opposite direction: the ruling party amended the sovereignty defence bill to narrow sanctions on companies linked to hydrocarbon exploitation in the Falklands, following objections raised by the United States.

World.title: “True president”, then “leader”: Bolsonaro’s letter from the United States
World.content:
“True president”, then “leader”: Bolsonaro’s letter from the United States

29th Thursday, October 2026 - 01:17 UTC Full article

In the letter, Bolsonaro says he did not flee but refused to submit to “political persecution” and judicial harassment

Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who arrived in Miami on Wednesday after leaving Brazil despite a court ban, released a letter in which he presented himself as “the true president-elect of Brazil”, alleged “electoral fraud” without evidence and thanked Argentine President Javier Milei for his “courage”. About 30 minutes later the text was changed and Bolsonaro described himself instead as Brazil’s “leader”.

“I address the Brazilian people and the international community as the true president-elect of Brazil. First of all, I want to thank President Milei for his courage, his sense of justice and legality, and President Trump and the wonderful American people for welcoming me,” the first version read, shared by commentator Paulo Figueiredo and by the senator’s allies. According to the newspaper O Estado de S. Paulo, the text went through three versions. The first carried the coat of arms of the “Estados Unidos do Brazil”, which fell out of use in 1968, and was later corrected.

In the letter, Bolsonaro says he did not flee but refused to submit to “political persecution” and judicial harassment, and accuses Supreme Court Judge Cristiano Zanin, whom he calls “Lula’s former lawyer”, of making possible “a mathematical impossibility” by extending voting hours: that Lula gained more than ten million votes between the first and second rounds. The president went from 53.9 million votes on October 4 to 64.2 million on Sunday, in an election in which both campaigns focused on mobilising the roughly 33 million voters who abstained in the first round. The head of the Superior Electoral Court, Kassio Nunes Marques, appointed by the senator’s father, said on Monday that the extension did not alter the result.

Bolsonaro says he will lead the opposition from the United States and compares his departure with those of Charles de Gaulle, Rui Barbosa, José Martí, Juan Guaidó, Edmundo González and María Corina Machado. The State Department has granted visas to him and his family. President Donald Trump said on Monday that the Brazilian election “looked like another rigged election”.

Argentina’s National Migration Directorate confirmed that Bolsonaro entered the country via the Tancredo Neves bridge at Puerto Iguazú on Tuesday night, with valid documents and “without any legal impediment”, before flying to Miami on a private plane. The letter does not specify what the thanks to Milei refers to, and the Argentine government, which has also not congratulated Lula on his re-election, had not commented on it. Bolsonaro is under investigation at the Supreme Court for alleged money laundering, which he denies.

World.title: King Charles begins a Caribbean tour overshadowed by calls for slavery reparations
World.content:
King Charles begins a Caribbean tour overshadowed by calls for slavery reparations

29th Thursday, October 2026 - 01:11 UTC Full article

The British government has ruled out both a formal apology and reparations, and Buckingham Palace has said the King will follow that line, since both matters are for the government

King Charles III arrived in the Bahamas on Tuesday to begin a nine-day tour of the Caribbean, his first since acceding to the throne in 2022, which will also take him to Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda, where he will attend the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting. The trip is overshadowed by calls for an official apology and reparations for Britain’s role in the transatlantic slave trade.

The British government has ruled out both a formal apology and reparations, and Buckingham Palace has said the King will follow that line, since both matters are for the government. His aides insist, however, that the monarch, who will give three speeches during the tour, “will not shy away” from the subject and that the visit will not take place “in a bubble”. Charles remains head of state of the Bahamas and of Antigua and Barbuda, while Guyana has been a republic since 1970.

Pressure has grown in recent months. Commonwealth Secretary-General Shirley Botchwey has asked the King to apologise; Jamaica has filed a petition for reparations that the Privy Council will examine in March; and Ghana has promoted a UN resolution describing the transatlantic slave trade as the gravest crime against humanity. “I think it is the most defining moment for the Commonwealth since its creation,” said Patrick Vernon, UK representative of the Global Jamaica Diaspora Council. Labour MP Bell Ribeiro-Addy said the King “should realise that people would not keep raising the issue if his actions were anywhere near enough”. In Nassau, Rastafarian groups protested during the visit.

The Guyana stop is seen as the most delicate. The King will hold an audience with President Irfaan Ali, who has reiterated that his country deserves an apology, and the two will attend a reception marking 60 years of bilateral relations. The Palace hopes their personal relationship will smooth the meeting.

Charles has gone further than his predecessors in expressing his “personal sorrow” over the monarchy’s historical links to slavery. The Prince and Princess of Wales’s 2022 Caribbean tour was marked by criticism and by several countries announcing their intention to drop the monarchy.

World.title: Falklands approves bill on oil pollution emergencies in relation to offshore installations, and responsibilities
World.content:
Falklands approves bill on oil pollution emergencies in relation to offshore installations, and responsibilities

28th Wednesday, October 2026 - 15:10 UTC Full article

The Director of Mineral Resources will be the competent authority – “Falkland Islands contingency plan” and “offshore installations” used in the OPRC Regulations.

The Falkland Islands Executive Council has approved a set of Regulations 2026 to amend the Maritime (Oil Pollution Preparedness, Response and Co-operation Convention) Regulations 2019 (“the OPRC Regulations”) to make provision for the preparation and maintenance of oil pollution emergency plans in relation to offshore installations and to require the persons responsible for offshore installations to report oil incidents where oil is discharged into the sea.

Regulations 1 and 2 provide for the title and commencement of the Regulations. Regulation 3 provides that these Regulations amend the OPRC Regulations and the following regulations provide for specific amendments to be made to those Regulations.

Regulation 4 amends regulation 3 of the OPRC Regulations, which sets out the objects of those Regulations, to include making provision for the preparation and maintenance of oil pollution emergency plans in relation to offshore installations.

Regulation 5 amends regulation 4 of the OPRC Regulations which contains definitions of words and phrases used in those Regulations. It adds new definitions for words and phrases used in the 17 amended provisions and replaces the definitions of “competent authority” – with the effect that in relation to ships, ports, harbours and oil handling facilities the Falkland Islands Maritime Authority (FIMA) is the competent authority, but in relation to offshore installations, the Director of Mineral Resources will be the competent authority – “Falkland Islands contingency plan” and “offshore installations” used in the OPRC Regulations.

Regulation 6 amends regulation 6 of the OPRC Regulations which is the application provision, to provide that the OPRC Regulations will apply to offshore installations.

Regulation 7 amends regulation 14 of the OPRC Regulations to require an operator of an oil handling facility to ensure that no activities that pose a risk of an oil pollution incident are undertaken unless the facility has an oil pollution emergency plan approved by the authority.

Regulation 8 inserts a new Part 3A into the OPRC Regulations which makes specific provision for the preparation and maintenance of oil pollution emergency plans in relation to offshore installations.

New regulation 15A requires the responsible person for an offshore installation to prepare and maintain an oil pollution emergency plan for each offshore installation for which they are responsible, although the Director of Mineral Resources may permit joint plans in specified circumstances.

New regulation 15B requires the person preparing an oil pollution emergency plan for an offshore installation to take into account guidance issued by the Director of Mineral Resources and for the plan to comply with the requirements contained in the new Schedule to the OPRC Regulations, which is inserted by regulation 13.

New regulation 15C sets out the procedure for the submission of an oil pollution emergency plan for an offshore installation to the Director of Mineral Resources for approval and the dates by which an application must be submitted.

New regulation 15D provides that an approved oil pollution emergency plan must be reviewed every five years or before then if specified events occur. The Director of Mineral Resources may require an oil pollution emergency plan to be reviewed at any time.

New regulation 15E sets out the consequences if a responsible person for an offshore installation fails to review, submit or amend an oil pollution emergency plan. These are that an oil pollution emergency plan ceases to be approved for an offshore installation and, as a result of new regulation 15G(1), this will mean that no oil or gas operations can be carried out.

New regulation 15F gives the Director of Mineral Resources power to direct, after consultation with a responsible person, that an oil pollution emergency plan be amended if it is not compatible with the Falkland Islands contingency plan or is not appropriate for dealing with oil pollution incidents in the area of the offshore installation.

New regulation 15G sets out the duties imposed on a responsible person for an offshore installation. These include: ensuring that no oil or gas operations are carried out unless the offshore installation is subject to an oil pollution emergency plan approved by the Director of Mineral Resources; maintaining relevant equipment; and undertaking exercises. In the event of an oil pollution incident, the oil pollution emergency plan must be implemented (new regulation 15G(3)).

New regulation 15H imposes duties on the licensee (defined as a person to whom a licence has been granted by the Governor under section 6 of the Offshore Minerals Ordinance 1994) to ensure that where it appoints responsible persons, those persons are capable of satisfactorily carrying out 18 the functions and discharging their duties and that they have access to adequate financial resources to discharge their duties.

New regulation 15I requires a responsible person for an offshore installation who observes or is made aware of any event involving a discharge of oil, or probable discharge of oil, or the presence of oil in the sea to report it to the Director of Mineral Resources. Regulation 9 amends regulation 17 of the OPRC Regulations to set out the steps FIMA and the Director of Mineral Resources must take in response to a report of a discharge etc of oil.

Regulation 10 amends regulation 18 of the OPRC Regulations to now contain provision for the inspection of ships, harbours, ports, oil handling facilities and offshore installations and the powers under which the respective inspectors may operate.

Regulation 11 amends regulation 19 of the OPRC Regulations to introduce offences where a person fails to comply with or perform duties introduced by these Regulations.

Regulation 12 introduces a new regulation 20 in the OPRC Regulations which empowers the Director of Mineral Resources, FIMA and Governor to share information obtained for the purposes of the OPRC Regulations with other agencies.

Regulation 13 inserts a Schedule in the OPRC Regulations that sets out the requirements for an oil pollution emergency plan in respect of offshore installations.

Regulation 14 makes transitional provision. Published by the Attorney General’s Chambers, Stanley, Falkland Islands

World.title: Finding home in Mexico, one ordinary day at a time
World.content:
In July, I spent two weeks in New York visiting family. By then I had been living in Querétaro for almost two years, and the trip gave me an extended stretch away from the daily life I had built here. I enjoyed seeing people I love, moving through places tied to an earlier part of my life, and hearing English everywhere without having to work for it.

Somewhere during those two weeks, I began thinking about going home, and I realized that the place I meant was Querétaro.

I noticed the language only after it had already formed in my head. Home has always been a complicated word for me, attached to places, people and periods of my life that do not fit together as neatly as they once did. New York holds family and history for me, and Santa Fe was home before I moved to Mexico. Both remain part of me in different ways.

When the visit was ending, though, I was ready to return to my house, my routines and the life waiting for me in Querétaro.

Finding standard ground in new routines

Much of my first year in Mexico was organized around the experience of having moved. There were residency matters to settle, work to reconsider and a language I could use only imperfectly. I was learning how to do ordinary things in a place where the assumptions behind those things were often different from the ones I had known. Even buying bread could become a small encounter with the fact that I had crossed a border and was learning how to live on the other side of it.

I wrote about one of those encounters in my first Mexico News Daily column, when I described standing in a panadería three weeks after arriving and realizing I had answered the wrong question twice. At the time, that moment helped me recognize that I had crossed from visiting Mexico into living here.

I understand that crossing differently now. Becoming a resident happened fairly quickly. Becoming someone whose life is here has taken longer.

William Bridges spent much of his work distinguishing change from transition, a distinction that has occupied me professionally and personally for years. Change describes what happens in our circumstances. Transition is the internal process through which we gradually reorganize ourselves around what has happened. A person can move on a particular day, carry boxes into a new house, complete the required paperwork and still need considerable time before the new life begins to feel inhabited from the inside.

The quiet shift from novel to familiar

I spent much of my first year somewhere in that internal reorganization. Querétaro was the place where I lived, and I remained aware of living in Querétaro. I noticed differences constantly. I compared things with the U.S. more often than I realized, translated language in my head and carried an ongoing awareness that I was still learning the rules. The newness was sometimes exciting and sometimes tiring, and in either case it reminded me that I was elsewhere.

That awareness has begun to recede. I still notice Mexico, of course, and some days I notice it a great deal. My Spanish remains a work in progress, and I continue to encounter situations that remind me how much I have to learn about the culture I entered. Increasingly, though, a day in Querétaro is simply a day. I work, decide what to eat, answer messages, run errands, spend time with people I care about and go to bed without having spent much time thinking about the country in which any of it occurred.

When I imagined moving to Mexico, I naturally imagined the parts that made Mexico different. I thought about the pace, the language, the culture and what it might feel like to build a life here. What I could not imagine was the eventual disappearance of much of that self-consciousness. A life becomes familiar through repetition, through doing ordinary things often enough that they become part of the day instead of evidence that the day is happening somewhere new.

Building history through small moments

I saw another version of that recently in my own house. For nearly a year, my dining room table was simply there. Then I finally set it, and the room looked inhabited in a way it had not before. A week later, two kittens, Frida and Georgia, came to live with me, and suddenly there were food bowls to fill, veterinary appointments to arrange and two small creatures learning the boundaries of a house they seemed determined to investigate completely.

Their arrival made the ordinariness even more visible to me. I did not experience adopting them as another milestone in my relocation to Mexico. I experienced it as bringing two kittens home. They entered a life that already existed here, and within days they became part of its routines. I now spend considerably more time wondering what they are getting into than thinking about the fact that all three of us happen to be doing this in Querétaro.

My relationships here have changed in much the same way. Friendships now have history. There are conversations that refer back to other conversations, familiar jokes, plans that get made and changed, and the ordinary accommodations people make when they know one another well enough to stop explaining everything. My second column grew out of recognizing how much being known here had changed me. Home seems to take shape partly through that accumulated familiarity, when a place contains people who know something about who you are and expect you to still be there next week.

Accepting the ongoing learning process

Mexico can still stop me in the middle of an ordinary day. Yesterday I was at the dentist when a Paquetexpress delivery driver called because he had a package for me. What I understood afterward was that he was asking a very simple question: Was the gate I was trying to describe gray? Under the pressure of a phone call, with no gestures or context to help me, I could not get there. We eventually understood enough of each other to call it a draw, and he left the package. A few minutes later I was back to whatever I had been doing, amused at how quickly an ordinary day can remind me that there is still plenty I am learning.

Perhaps this is the part of relocation we talk about less often. We spend a great deal of time thinking about leaving, arriving, adjusting and belonging. Eventually the move itself begins to occupy less of the story. The new country becomes the place where birthdays happen, friendships acquire history, kittens move in, groceries need buying, packages get delivered after imperfect phone calls, work gets done, and you leave for a while and find yourself thinking about going home.

That was the word that caught me in July. By the end of the visit, I was ready to go home, and there was no question in my mind where I meant.

Mark Arcuri, PhD, is an integrative wellness coach, Associate Dean, and writer based in El Refugio, Querétaro. His first book, “A Life Aligned: The Journey to Allowing the Magic in Your Life” (A Life Aligned Press, 2026), is available in paperback, ebook and audiobook, and opens a trilogy on the inner work of transition. The second, “Paradise (re)Discovered,” arrives this fall. Learn more at drmarkarcuri.com.

World.title: Trade negotiations between Mexico and India have officially started
World.content:
India and Mexico signed the Terms of Reference (ToR) for negotiations on a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA) on Monday, as the two nations seek to expand bilateral trade and investment.

Mexico’s Deputy Minister of Foreign Trade Luis Rosendo Gutiérrez Romano and India’s Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal signed the ToR, which sets out a roadmap for negotiations, during Agrawal’s official visit to Mexico.

The move advances an understanding reached by President Claudia Sheinbaum and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the sidelines of the G7 Summit in Canada in June 2025 to strengthen the bilateral partnership.

“India and Mexico are ready to turn untapped potential into tangible prosperity through balanced, ambitious and mutually beneficial negotiations,” the Indian Embassy wrote on the X social media site on Monday.

The proposed agreement includes key areas, such as market access for goods, rules of origin, customs procedures, trade facilitation, dispute settlement, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, technical barriers to trade and trade remedies.

Both countries are aiming to develop a “mutually beneficial and balanced PTA,” India’s Department of Commerce stated, emphasizing that Mexico is an important market for Indian exporters and investors.

Merchandise trade between India and Mexico totaled US$8.74 billion in 2024, with $5.73 billion in Indian exports and $3.01 billion in Mexican exports, resulting in a $2.72 billion trade differential, according to data from the Directorate General of Commercial Intelligence and Statistics.

The development of a PTA will help expand bilateral trade, create business opportunities, boost investment flows and strengthen supply chains. Potential areas of cooperation include automobiles, chemicals, electronics, pharmaceuticals, agri-food, energy, critical minerals, medical devices and advanced manufacturing.

In a February meeting between Mexico’s Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard and India’s Ambassador to Mexico Pankaj Sharma, the two officials also highlighted the need to foster greater cooperation in priority sectors such as science, technology and digitalization.

During the recent visit, Gutiérrez Romano and Agrawal discussed a potential Mexican business mission to India in the first quarter of 2027 to help identify commercial opportunities and further strengthen ties.

In 2024, India’s primary exports to Mexico included light vehicles, with a value of US $880 million, motorcycles ($390 million), base metals ($760 million), auto parts ($740 million), mechanical machinery ($460 million) and textiles and clothing ($410 million).

Meanwhile, Mexico’s main exports to India included crude petroleum oil ($1.7 billion), smartphones ($270 million), and gold ($170 million).

With reports from CNCV TV18

World.title: After its success in Mexico, Airbnb’s free medical stays will expand under a new funding model
World.content:
After a successful pilot year in Mexico, Airbnb will allocate US $500 million over the next five years to expand its provision of free accommodations for people experiencing medical emergencies, natural disasters or domestic violence, company CEO Brian Chesky announced on Tuesday.

Building on a new funding model similar to the one used in Mexico, the independent non-profit arm of the online rental platform, under the name Airbnb.org (rather than simply Airbnb), will establish a $500 million fund by contributing 10 cents of its own revenue for every stay booked on the platform, without increasing prices for travelers or reducing payments to hosts.

The dime-per-stay may not sound like much, but the cumulative effect is significant. “We tried to go as far as we could imagine,” said Chesky. “It’s a significant percentage of the company’s annual earnings.”

Airbnb.org has provided approximately 6,300 free nights in Mexico for various emergency situations, around 1,500 of which were for medical stays, according to Chesky.

The program also works with 20 nonprofit organizations in Mexico, including Fundación IMSS, Ronald McDonald House Charities Mexico and Lilo Foundation Mexico, to meet the needs of families of patients requiring specialized care who must relocate to the capital, since almost 40% of the country’s specialized medical care facilities are concentrated in Mexico City.

The program “was successful because the families were really satisfied with the service, and we felt there was enough demand to expand it,” said Chesky.

In May, Airbnb.org announced a $1.1 million contribution to expand its medical stay program in Mexico for three years. This was before the new 10 cents-per-stay fund.

The roots of Airbnb’s accommodations initiative go back to 2012, when a New York host offered her home to people displaced by Hurricane Sandy, encouraging other hosts around the world to do the same in subsequent disasters. Airbnb.org was formalized in 2020 and has had a global reach even before the newly announced initiative.

The new funding model launched on Tuesday is expected to serve more than 20 countries. The contributions will only apply to completed stays, not reservations canceled before check-in or to Airbnb Experiences or Services. The goal is to reach 1 million free nights per year for the next four or five years.

With reports from Expansión

World.title: Ebrard: More than US $8B in data center projects in the works
World.content:
Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard said Tuesday that companies have announced plans to invest more than US $8 billion in data center projects in Mexico.

Speaking to reporters after an event in Mexico City, Ebrard said that the planned data center projects are proceeding as expected.

Various companies have recently announced plans to build new data centers in Mexico.

They include Mexican company KIO, which announced it would invest up to $1.3 billion to develop a new data center in Querétaro, and U.S. company Cloud HQ, which plans to invest an estimated $4.8 billion to build six data centers and complementary infrastructure on a single site in Querétaro. The latter project is currently under development.

Querétaro is Mexico’s main data center hub, but it’s not the only state attracting investment in the booming sector.

The Guanajuato government said in September that the state had attracted $630 million in data center investment, while in New York earlier this month, Nuevo León Governor Samuel García said he had secured US $600 million in investment to develop industrial facilities, primarily data centers, in his state.

On Tuesday, Ebrard said that investment in data centers in Mexico will allow the country to strengthen its technological capabilities and its participation in the development of artificial intelligence.

“What we’re experiencing is an epochal shift and data centers are a significant part of that,” he said, referring to the rise of AI.

Ebrard acknowledged that the operation of data centers requires additional electricity infrastructure. He said that data center companies are working with the Federal Electricity Commission to ensure adequate power supply. Ebrard said that private investment in electricity projects related to data centers could reach around $400 million.

The economy minister also said that data center cooling systems use less water than they used to. He indicated that Mexican authorities are open to more data center investment in the country.

“I think we’re going to continue encouraging their installation and operation in our country,” Ebrard said.

For her part, President Claudia Sheinbaum said in August that Mexico needs data centers “to advance in artificial intelligence.”

But, she added, “Mexico does not necessarily have to be the data center [hub] for other parts of the world, because [their operation] requires high energy and water consumption.”

According to an Energy Ministry (SENER) report published in August, there were 170 data centers in operation in Mexico in 2023 and 200 in 2025. That number is projected to rise to 230 in 2027 and 243 in 2029.

“The sustained growth of this infrastructure is driven by the increase in data traffic, industrial digitization, and the expansion of cloud services,” SENER said in its report, titled “Energy Efficiency in Data Centers: Challenges, Trends and Opportunities.”

“Querétaro has established itself as the country’s leading hub, thanks to its geographic location, energy availability, and fiber-optic connectivity,” the ministry said.

“This development has spurred the creation of specialized technology parks and attracted foreign direct investment, primarily from U.S., European, and Asian companies. However, it has also created new challenges in terms of electricity capacity, water supply, and sustainable energy management, underscoring the need to incorporate energy efficiency into the planning and design of these facilities,” SENER said.

With reports from Milenio and Vanguardia Industrial

World.title: El Jalapeño: Uber to replace canceled Tulum flights with 22-hour drive in a Nissan Versa
World.content:
All stories in El Jalapeño are satire and not real news. Check out the original articles here and here.

TULUM, Quintana Roo — In a bold display of logistical agility, ride-hailing giant Uber announced Friday that it will step in to replace canceled commercial airline routes to Tulum by dispatching drivers in 2018 Nissan Versas for direct, 22-hour interstate road trips from the United States.

The move comes after major carriers, including American Airlines, Aeroméxico and Volaris, announced reductions or pauses in service to Felipe Carrillo Puerto International Airport, leaving thousands of vacationers searching for alternative flight arrangements to the Quintana Roo resort town.

Under the company’s newly launched “UberLongHaul” tier, passengers stranded in hub cities like Miami, Charlotte or Atlanta can bypass commercial aviation entirely and hail a subcompact sedan straight to their beachside hotel lobby. The app automatically calculates toll fees, international border wait times and recommended driver shifts along the 1,400-mile highway route.

“While airlines are constrained by pilot shortages and complex airspace logistics, our driver-partners remain completely nimble,” said Uber regional strategy director Carlos Mendoza. “If a traveler in Florida needs to reach a wellness retreat in Quintana Roo, they shouldn’t be limited by flight schedules. They can simply tap a button and settle into a comfortable subcompact ride through a dozen or so picturesque states in the U.S. and Mexico.”

To accommodate long-haul passengers unused to multi-day highway commutes, participating drivers will provide onboard amenities including room-temperature bottled water, periodic air conditioning and head and neck pillows for sleeping.

Transportation experts have praised the initiative as a practical response to shifts in international transit patterns, noting that while jetliners face strict operational hurdles, a compact sedan can easily adapt to evolving travel demands provided passengers maintain patience through the long journey.

State tourism officials expressed optimism about the service integration, calling it a testament to modern flexibility. “Whether visitors arrive via direct flight or a multi-day highway ride-share, the important thing is that they get here,” said regional transit consultant Maria Gutierrez.

World.title: Mexico City opens investigation into fatal poisoning of dogs in Condesa
World.content:
Suspected poison hidden inside sausage at Parque España in Mexico City might have killed at least three dogs Tuesday, prompting a criminal investigation and warnings for pet owners in the capital’s Condesa neighborhood.

The Mexico City Attorney General’s Office opened an animal cruelty investigation after dogs became ill following walks in the 105-year-old park.

Residents reported four deaths, according to Uno TV, while Cuauhtémoc borough Mayor Alessandra Rojo de la Vega reported at least three, Infobae reported.

Police found a piece of longaniza, a seasoned sausage, containing a blue pill with white powder inside, La Crónica reported. However, authorities had not publicly identified the substance or established whether it was linked to the dogs’ illnesses.

Residents also reported finding suspected poisoned meat one block from Parque España, at the intersection of Avenida Veracruz and Calle Atlixco, La Crónica reported.

Excélsior reported that five dogs arrived at the Vetme veterinary hospital suffering from seizures, prompting staff to alert authorities. Three died and two remained hospitalized.

Among those that died was Rufián, a 4-year-old Irish setter-golden retriever mix.

“Three minutes after he arrived home, he started convulsing,” said Sofía Suárez, the dog’s owner and the mother of a 2-year-old.

“How am I going to tell my daughter that she doesn’t have a dog anymore? We’d go to the park every morning and every afternoon,” she said.

Two other dogs, a Belgian shepherd named Kiara and a small-breed dog named Siberia, remained hospitalized, Excélsior reported.

Their owner, Brenda Gómez Magaña, told the newspaper that blue capsules were recovered during a stomach lavage. Kiara appeared to be improving, while Siberia remained in serious condition.

Rojo de la Vega requested a review of surveillance footage and announced legal assistance for families filing complaints.

Investigators were collecting owners’ statements, examining evidence and seeking help from veterinary specialists. Excélsior reported Tuesday evening that authorities had collected nine pieces of evidence suspected of containing poison.

A neighborhood representative said the park would remain open, but its popular dog run and children’s areas would close pending cleanup. Residents wanted the entire park cleaned once prosecutors authorized the work.

Authorities began preventive patrols. Rojo de la Vega urged visitors to Parque España and nearby Parque México to prevent pets from eating anything off the ground and report information to investigators.

With reports from Infobae, Uno TV, Excélsior and La Crónica

World.title: Navy kills cartel operator Jesús ‘Chuy’ González, wanted by the US for $5M
World.content:
Jesús “Chuy” González Peñuelas, an alleged leader of the Guasave Cartel, is believed to have been killed during a clash with Mexican Navy personnel in Sinaloa on Monday, federal authorities said.

The death of González — a 56-year-old alleged drug trafficker who was wanted in the United States — was first reported by media outlets in Sinaloa.

In a social media post on Wednesday, the Navy Ministry (SEMAR) said that its personnel, in coordination with federal Security Ministry agents, “repelled an armed attack” near the community of Alfredo V. Bonfil, located in the municipality of Sinaloa in the state of the same name.

Personal naval de la @SEMAR_mx en coordinación con @SSPCMexico, repelió una agresión armada en inmediaciones de Alfredo V. Bonfil, #Sinaloa. Esta acción derivó de trabajos de inteligencia naval y como resultado se aseguraron 4 vehículos con reporte de robo, 3 armas largas, cargadores y municiones. Durante el enfrentamiento fallecieron 2 personas, cuya identidad podría corresponder a Jesús “N” (a) Chuy Peñuelas operador de 2do orden, solo por debajo de Fausto Isidro Meza Flores (a) Chapo Isidro, líder del Cartel de Guasave y Cesáreo “N”, quedando pendiente la confirmación pericial. Los indicios quedaron a disposición de la @FGRMexico para las investigaciones correspondientes. #Marina refrenda su compromiso de contribuir a la seguridad de la población, mediante la coordinación interinstitucional, con apego al marco legal y respeto a los derechos humanos. — SEMAR México (@SEMAR_mx) October 28, 2026

SEMAR said that two people died during the confrontation, adding that their “identities may correspond to” González and a man identified as Cesáreo “N”.

In a separate social media post, federal Security Minister Omar García Harfuch said that, “according to the available information,” González was one of the two people killed in the clash with military personnel on Monday.

SEMAR said that “expert confirmation” that González and Cesáreo “N” were the two people killed was “pending.”

Cesáreo “N” was identified in media reports as Cesáreo Peñuelas Ruiz, aka “El Profe” (The Teacher). He was reportedly González’s uncle.

The Navy Ministry said that its operation in the municipality of Sinaloa on Monday “stemmed from naval intelligence work.”

During the operation, four vehicles reported as stolen, three long guns, magazines and ammunition were seized, SEMAR said.

Who was Jesús ‘Chuy’ González Peñuelas?

According to SEMAR, González was the Guasave Cartel’s second-in-command, below only Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, aka “Chapo Isidro.”

The Guasave Cartel is also known as the Meza Flores Organization and Los Mazaltecos. It is based in the municipality of Guasave in northern Sinaloa.

While SEMAR and García Harfuch said on Wednesday that Gonzalez was a member of the Guasave Cartel, U.S. authorities have accused him of running his own drug trafficking organization.

In January 2024, the U.S. Department of State announced a reward of up to US $5 million for information leading to the arrest and/or conviction of González, saying at the time that he “reportedly leads an independent methamphetamine, marijuana, heroin, and cocaine distribution and production organization.”

The State Department noted that González had been indicted on international narcotics charges in the District of Colorado and the Southern District of California.

The U.S. Department of the Treasury said in May 2021 that González and his drug trafficking organization were “among the largest sources of raw opium gum and heroin in northern Mexico, and increasingly are a major distributor of fentanyl to U.S. markets.”

At that time, Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control designated González and his drug trafficking organization as “significant foreign narcotics traffickers pursuant to the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Designation Act.”

The Department of the Treasury said that González oversaw “multiple heroin processing laboratories in Sinaloa” and that “the upper echelons” of his drug trafficking organization (DTO) hierarchy consisted of his family members.

“The González Peñuelas DTO cooperates with other DTOs within Mexico, including acting as an enforcement arm for the various Mexican DTO’s trafficking routes, and is aligned with Mexican drug kingpins Fausto Isidro Meza Flores and Rafael Caro Quintero, both of whom are subject to Treasury sanctions,” the department said on May 12, 2021.

With reports from Río Doce, EFE and El Financiero

World.title: Tropical Storm Vance heads toward Sinaloa, bringing more heavy rainfall to northwest Mexico
World.content:
Tropical Storm Vance continues to move northward off the coast of western Mexico and is projected to turn toward the coast of Sinaloa, where it could make landfall by the end of this week.

The U.S. National Hurricane Center forecasts that Vance will lose strength and become a post-tropical remnant low on Thursday, potentially approaching Sinaloa between Thursday and Friday. Landfall as a tropical storm is unlikely.

According to the National Meteorological Service, as of 12 p.m. today, Vance was located approximately 365 kilometers west-southwest of Cabo Corrientes, Jalisco, and 390 kilometers west-southwest of Punta Mita, Nayarit. The storm had sustained winds of 65 kilometers per hour, with gusts reaching up to 85 kilometers per hour and was heading north at a speed of 17 kilometers per hour.

A las 12:00h, la #TormentaTropical #Vance se localiza a 365 km al oeste-suroeste de Cabo Corrientes, #Jalisco, con vientos máximos sostenidos de 65 km/h y rachas de 85 km/h. Se desplaza hacia el nor-noroeste a 17 km/h. ⚠️ Para las próximas 24 horas se pronostican lluvias muy fuertes con puntuales intensas (75 a 150 mm) en Baja California Sur, Sinaloa, Nayarit, Jalisco y Durango. En Colima, lluvias puntuales fuertes (25 a 50 mm). 🌬️ En la costa de Jalisco se esperan vientos de 30 a 40 km/h con rachas de 50 a 70 km/h y 🌊 oleaje de 2.5 a 3.5 metros. En las costas de Baja California Sur, Sinaloa, Nayarit y Colima, oleaje de 1.5 a 2.5 metros. 📲 Consulta solo fuentes oficiales: @conagua_clima y @CNPC_MX. — Coordinación Nacional de Protección Civil (@CNPC_MX) October 28, 2026

Vance is expected to cause heavy rain across Mexico’s western states.

On Wednesday, rainfall totals of 75 to 150 millimeters are expected in central and southern Sinaloa, Nayarit, Durango, the southern tip of Baja California Sur and the coast of Jalisco.

The coastlines of Baja California Sur, Sinaloa, Nayarit and Colima could get hit with sustained winds of 20 to 30 kilometers per hour with gusts of 40 to 60 kilometers per hour and waves of 1.5 to 2.5 meters, while Jalisco could see waves of up to 3.5 meters.

In Baja California Sur, the Public Education Ministry (SEP) suspended all school activities for Wednesday in San José del Cabo and Cabo San Lucas. This suspension applies to all public and private educational institutions at every level.

Given the potential for rivers and streams to swell, authorities warned residents in affected states to avoid crossing watercourses or flooded areas, stay alert to weather advisories and follow the instructions provided by Civil Protection authorities.

With reports from López Dóriga

World.title: McLaren Plans Upgrades for Brazil
World.content:
McLaren, the British Formula 1 team, says it will bring new car parts to the São Paulo Grand Prix, as it tries to climb back from fourth place in the constructors’ championship. Team principal Andrea Stella said on 29 October that the aim is to fight for podiums again and, if the gains arrive, for wins.

Our São Paulo Grand Prix coverage follows every step before the race.The race is Sunday 8 November at Interlagos, the São Paulo circuit officially named Autódromo José Carlos Pace.

It starts at noon Eastern Time, a convenient midday slot for viewers in the United States.

Key Facts What: McLaren will bring upgrades to Brazil and more to Las Vegas, says team principal Andrea Stella.

Standing: McLaren is fourth in the constructors’ championship, the team points table.

When: Race Sunday 8 November, noon Eastern Time (9:00 a.m. Pacific Time), 14:00 in São Paulo.

Prediction markets: Kimi Antonelli 99.2% to win the 2026 drivers’ title on Polymarket, as of 1:25 p.m. ET, 29 October.

This story is part of our coverage of the São Paulo Grand Prix 2026. Dates, times and how to follow it are in our guide. Latest: São Paulo Grand Prix Unveils Titanium Trophy

Why McLaren Wants Brazil to Count

McLaren has lost ground this season as rivals including Red Bull have improved. Stella wants the team to be consistently in the fight for podiums, and to lean on that form to chase victories.

He said Mexico City, which hosts the race before Brazil, would bring very little new. Brazil and Las Vegas are where the bigger parts are due.

The race starts on Sunday 8 November 2026 at noon Eastern Time (9:00 a.m. Pacific Time). That is 14:00 in São Paulo, which is three hours behind UTC.
