World.title: Democrats Need Four Seats, Lead Four Races
World.content:
File photo: the US Capitol, where the Senate meets, seen from Pennsylvania Avenue in Washington.

US Midterms 2026

Published Thursday, 29 October, 12:45 p.m. ET (12:45 p.m. Washington) · Source: SSRS poll data

Five days before Americans vote, the fight for control of the Senate has stopped looking like a long shot for Democrats. Four new polls from SSRS, a nonpartisan US polling firm, put Democrats ahead in Michigan, Texas, Maine and Kansas.

The leads in Michigan and Texas sit outside the margin of error, the built-in uncertainty of any poll. The ones in Maine and Kansas do not, so those races remain open.

For the full picture, see our 2026 US midterm elections guide.

Key Facts What happened: SSRS polls show Democrats leading Senate races in all four states surveyed.

The numbers: Michigan 49%–42%, Texas 49%–43%, Maine 49%–45%, Kansas 49%–45%.

What happens next: Election Day is Tuesday, 3 November 2026.

Prediction markets: Kalshi prices Democratic Senate control at about 68% (12:40 p.m. ET, 29 October).

This story is part of our coverage of the 2026 US midterm elections. Dates, times and how to follow it are in our guide. Latest: Judge Cites Havoc in Ballot Ruling

In plain English Republicans hold 53 of the 100 Senate seats, and Democrats hold 47. Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take control, which would let them block or steer President Donald Trump’s agenda and judicial nominations.

Four States, Four Close Races

In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed, a physician and former Detroit health director, leads Republican Mike Rogers, a former congressman, 49% to 42% among likely voters. The poll of 768 likely voters has a margin of error of 4.7 percentage points.

In Texas, Democrat James Talarico, a Texas state representative, leads Republican Ken Paxton, the state’s attorney general, 49% to 43%. That survey of 923 likely voters has a margin of error of 4.2 points.

In Maine, Democrat Troy Jackson, a former Maine state Senate president, leads Republican Sen. Susan Collins 49% to 45%. The survey of 783 likely voters has a margin of error of 4.5 points, so the race is within the noise.

In Kansas, Democrat Adam Hamilton leads Republican Sen. Roger Marshall 49% to 45%, also inside a 4.5-point margin of error. A Democrat has not won a Senate seat there since 1932.

The Michigan and Texas polls ran from 20 to 27 October, and the Maine and Kansas polls from 20 to 26 October. SSRS interviewed likely voters online and by phone.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why Four Seats Is a Steep Climb

Three of these four seats are Republican-held, which is why they matter for the majority. Michigan is a Democratic-held seat that Republicans had hoped to take, so a Democratic win there protects the party’s base rather than adding to it.

Democrats would have to hold Michigan and flip several Republican seats at once. Even if every lead above held, the four polls alone would not hand them the chamber.

What Prediction Markets Say

Kalshi, a prediction market regulated in the US by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), the federal derivatives watchdog, prices a Democratic Senate majority at about 68%. Its “Who will control the Senate?” market has traded about 21.7 million contracts across both sides of the market, and the figure was read at 12:40 p.m. ET on 29 October.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for US Readers

A Senate under Democratic control would shape tax, trade and tariff policy, and it would hold the power to confirm judges and cabinet officials. Markets that price in policy risk, from Treasury yields to defence and energy stocks, tend to react to shifts like this.

Our midterm odds page tracks how the numbers move.

What Is Not Known

A poll is a snapshot of stated preferences, not a forecast of turnout. Late deciders, early votes already cast and the quality of the likely-voter screen could all move the final results.

Nor do the polls say whether Democrats can win all the races they need at once. Official results will come from state election authorities after polls close on 3 November.

Frequently Asked Questions

Are Democrats now favoured to win the Senate?

Not yet. They lead in four polls, but Republicans hold 53 seats and Democrats need a net gain of four. Maine and Kansas are within the margin of error.

When is the US midterm election?

Tuesday, 3 November 2026. See our midterm poll closing times guide for when results start to arrive.

Sources: SSRS survey data for four Senate races, 20–27 October 2026; Kalshi market data, 29 October 2026; US Senate seat counts. More: midterm polls 2026 data room and the US midterms 2026 dossier.

World.title: CIA Operation Tops Cuba Invasion Poll
World.content:
Domino Park in Little Havana, Miami, a gathering place for the Cuban community. File photo: Phillip Pessar, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

Published Thursday, 29 October, 12:45 p.m. ET (12:45 p.m. Havana) · Source: Florida International University (FIU) Cuba Poll 2026, Polymarket

Most Cuban Americans in Miami want Washington to squeeze Havana hard, and to feed and medicate ordinary Cubans at the same time. A new survey by Florida International University (FIU), a Miami public university, found that 73% support US military action to overthrow Cuba’s government.The same people back selling medicine to the island (73%) and helping its private businesses (74%).The poll adds a Miami voice to the wider debate over cuba news and the Trump administration’s pressure campaign.

Key Facts What happened: 73% of Miami-Dade Cuban Americans back US military action to overthrow Cuba’s government.

73% of Miami-Dade Cuban Americans back US military action to overthrow Cuba’s government. The balance: 73% also favour unrestricted medicine sales to Cuba, and 74% favour US aid to its private sector.

73% also favour unrestricted medicine sales to Cuba, and 74% favour US aid to its private sector. The poll: 1,004 Cuban American adults, 4 to 29 September 2026; margin of error 3.1 points.

1,004 Cuban American adults, 4 to 29 September 2026; margin of error 3.1 points. Prediction markets: Polymarket put a US invasion of Cuba in 2026 at 5.5% (US$3.68 million traded; 12:30 p.m. ET, 29 October).

This story is part of our coverage of the cuba news. Dates, times and how to follow it are in our guide. Latest: Argentina Again Backs US Embargo on Cuba

In plain English The FIU Cuba Poll has asked Cuban Americans in Miami-Dade County, Florida, about US policy toward Cuba since 1991. It tells us what a politically powerful community wants, not what Washington plans to do.

A Community Split Over the Method, Not the Goal

The report says Cuban Americans want change in Cuba and differ over the road to it. Support for “maximum pressure”, the Trump administration’s policy of sanctions and an oil blockade, stands at 77%, while 69% say Washington should also improve ordinary Cubans’ well-being.

Unsubscribe with one click at any time; see our privacy policy. Your checklist is ready. Download the PDF checklist

How Much Appetite for Force?

The 73% figure is a majority view in a poll of one county, and it hides sharp divides. Among the Cuban Americans polled, support reaches 87% of Republicans and 68% of independents, but only 38% of Democrats.

Asked what kind of action they would back, 43% chose a clandestine operation by the CIA, the US spy agency, or other secret activity. Another 28% preferred bombing selected military targets, 14% a land invasion, and fewer than 1% bombing urban areas.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Cuba ranks 14th of 14 with 22.5 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (53); weakest: economic weight (0). Alignment group: Closer to Beijing. Some pillar data are incomplete for Cuba; see the index notes. WatchNo sovereign rating; economy contracting (-3.8%); incomplete data (‡). See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Embargo and Oil Blockade Still Have Majorities

Among those who gave an opinion, 61% favour continuing the US trade embargo on Cuba, now 64 years old. Counting “don’t know” answers, the figure is 56%.

The US blockade, which cuts off fuel shipments to the island, draws 65% support. Among Republicans it is 83%, among Democrats 21%, and respondents born outside Cuba split, at 45%.

The Other Half: Medicine, Food and Private Business

Alongside the hard line, 73% favour unrestricted US company sales of medicine to Cuba and 70% favour unrestricted food sales. A further 74% favour US assistance to Cuba’s private sector to ease the humanitarian crisis.

What Prediction Markets Say

Traders on Polymarket, a crypto-based prediction market, price a US invasion of Cuba in 2026 at 5.5%, with US$3.68 million traded. A second market, on a US drone, missile or air strike on Cuba by 31 December, stands at 9.5%, with US$5.49 million traded (as of 12:30 p.m. ET, 29 October).

These are bets, not polls, and they sit far below the 73% who back military action in Miami. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely.

We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for US Readers

Florida’s Cuban American vote is one of the best-organised blocs in US politics, and this poll shows where it leans before the US midterm elections on 3 November. A White House that tightens pressure on Havana will find support in Miami, while any move to ease sanctions will have to be framed around medicine, food and private business.

What Is Not Known

The poll covers Cuban Americans in Miami-Dade only, so it says little about Cubans on the island or Cuban Americans elsewhere. Results for small groups, such as recent arrivals, carry larger errors.

Nor does it show that the US government is weighing military action. It measures opinion, and no official source cited here describes such a plan.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many Miami Cuban Americans back US military action against Cuba?

73% support US military action to overthrow the Cuban government, according to the 2026 FIU Cuba Poll. Support is 87% among Republicans and 38% among Democrats.

Do they also support aid to Cuba?

Yes. 73% favour unrestricted medicine sales, 70% unrestricted food sales and 74% US assistance to Cuba’s private sector, while 61% of those with an opinion back the embargo.

Sources: 2026 FIU Cuba Poll report (Florida International University); Polymarket; Polymarket.

World.title: Africa Cup Qualifiers Resume on November 11
World.content:
Senegal’s squad celebrates the 2021 Africa Cup of Nations title in Yaoundé (file photo; Jeanpierrekepseu, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Africa’s road to its biggest football tournament goes quiet until Wednesday, 11 November 2026, when the qualifiers restart. Our AFCON 2027 qualifiers hub tracks the Africa Cup of Nations, the continent’s national-team championship, as the field of 48 teams heads into the middle two rounds.

The Confederation of African Football (CAF), the body that runs the competition, set 9 to 17 November for the next international window. For readers in the United States, Matchday 3 means a daytime kick-off.

This story is part of our coverage of the AFCON 2027 qualifiers. Dates, times and how to follow it are in our guide.

Key Facts

Next round: Matchday 3, Wednesday, 11 November 2026, first kick-off 17:00 UTC (12:00 p.m. Eastern, 9:00 a.m. Pacific).

Matchday 3, Wednesday, 11 November 2026, first kick-off 17:00 UTC (12:00 p.m. Eastern, 9:00 a.m. Pacific). After that: Matchday 4 on Sunday, 15 November; no single kick-off time is confirmed.

Matchday 4 on Sunday, 15 November; no single kick-off time is confirmed. Format: 48 teams in 12 groups of four, six matches each, 24 places at the finals.

48 teams in 12 groups of four, six matches each, 24 places at the finals. Prediction markets: Nigeria 54.5% and Guinea-Bissau 41.2% to win Group L (Polymarket, as of 12:22 p.m. ET, 29 October 2026).

When The Qualifiers Return

Matchday 3 is listed for Wednesday, 11 November, with all 24 fixtures sharing a first kick-off of 17:00 UTC. That is 12:00 p.m. Eastern, 11:00 a.m. Central, 10:00 a.m. Mountain and 9:00 a.m. Pacific, because US daylight saving time ends on 1 November.

Matchday 4 follows on Sunday, 15 November. A “matchday” is one round in which every group plays two games.

The kick-off times come from a fixture list published by a sports-news site, not from CAF. Individual times and venues may still change, so check each match closer to the date.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Africa Cup of Nations Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

How Qualification Works

The 48 teams are split into 12 groups of four, and each team plays six matches, three at home and three away. The campaign runs across three international windows, the FIFA-agreed breaks when clubs must release players, between September 2026 and March 2027.

Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda are co-hosts of the finals and qualify automatically. In the nine groups without a host, the top two teams go through, for 18 places.

In the three groups that contain a host, only the best-placed non-host team qualifies. The final qualifying window, Matchdays 5 and 6, is set for 22 to 30 March 2027.

Why Group L Is The One To Watch

Nigeria lost 3–0 away to Guinea-Bissau in Bissau on Tuesday, 29 September. That put Guinea-Bissau top of Group L on six points after two games, with Nigeria second on three.

Tanzania, a co-host, sit in the same group. That leaves a single place for Nigeria, Guinea-Bissau and Madagascar to contest.

Elsewhere, Egypt beat South Sudan 5–0, South Africa beat Eritrea 5–0, Morocco beat Lesotho 2–0 and DR Congo beat Zimbabwe 2–1. No Matchday 3 or 4 results exist yet.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, a platform where users trade on the outcome of events, lists a Group L winner market with US$13,182 traded as of 12:22 p.m. ET on 29 October 2026. Its prices read as implied probabilities.

Nigeria: 54.5%

Guinea-Bissau: 41.2%

Madagascar: 4.0%

Tanzania: 3.8%

These prices are bets, not polls, and the volume is small. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Egypt’s Mohamed Salah on the ball against Senegal in the 2021 final at Olembe Stadium, Yaoundé (file photo; M. L’incroyable, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

The Finals Come To East Africa

The tournament itself runs from 19 June to 17 July 2027 in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda. It is the first time East Africa has hosted since Ethiopia in 1976.

The qualifiers decide which 21 non-host teams join the three hosts.

What It Means For US Readers

The 17:00 UTC start puts Matchday 3 in the late morning on the East Coast and early morning on the West Coast. Those who follow Nigeria, Egypt or Morocco can plan around that window.

The Group L market gives a quick read on how traders see Nigeria’s chances of recovering from the Bissau defeat.

What Is Not Known

CAF has not published a consolidated venue list or confirmed match-specific kick-off times for Matchdays 3 and 4. No broadcaster for US viewers has been confirmed in the sources we reviewed.

Updated standings after the next round will show whether the picture in Group L has changed.

Frequently Asked Questions

When do the AFCON 2027 qualifiers resume?

The next window runs from 9 to 17 November 2026. Matchday 3 is listed for Wednesday, 11 November, and Matchday 4 for Sunday, 15 November.

What time do the 11 November matches start in the US?

The first kick-off is listed at 17:00 UTC. That is 12:00 p.m. Eastern and 9:00 a.m. Pacific.

How does qualification work with three co-hosts?

Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda qualify automatically. In groups without a host the top two advance, and in host groups only the best non-host team does.

Who is favoured in Nigeria’s group?

Polymarket prices Nigeria at 54.5% and Guinea-Bissau at 41.2% to win Group L. These are bets, not polls.

Sources: Confederation of African Football (cafonline.com), Polymarket, national football federations, fixture listings.

World.title: UN Climate Summit in Turkey Nov. 9-20
World.content:
The old city walls of Antalya, Türkiye, in a file photo (Photo: Wikimedia Commons)

World leaders are due in a Turkish resort city on 11 and 12 November for one of the biggest climate meetings of the year. The COP31 climate summit in Antalya opens two days earlier, on 9 November.

COP31 is the 31st annual UN climate conference, held in Türkiye with Australia leading the negotiations. Türkiye’s environment minister says 85 world leaders have confirmed they will attend.

Key Facts

Conference: Monday, 9 November to Friday, 20 November 2026, at the Antalya Expo Center.

Monday, 9 November to Friday, 20 November 2026, at the Antalya Expo Center. Leaders’ summit: Wednesday, 11 November and Thursday, 12 November, in the first week.

Wednesday, 11 November and Thursday, 12 November, in the first week. Attendance: Environment Minister Murat Kurum said on 22 October that 85 world leaders have confirmed.

Environment Minister Murat Kurum said on 22 October that 85 world leaders have confirmed. Not yet known: Official programme times; we will add them in US Eastern Time once published.

Who Is In Charge

Murat Kurum, Türkiye’s environment minister, is the president-designate of COP31 and chairs the conference. Chris Bowen, Australia’s climate minister, is president of negotiations, the role that steers the talks between countries.

Türkiye is the host country, while Australia leads the negotiating side.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What To Expect On 11 And 12 November

The leaders’ summit sits in the first week, before ministers settle down to negotiate. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, UN Secretary-General António Guterres and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese are expected to give remarks.

The first day closes with a gala dinner hosted by Erdoğan and his wife, Emine Erdoğan, for heads of state and government. Delegates will be split between a Blue Zone for registered participants and a public Green Zone.

What It Means For US Readers

Antalya is in Türkiye’s time zone, three hours ahead of Greenwich Mean Time. When US daylight saving ends on 1 November, that puts it eight hours ahead of New York, so a noon session in Antalya is 4 a.m. Eastern.

US climate policy and money are likely to be watched closely, but whether Washington sends a high-level delegation has not been confirmed.

What Is Not Known

The detailed hourly programme is still marked preliminary, so we are not publishing session times yet. Which leaders will attend is not public beyond the count of 85.

Nobody knows yet whether the summit will produce new national climate pledges or finance announcements.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is COP31?

COP31 runs from 9 to 20 November 2026 at the Antalya Expo Center in Türkiye. The leaders’ summit takes place on 11 and 12 November.

Who leads COP31?

Türkiye’s environment minister Murat Kurum is the president-designate. Australia’s Chris Bowen is president of negotiations.

World.title: 6 Million Haitians Hungry as Vote Slips
World.content:
The National Palace, Haiti’s seat of government, after the January 2010 earthquake (file photo; Wikimedia Commons)

Haiti has finally put dates on the calendar: voters are due at the polls on 18 July 2027. The new schedule from the country’s haiti crisis coverage hub explains why a vote is still far from certain.

Haiti’s Provisional Electoral Council, the body that runs its elections, announced the timetable on Wednesday, 28 October 2026. It pushes back the first round from 13 December 2026.

This story is part of our coverage of the haiti crisis. Dates, times and how to follow it are in our guide. Latest: Haiti Food Crisis Seen Hitting Record

Key Facts

First round: Presidential and legislative voting is set for 18 July 2027.

Presidential and legislative voting is set for 18 July 2027. Runoff: A second round follows on 4 October 2027, with final results due on 23 October.

A second round follows on 4 October 2027, with final results due on 23 October. Security: The UN-backed Gang Suppression Force has about 1,500 personnel, against a target of 5,500.

The UN-backed Gang Suppression Force has about 1,500 personnel, against a target of 5,500. Unknown: Gangs still block roads and parts of the country, so the dates may slip again.

A Vote Delayed Again

The council’s calendar puts the first round of presidential and legislative elections on 18 July 2027. A runoff would be held on 4 October 2027, and the council expects final results on 23 October.

It would be Haiti’s first national vote since 2016. The country has had no elected president since Jovenel Moïse, its last head of state, was assassinated in July 2021.

Earlier dates, in December 2026 and February 2027, were dropped. Each delay prolongs a period without an elected government.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Haiti elections Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why The New Dates Are Fragile

Armed gangs control or contest large parts of Port-au-Prince and many roads out of it. That makes it hard to register voters, move ballots and open polling stations.

The Gang Suppression Force, a UN-backed international mission, has about 1,500 personnel deployed. Its authorised strength is 5,500, so it is less than a third of the way there.

El Salvador is adding to the effort. About 1,000 Salvadoran soldiers are in Haiti, with more than 2,000 planned, after four members of its air force went missing in a gang ambush near Port-au-Prince on 18 October.

Hunger Adds To The Pressure

A new analysis by the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), a UN-backed hunger scale, found nearly 6 million Haitians in severe hunger. Almost 2 million of them are at the Emergency level, the second-worst of five.

The figure is up by nearly 250,000 since April. The IPC projects it could reach 6.35 million by mid-2027, more than half the population, as violence, displacement and El Niño, a weather pattern that brings drier, hotter conditions, disrupt farming.

The UN’s World Food Programme, its food-aid agency, says it needs US$78 million to keep operating in Haiti through March 2027.

What It Means For US Readers

Haiti lies close to Florida, so instability there reaches US politics through migration and aid. Temporary Protected Status, the programme that shielded up to 350,000 Haitians from deportation, ended in August 2026.

A credible election would give Washington and other donors a government to work with. A new delay would keep the question of returns, security funding and aid open through next year.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether gangs will allow campaigning and voting in July 2027, or whether the Gang Suppression Force will reach its full size by then. No prediction-market price on Haiti’s election was found.

The council has not yet published detailed plans for voter registration in gang-held areas.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is Haiti’s next election?

Haiti’s Provisional Electoral Council set the first round of presidential and legislative elections for 18 July 2027. A runoff is planned for 4 October 2027.

Why might the new date slip?

Gangs control or contest large areas, and the UN-backed security force has about 1,500 personnel against a target of 5,500.

Published Thursday, 29 October 2026, 11:50 a.m. ET (same time in Port-au-Prince) · Sources: Haiti’s Provisional Electoral Council, IPC, World Food Programme, UN.

World.title: Mayor’s Own Welfare Chief Held Over Murder
World.content:
Security: Mexico

Key Facts Who. Alejandra Vargas, welfare secretary of Uruapan, a city in Michoacán state, was arrested on 29 October 2026.

Charge. Prosecutors suspect encubrimiento, meaning covering up a crime, tied to the murder of Carlos Manzo, the late mayor of Uruapan.

Case. More than 30 people have now been arrested in the Manzo investigation.

Status. She is a suspect, not convicted; a judge now decides her legal status.

Time. As of 29 October 2026, 15:00 GMT

A city that lost its mayor at a candle festival has now seen one of its own senior officials arrested over the killing. Uruapan sits in Michoacán, Mexico’s main avocado state and a place the US government warns Americans about.

What We Know

Agents of the Michoacán state prosecutor’s office, known in Spanish as the Fiscalía General del Estado, arrested Alejandra Vargas on Thursday, 29 October 2026. The state security department, the SSP, backed them, and they acted under a judge’s search warrant.

The raid took place in Infonavit Balcones, a residential neighbourhood of Uruapan; Infonavit is Mexico’s workers’ housing fund. Prosecutors suspect her of encubrimiento, which means helping to cover up a crime, in connection with the murder of Mayor Carlos Manzo.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 with 71.4 points. Strongest pillar: economic relationships (90); weakest: state capacity & security (46). Alignment group: Hedging. Watch21 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.7 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Mexican prosecutors usually name suspects only by an initial, but the name Alejandra Vargas has been made public for her. She holds the post of secretary of welfare, or Bienestar, in Uruapan’s city government.

She was handed to a jueza de control, a judge who oversees the early stage of a criminal case and rules on detention. Prosecutors say that judge will decide her legal situation in line with the law and due process.

A search warrant means a judge approved the raid in advance. Such a warrant lets investigators enter a property and look for evidence.

More than 30 people have now been arrested in the wider investigation into Manzo’s murder. Thursday’s arrest adds one more name to that list.

Main square of Los Reyes, Michoacán, a town in the same state as Uruapan (file photo, not the scene of the arrest).

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Uruapan (Mexico) Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What Is Not Known

The prosecutors’ statement does not say what exactly Vargas is accused of having done. It does not say when the alleged cover-up took place or whom it was meant to protect.

We have seen no response from her or from any lawyer acting for her. Without one, we cannot say whether she denies the accusation.

It is also unclear whether further arrests will follow. Prosecutors have not said whether other officials are under investigation.

No court has ruled on the case against her. Until one does, she is a suspect, and the law presumes her innocent.

Who Carlos Manzo Was

Carlos Manzo was mayor of Uruapan, a city in Michoacán known for its avocado orchards. He took office in September 2024 as an independent candidate, outside Mexico’s main political parties.

Los del Sombrero, or the Hat Wearers, was the name of his independent movement. It gave him a political base outside the traditional parties.

He was shot dead on Saturday, 1 November 2025, during the Festival de las Velas, a candle festival in the city centre. The attack happened in front of hundreds of people.

Manzo had spoken openly against organised crime and had asked President Claudia Sheinbaum for federal help to confront it. His killing set off national anger and protests across Mexico.

In July we reported the capture of an alleged mastermind known as “El R1”. The investigation has kept widening since then, and Thursday’s arrest is the latest step.

Why It Matters Beyond Uruapan

Michoacán is Mexico’s leading avocado-growing state, and the United States is the biggest buyer of Mexican avocados. Nothing in this case points to any effect on supply, but it concerns a region that many American households rely on for the fruit.

Violence against local officials is a long-running concern in Mexico, and Manzo’s killing drew national attention to it. His death set off the protests described above.

The US State Department has long advised Americans against travel to Michoacán. Today’s arrest does not change that advice, and travellers should check the current advisory before any trip.

The arrest of an official of the city government shows the inquiry reaching into local politics. Whether it reaches further is unknown, and that depends on what prosecutors and the court disclose.

American readers can treat this as a legal step, not a verdict. A judge, not the prosecutors, will decide whether the accusation holds.

The next step is the control judge’s decision on her legal status. Until then, the case rests on the prosecutors’ account alone.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Alejandra Vargas?

She is the secretary of welfare in Uruapan’s city government, a post known in Spanish as Bienestar. Prosecutors detained her on 29 October 2026 as a suspect, and no court has found her guilty of anything.

What is she suspected of?

Prosecutors cite encubrimiento, meaning helping to cover up a crime, linked to the murder of Mayor Carlos Manzo. They have not said what specific acts she is accused of.

Who was Carlos Manzo?

He was the independent mayor of Uruapan, a city in the Mexican state of Michoacán. He was shot dead on Saturday, 1 November 2025, during the Festival de las Velas candle festival.

How many people have been arrested in the case?

More than 30 people have been arrested in the investigation so far, including this welfare secretary. Those held are suspects until a court rules.

Sources Michoacán State Prosecutor’s Office (Fiscalía General del Estado de Michoacán) statement, 29 October 2026.

World.title: All Three VIP Lounges at Juan Santamaría Airport Close Sunday
World.content:
If you are flying out of Juan Santamaría International Airport this Sunday, Nov. 1, plan on waiting at the gate. All three VIP lounges at Costa Rica’s main airport will be closed that day, and one of them has no date to reopen. The closures start Saturday, Oct. 31, and each lounge is on a different schedule. BAC Credomatic said the special hours are the result of an operational adjustment scheduled by the airport’s management and outside the bank’s control.

Here is how each lounge is affected:

Lounge BAC closes at 6 p.m. Saturday, Oct. 31, two hours earlier than usual. It reopens at 4 a.m. Monday, Nov. 2. That is 34 hours without service.

closes at 6 p.m. Saturday, Oct. 31, two hours earlier than usual. It reopens at 4 a.m. Monday, Nov. 2. That is 34 hours without service. VIP Santamaría , next to Gate 5, closes for Sunday, Nov. 1, only.

, next to Gate 5, closes for Sunday, Nov. 1, only. VIP Lounge Costa Rica, the Mastercard lounge that also operates as the Copa Club, closes Saturday, Oct. 31, until further notice.

That last closure is the one to watch. If you usually get in with a Mastercard card or a Priority Pass membership, you will lose that option for an open-ended period. The lounge’s own notice gives no reopening date, and Priority Pass now lists it as temporarily closed from Oct. 31 until further notice.

Aeris, the company that runs the airport, has not said what the adjustment involves. Asked whether the lounges would change operators, the company said it recognizes the lounges as an important part of the airport experience. It added that any official information will be released through its own channels.

The lounges normally open from 4:30 a.m. to 8 p.m. Priority Pass also lists VIP Santamaría as undergoing renovation work, and warns that space may be limited even when it is open. Nothing announced so far affects flight schedules. If you were counting on lounge food or a quiet place to work this weekend, eat before you head to the airport and bring a charged phone and laptop.

Check with your bank or lounge program before you leave home, since access rules differ from one lounge to the next. If you are heading to the United States, you will also need to sign a new passenger form starting Nov. 3. The lounge closures come a week after a power failure disrupted the airport’s control tower. From Monday, the BAC and VIP Santamaría lounges are expected back on normal hours. The Mastercard lounge may stay closed well beyond that.

World.title: Elena Rybakina Clinches Year-End World No. 1 Ranking After Tokyo Victory
World.content:
Elena Rybakina has won the year-end World No. 1 ranking for the first time in her career, defeating fellow Kazakh Yulia Putintseva 6-2, 6-3 at the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo on Thursday. The 27-year-old needed just one more victory to guarantee that Aryna Sabalenka could not overtake her before the end of the season. She accomplished that in 70 minutes, adding another milestone to a remarkable year that has already brought her two Grand Slam titles.

Rybakina becomes the 17th woman in WTA history to finish a season ranked No. 1 and the first player representing Kazakhstan, male or female, to achieve the year-end top ranking in singles or doubles. Thursday’s result also means Rybakina will enter the 2027 season at the top of women’s tennis, regardless of what happens at next month’s WTA Finals in Indian Wells, California.

Her performance against Putintseva was convincing from the start. Rybakina never lost her serve, fired six aces and faced only one break point, which she saved in the final game before closing out the match. The victory extended her winning streak to five matches following last week’s title at the Ningbo Open in China.

Rybakina’s rise to the top has been one of the biggest stories in women’s tennis this season. She began 2026 by winning the Australian Open, defeating Sabalenka in the final to claim her second Grand Slam title. Her first major championship came at Wimbledon in 2022. In September, she added the US Open title, again beating Sabalenka in the championship match. That victory brought her Grand Slam total to three and helped her take over the World No. 1 ranking for the first time, ending Sabalenka’s 99-week run at the top.

But Rybakina’s success has extended well beyond the Grand Slams. She has won four singles titles this season, more than any other player on the WTA Tour, with victories at the Australian Open, Stuttgart, US Open and Ningbo. She has also reached six finals and recorded a tour-leading 54 match wins.

Her consistency has been particularly important in the race for the year-end ranking. Despite finishing runner-up at major tournaments in Indian Wells and Toronto, Rybakina continued collecting ranking points throughout the season, gradually building an advantage over her closest rivals.

There were setbacks along the way. After winning the US Open, she lost her opening match in Beijing and missed the Wuhan Open because of a leg injury. She responded by successfully defending her Ningbo title, the first time in her career she had won the same tournament in consecutive years.

That victory left her needing only one more match win to secure the year-end No. 1 ranking, and she wasted little time accomplishing that goal in Tokyo. “I’m really proud of what I’ve achieved this season and the consistency I’ve shown throughout the year,” Rybakina said in a statement released by the WTA.

She now advances to the Tokyo quarterfinals, where she will face Canada’s Leylah Fernandez in a rematch of last week’s Ningbo final. Fernandez earned her place by defeating Belgium’s Elise Mertens 6-2, 7-6 (8) on Thursday. Rybakina won their previous meeting 6-2, 6-2 and holds a 4-2 career advantage over the Canadian.

A title in Tokyo would give Rybakina her fifth trophy of 2026 and the 16th singles title of her career. Beyond Tokyo, her next major challenge will be the WTA Finals, scheduled for November 8–15 at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden in California. The tournament brings together the eight leading singles players of the season and features a round-robin format before the semifinals and final.

Rybakina enters as the defending champion after winning the 2025 WTA Finals in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. She will attempt to become the first player since Serena Williams to successfully defend the season-ending championship. She will also receive the Chris Evert WTA No. 1 Trophy during a presentation at Indian Wells, recognizing her achievement as the world’s top-ranked player at the end of the season.

Although her position at No. 1 is now secure, Rybakina still has an opportunity to finish an already historic season with another major championship.

World.title: Costa Rica’s Nosara Free Nature Trails Through Forests and Wetlands
World.content:
Nosara is best known for its beaches, surfing and laid-back lifestyle, but visitors to this popular destination on Costa Rica’s Nicoya Peninsula have another way to enjoy the outdoors without spending a dollar. A network of 18 kilometers (11.2 miles) of free walking trails connects tropical forests, wetlands, beaches and public spaces, offering a different look at one of Guanacaste’s most visited coastal communities.

The network brings together nine routes ranging from 500 meters (0.3 miles) to 4 kilometers (2.5 miles), giving you a choice between short nature walks and longer hikes through the surrounding countryside. Some trails wind through patches of tropical dry forest, while others pass streams, mangroves and areas where native vegetation is slowly reclaiming previously disturbed land.

The project is coordinated by the Nosara Civic Association (NCA), with support from Costa Rica’s National System of Conservation Areas (SINAC) and the Municipality of Nicoya. Rather than operating as a traditional national park, the trail network connects several existing conservation and community areas, including the association’s private reserve, sections of the Ostional National Wildlife Refuge and the embankment along the Nosara River.

For those who want to see wildlife, the trails offer opportunities to see animals that are commonly found in this part of Costa Rica. Howler monkeys can often be heard calling from the treetops, while white-nosed coatis, deer and blue morpho butterflies are among the species that inhabit the surrounding forests. Large guanacaste trees, mangroves and other native plants provide shelter for wildlife and help maintain the natural landscape.

One of the biggest bonuses is the price. All nine routes are free to use, thanks to financial support from local hotels, businesses and families who help cover maintenance costs. That arrangement allows residents and tourists to enjoy the trails without paying the entrance fees commonly associated with Costa Rica’s national parks and private nature reserves.

The initiative also serves a practical purpose for the community. Some routes connect residential neighborhoods with public spaces, beaches and commercial areas, giving people an alternative to traveling short distances by car. That is particularly useful in Nosara, where growing tourism and residential development have increased traffic on roads that were originally built for a much smaller population.

The trail system is not a newly opened experience. Nosara has maintained a network of nature paths for years, and the latest effort brings renewed attention to how these routes are connected and maintained. Local conservation organizations have worked to preserve public access to forests and other natural areas even as the surrounding community continues to grow.

That growth has brought both opportunities and challenges. Nosara has become an international destination for surfing, yoga and wellness tourism, attracting visitors and property buyers from around the world. At the same time, new construction has placed increasing pressure on wildlife habitats, roads and public infrastructure.

Maintaining natural corridors is especially important in a region where animals move between forested areas, waterways and the coast. Keeping those habitats connected gives wildlife room to move while allowing residents and visitors to experience the environment without having to travel far from town.

The trail network has also attracted interest as an example of community planning. The Municipality of Nicoya presented the initiative at an international urban landscaping conference in San José in 2025, highlighting the value of connecting public spaces through walking routes rather than relying entirely on roads.

Anyone going is encouraged to stay on marked paths, respect protected areas and avoid disturbing wildlife. The Nosara Civic Association recommends using the trails during daylight hours, keeping noise to a minimum and taking any trash back out. Dogs are permitted on leashes, and people using bicycles are asked to give way to walkers.

Anyone planning a hike should also remember that conditions can change during the rainy season, when some paths become muddy and streams can rise. Comfortable walking shoes, drinking water and insect repellent are sensible additions for exploring the area.

For tourists who usually spend their time around Playa Guiones or Playa Pelada, the network offers a chance to see another side of Nosara. A short walk away from the busy beach areas can lead into forests filled with birdsong, monkeys and the sights and sounds of tropical Costa Rica.

For those that live in the area, the trails offer something equally important: access to green spaces in a community where development continues to reshape the landscape.

Visitors can consult the Nosara Civic Association’s official trail map for routes and guidelines before heading out. The network shows how a coastal community can make nature part of everyday life while protecting the forests and wildlife that helped make Nosara such an attractive place to begin with. And unlike many tourist activities in Costa Rica, enjoying it doesn’t cost anything.

World.title: Sarapiquí Bus Crash Toll Rises to Three as Bus Lacked Excursion Permit
World.content:
A third woman has died following Wednesday’s bus rollover in Sarapiquí, and transport regulators say the vehicle was authorized only to carry students, not the excursion group of older adults it was transporting when it left the road. The Judicial Investigation Agency (OIJ) confirmed Wednesday afternoon that a 69-year-old woman surnamed Castro died of complications at Hospital de Guápiles. She had been injured in the crash on National Route 4 in La Chiripa de Río Frío, Horquetas de Sarapiquí.

The OIJ identified the other two victims as Isabel Brenes Mora, 62, who was trapped inside the bus and died at the scene, and a 70-year-old Nicaraguan woman surnamed Ruiz, who died while being taken by ambulance to the same hospital. The 54 passengers were older adults from Jiménez, Suerre and other communities in Pococí, Limón, on a trip to the hot springs in La Fortuna de San Carlos. The bus overturned onto its side around 7:55 a.m., about 400 meters (1,312 feet) from the Palmitour restaurant.

The Public Transport Council (CTP) said the bus, belongs to Transportes Transpal of Guápiles. According to the council, the company holds a valid operating permit for student transportation only, and the bus was not authorized to provide excursion service. The Ministry of Public Works and Transport (MOPT) said the vehicle’s technical inspection with Dekra was current, its policy with the National Insurance Institute (INS) was active and the bus was within its permitted service life.

Public Works and Transport Minister Efraím Zeledón Leiva ordered an investigation into the conditions under which the bus was operating. The CTP has opened its own administrative inquiry into the company and said its findings will go to the council’s board of directors as soon as possible.

MOPT and the CTP said in a joint statement that sanctions will be applied if irregularities are confirmed. No penalties have been announced. Authorities have not established what caused the bus to leave the road. Survivors interviewed by local media described the bus overturning suddenly, and one witness said the driver was trying to avoid an object on the roadway. Investigators have not confirmed those accounts.

The Costa Rican Red Cross said it attended to 54 people at the scene, classifying seven as critical and 32 as urgent, while 13 did not need hospital transfer. Patients were taken to hospitals in Guápiles, San Carlos and Heredia and to clinics in Río Frío and Puerto Viejo de Sarapiquí.

The condition of the driver has not been publicly reported. The OIJ continues to investigate the circumstances of the crash, while the CTP review will determine whether the company faces administrative penalties for operating the trip without the required authorization.

World.title: Costa Rica Pension Overhaul Could Require 30 Years of Work Instead of 25
World.content:
Workers in Costa Rica’s main public pension system could need five more years of contributions before they can retire, receive a smaller share of their salary once they do, and pay part of their pension toward health coverage, under 20 reform proposals now before a national dialogue convened by the Costa Rican Social Security Fund (CCSS).

The technical panel on the Disability, Old Age and Death (IVM) regime held its opening session yesterday. Jaime Barrantes, the CCSS pensions manager, confirmed that the panel will work from the 20 proposals and has a one-year timeline, with results expected around October 2027.

The IVM is our largest pension program and according to figures the CCSS presented in May, it has about 1.78 million contributors, covering roughly 63% of the workforce. It operates alongside the mandatory supplementary pension (ROP), which is managed by pension fund operators.

The proposal with the greatest consequence for future retirees would raise the minimum number of monthly contributions required for an old-age pension from 300 to 360, the equivalent of moving from 25 to 30 years of work. Barrantes has said the package does not raise the normal retirement age.

A second proposal would lower the IVM replacement rate, the share of a worker’s reference salary paid out as a pension, from the current range of 43% to 52.5% to between 40% and 43%. CCSS planners have framed that change around a combined IVM and ROP replacement rate of about 60%.

Current retirees would also be affected. One measure would require IVM pensioners to contribute 5% toward the CCSS health insurance program, a deduction already applied to retirees under the teachers’ and judiciary’s pension systems. Another would apply a solidarity contribution, at a rate not yet specified, to the highest pensions, and a third would calculate the minimum pension independently rather than tying it automatically to the minimum contribution base.

Barrantes said the CCSS is not proposing higher contribution rates or new taxes at this stage, and is instead focused on gradually reallocating existing spending. One measure would redirect to the IVM the 0.25% employer contribution that now flows from Banco Popular to the ROP. Another would shift to the IVM the employer charges that currently fund the National Training Institute (INA) and the Social Development and Family Allowances Fund (Fodesaf), about 7.25% of payroll charges, which would place the IVM contribution rate between 15% and 16%.

According to Barrantes, that shift would be offset by fiscal space freed up as pensions paid from the national budget decline. Costa Rica devotes around 10% of its national budget to pensions, mostly for former public employees in special regimes that are already closed, and that spending is expected to fall over the next 30 years. He said the IVM represents about 4% of GDP and that roughly two percentage points of that warrant analysis.

The broader package includes automatic enrollment of self-employed workers in the ROP with the option to opt out, more flexible coverage for platform and online workers, and a so-called consumption pension that would direct 1% of value-added tax to voluntary retirement accounts. Other items would reward workers who retire after age 65, recognize contributions for women based on the number of children they have and their caregiving responsibilities, and diversify IVM investments into public works and international markets.

The proposals came from an interinstitutional team that included the CCSS, the Superintendency of Pensions (Supen), the National Women’s Institute (Inamu) and the Ombudsman’s Office, which reviewed 1,248 initiatives before narrowing them to 20. CCSS Executive President Mónica Taylor said in May that the reforms would require national consensus. Some measures could be adopted by the CCSS board, while others would need approval from the Legislative Assembly.

The debate comes as the CCSS faces pressure on several fronts, from overcrowded hospital emergency rooms to a board that went months without meeting earlier this year. The changes under discussion concern the IVM, not the foreign pensions that qualify retirees for Costa Rica’s pensionado residency, though the government has separately proposed a 15% tax on certain foreign income.

An updated actuarial valuation of the IVM, using data through December 2025, could be ready by the end of 2026 and is expected to inform the panel’s work. For anyone here contributing to Costa Rica’s social security system today, the outcome will shape how long they must work and how much they can expect to receive when they stop.

World.title: Flying to the US Soon? Every Passenger Must Sign a New Form From Nov. 3
World.content:
If you are flying to the United States after Tuesday, Nov. 3, you will have to sign a short health declaration before you board. Skip it and the airline will not let you on the plane. The rule applies whether the United States is your final stop or just a connection. A trip from San José to Madrid with a change of planes in Miami counts. So does a flight home to Toronto through Houston.

The requirement covers flights leaving at or after 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on Nov. 3. That is 10:59 p.m. the same night in Costa Rica, so a late departure from Juan Santamaría or Liberia that evening could be among the first affected. The form asks one thing. You confirm that you have not been in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) during the 21 days before your flight. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) ordered it on Oct. 22 to keep travelers who may have been exposed to Ebola from bringing the virus into the country.

The 21-day window is the longest time Ebola can incubate before symptoms appear. Anyone who left the DRC more than three weeks ago is past the point of risk. Never having been near the DRC does not get you out of signing. Every passenger has to sign, whatever their nationality, including U.S. citizens and green card holders.

Your airline collects the form. The CDC lets airlines take it on paper or digitally, and is urging them to build it into online check-in and their apps. Expect to see it at check-in or at the gate at your last airport before the United States. If you are unsure how your airline will handle it, check its website or app before you leave for the airport.

Each traveler needs their own form, so one signature cannot cover a whole family. A parent or guardian signs for children under 18. A relative or companion can sign for someone with a disability who cannot sign. Read it before you tick the box. The CDC warns that knowingly giving false information is a federal crime that can bring fines and prison time. Changing planes at an airport in the DRC counts as having been in the country, even if you never left the aircraft.

The declaration is not a test or a vaccine requirement, and it does not replace your passport, visa or ESTA. It applies only to air travel, so crossing into the United States by land or arriving by sea is not covered. The form sits on top of restrictions already in place. Since May, anyone who has been in the DRC within the past 21 days has been barred from boarding flights to the United States, and that bar was extended to U.S. citizens in July. Foreign nationals recently in the DRC, Uganda or South Sudan are also blocked from entering.

The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, has killed about 4,700 people in Africa, according to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention. The CDC says no cases linked to the outbreak have been reported in the United States and that the risk to the American public remains low.

The requirement is set to stay in place through Dec. 18 unless the CDC changes it sooner. That covers Thanksgiving and most of the December travel rush, so if you are flying north for the holidays, allow a few extra minutes at check-in.

World.title: El Salvador’s Marcelo Arévalo Qualifies for ATP Finals Despite Vienna Upset
World.content:
El Salvador’s Marcelo Arévalo and Croatian partner Mate Pavić have secured their place in the 2026 ATP Finals for the third consecutive year, although their preparations suffered a setback Wednesday when they lost their opening doubles match at the Vienna Open. The third-seeded pair fell 7-6 (8), 7-5 to Argentina’s Francisco Cerúndolo and Tomás Martín Etcheverry in a match lasting two hours and 27 minutes.

The result came just two days after the ATP confirmed that Arévalo and Pavić had earned one of the eight doubles spots at the season-ending championship in Turin, Italy.Despite the Vienna defeat, the qualification marks another successful season for the Salvadoran, who has established himself among the leading doubles players in professional tennis.

Arévalo and Pavić had recorded 39 tour-level victories together when their qualification was announced Monday. Their best result of the season came in June at Queen’s Club in London, where they defeated Finland’s Harri Heliövaara and Britain’s Henry Patten to capture their first title of 2026.

The pair also reached the Wimbledon doubles final in July but lost to Heliövaara and Patten in two tiebreaks. Additional runner-up finishes in Montreal, Monte-Carlo and Dubai helped them accumulate enough ranking points to qualify for Turin before the final tournaments of the regular season.

Wednesday’s result in Vienna was a notable upset. Cerúndolo and Etcheverry, better known for their singles careers, recovered from first-round singles defeats earlier in the week to eliminate one of the established doubles teams on the ATP Tour.The Argentines held their nerve in a closely contested opening set, winning the tiebreak 10-8 before securing the decisive break of serve in the second set.

For Arévalo, the larger objective remains the ATP Finals, where he and Pavić will attempt to improve on their runner-up finish in 2024. That year, the pair reached the championship match before losing to Germany’s Kevin Krawietz and Tim Pütz. They returned in 2025 but failed to advance beyond the group stage.

The Salvadoran and Croatian have been partners since the beginning of 2024. They won the French Open doubles championship that year and finished the season as the world’s top-ranked doubles team. Their return to Turin also extends Arévalo’s presence at the highest level of the sport, giving Central America another representative at one of professional tennis’s most exclusive events.

The 2026 ATP Finals will take place November 15–22 at the Inalpi Arena in Turin, bringing together the eight leading singles players and eight leading doubles teams based on their results throughout the season. With their qualification secured, Arévalo and Pavić can focus on preparing for another opportunity to win a season-ending championship that has so far eluded them.

World.title: Costa Rica Drops Bid to Join Pacific Trade Pact and Fires Its Trade Minister
World.content:
Today, President Laura Fernández removed Foreign Trade Minister Indiana Trejos and ordered that Costa Rica not sign its accession to the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership, ending a four-year effort to join one of the world’s largest trade blocs.

The president said she had instructed the Foreign Trade Ministry (Comex) to share the full terms of the agreement with the sectors it would affect, and that the order was not carried out. She said the negotiators had declared the complete text confidential, so almost no one knew what it contained, whom it would benefit or whom it would harm.

She also said she could not put at risk the future of thousands of Costa Rican families who make their living from cattle ranching, dairy production and small and medium-scale fruit and vegetable farming. She ordered the accession file archived. The decision reverses a policy the government had defended and that she had included in her government plan.

Former president Rodrigo Chaves, now Minister of the Presidency and Minister of Finance, celebrated the conclusion of negotiations in early May as a major victory for the country. The CPTPP groups 12 economies: Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Peru, Singapore, the United Kingdom and Vietnam.

The president acknowledged the agreement’s commercial value, citing access to a market of roughly 600 million consumers. Costa Rica formally applied to join in August 2022, and members agreed in November 2024 to open the accession process. According to Comex, the remaining steps after the May announcement were the legal review and drafting of the accession protocol, its signature and its submission to the Legislative Assembly.

Costa Rica had been expected to decide whether to sign at a meeting of members scheduled for Nov. 23 to 27. Trejos, who had been vice minister before taking over the ministry when the new administration began in May, defended the negotiation before lawmakers. Appearing before the Legislative Assembly’s Treasury Affairs Committee on Oct. 13, she said the process had been transparent and that the terms closed in May could not be renegotiated.

President Fernández met with representatives of the productive sectors on Oct. 9 in a session that lasted nearly seven hours. Afterward, she criticized the previous Comex administration for a lack of dialogue and transparency. Agricultural groups led the opposition. Ivannia Quesada of the National Chamber of Milk Producers said the agreement was not in the interest of the country or the national agricultural sector, citing import competition and the risk to domestic production and dairy jobs.

The Coffee Institute of Costa Rica, through Gustavo André Jiménez Elizondo, raised concerns about rules of origin and coffee traceability in a sector already under pressure from the strong local currency. Business groups had backed accession. Arturo Rosabal of the Chamber of Commerce said productivity gaps should be closed through improvements in production, while Rodney Salazar of the Costa Rican Chamber of Exporters (Crecex) supported the deal and acknowledged the concerns of agricultural producers.

The agreement also faced an uncertain path in the Legislative Assembly, where the National Liberation Party had said it would not support it under current conditions. Nogui Acosta, a lawmaker for the ruling Pueblo Soberano party, had defended an export-oriented trade policy and said the party would be watching for the signing.

The president said Comex will continue its work with support from the Agriculture and Economy ministries. She announced support for farmers who do not export, including a stronger Institutional Supply Program, run by the National Production Council, to increase government purchases from local producers, along with action against smuggling and illicit trade.

She did not give a budget or timeline for those measures, and the government did not immediately name a replacement for Trejos.

World.title: As campaign gears up, aspiring Mayor says farewell to CAYO CET
World.content:
As campaign gears up, aspiring Mayor says farewell to CAYO CET

By Zoila Palma: Aspiring Mayor of San Ignacio and Santa Elena, PUP Mayoral candidate Aaron Mai has said farewell to Cayo Centre for Employment Training (Cayo CET).

“It is with a heart full of gratitude and appreciation that I announce my transition into a new season. Today marks the end of my journey at Cayo CET, an institution that has been an important part of my professional life.

Leaving behind my students, colleagues, and an establishment that has given me the privilege of inspiring and shaping so many young minds is not easy. However, I consider it one of the greatest accomplishments and most rewarding experiences of my professional journey. The opportunity to teach, mentor, encourage, and contribute to the development of our young people is something I will forever cherish,” Mai said.

Mai said that this is a transition into a new season of public service and pursue his vision of becoming Mayor of San Ignacio and Santa Elena.

“I do so with faith, humility, and a heart ready to serve. I believe the skills, experiences, and lessons gained through education have prepared me to serve our community at an even greater capacity.

Sometimes, God closes one chapter to prepare us for another. While I leave this chapter with a sense of nostalgia, I step into the next with excitement, courage, and unwavering faith in His plans for my life,” he added.

Mai thanked Cayo CET, for having been given the opportunity to serve as educator for 8 years.

World.title: International News: Trump’s Immigration crackdown pushes migrants to build new lives in Mexico
World.content:
International News: Trump’s Immigration crackdown pushes migrants to build new lives in Mexico

By Zoila Palma: Thousands of migrants hoping to reach the United States are reconsidering their plans following President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown, with some choosing to settle in Mexico instead.

Among them is Milko Garcia, a 29-year-old Venezuelan who was preparing to seek asylum at the US-Mexico border when his appointment was abruptly cancelled two days after Trump took office in January 2025. Garcia has since established himself in Tijuana, where he works as a real estate agent and says he is comfortable with his new life, AFP reports.

The cancellation followed Trump’s decision to shut down CBP One, a mobile application previously used to schedule appointments for asylum seekers and other applicants seeking legal entry into the United States.

At the time, the application had approximately 270,000 pending cases, including 30,000 involving people seeking a legal pathway into the US from Mexico. Garcia, who travelled north from Venezuela after his family migrated to Peru in 2014, said he no longer wants to start over in the United States. He also rejected the idea of paying human smugglers, who he said were demanding US$10,000 to help migrants cross the border illegally.

A 2025 survey by the International Organization for Migration found that 45% of migrants interviewed in the area had decided to make Mexico their home.

Meanwhile, organizations assisting migrants have shifted their focus toward helping them navigate Mexican immigration procedures and obtain legal status as opportunities to enter the United States become more limited.

World.title: United Nations Belize and Belize Chamber of Commerce sign declaration to strengthen business collaboration
World.content:
United Nations Belize and Belize Chamber of Commerce sign declaration to strengthen business collaboration

By Zoila Palma: The United Nations in Belize and the Belize Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BCCI) have signed a Declaration of Intent aimed at strengthening collaboration with the private sector to support Belize’s development priorities.

The agreement was signed on Thursday, October 22, following the signing of the Multi-Country Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (MSDCF) 2027–2031 earlier that day. The partnership seeks to encourage greater private sector involvement in advancing sustainable development initiatives across the country.

The Declaration outlines areas for cooperation, including dialogue and knowledge-sharing with the business community, identifying opportunities for joint initiatives, and promoting responsible, inclusive, and sustainable business practices. It is intended to strengthen engagement between the United Nations and businesses in support of Belize’s development goals under the new cooperation framework.

During the event, Kyana Bowen, Executive Director of the UN Global Compact Network Caribbean, highlighted the role businesses can play in promoting sustainable development. She discussed how the UN Global Compact encourages companies to align their strategies and operations with principles covering human rights, labour, environmental protection, and anti-corruption. The initiative also supports businesses in contributing to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.

Through the Declaration, the United Nations in Belize and BCCI aim to encourage businesses to adopt responsible practices and explore opportunities to contribute to national development.

World.title: Belize advances National Strategy for Cultural and Creative sector
World.content:
Belize advances National Strategy for Cultural and Creative sector

By Zoila Palma: The National Institute of Culture and History (NICH), through the Institute of Creative Arts (ICA), has marked a major milestone in developing Belize’s National Strategy and Roadmap for the Cultural and Creative Sector (NSAR-CCS).

The project closing ceremony was held on Friday, October 23, at the Bliss Center, bringing together representatives of UNESCO, the European Union, government agencies, cultural practitioners, and other stakeholders to review the project’s achievements and discuss the future of Belize’s creative industries.

During the ceremony, ICA Director Kim Vasquez highlighted the importance of collaboration in strengthening the country’s cultural and creative sector. “The development of our cultural and creative sector cannot rest on any one institution. It requires a shared understanding of the challenges and a coordinated approach to addressing them,” Vasquez said.

The initiative has involved national consultations, sector mapping, capacity-building activities, and international peer exchanges to identify opportunities, challenges, and development needs within Belize’s cultural and creative industries.

Following the ceremony, approximately 20 National Team members and representatives of the inter-agency Technical Work Group participated in a joint working session to review emerging strategic pillars and objectives.

Participants represented various fields, including film, visual arts, music, dance, design, heritage, arts education, cultural administration, and cultural organizations. Institutional representatives from NICH, the Economic Development Council, and BELTRAIDE also contributed to discussions on practical measures to strengthen the sector.

The contributions from the working session will inform the next stages of drafting and validating the national strategy, moving the process from identifying priorities toward developing actionable measures.

World.title: International News: King Charles shows off dance moves in parade during Caribbean tour in The Bahamas
World.content:
International News: King Charles shows off dance moves in parade during Caribbean tour in The Bahamas

By Zoila Palma: King Charles III set aside royal formality on Wednesday, joining a lively Jankunu parade during the second day of his nine-day Caribbean tour in The Bahamas, BBC reports.

Carrying maracas in the colours of the Bahamian flag, the King danced alongside performers dressed in colourful costumes and feathered headdresses as cheering spectators watched. The cultural celebration offered a lighter moment during a visit that has also brought renewed attention to the painful history of slavery and calls for reparations.

Earlier in the day, Charles paid tribute to fallen members of the Royal Bahamas Defence Force, laying a wreath at the Flamingo Monument in honour of four marines killed in May 1980 when Cuban MiG fighter aircraft sank HMBS Flamingo. He also visited the Bahamas Boxing Academy in Nassau, where he watched young fighters spar and met aspiring athletes. The academy trains boys and girls between the ages of eight and 18, and the King encouraged the youngsters as they pursue their sporting ambitions.

The King also visited Bonefish Pond National Park, where conservation efforts are helping protect vulnerable coastal ecosystems from climate change. The site, once used as a rubbish dump, has been transformed into a protected wetland covering approximately 1,235 acres of mangroves.

During his visit, King Charles walked along a boardwalk through the wetlands and spoke with students conducting fieldwork, including those interested in marine biology. Environmental protection and climate resilience are among the key themes of his Caribbean tour.

Despite the celebrations, the visit has also highlighted calls for Britain to acknowledge its historical role in the transatlantic slave trade and provide reparations.

On his arrival in The Bahamas on Tuesday, the King acknowledged the suffering caused by slavery, saying the country’s culture was “born out of darkness” and that it was right to recognise historical injustices.

The Caribbean tour continues in Guyana, with engagements focused on the environment and biodiversity, before the King travels to Antigua and Barbuda, where Queen Camilla will join him for the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting.

World.title: Belize supports UN resolution on lifting US Embargo on Cuba
World.content:
Belize supports UN resolution on lifting US Embargo on Cuba

By Zoila Palma: The United Nations General Assembly has adopted a resolution calling for an end to the United States’ economic, trade, and financial embargo against Cuba, with Belize voting in favour.

The resolution received 130 votes in support, 17 against, and 25 abstentions, marking its weakest backing since 1995. The annual vote comes as Washington intensifies pressure on Cuba through sanctions and restrictions that have further strained the island’s economy.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs says the country’s position remains rooted in its longstanding foreign policy principles.

Chief Executive Officer of the Ministry Oscar Arnold, explained Belize’s decision to continue supporting the resolution, noting that every country has the right to determine its own vote. “Belize’s foreign policy remains grounded on some very basic principles, and so that is why we continue to support the lifting of the embargo and the sanctions,” Arnold said.

Arnold acknowledged that support for the resolution has shifted over the years, with more countries abstaining or voting against it. “I really can’t speak to why other countries would vote the way they do, but we have noted that over the years, there has been a few more abstentions and even a few more votes going against it,” he said.

The vote comes amid heightened diplomatic tensions between Cuba and the United States, with Cuban officials accusing Washington of pressuring other countries to withdraw their support for the resolution.

World.title: Iran war tops US$47 billion as Belizeans feel the pain through higher fuel and electricity costs
World.content:
Iran war tops US$47 billion as Belizeans feel the pain through higher fuel and electricity costs

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): The United States says its war on Iran has now cost American taxpayers at least US$47.1 billion, and the economic fallout continues to reach Belize.

The Pentagon told US lawmakers that the cost of the war as of October 16 had risen to at least US$47.1 billion. The estimate includes about US$29 billion to replace bombs, bullets and other munitions used since the war began on February 28.

The figure is higher than earlier estimates of US$38 billion from the Congressional Budget Office in September and US$37.5 billion given by US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in July. The CBO has said the war could cost US$2 billion to US$3 billion per month for as long as it continues.

For Belize, the biggest impact has come from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Iran shut the critical shipping route in early March. About one fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas passed through it before the war, and its closure has sent fuel prices soaring and caused shortages around the world.

That has shown up directly on Belizean electricity bills. BEL Executive Chairman Lynn Young said this week that the diesel BEL buys has jumped from about $6 a gallon at the start of the year to close to $12. Mexico’s CFE, which supplies much of Belize’s power, has also raised prices as natural gas costs climb.

BEL has now asked the Public Utilities Commission to double the COPA cap from 5% to 10%, while government moves to buy $73 million in BEL preference shares to shore up the utility.

With the war now in its ninth month and no peace deal in sight, there is little sign of relief for fuel prices in Belize or abroad.

World.title: International News: El Salvador to send over 2,000 soldiers to Haiti for rescue mission
World.content:
International News: El Salvador to send over 2,000 soldiers to Haiti for rescue mission

By Zoila Palma: El Salvador plans to deploy more than 2,000 soldiers to Haiti to support anti-gang security operations and help rescue missing personnel, Reuters report.

The announcement follows the disappearance of four Salvadoran aircraft technicians who were reportedly ambushed while travelling through a gang-controlled area on the outskirts of Port-au-Prince.

El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele has already sent hundreds of soldiers to Haiti as part of efforts to locate the missing technicians and address the country’s worsening security crisis.

El Salvador’s Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday that Bukele had spoken by telephone with Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé about the deployment. Fils-Aimé’s office confirmed the call, stating that both leaders reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral coordination and operational cooperation through the United Nations-backed Gang Suppression Force. The additional troops are expected to support rescue operations and respond to security challenges, although it remains unclear whether they will join the existing international mission or operate separately.

Meanwhile, Haiti’s electoral council has postponed the country’s planned presidential and legislative elections, further delaying a return to democratic governance.

World.title: Shift in policy
World.content:
Foreign Affairs Minister Senator Kamina Johnson Smith explains to individuals attending Wednesday’s post-Cabinet press briefing at Jamaica House in St Andrew the country’s decision to abstain from voting on the United Nations resolution calling for an end to the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States against Cuba.The resolution was passed on Wednesday but with the lowest level of support in 30 years with 130 countries voting in favor, 17 against, and 25 abstentions. (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

THE Opposition People’s National Party (PNP) on Wednesday flayed the Government for its decision to abstain from voting on the United Nations resolution calling for an end to the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States against Cuba, insisting that the Administration’s sudden shift in policy was an “inconsistency” which has left Jamaicans in the dark.



The outcry followed on indications by Foreign Affairs Minister Senator Kamina Johnson Smith during Wednesday’s post-Cabinet press briefing at Jamaica House in St Andrew that the island was one of 25 countries that abstained on the resolution on the Cuban embargo, entitled the ‘Necessity of Ending the Economic, Commercial and Financial Embargo’, imposed by the United States against Cuba, when the vote was taken in the UN General Assembly.

Johnson Smith, who admitted that the decision was “a shift in policy”, said, “We did not vote ‘against’ because we do not support unilateral actions in accordance with the UN Charter, and we did not vote ‘for’ because it is clear that continuing to do the same thing each year to support the resolution simpliciter with no improvement in the circumstances is but in fact a deepening of the humanitarian crisis and suffering. This does not serve the benefit of the Cuban people.”

She further said the position taken is also consistent with the country’s broader perspective on multilateralism as stated in the national policy statement.

“We cannot simply continue to defend it and do the same things and believe that in a changing world it will somehow magically manifest Agenda 2030 and the systems be deemed to be fully effective. We believe that the systems need reform, and this requires us to act differently,” she said adding that an explanation of vote was also presented by Jamaica’s ambassador to the United Nations on Wednesday morning.

The vote marked a titanic shift, as historically Jamaica has been voting “yes” in favour of ending the US embargo against Cuba for over 30 years since the annual UN resolution began.

The resolution was passed with the lowest level of support in 30 years with 130 countries voting in favour, 17 against, and the 25 abstentions.

Wednesday, Opposition spokesperson on foreign, regional and diaspora affairs Senator Donna Scott-Mottley, in a statement to the media, expressed grave concern over Jamaica’s decision to abstain.

“For decades, Jamaica has joined the overwhelming majority of the international community in calling for an end to the embargo against Cuba. That position has transcended changes of Administration and has reflected our commitment to sovereignty, self-determination, and the right of nations to pursue their development free from external coercion. It is therefore deeply concerning that Jamaica should now depart from that position without any explanation to the Jamaican people,” she said.

The Opposition spokesperson pinpointed what she described as an apparent inconsistency between Jamaica’s abstention at the UN and the proceedings in the House of Representatives on Tuesday when a motion concerning Cuba, brought by the Government, was passed without objection.
