Three recent outbreaks of bird flu have led agriculture secretary Silvio Erkens to order farmers to keep their poultry indoors.

Two of the outbreaks occurred in Groningen and one in Noord-Holland. Wild birds, which are currently migrating south, have also been found to carry the disease.

“It is important to limit contact between kept birds and potentially infected wild birds as much as possible,” Erkens told broadcaster NOS. “That way we are doing everything we can to prevent new outbreaks.”

Bird hobbyists don’t have to comply with the order, but they must shield their birds in aviaries or other shelters. All non-essential visitors are also banned from places where birds are kept.

Consumers

While poultry farmers are hard-hit, the price and availability of poultry have remained relatively stable.

“The prices have been high enough for the past couple of months, so they are stable for now,” says Babak Sadeghi, who owns Chris Kip in Amsterdam’s Albert Cuyp Market. “But increased transport and petrol prices have affected suppliers and deliveries.”

Bird flu has also been found in Denmark, Germany, the United Kingdom and other places.

Erkens is pushing for mandatory vaccinations of egg-laying hens against bird flu.

World.title: Mass starfish stranding on Noordwijk beach
World.content:
Thousands of starfish washed ashore on Tuesday in Noordwijk, creating a visual feast for beachgoers and a literal feast for seagulls.

Experts say the strong winds and currents from recent storms, including the weekend’s storm Boelo, likely dislodged the starfish from the seabed, where they cling to the ground with suction cups, and carried them towards the shore.

Mass starfish strandings are common on Dutch shores, particularly after storms. They wash back out to sea once the water level rises, although many are left for bird prey as they die quickly on land.

The phenomenon, which typically occurs four to eight times a year, is a natural one that doesn’t pose problems for the ecosystem, broadcaster NOS reported. But it could if it occurs more frequently in the future, possibly due to climate change.

Starfish feed on mussels, so if they’re stranded on the shore, the mussel population explodes and weaker ones can survive, leading to disease outbreaks.

World.title: Jetten backpedals on plans to tax the royals
World.content:
Prime minister Rob Jetten is refusing to act on calls for the royal family to pay taxes, despite his party D66 having actively backed the idea for years.

The Dutch royals receive personal salaries, which is only a fraction of their overall wealth, and plans to tax them on their incomes have been debated by parliament for more than a decade.

The king, for example, will receive roughly €7.5 million from the state next year, of which €1.2 million is personal income and the rest covers staff and running costs. He pays no tax on it. In January 2024 D66 tabled a motion calling on the government to change the constitution so that the royals would pay income tax.

For the first time in history, the motion got two-thirds parliamentary support, with over 100 MPs backing it. But the successive prime ministers Mark Rutte and Dick Schoof both refused to push the plan forward.

Last December D66 also voted for a similar motion by GroenLinks-PvdA (Pro) MP Laura Bromet, asking that royals who receive an allowance pay the same taxes as everyone else.

Now Jetten appears to be doing the same. He told MPs on Wednesday that the yearly debate had become an “unproductive dynamic” and that he wants a broader review of a “future-proof monarchy” instead.

He promised the Christian Democrats (CDA) that it would not lead to a ceremonial monarchy. Ending the exemption would also require a change to the constitution, which exempts the king from tax on his allowance.

Opposition parties are furious at his backpedalling on the issue. “D66 was angry every year that the motions were not implemented. Now the party has a unique opportunity to reflect on the future of the monarchy,” Socialist (SP) MP Sandra Beckerman told NOS. “You would think that you would seize that opportunity.”

Dutch republican group Republiek, which campaigns for the abolition of the monarchy, wrote an open letter to Jetten saying “a large majority of the population indicates time and again in polls that they are in favour of the king paying taxes.”

“For twelve years now, there has been a majority in the House of Representatives in favour of abolishing the tax exemption for the royal family. Time and again, the plans failed during the implementation by the prime ministers. But now you are our prime minister.”

The letter is signed off using the campaign slogan D66 used to come to power in the current coalition: “In your own words: het kan wel” (it’s possible).

MPs will soon vote on a motion from Bromet backing Jetten’s review, and one from Beckerman telling the cabinet to act on the royal tax motions parliament has already passed.

World.title: Polish opposition leader sparks controversy with speech on potential EU exit talks
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Jarosław Kaczyński, the leader of Poland’s largest opposition party, has sparked controversy by appearing to suggest that Poland and some other allied European Union member states could launch the process of leaving the EU if they fail in efforts to reform it. His remarks were condemned by Prime Minister Donald Tusk and other figures from the pro-EU ruling coalition, who have long accused Kaczyński and his national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party of seeking “Polexit” from the EU. However, Kaczyński responded by accusing Tusk of misrepresenting his words, insisting that he wants Poland to reform the EU rather than leave it. Kaczyński pomylił Krynicę z Kremlem. pic.twitter.com/tX0G04krze — Cezary Tomczyk (@CTomczyk) October 29, 2026 The comments in question came in an hour-long speech by Kaczyński at the Krynica Forum, an annual conference bringing together leaders from politics, business and civil society, which he used to outline his vision for sweeping reforms of the EU. Repeating his longstanding criticism of Brussels, Kaczyński warned that there had been a “consistent drive to transform the EU into a centralised state” with too much power over national governments. He also called the European Parliament in its current form a “parody”. But soon, said Kaczyński, “a window of opportunity” for reform may appear because “completely different governments could emerge” in Poland, France and Spain, all of which will hold elections within the year. PiS has previously enjoyed close relations with Marine Le Pen’s far-right National Rally (RN) party in France and the nationalist Vox party of Santiago Abascal in Spain. The EU is preparing a "German plan" that would "annihilate the Polish state", said Kaczyński as Poland marks Independence Day. He warned that the incoming opposition government will "strive to implement this plan" and called on Poles to "fight" against it https://t.co/QDbxmiaazJ — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 11, 2023 Kaczyński suggested that Poland, if led by PiS, could work with other like-minded EU governments to push for reform of the bloc by influencing public opinion, identifying breaches of EU treaties, creating a blocking minority in the European Council, and trying to change the EU’s treaties. However, the PiS leader then warned that, “if [those] approaches fail to yield results, the states that want change could conclude a new treaty with the elements we are seeking, but with a delayed entry into force”. Kaczyński then noted that the EU treaties “include provisions specifying the terms under which a state may withdraw from the EU. This all begins with negotiations. And simply begin these negotiations”. “It is a tough approach, a risky one, but the situation is so dire that it is worth employing such a method if all others fail to yield results,” he added. The remarks immediately prompted condemnation from figures in Tusk’s ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right. They accused Kaczyński of effectively calling for Polexit – something they have long claimed he wants, even though PiS has not explicitly called for it before. “Jarosław Kaczyński has just announced that Poland should begin negotiations on the terms of its withdrawal from the EU,” wrote Tusk himself on X. “This is, among other things, what the current struggle in Poland is about – a tough struggle. I do not intend to lose it.” “So they do want Polexit after all,” wrote foreign minister Radosław Sikorski. “Customs borders with Germany, the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Lithuania…An end to subsidies for farmers and investments…And they swore on their lives that they’d never do that.” In a video published later on Thursday, Tusk declared that next year’s parliamentary elections would help decide “whether Poland remains in the European Union or leaves it”. Jarosław Kaczyński ogłosił właśnie, że Polska powinna zacząć rokowania o warunkach wyjścia z Unii Europejskiej. O taką między innymi stawkę toczy się dziś w Polsce walka. Twarda walka. Nie zamierzam jej przegrać, nawet jeśli nie wszyscy zagrają ze mną. — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) October 29, 2026 Kaczyński responded by saying that “Tusk is lying as usual”. He emphasised that he believes “the EU is needed but it requires thorough reform” so that it “benefits not the elites, but ordinary citizens”. PiS deputy leader Przemysław Czarnek said on Thursday that his party was “considering all scenarios, including the possibility that the EU will kill itself”. However, he added that the priority remained reforming the bloc and “PiS has no plans to leave the EU”, reports the Polish Press Agency (PAP). When PiS was in power from 2015 to 2023, it regularly clashed with Brussels over a variety of issues, including judicial reform, trade, climate policy, and migration. Since Tusk, a former president of the European Council, took power in 2023, his government has greatly improved relations with Brussels. Tusk jak zwykle kłamie. Najwyraźniej wychodzi z założenia, że dzień bez kłamstwa jest dniem straconym… Unia Europejska jest potrzebna, ale wymaga gruntownej reformy. Kryzys i zapaść w jej obecnym kształcie to efekt rządów Merkel i jednego z jej pomocników, Tuska. Nie ma co się… — Jarosław Kaczyński (@OficjalnyJK) October 29, 2026 Poland has been the largest net recipient of EU funding since joining the bloc in 2004. A study published earlier this year found that the country’s economy is 42% larger than it would have been had Poland not been part of the EU. Opinion polls consistently show a large majority of Poles in favour of remaining part of the EU. However, recent years have seen an uptick in support for Polexit, as well as for anti-EU far-right parties. Regular polling by state research agency CBOS shows that, while opposition to EU membership fell to a record low of 5% in 2022, it has subsequently risen and stood at 14% in the most recent survey. World.title: Polish bishop convicted for failing to promptly report child sex abuse allegations
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. In the first ruling of its kind in Poland, a Catholic bishop has been found guilty of failing to promptly inform the law enforcement authorities about allegations of child sex abuse committed by priests under his authority. Andrzej Jeż, the bishop of Tarnów, was handed a non-custodial sentence that will require him to donate 25% of his earnings for two years to a charity that supports victims of child sexual abuse. However, the verdict can still be appealed, and the diocese of Tarnów has already announced that it “disagrees with the court’s ruling” and that an appeal will be filed. Pierwszy taki wyrok w Polsce. Biskup skazany za zwlekanie z powiadomieniem prokuratury o pedofilach w sutannach Ordynariusz tarnowski bp Andrzej Jeż jest pierwszym biskupem oskarżonym o zbyt późne powiadomienie prokuratury o pedofilii w Kościele. I pierwszym, który który został… — Bartosz T. Wieliński 🇵🇱🇪🇺🇺🇦🇬🇱 (@Bart_Wielinski) October 29, 2026 The case relates to alleged abuse by two priests who worked under Jeż’s authority. They can be identified only as Stanisław P. and Tomasz K. under Polish privacy law. In 2022, prosecutors discontinued an investigation into allegations against Stanisław P. because the statute of limitations had expired, despite concluding that he had harmed at least 95 children and committed “sexual acts” against 77 of them over several decades in parishes in Poland and Ukraine. In 2023, prosecutors decided to charge Tomasz K., who allegedly sexually abused children as early as 2018. However, they have been unable to formally present the charges to him because of his poor health, news website OKO.press reported earlier this year. Though Jeż was not accused of complicity in the alleged abuse itself, he was charged under a 2017 law making it a criminal offence not to “immediately notify the authorities” of “credible information” about sexual abuse of minors. The offence is punishable by up to three years in prison. Investigators say that, although an internal church probe into Stanisław P. was initiated in the 2000s and a decision to remove him from the clergy was made in 2013, Jeż only notified the prosecutor’s office in 2020. In the case of Tomasz K., the bishop notified prosecutors only in 2021. In court, prosecutor Marcin Stępień said that Jeż’s failure to report the abuse promptly had allowed the statute of limitations to expire in the case of some of Stanisław P.’s victims. Stępień also noted that the bishop had only come forward with the information when media coverage brought the allegations against Stanisław P. to light, reports broadcaster TVN. A church commission set up to investigate child sex abuse in a Catholic diocese in Poland has identified at least 50 victims and 29 abusers. It also found that bishops repeatedly failed to take action when credible reports of abuse were submitted to them https://t.co/MRNl5vWp4E — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 13, 2026 Prosecutors sought a 10-month prison sentence, suspended for three years, and a fine of 20,000 zloty (€4,550). Jeż, however, denied the allegations against him and sought an acquittal. He argued that he had reported the alleged abuse to the authorities as soon as there was credible information. On Thursday, the court found the bishop guilty, giving him a sentence known as “restriction of liberty” (ograniczenie wolnośći), under which a convict is not imprisoned but required to do some kind of social good. In Jeż’s case, the court ordered that 25% of his salary for two years be donated to the Empowering Children Foundation (Dajemy Dzieciom Siłę), which supports victims of child abuse. He was additionally ordered to pay 20,000 zloty to the Fund for Assistance to Victims and Post-Penitentiary Assistance. In a statement after the verdict was issued, the diocese of Tarnów said that it “disagreed with the court’s ruling” and that, after a written justification from the court was reviewed, “an appeal will be filed”. The Catholic church in Poland has in recent years been hit by a series of revelations regarding historical abuse of minors by members of the clergy and allegations that bishops covered cases up. The Vatican has taken action against a number of Polish bishops over the issue. Most recently, in 2024, the Vatican announced the resignation of the bishop of Łowicz, Andrzej Dziuba, due to his “negligence in handling cases of sexual abuse against minors”. In February, a commission created by the diocese of Sosnowiec following a series of scandals announced that it had identified at least 50 children who were harmed and 29 people suspected of abusing minors, most of them members of the clergy. World.title: Turkish engineer creates live 3D pixel map of adopted hometown Warsaw
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A Turkish software engineer has, with the help of AI and vast quantities of Polish public data, created a precise digital replica of Warsaw, the city where he lives. The map, which can be explored for free online, features almost 200,000 buildings, moving trams that match their real-life schedules, changing light and weather conditions, and over 45,000 accurately placed streetlamps that turn on at night. It is even possible to fly a virtual plane through the city. The person behind the project, Bedirhan Yildirim, was inspired by recent efforts to produce similar maps of New York and London. While he initially considered producing one of Istanbul, his hometown, he decided instead to pick the city he lives in, Warsaw. “It is smaller, mostly flat, and I walk its streets every day,” he explained of his choice. Yildirim then used AI coding agents to create the map through a process of trial and error, constantly tweaking and improving the model. The initial version took only two days to produce and was launched on 22 October, but it has been regularly improved since then based on feedback from users. The work was made possible by what Yildirim says is the “incredible amount of data” Poland’s national mapping office, GUGiK, provides for free, including 3D building models, terrain scans, and even details of almost 2 million trees. Further information, including on parks, streetlamps, and traffic lights, was taken from OpenStreetMap, a freely licensed database. Meanwhile, timetables from Warsaw’s public transport authority, ZTM, and Poland’s national rail operator, PKP, allowed the map to feature accurately timed trams and trains. Current weather conditions are input from Open-Meteo, an open-source meteorological service. But users can also choose to manually adjust the time of day or year, with light and weather changing accordingly. An observation deck at the top of the EU's tallest building, Varso Tower in Warsaw, has opened to the public. Located 230m up on the tower's 53rd floor, the attraction offers a 360° panorama of Poland's capital.https://t.co/VeEapOmh4s — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 9, 2025 The result is an incredible level of explorable detail, from major landmarks, such as the communist-era Palace of Culture and Science and Varso Tower, the EU’s tallest building, down to the seating steps and bars along the Vistula River boulevards. The map also features graveyards reflecting Warsaw and Poland’s diverse past, including Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Jewish and Tatar Muslim graves. Around 1 November, when Poles visit cemeteries around All Saints’ Day, candles glow around the graves. A final touch Yildirim has added is a flight simulator, allowing users to travel over the city – and complete missions – in a Cessna aeroplane, an air ambulance, a flying car, or even a UFO that takes off from the Copernicus Science Centre and travels to the National Stadium. I turned Warsaw into a flight sim 🛩️ Take off from Chopin, fly through the ring over the Palace of Culture, then land a UFO inside Stadion Narodowy as the roof opens 🛸 Desktop only for now. Can you land it? 👇 pic.twitter.com/DT2fdk1Vem — Bedirhan (@bedcodes) October 27, 2026 Speaking to Notes from Poland, Yildirim says that he moved to Poland in 2022 to pursue a job in IT before starting his own business. Initially living in Kraków, the country’s second-largest city, he then moved to Warsaw in 2025. Asked what his own personal favourite places in the city are, Yildirim points to Warsaw’s parks, such as Skaryszewski, Pole Mokotowskie and Łazienki. His favourite neighbourhood is Saska Kępa on the right bank of the Vistula. The software engineer adds that his project is an example of how AI can be an “amazing tool to do 90% of the job very quickly”. The remaining 10% of human input “is what keeps it from being ‘AI slop'”. Yildirim says that, without the use of AI, the map of Warsaw he created would have needed an entire team to build over a period of months. World.title: Poland detains Ukrainian accused of arson attack in Romania on behalf of Russia
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has detained a Ukrainian citizen who is wanted by Romania on suspicion of involvement in an arson attack on a defence company carried out on behalf of Russia. On Tuesday, the Polish police’s Central Investigation Bureau (CBŚP) announced that anti-terrorism officers had detained the man, who can be named only as Artem S. under Polish privacy law, in Warsaw under a European Arrest Warrant issued by Romania. In the early hours of 14 September, a fire broke out in the city of Brașov, Romania, in the immediate vicinity of premises belonging to Carfil, a manufacturer of military equipment. Carfil is a subsidiary of ROMARM, a state-owned defence company. On Monday this week, the Romanian Intelligence Service (SRI) said it had determined that the fire had been deliberately caused by a “sabotage network coordinated from Russia”. It added that “several citizens of former Soviet states who reside in the EU” had been involved in the arson attack. The SRI also revealed that the group’s activities were not limited to Romania. “Its coordinators in Russia had assigned it a wide range of targets across the region, including state-owned and private arms manufacturing facilities, as well as sites of military and industrial interest.” In a separate statement, Romania’s Directorate for Investigating Organised Crime and Terrorism (DIICOT) confirmed that the suspects were a Ukrainian, who was at large in Poland, and two Belarusians, who had already been detained in Germany, where they “had been preparing to commit similar acts”. Polish broadcaster RMF reports, based on sources, that Artem S.’s role in the Brașov attack was to identify a target and to arrange payment for those involved. A Polish court will now decide whether the 25-year-old should be extradited to Romania. Poland itself has been a primary target for Russia’s campaign of sabotage and other so-called “hybrid actions” in Europe. Many of those detained and convicted have been Ukrainian and Belarusians, though some Polish citizens have also been implicated. Poland is the "primary focus" of Russia's sabotage campaign in Europe, finds a new report by the International Centre for Counter-Terrorism. Among 151 incidents identified since 2022, 31 of them took place in Poland – more than in any other country https://t.co/QXfSI00FD6 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 3, 2026 In some cases, such operatives are amateurs – so-called “disposable agents” – recruited, coordinated and paid through messaging service Telegram. Some have also been pre-existing criminal groups hired by Russia to carry out such tasks. In August, a drone production plant belonging to private Polish arms company WB Electronics was targeted in an arson attack that Poland has blamed on Russia. The following month, a ground station in Poland used by Starlink, Elon Musk’s satellite internet company, was likewise hit by an arson attack that Poland blamed on Russia. Two Turkish men were later detained in Germany on suspicion of carrying out the attack. World.title: Poland and UK sign Warsaw Defence Plan to “deter Russian threats”
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland and the United Kingdom have signed the Warsaw Defence Plan, an agreement to enhance their cooperation on security. The aim, says the British Ministry of Defence, is to “deter Russian threats”. The plan, which follows on from the two countries signing a strategic defence partnership earlier this year, will include joint development and production of defence technologies and military exercises in the Baltic Sea. The UK and Poland share a deep and historical defence partnership. Today, Defence Secretary @WesStreeting signed the Warsaw Defence Plan to bring our two nations’ Armed Forces and industries closer together and help ensure collective security in Europe. 🇬🇧🤝🇵🇱 pic.twitter.com/IP98D1Qs1L — Ministry of Defence 🇬🇧 (@DefenceHQ) October 27, 2026 “Poland is one of the UK’s closest allies – from flying together in the Battle of Britain, to breaking the Enigma code, they have been a vital partner for our defence for nearly a century,” said British defence secretary Wes Streeting on a visit to Warsaw. “The new Warsaw Defence Plan honours this cooperation and sets out how we will continue to work together today, building a stronger Europe in a stronger NATO,” he added. His Polish counterpart, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, declared that “the Polish-British alliance has never been as strong as it is now”. Both he and Streeting also emphasised the importance of working together to support Ukraine. Among the aims listed for the plan are collaboration in the development and manufacture of next-generation air-defence missiles, as well as drones and counter-drone technologies. Earlier this year, Poland and the UK, along with Germany, France and Italy, agreed to jointly develop and procure air-defence systems, including missiles and drones. The Warsaw Defence Plan also pledges to “increase defensive maritime activity in the Baltic Sea through exercises and regional coordination, helping British and Polish forces protect vital lines of communication in the sea”. The two countries will also seek to build upon existing cooperation between their defence industries, including Poland’s purchase of CAMM-ER surface-to-air missiles and 100 launchers from MBDA and last year’s strategic partnership on ammunition production between Poland’s PGZ and Britain’s BAE Systems. Poland and the UK have signed a major new defence and security treaty. The agreement includes plans to jointly develop a new air-defence missile, hold large-scale military exercises, and cooperate on countering Russian hybrid attacks https://t.co/cXeYT2u1lw — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 27, 2026 This week’s agreement builds upon the Northolt Treaty signed by Poland and the UK in May this year, under which the two countries agreed to cooperate more closely on security. Last year, Poland signed a similar agreement upgrading relations with France. That followed a strategic partnership agreement with Sweden the previous year. In April this year, Poland signed new comprehensive strategic partnership agreements with South Korea and Japan. This year, it has also deepened security ties with Canada and Norway. In November, Poland will host the first military exercises organised by the so-called Coalition of the Willing. Thousands of personnel from the UK, Poland, France and Germany will test operational readiness for a multinational force to secure a potential future Ukraine peace deal. World.title: US chooses Poland to host service facility for Patriot missiles
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The United States has chosen Poland to host a new centre for servicing and maintaining missiles used in Patriot air defence systems, in a decision described as “historic” by both Washington and Warsaw. It was chosen ahead of bids from four other European countries. The new centre, the first of its kind ot be located outside the US itself, will “dramatically shorten turnaround times and further secure critical supply lines”, said the US Department of War, announcing the decision on Tuesday. Undersecretary of War Michael P. Duffey added that the choice of a country on NATO’s eastern front “sends a clear message [that] the Alliance is united, serious about deterrence, and ready to back our words with action”. Poland Selected to Host Historic PAC-3 Missile Maintenance Facility, Strengthening Allied Burden-Sharing and Transatlantic Security – U.S. Department of War – Release | @DeptofWar https://t.co/2caqADRRx8 — US Embassy Warsaw (@USEmbassyWarsaw) October 27, 2026 The decision was welcomed by Polish leaders, with defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz saying that it shows “Poland is a trusted ally and holds an extremely important place on the map of global security”. His deputy minister, Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka, said that Poland was chosen ahead of rival bids from Germany, the Netherlands and Norway to host the facility. However, US ambassador to Poland Thomas Rose indicated that Sweden, not Norway, was the fourth candidate. Kosiniak-Kamysz and Sobkowiak-Czarnecka both pointed to the role President Karol Nawrocki had played in securing the deal. On many issues, the government is in conflict with the opposition-aligned president, but the two sides worked together on the Patriot bid. Historyczna decyzja! Centrum serwisowania pocisków PAC-3 do systemów Patriot powstanie w Polsce! 🇵🇱 O europejską lokalizację tej inwestycji rywalizowały cztery państwa, obok Polski – Niemcy, Holandia i Norwegia. Już na etapie składania wniosków polska oferta została oceniona… pic.twitter.com/wUgFhzlzUk — Magdalena Sobkowiak (@magdasobkowiak) October 27, 2026 Nawrocki, a conservative, is a close ally of his US counterpart, Donald Trump. The Polish president’s national security advisor, Bartosz Grodecki, claimed that it was “thanks to a conversation between” the two presidents that the new Patriot servicing centre was being established in Poland. The head of Nawrocki’s foreign policy office, Marcin Przydacz, meanwhile, thanked Washington for choosing Poland to host the new centre. “The Polish-American alliance and the good atmosphere in relations once again yield results,” he declared. “We can see what positive effects the President’s activity brings for Poland.” Poland is one of a number of European countries that operate Patriot air defence systems. Others include Germany, Greece, the Netherlands, Romania, Sweden and Ukraine. The new centre will service the PAC-3 missiles used in Patriot batteries. The competition to host the facility was announced in July, with the selection made by the US government in conjunction with American defence giant Lockheed Martin, the producer of missiles. In its press release, the Pentagon emphasised that, although Poland would host the new centre, its work would “be underpinned by robust, transatlantic industrial cooperation, with critical supply chain integration led by Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden”. Sweden will deploy Patriot air defence systems and around 100 accompanying military personnel to Poland later this year to protect the NATO logistics hub in the city of Rzeszów, which is the main conduit for aid to Ukraine https://t.co/cq9p7OVO7E — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 6, 2026 Global demand for Patriot systems has risen significantly, with the United States expending at least 1,500 interceptors in its war with Iran, according to the Center for Strategic and International Studies. Patriot systems have also been crucial in Ukraine’s defence against Russian ballistic missile attacks, although Ukraine’s supply of missiles is now almost entirely exhausted. After Trump recently suggested that he would authorise Ukraine to produce its own missiles, Poland offered to host any such factory, to ensure its security. However, today’s announcement concerns a site for maintaining and servicing, rather than producing, the missiles. Poland has proposed that, if the United States grants Ukraine permission to produce its own missiles for Patriot air-defence systems, the facility could be located on Polish territory to ensure its security https://t.co/jaQng5wtGg — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 28, 2026 The decision cements Poland’s position as one of Washington’s most important security partners in Europe. War secretary Pete Hegseth has praised Poland as a “model ally”, noting that it has for years met NATO’s defence spending targets, unlike many other member states. Poland has also been a significant customer for US defence firms. Between 2021 and 2025, Poland was NATO’s biggest arms importer, with 44% of the equipment it purchased coming from American suppliers. Last year, Poland signed a $2 billion deal for the US to provide logistical support and training for Patriot systems. This year, it was announced that Polish state defence group PGZ would become the first European producer of American Barracuda-500M cruise missiles. Poland will become the first country in Europe to produce cruise missiles developed by US defence firm Anduril Industries The agreement will "transform the continent's defence industry", claims Anduril https://t.co/LPJnwOLfp2 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 7, 2026 Warsaw is also currently lobbying for a new permanent US military base to be established in Poland, with the government and the president once again putting aside their differences to promote the idea. World.title: Germany’s economy minister hails Poland as “example of great success”
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Germany’s economy minister, Katherina Reiche, has praised Poland as an “example of great success”, saying that it offers a model for other countries. Speaking at the fourth Polish-German Economic Forum in Warsaw, which she opened on Monday alongside Polish finance minister Andrzej Domański, Reiche highlighted the deepening trade ties between the two countries. She noted that bilateral trade last year exceeded €180 billion for the first time, up from €25 billion in 2000, reports Deutsche Welle. Germany has been Poland’s biggest trading partner for decades, although recent data suggest that China, for the first time in history, overtook Germany as Poland’s largest source of imports in July this year. Germany has also long been a major investor in Poland. But Reiche welcomed growing recent investments by Polish companies in Germany, which she said was helping to create jobs. Earlier this year, for example, Poland’s largest manufacturer of trains and trams, Pesa, announced the acquisition of German rival HeiterBlick as part of its efforts to expand its operations across Europe. Reiche noted that around 1,000 Polish companies have invested in Germany, while about 1,600 German companies have invested in Poland, reports Reuters. Poland’s largest manufacturer of trains and trams, Pesa, has announced the acquisition of German rival HeiterBlick as it seeks to expand its operations across Europe https://t.co/N1wE1aYL5m — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 12, 2026 Among leading German firms with a presence in Poland are carmakers Mercedes-Benz, which recently invested around €1 billion to build its first electric-only van plant there, which produces its Crafer vans at a plant near the city of Poznań. Reiche also pointed to Poland’s stellar economic performance since joining the European Union in 2004, noting that its GDP has grown by an annual average of 3.8% over that period – twice the EU-wide average. Poland’s economy is on the verge of becoming the 20th largest in the world, with the country hoping to become part of the G20. Meanwhile, Domański used his remarks at the Polish-German Economic Forum to warn Europe against repeating past mistakes as it confronts a rapidly changing geopolitical landscape. He said the continent faced a “unique” historical moment. “The world is changing faster than ever, and we are facing new geopolitical, strategic, and technological challenges.” Europe would need a strong economy and new sources of growth to meet those challenges, he added, warning against what he called “economic naivety” and urging Europe – and Germany in particular – not to return to its previous approach to Russia. “I would like to state this very clearly: Europe must learn from the past. Under no circumstances can there be a return to the previous approach toward Russia. Poland will never agree to that,” Domański said, noting that this position applied in particular to renewed use of Russian energy imports. “We will only be resilient once we are truly independent of external, unstable suppliers of raw materials,” he added, emphasising that Poland and Germany must “work together to modernise the European energy market, focus on technological change and bear security in mind”. Debata ministra @Domanski_Andrz i minister @BMWE_ Katherina Reiche podczas IV Polsko-Niemieckiego Forum Gospodarczego. 💬 Powinniśmy skupić się na cenach energii, ale potrzebne jest znacznie bardziej zdecydowane podejście do ochrony rynku europejskiego. I nie chodzi tu tylko o… pic.twitter.com/NVPUjwx7jA — Ministerstwo Rozwoju i Technologii (@MRiTGOVPL) October 26, 2026 Following the forum, Domański and Reiche attended a meeting of the Friends of Industry, an informal initiative bringing together EU member states to coordinate positions on industrial policy, competitiveness and the operating conditions for European industry. The meeting was attended by representatives of 21 EU member states and European Commission Vice-President Stéphane Séjourné. Discussions focused on protecting and strengthening European industry’s competitiveness and economic security amid geopolitical challenges. “Today, we are facing the consequences of the fact that, in the past, competitiveness was often relegated to second, third or fourth place. Competitiveness took a back seat to other priorities, with the result that European industry now faces serious challenges,” said Domański. He proposed making competitiveness a core EU policy priority, cutting red tape, strengthening the single market, lowering energy costs, investing in strategic technologies such as AI, and tightening trade protections against unfair foreign competition. World.title: Witness testifies Polish president discussed “making money bringing girls” to hotel where they worked 20 years ago
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A former colleague of Polish President Karol Nawrocki from when he worked as a security guard in a hotel two decades ago testified in court that he told her it was possible to “make some extra money by bringing in girls”. She says she saw him escort a woman onto the premises. The testimony was given after the president himself sued the owner of a website that, just before last year’s presidential election, published claims that Nawrocki had been involved in procuring prostitutes while working at the luxury Grand Hotel in the town of Sopot. The court case began in September but, until now, hearings have been held behind closed doors. However, the judge decided that today’s session would be open to the public, with two former colleagues of Nawrocki giving evidence. The president himself is due to appear before the court in January. 🗣️ "Moją automatyczną oceną było, że to prostytutka i alfons." Nowe zeznania w procesie Karola Nawrockiego z wydawcą Onetu. Przed sądem stanęła była współpracowniczka prezydenta z sopockiego Grand Hotelu. pic.twitter.com/Cn6KyMSjcv — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) October 27, 2026 In May last year, less than a week before the second round of the election, in which Nawrocki was standing in a run-off against rival Rafał Trzaskowski, Onet, a leading news website, published an article titled “Karol Nawrocki and the secrets of the Grand Hotel”. It claimed, based on information provided by unnamed former colleagues of the future president, that he had “participated in bringing prostitutes for guests of the Grand Hotel in Sopot while working there as a security guard” almost 20 years earlier. Onet said that its interlocutors wished to remain anonymous for their own safety, but had expressed their willingness to testify in court if required. The revelations caused a major scandal, but were vigorously denied by Nawrocki, a conservative candidate aligned with the right-wing opposition, who called them a “pack of lies”. He then went on to narrowly defeat Trzaskowski in the election. Conservative presidential candidate @NawrockiKn says he will sue news website @onetpl for claims it published today that he procured prostitutes for clients at a luxury hotel when working there as a security guard. He called the report "a bunch of lies" https://t.co/WZ4rZWfFT1 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 26, 2025 Nawrocki then sued Ringier Axel Springer Polska (RASP), the Polish subsidiary of a German-Swiss media house that owns Onet, demanding an apology. RASP stood by Onet, saying that its reporting was “factual”. At today’s hearing, one of Onet’s sources, Natasza Geldon, who worked at the hotel in 2006 and 2007, was questioned. She said that, one evening, she had noticed Nawrocki leading a man and a woman into the hotel, before then taking only the woman into a lift and returning alone. This had struck her as unusual, because staff were not supposed to escort guests into the hotel, “let alone take them upstairs”, said Geldon, quoted by broadcaster TVP. “When Karol came back downstairs, I asked him what was going on,” continued the witness. “He said it was possible to make some extra money by bringing girls in, and asked if I wanted to join in.” Geldon refused the offer, telling the court that, “as a young girl, 19 years old, I had the impression that a pimp had been coming in with a prostitute”. However, when asked to confirm if she had seen prostitutes in the hotel, Geldon said: “I don’t know. It’s hard to say. It was just that one incident.” A second witness, Łukasz Franczak, described as a longtime friend of Nawrocki who worked alongside him in security at the Grand Hotel, also gave evidence on Tuesday after being called by Nawrocki’s legal team. He testified that there had been prostitutes in the hotel. However, he added that he had not heard of any organised operation to supply them to guests; nor had he witnessed Nawrocki procuring prostitutes or discussing payment for them, reported Onet from the hearing. Franczak’s testimony was welcomed by Nawrocki’s former national security advisor, Sławomir Cenckiewicz, who said that it showed that those making claims against the president have no evidence of his involvement in any wrongdoing. Oni się wszyscy teraz nakręcają jak szaleni, nie czytając tego co sami piszą na własnej stronie… No i dowiedzieli się dzisiaj, że w hotelach bywają prostytutki 🙂 A ja to wszystko czytam na bieżąco, a tam słynny Łukasz z Gdańska, ulubiony świadek-historyk Antka Dudka, i… https://t.co/9sKGZT4PpD — Sławomir Cenckiewicz (@Cenckiewicz) October 27, 2026 RASP’s lawyers have called for Nawrocki himself to testify in the case. The president’s legal team wanted him to provide his testimony in writing, according to Onet. But on Tuesday, judge Aleksandra Orzechowska ordered Nawrocki to give testimony directly – either in person or remotely – at the next hearing, which is scheduled for 18 January 2027, reports broadcaster TVN. World.title: Guitar Legend Carlos Santana to Return to Czech Republic in 2027
World.content:
Legendary guitarist Carlos Santana will return to the Czech Republic on July 22, 2027, for an outdoor concert in the Castle Gardens of Slavkov u Brna, near Brno.

The ten-time Grammy Award winner will perform as part of his Planet of Free Will Global Tour 2027, bringing more than five decades of music to the Czech audience.

Known for blending rock, blues, jazz and Latin rhythms, Santana has built a distinctive sound that has influenced generations of musicians and listeners.



His performance at the 1969 Woodstock festival helped establish him as an international star, while early albums such as Santana*(1969) and Abraxas (1970) produced classics including “Evil Ways,” “Black Magic Woman” and “Oye Como Va.”

Santana reached another career milestone with the 1999 album Supernatural, which featured collaborations with artists including Rob Thomas. The record became a global hit, spawning the singles “Smooth” and “Maria Maria” and winning nine Grammy Awards, including Album of the Year.

Over his career, Santana has received ten Grammy Awards and three Latin Grammy Awards. He was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1998, received the Kennedy Center Honors and was ranked 11th on *Rolling Stone* magazine’s list of the 100 greatest guitarists of all time.

Despite his long career, Santana continues to release new music and perform internationally. His live shows are known for extended guitar solos, Latin-inspired rhythms and a mix of classic hits and newer material.

Tickets will cost CZK 2,000, plus booking fees.

General ticket sales start on October 30, 2026, at noon, through Ticketmaster and Ticketportal.

World.title: Prague Metronome Lets People Donate to Charity for Just 50 CZK
World.content:
Prague’s Metronome is taking on a charitable role through a new initiative that allows people to pay for a minute of illumination while supporting one of six nonprofit organizations.

The project, called Puls města (City Pulse), was launched by real estate company PSN, which operates the landmark on Letná Hill. Donations start at 50 Czech crowns, and participants can choose which organization they want to support.



The new initiative connects its lighting system with fundraising, allowing members of the public to contribute through the project’s website.

Six Colors, Six Charitable Causes

Each participating organization is represented by a different color. Red supports the Tereza Maxová Foundation for Children, while light blue represents the Kapka naděje (Drop of Hope) Endowment Fund.

Yellow is associated with Díky, že můžem, an initiative focused on civic engagement and democratic values. Pink represents Pink Crocodile, dark blue supports the AutTalk Endowment Fund, founded by Kateřina Sokolová, and green is dedicated to the Fund for Endangered Children.

Visitors can select a cause and make a contribution directly through the project’s website.

Donations Start at 50 CZK

Contributions range from 50 to 9,999 CZK. Regardless of the amount donated, each payment purchases exactly one minute of illumination. A larger contribution therefore does not extend the lighting time.

The website also displays the amount raised for each organization, allowing donors to follow the campaign’s progress. A virtual queue shows when each participant’s turn is scheduled, with the expected time provided after payment.

World.title: Prague’s Golden Eye to Host Japanese Brunch With Live Chef Demonstrations
World.content:
Prague’s Golden Eye bar at Fairmont Hotel is hosting a Japanese-inspired brunch combining traditional ceremonies, live sushi preparation, premium food and signature cocktails.

The afternoon will begin with Kagami Biraki, a traditional Japanese sake barrel-opening ceremony often associated with celebrations and new beginnings.



Guests will then be able to watch a live tuna carving, one of the event’s main attractions.

The programme will also include omakase bites, with chefs preparing sushi at a live station. Guests can pair the food with signature cocktails and a curated selection of wines throughout the afternoon.

A live DJ will provide the soundtrack, adding music to the Japanese-inspired dining experience.

The event is designed exclusively for adults, with tickets priced at CZK 7,900 per person. Full prepayment is required to secure a booking.

Reservations can be made through Golden Eye’s online booking page.

World.title: Hip-Hop Star Xzibit Coming to Prague’s Roxy on November 17
World.content:
West Coast rap legend Xzibit will perform at Prague’s ROXY on November 17, bringing his show featuring tracks from his latest album and some of his best-known hits.

Presented by Gotobeat and Enjoy Events, the show will feature music from *Kingmaker*, alongside career highlights including “X,” “Multiply,” “Paparazzi” and “What’s the Difference.”



Xzibit returns with new album Kingmaker

A major name in West Coast hip-hop since the 1990s, Xzibit built his reputation through his distinctive deep voice, forceful delivery and collaborations with some of the genre’s biggest artists.

His albums Restless, Man vs. Machine and Weapons of Mass Destruction helped establish him as one of the defining rappers of his generation. His work with Dr. Dre, Eminem, Snoop Dogg and Ice Cube further cemented his place in hip-hop, while his television career brought him to a wider audience as the host of MTV’s Pimp My Ride.

Released on May 16, 2025, Kingmaker marked Xzibit’s first solo studio album since 2012.
