World.title: Flu Season Arrives in Croatia Early, But Vaccines Are Late
World.content:
October the 29th, 2026 – Despite flu season having arrived earlier than ever in Croatia this year, the vaccines are late. There are already around 200 people with more severe clinical pictures requiring medical care.

This year, the flu season has arrived earlier than expected in Croatia, and the vaccine is unfortunately not yet available. Lucija Zderic reports for Index that while the regular vaccination process is currently awaited, paediatric clinics are already full of children dealing with more severe respiratory and intestinal infections. Colds and other viruses are also duly expected to cause issues at this time of year, but the early arrival of flu is particularly worrying because the virus has begun to spread before protection through vaccination has even become available.

there are currently around 200 more serious cases

Last year, flu vaccines were secured for Croatia right at the beginning of October, and vaccination began in the middle of the month. This year, however, October is nearing its end, the vaccines have not yet arrived in Croatia, and the number of cases is rising in the meantime.

“In Croatia, 201 reports of flu cases have been received. Cases have been recorded in around ten counties, and the highest reporting rate was recorded in Dubrovnik-Neretva County. Flu mostly affects preschool children. Laboratory analyses have sporadically confirmed influenza virus type A, and individual cases are also being recorded in other EU countries, where this type of virus also predominates,” the Croatian Institute of Public Health said. We asked why the vaccine delivery is delayed, when its availability is expected, and whether shifting the start of vaccination will affect the timely protection of citizens ahead of the peak of the flu season.

“This season, a total of 420,000 doses of flu vaccine were ordered according to the needs expressed at the end of last season. Due to the simultaneous change of all three vaccine strains at the request of the World Health Organization, the manufacturer informed us of a possible delay in the delivery of the seasonal flu vaccine and the possibility of delivering the ordered doses in three parts. According to announcements, we expect the vaccine to be available at the beginning of November, but the exact date will be known in a few days. A similar situation exists in most European countries, i.e. it is a global delay in the delivery of vaccines from various manufacturers for the stated objective reasons.”

the very peak of the flu season is expected at the end of 2026

According to the World Health Organisation, after flu vaccination it takes approximately two weeks for the body to develop protection against the flu virus. “In Croatia, flu usually occurs most intensively after the Christmas holidays, with the peak usually in mid-February. As soon as the vaccine is available, it will be distributed to the final vaccinators. Additionally, we must emphasise that for many years we usually started seasonal vaccination at the beginning of November; only in the last few years has vaccination begun at the end of October,” the Croatian Institute of Public Health said.

The right to free vaccination primarily belongs to people at increased risk of a more severe form of the disease and the development of complications. Those who do not belong to these groups can be vaccinated at their own expense by requesting a private prescription from their family doctor, buying the vaccine at a pharmacy and bringing it to the doctor who will vaccinate them. The price of the vaccine ranges from approximately €15 to €25, depending on availability and place of purchase.

children are spreading rsv, rotavirus and rhinovirus

Despite being the most dangerous by far, influenza is not the only virus filling paediatric waiting rooms these days. Among children, common colds, RSV and rotavirus, which cause intestinal infections, are also spreading with ease.

“RSV season is a period in which we must take particular care of the youngest children. When the virus starts to spread, the increase in the number of ill children can be sudden, so a larger number of young patients with similar symptoms can appear in a single day. RSV is particularly dangerous for infants, especially children in the first year of life, while older children usually have a milder clinical picture. Children with chronic diseases, for example heart and lung diseases and certain hereditary diseases, are also at increased risk. The infection can start with cold-like symptoms and then develop into a severe cough and difficulty breathing,” paediatrician Snježana Kapor Jeričević revealed.

She added that treatment mainly includes inhalation therapy, re-hydration and cleaning of the upper airways.

what should parents know?

“We give parents instructions on caring for their child at home and the symptoms they should pay attention to, such as refusal of food, unusual tiredness and difficulty breathing. Signs of difficulty breathing can include flaring of the nostrils, more pronounced abdominal movement when breathing, and unusual sounds when inhaling or exhaling. In diagnostics, rapid tests now help us determine which virus is involved, which makes it easier and faster for us to make a diagnosis.”

When it comes to rotavirus, which is present throughout the year but is somewhat more frequent at the end of summer, the paediatrician explains that it is the cause of intestinal infections that most often manifest as vomiting and diarrhoea. In treatment, re-hydration is the most important. “The most important thing in treatment is to replace the lost fluid and electrolytes, and this by using re-hydration solutions, not just water. Children lose large amounts of electrolytes through vomiting and diarrhoea, which parents sometimes forget. Probiotics can also help in treatment, as they can shorten the duration of the illness by a day or two,” paediatrician Kapor Jeričević noted.

While other respiratory and intestinal infections are already spreading among the youngest, the question remains whether the flu vaccine will arrive in time for citizens to protect themselves before the expected rise in the number of cases. The Croatian Institute of Public Health says its availability is expected at the beginning of November, but until then vaccination remains on hold, despite the fact that flu cases have already been recorded.

World.title: Calls for Protest Are Spreading Across Zagreb
World.content:
October the 28th, 2026 – Calls for a protest are currently spreading across Zagreb, with the organisers insisting that there are no political parties involved.

Posters have begun appearing across Zagreb calling on the public to a protest named “Voice of Change/Glas Promjene”, announced for Saturday the 21st of November, at 10:00 on Ban Josip Jelačić Square. Behind the call stands the civic initiative “Time for Change/Vrijeme za Promjenu”, which, via social media, is inviting people to gather against corruption, abuse of power and institutional irresponsibility.

Index reports that the posters highlight the message “All of Croatia, one voice”, and the organisers say they want to bring together people who are dissatisfied with the standard of living, the political situation and the work of institutions. “Want change? Then don’t be the person who doesn’t come to Ban Josip Jelačić Square at 10:00 on the 21st of November,” one of the posts calling for the protest states.

“no more empty promises”

The organisers point to the rising cost of living, the increasingly difficult independence of young people and the feeling that wages are not keeping up with prices. “Basic life needs are becoming a luxury, young people cannot afford to leave their parents’ home for something of their own, wages are getting lower, while the quality of life and prices demand more and more,” they state in a post.

The organisers answered several questions about the goals of the protest. “The protest is directed against corruption, abuse of power and the lack of institutional accountability. We demand transparent management of public money, equal laws for everyone, accountability of those who hold public office and concrete systemic changes, not just empty promises,” they said. They emphasised that the initiative is not connected to any political party and that its goal is not to replace one set of politicians with another. “The initiative is not tied to any political party, nor is the goal to replace one politicians with others, but to demand a system in which institutions work in the interest of citizens,” they stated.

They added that they want to shape the concrete demands together with citizens so that they are clear, achievable and measurable.

is the protest against hdz or just corruption asa vague term?

One of the questions put to the organisers was whether the protest is directed against HDZ. “The protest is directed against corruption, abuse of power and the lack of institutional accountability, regardless of who is in power. That includes the actions of the HDZ when they are the subject of such criticism,” they replied. In a separate post they further emphasised that the protest is not organised in the name of any political party and that they do not belong to any political option. “This is a civic initiative for all people who have had enough of corruption, lack of transparency, institutional irresponsibility and an uncertain future for us and our children,” they said.

serbian protests were mentioned

The organisers also commented on the protests in Serbia, answering the question of whether the situation there prompted them to organise a gathering in Croatia. “The situation in Serbia has certainly shown how important civic unity and persistence are, but the motivation is much broader than that,” they stated. They added that their goal is to encourage citizens of different political views to act together. “The goal is for all of us, regardless of political views, to become active and together build a better future. Change begins when we stop just watching and decide to participate,” they said.

they want to see protests across croatia

Although a protest in Zagreb has so far been announced, the organisers are also thinking about gatherings in other Croatian cities. When asked whether the protest would have a greater impact if all citizens gathered in one city, they replied that for the start it is more important to enable people to participate in their own communities. “I think that for the start it is important to enable people to gather in their own cities because not everyone has the possibility to travel to another location,” they stated. They added that, depending on the turnout and organisation, one large joint gathering could later be held. “And when we see the turnout and the strength of the organisation in each city, we can make one large joint gathering that will send an even stronger message. Step by step, city by city,” they said.

who is actually behind this initiative?

Calls for the protest are spreading via social media, among other things through the Instagram profile @vrijemezapromjene and the TikTok profile @glas.promjene. One of the posters also lists the TikTok profile @ala_secera as a contact for joining the Zagreb group. The organisers emphasise that all citizens can participate in the protest, regardless of age or occupation, including students, high-school graduates, employed people and pensioners. It is not yet known who the people behind the initiative are, how many of them are involved in the organisation, or whether the protest has been reported to the police. Details of the gathering programme have also not been published. The protest is, once again, announced for the 21st of November at 10:00 on Ban Josip Jelačić Square in central Zagreb.

World.title: Why Did Over 100,000 Croatian Landlords Turn Their Backs on Protesters?
World.content:
October the 28th, 2026 – Over 100,000 Croatian landlords who rent out their properties to tourists turned their backs on protesters fighting for their rights in Zagreb, but why?

The recent protest by private landlords held at Zrinjevac in Zagreb once again opened key questions about representation, expertise and the future of private accommodation in Croatia. Morski reports that although the organisers’ communication channels were burning with announcements of a mass turnout and a blockade of the capital, digital engagement analytics and sociological parameters indicated in advance the modest reach of the gathering. Despite the protest platform on social media gathering around 15,000 followers, the rate of active interaction at the peak of the campaign barely reached 10 percent. When these figures are run through the usual conversion rates to physical turnout, the final outcome on Zrinjevac brought only a few hundred people, a number comparable to a larger group of mushroom pickers rather than a serious national protest.

This modest turnout confronted the organisers with the relentless mathematical reality. Application of the sociological model of the Law of Dispersion of the Passive Majority clearly shows that in moments of major legislative upheavals the vast majority of affected actors consciously choose passivity and distance themselves from reactive groups. In this case, support from as many as 105,000 Croatian private landlords was absent from the public uproar. The silent majority, which avoids street activism, thereby sent a clear message that it rejects street pressure and demands institutional strength, expertise and well-founded arguments.

a hidden internal division…

The relatively weak turnout is also a direct consequence of a completely failed communication model. The use of populist rhetoric permeated with expressions about “serfs”, “cash machines” and accusations of a “witch hunt”, along with bizarre political constructions about secret coalitions and open threats of electoral votes from the podium, disqualified the organisers from serious professional dialogue. Serious professional associations do not negotiate with the authorities through street blackmail, but with exact indicators, legal analyses and constructive proposals.

Additionally, the protest revealed a deep, though publicly unspoken, socio-economic stratification within the sector itself. Namely, around 43,000 high-category facilities with 4 and 5 stars, in which significant funds have been invested, attract guests of higher purchasing power and naturally no longer share the same interests with the rest of the base that persists with the basic 3-star model. Nevertheless, owners of higher-quality accommodation, for pragmatic reasons and the desire to preserve good-neighbourly relations in local communities, choose complete passivity, leaving the protest margins to the loudest groups.

are amendments making landlords kick the can down the road?

On the other hand, uncertainty on the ground has been further heightened by the fact that the Government and the Ministry of Tourism and Sport (MINTS) have, through months of administrative silence, delayed precise clarifications of the new legislative amendments and the announced re-categorisation. This created information vacuum has served as fuel for the spread of panic, although it is clear that the state does not want to wipe out private accommodation, but to introduce necessary regulatory order and balance the interests of landlords with the remaining 90 percent of people. It is also expected that expert teams will take a sharper approach towards non-commercial accommodation which, under the guise of hosting, often represents a source of unfair competition.

Despite the tensions, the financial contribution of private landlords to Croatian tourism remains extremely significant. On the basis of around 600,000 registered beds, landlords through the fixed lump-sum tourist membership fee of €5.97 per bed generate around €3.58 million annually, while through the lump-sum tourist tax, with a conservative average of €50 per bed, they pay an additional €30 million. As such, more than €33.5 million of original money flows into the budgets and the system of tourist boards every year.

a constructive proposal…

Instead of directing these funds into ineffective general promotion or spending from the general state budget, a real and sustainable alternative offers the redirection of part of this earmarked pool into a National Programme of Targeted Vouchers for Apartment Transition. Modelled on successful European practices, such as Italian regional micro-grants in Tuscany and Apulia or the French Gîtes de France network, this model would directly help raise the quality of accommodation on the ground. The proposed vouchers would not be distributed in cash nor would they be intended for high-category 4- and 5-star facilities that already operate well. They would be used exclusively for co-financing the costs of interior modernisation and the purchase of equipment in 3-star facilities that demonstrably move into a higher category. Functioning as closed instruments intended for payment of works to registered domestic craftsmen and companies and for the purchase of equipment in Croatian shops, these millions would return directly into the entire Croatian economy, turning fiscal contributions into a driving force of sustainable market evolution.

World.title: Hungary Bins Orbán and Serbia Bins Vučić, Is Croatia Next?
World.content:
October the 28th, 2026 – Hungary toppled Viktor Orbán after 18 years in power, and now Serbia has binned Aleksandar Vučić, many are now asking the question of whether or not a big change for Croatia is next.

After almost 14 years of political dominance, Aleksandar Vučić just suffered a staggering electoral defeat in Serbia. Only a few months earlier, Viktor Orbán was toppled from power in Hungary after 16 years. Can Croatia, where the HDZ has been in power continuously since 2016, be next? Vedran Salvia reports for Index that although it is abundantly clear that Plenković’s government has not built an authoritarian system of the kind established by Orbán and Vučić, all three countries share long-term dominance by a single political option that has over time developed a strong network of influence in state institutions and the public sector.

Croatia is thus marked by strong clientelism, party-based appointments, corruption and seriously eroded institutions. During the ten years of Plenković’s rule, the HDZ has not attempted to confront this way of running the state, but has further strengthened it. A party membership card and connections still all too often count for more than knowledge and ability, and the consequences of such a system are felt in almost all parts of society.

both hungary and serbia seek to forge new paths

Interestingly, neither Orbán nor Vučić was defeated by the traditional opposition parties. In Hungary this was achieved by Péter Magyar, a former man of Orbán’s system, who with his party Tisza gathered a broad circle of voters dissatisfied with long-term rule. Among them were also people who had previously supported Orbán’s Fidesz. In Serbia, the situation was somewhat different. Vučić was defeated by the Student List, which emerged from the protests after the tragedy in Novi Sad, where on the 1st of November 2024, a railway station canopy collapsed and killed 16 people. The accident opened questions of corruption and institutional responsibility, and the protests grew into a mass movement against Vučić’s government.

75% of people think croatia is heading in the wrong direction

In Croatia, there is no shortage of dissatisfaction with the government. According to the latest CRO Demoskop, conducted from 6 to 8 October, more than 75 percent of respondents believe that the country is going in the wrong direction. Only a little over 17 percent think that Croatia is going in the right direction. At the same time, HDZ, although recording a drop in popularity, remains the strongest individual party with 25 percent support. The SDP is at a little under 20 percent, Možemo at almost 14 percent, and Most has approached 10 percent.

Interestingly, both HDZ and SDP are declining at the same time, while Možemo is growing. In other words, dissatisfaction with those in power is not automatically translating into growth for the largest opposition party, and this is one of the biggest differences between Croatia and the two neighbouring countries. In Hungary, Tisza managed to become the main political alternative to Orbán. In Serbia, the students almost completely pushed aside the traditional opposition and turned into a movement that can win power on its own.

Croatia does not have such a political force. It has several opposition parties, some of which govern important cities and have significant voter support, but none has so far managed to gather such a broad circle of dissatisfied citizens. At the same time, the Croatian opposition doesn’t have an individual who, like Magyar, could attract a significant part of the ruling party’s voters. Magyar’s success was not based solely on criticism of Orbán. As a man who came from within the Fidesz system, he was able to convince even some conservative voters that a change of government does not necessarily mean abandoning their political beliefs.

electoral maths still favours hdz…

Croatian electoral mathematics are also highly important. Croatia is divided into ten territorial electoral units, in each of which 14 seats are distributed separately. Therefore it is not only the total number of votes that matters, but also their distribution. HDZ greatly benefits from a strong party organisation and stable support in numerous parts of the country.

The boundaries of the electoral units were redrawn in 2023 after the Constitutional Court repealed the previous law. The new model was adopted by an HDZ majority and drew criticism for the illogical linking of certain areas. Political scientist Goran Čular then warned for Gong: “The prime minister said that the arrangement of electoral units is a technical issue, but HDZ is doing everything to ensure that it is not just a technical issue.” Nevertheless, HDZ’s victory back in 2024 cannot be attributed solely to the electoral system. Its coalition won 61 seats, fully 19 more than the SDP coalition, and it formed the government again with the help of the Homeland Movement. The electoral system can be an additional advantage for it, but for a change of government the opposition must first and foremost win significantly broader voter support.

the clear differences between hungary, serbia and croatia

Political scientist Tihomir Cipek, a professor at the Faculty of Political Science in Zagreb, spoke about why long-term governments fell in Hungary and Serbia, while in Croatia the HDZ still does not have an equally strong opponent. Cipek emphasises that the situations in Croatia, Hungary and Serbia are different. “In Hungary, a strong movement against Orbán was formed, which Péter Magyar gathered around his new party. Something similar happened in Serbia with the Student List. There we have a broad movement that brought together very different people, from liberals open to the world and cooperation with the European Union to Serbian nationalists who accused Vučić of betraying Kosovo and Metohija. Among them are both those who support sanctions against Russia and those who oppose them. Despite major political differences, what connected them all was opposition to Vučić,” Cipek said.

why has no similar movement emerged in croatia?

He explained that a similar movement against Plenković’s government has not emerged in Croatia because the political scene is already clearly divided among the existing parties. “In Croatia, the political system is structured along party lines. The type of people who found themselves together on the Student List in Serbia are already organised in different parties here. Here you have Možemo, which is for a more open society and, for example, cooperation with the EU, and on the other side Most, which has different views on migration and the openness of society.

It’s very difficult to imagine them all uniting into one front against the government. In addition, the electoral system in Croatia must also be taken into account. Serbia is one electoral unit, while Croatia has ten, so it is important how the opposition will perform in each of them,” Cipek explained. He believes that the successes of the students and Magyar show that even long-term power is no guarantee of political survival. “That victory in Serbia shows that nothing is certain. You can be in power for a long time, build strong influence in state structures, but citizens can still remove you with their activity and energy. In Croatia it is much harder to create such a broad movement, but that does not mean that it is impossible to change the government,” Cipek concludes.

is there even any potential for governmental change in croatia?

“There is potential for a change of government because dissatisfaction is high. The key is how it will be politically articulated. If the SDP and Možemo organise well, change is possible,” Cipek says. He believes that the opposition parties have drawn lessons from earlier electoral defeats, when they ran separately or tried to form alliances that did not bring the expected result. “There is dissatisfaction, but it needs to be turned into a political programme. With clear messages, good organisation and voter mobilisation it is also possible for the Croatian opposition to win. Nothing is eternal,” Cipek concluded.

World.title: Dubrovnik Airport: The Biggest Corruption Scandal Involving EU Cash?
World.content:
October the 28th, 2026 – The mayor of Dubrovnik has referred to the situation with Dubrovnik Airport being “the biggest corruption scandal involving EU cash in Croatia”.

Dubrovnik’s Ruđer Bošković Airport had to return a total of €22 million in European Union funds due to irregularities in public procurement procedures during a major airport modernisation project. Index reports that in addition to all kinds of financial problems, it was also revealed that part of the expensive infrastructure was never put into operation. Among such projects is the aircraft fuel supply system, in which pipes of the type used for sewage systems were allegedly installed.

These are irregularities in the modernisation project for Dubrovnik Airport that was carried out from 2013 to 2017. Around €200 million was secured from EU funds for the renovation, but due to disputed public procurement procedures, part of that money had to be returned. The latest obligation of three million euros recently became due. Dubrovnik Airport director Viktor Šober explained how the irregularities financially burdened the airport’s operations. “In one part we returned it, in one case it was automatically deducted from us, so we had to take out loans ourselves or use our own funds to make up for that shortfall which occurred primarily because of problematic public procurement procedures,” Šober said.

dubrovnik’s mayor calls out the airport’s director

Dubrovnik’s HDZ mayor Mato Franković recently spoke about the problems at Dubrovnik Airport and, at a session of the parliamentary Transport Committee, called out the former airport director Roko Tolić.

“When you take the overall damage that occurred at Dubrovnik Airport, we can say that this is the biggest corruption affair involving European money in the Republic of Croatia that no one is talking about,” Franković said. Tolić ran Dubrovnik Airport for a long period, more specifically from 2009 to 2018, when he was dismissed due to irregularities in public procurement. Since 2024 he has held the position of executive director of Aerodromi Crne Gore, the company that manages the airports in Podgorica and Tivat.

Tolić was previously politically active in the HSS. From 2000 to 2001 he was deputy mayor of Dubrovnik under Vito Bogdanović as a representative of that party. In the 2021 local elections he ran for Dubrovnik-Neretva County prefect as an independent candidate with the support of the SDP and HNS, but did not make it to the second round.

the alleged installation of sewage-type piping

In addition to returning an enormous sum of EU money, Dubrovnik Airport is also facing problems due to the unfinished aircraft fuel supply system. Although the system was paid for, it has not been used for years because serious mistakes were made during design and construction.

“The problem here is incorrect design and incorrect execution of the works. Plastic and glass pipes were installed that are essentially not used for the flow of fuel. Later, when studying the technical specifications, we realised that pipes used for sewage systems were installed there,” said Marina Bukvić from Ruđer Bošković Airport. The airport management hired a German company to check whether the system could be repaired and put into operation. However, the experts concluded that additional investments of several million euros would be needed to make it functional. This means that the airport has already paid for infrastructure it cannot use, and repairing it would require new large expenditures.

“we bought something we can’t use”

Šober warns that a way to solve the problem will have to be found, and he does not rule out legal steps either. “If this is not resolved, of course that part will be problematic for us as an airport. We paid for something we cannot use. In that case we will have to look for some solutions. Whether of a legal nature or some kind of agreements, but difficult talks certainly await us on this,” Šober said. Former director Roko Tolić did not wish to comment on the accusations against him. Dnevnik.hr also contacted the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) to check whether an investigation has been launched against those responsible for the irregularities in public procurement. They have not yet received a response.

World.title: Starship plans software changes to improve delivery robots' safety
World.content:
Safety improvements to the autonomous delivery robots on Estonia's streets will be primarily software-based, said Starship Technologies, after one of its machines was involved in a collision with a bus earlier this week.

A bus and a delivery robot collided in Tallinn on Monday evening, injuring several people after the driver braked sharply to avoid an accident.

Tallinn Transport (TLT) board member Andrei Novikov said the accident occurred during rush hour, when it was dark outside. A moving object suddenly appeared in front of the bus. "I don't know whether the bus driver was immediately able to understand whether it was a delivery robot, an animal or, for example, a cyclist," he noted.

He said the bus driver acted correctly by hitting the brake. Novikov added that, judging by the camera footage from the bus (see below), the "consequences would have been much worse" if the stop had been more sudden.

Novikov said that once the bus had stopped, the first thing the driver did was ask the passengers whether anyone needed help and whether an ambulance should be called. No one in the passenger compartment indicated that an ambulance was needed.

The driver then called TLT's control center and reported the situation. The driver asked what to do next. Together, they decided to continue operating the route, as the damage to the vehicle was minimal, none of the passengers needed an ambulance, it was rush hour and remaining stationary could have obstructed traffic throughout the area.

Passenger files health complaint

Novikov said, after the collision, the bus driver did not want to continue his working day because of his emotional state. He was sent home and a replacement bus driver took over. TLT has now filed a police report. Later, TLT received a complaint from a passenger concerning their health condition.

Lauri Potsepp, a board member of the Estonian Motor Insurance Bureau, said a bus driver is liable for damage caused to others by the bus regardless of fault. Therefore, if a person falls on a bus because the bus brakes sharply, the passenger can claim compensation from the bus's motor insurance provider, regardless of who caused the accident.

"Once the insurer has compensated for the damage, it will be determined who caused the accident, meaning what each of the drivers should have done to prevent the accident," Potsepp explained.

If it turns out that the accident was caused by the delivery robot or its operator, the motor insurance provider may seek reimbursement from the robot's owner for the compensation paid to the victims.

Potsepp added that, in addition to personal injuries, people's belongings may also have been damaged in such a situation. For example, clothing or a phone.

If a person does not know which insurer to submit a compensation claim to but knows the bus's registration number, they can find the insurer on the Motor Insurance Bureau's website.

"If they don't know the registration number, they can send an email to the Motor Insurance Bureau. We will determine who they can claim compensation from and direct the customer there," Potsepp said.

Robots move autonomously

Pepe Aaviksoo, head of operations at Starship Technologies, said the company is currently conducting an internal investigation to find out exactly what happened during the accident. Once the company has completed its assessment, it will share the information with the public and the police.

However, Aaviksoo could already say which improvements need to be made to prevent such situations. "The robot is largely a software-based machine, and the improvements are primarily software-based," he explained.

Aaviksoo said that, generally, the robots move autonomously. However, there are cases where a robot is connected to an office-based team, which takes over control if necessary. This is done either for safety reasons or because of a specific incident.

The office team then assesses what happened in the particular situation. However, Aaviksoo explained that robots are not constantly monitored. "This is simply not physically possible or economically sustainable, because we have several thousand robots around the world," he explained.

Yesterday, it was reported that the Robot left the scene of the accident. But Aaviksoo disputes this version of events. "After the robot was involved in the incident, it contacted the back-office team, whose task was to move the robot off the road to a safe location," he explained.

This meant that the robot had to move away from the middle of the road, and it waited by the curb. "From our perspective, the situation was clear, as indicated by the fact that the bus left the scene and we did not detect any rescue vehicles or police at the scene," Aaviksoo outlined.

The robot remained at the scene for approximately 10 minutes, he said.

Not all risks can be ruled out

Aaviksoo explained that although robots independently cross intersections every day, not all risks can be ruled out. "Just as a pedestrian, cyclist or driver cannot be absolutely safe," he said.

Aaviksoo added that this is an inevitable part of traffic, and the company's task is to do everything it can to ensure that its robots move safely in traffic.

Maria Pashkevich, head of the Transport Administration's Road Safety Department, said that specific traffic and safety requirements have been established for delivery robots in Estonia. For example, when crossing a road, a robot must ensure that it is safe to do so, comply with the obligation to give way and must not endanger other road users.

Pashkevich explained that in the event of a traffic accident, the robot's operator or user must ensure that the robot comes to a stop and does not pose any further danger to other road users.

If a person has been injured or killed in a traffic accident and the robot's operator is able to recognize this, for example through a camera, the operator or user must notify the Emergency Response Center and act according to the instructions received.

Pashkevich said that no traffic accidents involving delivery robots and resulting in human casualties have so far been registered in the Transport Administration's traffic accident information system.

"Although this does not mean that dangerous situations or such traffic accidents have not occurred," she added. For example, some incidents may not have been reported to the police.

World.title: European Commission rejects Baltics' €500 million anti-drone request
World.content:
The European Commission rejected an appeal from the Baltic defense ministers for €500 million in additional support for drone defense for the eastern flank, suggesting they borrow the money instead.

The ministers from Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania sent the request at the end of September.

The letter was classified, but Lithuanian Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas told Lithuanian public broadcaster LRT that the Baltic states wanted to combine drone detection, artificial intelligence and interception technology into an integrated air defence system.

However, the European Commissioner for Defense and Space, Andrius Kubilius, told LRT on Wednesday that the Commission had sent its response but could not offer the additional funding the Baltic states had sought.

"One possibility now is to make use of additional funding under the SAFE instrument. We will announce a new call in the near future, because €21 billion remained after the first call," Kubilius said.

The Security Action for Europe, or SAFE, instrument was launched last year and provides €150 billion in favourable loans for defense procurement across the EU.

World.title: FM: Zelenskyy wants to attend Ukraine Recovery Conference in Tallinn
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) said Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wants to participate in the Ukraine Recovery Conference in Tallinn next year alongside other world leaders.

Speculation recently circulated in the media that Ukraine's senior leadership would be unable to travel to Estonia for the conference at the end of January because of what is expected to be a difficult winter of war.

The minister said Zelenskyy and Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform) have already signed the personalized invitations to leaders for the event in January.

"And he certainly wants to participate here. And now we are moving forward. There is no longer any hesitation about whether the Ukraine Recovery Conference will take place here and at what level. It will be at the level of world leaders. And these leaders have been invited here to Tallinn by Ukrainian President Zelenskyy," Tsahkna said at the government's weekly press conference on Thursday.

However, his attendance will depend on the situation in Ukraine in January.

"So the aim is to do everything possible, including on Ukraine's part, to ensure that all world leaders, led by President Zelenskyy, participate here. But let's be honest, there are three months to go. This does not change our preparations and plans with Ukraine in any way," he added.

The foreign minister said the aim of the conference is to provide Ukraine with additional funding.

"We are not talking here about a few million that were promised or given to Ukraine – we are talking about billions and billions," he said.

Tsahkna said it is very much hoped Zelenskyy will be physically present at the conference, but if the situation in Ukraine is "so drastic by then" that the president cannot attend, it may help the conference meet its goal.

"The contributions will be even higher and there will be even greater commitment from other world leaders, because that would be a sign that the situation is indeed becoming very difficult," Tsahkna said.

The Ukraine Recovery Conference URC27 is scheduled to take place in Tallinn on January 28 and 29.

World.title: European Commission: Estonia among Europe's safest countries for road deaths
World.content:
Estonia saw 43 road deaths last year, placing it sixth overall among Europe's safest countries, according to final European Commission figures for 2025.

This figure, at 31 deaths per million, puts it slightly ahead of Finland, Germany and the Netherlands and significantly better than Latvia and Lithuania.

Roads in built up areas of Estonia were, however, significantly safer than those in rural areas, and while the incidence of deaths on the roads continues to fall in Estonia, it is not falling at a rate fast enough to meet a state target of half of 2019's figure by or in 2030. Also, the first half of this year saw a rise in road deaths in Estonia.

Sweden and Norway recorded 19 road deaths per million in 2025, followed by Denmark and Switzerland at 24, and Iceland at 26.

These were the only countries to post figures better than Estonia's 31 per million. Estonia was followed by Malta and Ireland at 33, Finland, Germany and the Netherlands (all 34) and Spain at 36, according to figures published on Wednesday.

Lithuania posted 138 road deaths last year, or 48 per million, while Latvia's figure was 64 per million.

The other highest rates were seen in Serbia (75 per million), Bulgaria (71), Romania (68) and Croatia (67).

Across the EU, EFTA countries and Serbia, 19,350 people died on the roads last year, or 43 per million,

The Commission said road deaths across Europe fell 3 percent on year to 2025 (580 fewer), and by 15 percent compared with 2019 (3,400 fewer road traffic deaths).

The Commission noted that, however, compared with the EU average, Estonia had a higher share of fatal road accidents on roads outside urban areas.

Between 2019 and 2025 road deaths in Estonia fell 17 percent. This, the Commission says, suggests Estonia will likely not meet its 2030 target of halving road deaths compared with 2019, though the Commission noted that annual figures can fluctuate significantly given the country's small population and low number of deaths in absolute terms.

The same data shows that in the first months of 2026 road deaths in Estonia rose sharply again, by over 10 percent. ERR reported in August that 30 people had died on Estonian roads in the first seven months of this year, four more than in the same period a year earlier.

For Europe as a whole, preliminary 2026 data show that in the first half of the year more countries saw road deaths fall by more than 5 percent compared with the same period in 2025 than saw them rise. The overall trend is therefore positive, the Commission said.

World.title: Police officers and rescue workers to see pay rises in 2027
World.content:
The government has allocated €7.3 million to increase the salaries of rescue workers and police officers, mainly those who are "lower-paid frontline employees," Minister of the Interior Igor Taro (Eesti 200) said on Thursday.

Speaking at the government's weekly press conference, he said rescue workers, police officers, border guards and emergency response operators at the Emergency Response Center are set to benefit from the funding boost.

"The government has allocated €7.3 million to our area of administration for pay raises. Salaries will increase in 3,764 positions from the beginning of next year," he said. In total, almost 8,000 people work in the ministry's area of administration.

"All of them deserve fair pay for their work. But the state's financial resources are limited, and this requires clear choices," Taro said.

"We are not distributing this additional money evenly as a percentage increase, but directing it primarily to lower-paid frontline employees," he explained.

Igor Taro. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

Rescue workers will receive the largest pay raise, with their salaries increasing by €140 per month, Taro said. This means the minimum salary for a rescue worker will rise by nearly 9 percent and the average salary by 8 percent.

"This will bring the average salary of rescue workers to approximately 85 percent of the Estonian average. This is a necessary step forward, but it cannot be considered sufficient," the interior minister acknowledged. The average salary was €2,092 in 2025.

Taro said the minimum salary for a police officer will rise by 4.4 percent, the average salary of a patrol police officer will rise above the Estonian average, and the minimum salary of an emergency response operator at the Emergency Response Center will rise by nearly 5 percent.

He added that SMIT technicians and customer support specialists will also receive pay raises. "The pay raise will be €90 per month," Taro said.

"The pay raise also covers the immediate supervisors of frontline employees who themselves perform operational duties. Other managers' salaries will not increase. Salaries at the Ministry of the Interior will not increase," he said.

World.title: Coolbet Estonia to shed up to 134 jobs at Tallinn HQ
World.content:
Estonian online gambling operator Coolbet is to lay off over 130 people, the company has announced.

Coolbet's Estonian headquarters notified the Unemployment Insurance Fund (Töötukassa) of its plans.

Coolbet COO Tomas Graham told ERR that the restructuring planned at VG Estonia, part of the Coolbet group, affects around 130 positions across the organisation. "We have started the official collective redundancy consultation process, and the final scope of the redundancies and the positions affected will become clear after it ends. Nothing has been finally decided today," he said.

Graham said the restructuring is needed to adapt to changing business needs and market conditions. "The need for restructuring stems from a combination of factors, including business challenges, weaker than expected results in the B2B side and growing regulatory and tax pressure in several of our markets," he said.

"The aim of the restructuring is to ensure Coolbet's long-term sustainability and competitiveness," Graham added. "We understand that the planned changes affect our employees and we are committed to ensuring the whole process is carried out responsibly and with respect."

The total number of layoffs is 134, business daily Äripäev reported.

VG Estonia OÜ, Coolbet's registered Estonian company name, had more than 300 employees on payroll as of the end of the third quarter this year, meaning nearly half of these are to be laid off.

The company says on its website that its international team comprises more than 1,100 people, including the 300 at the Tallinn head office.

The company has not yet filed its annual financial report for 2025, but in 2024, VG Estonia's turnover was reported at €23 million, with a net profit of €311,000.

According to quarterly reports submitted to the Tax and Customs Board (MTA), turnover this year has come to nearly €60 million. The average wage was reported at €4,100 per month gross.

Coolbet operates a second Estonian company, Staycool OÜ, which provides online gambling and sports betting services inside Estonia.

World.title: Estonia's volunteer rescuers send 146th aid shipment to Ukraine
World.content:
The Estonian Rescue Association (Päästeliit) has sent aid to Ukrainian rescuers, funded by donations and the Foreign Ministry, providing shelter, power and heating for over 30,000 people this winter.

The Kyiv consignment has included a minibus, two high-pressure tents with trailers, diesel heaters, power stations, lighting towers and heated blankets, enough to set up two emergency centers, Estonia's Embassy to Ukraine announced.

"This was our 146th shipment to Ukraine. Every time we hand over new equipment, we hope the situation will improve. Unfortunately, the head of Kyiv's rescue service confirmed that the situation is already worse than ever, and that the coming winter will put civilians — especially children — in an even more difficult position than last year," said Piia Kallas, head of the Estonian Rescue Association, a volunteer organization which complements the Rescue Board (Päästeamet).

Estonian Rescue Association delivered emergency tents and equipment to Ukraine's rescue services @SESU_UA. The aid will provide temporary shelter, electricity and heating for more than 30,000 people during the winter. The package was funded by @MFAestonia and donations. https://t.co/fOGAZI2tOy — Estonia in Ukraine (@EE_Ukraine) October 28, 2026

The shipment delivered to Kyiv included a minibus, two high-pressure tents with trailers, diesel heaters, battery power stations, battery-powered lamps, lighting towers, heated blankets, folding tables and chairs, fast chargers, thermos flasks, changing mats, children's toys and play mats. With this equipment, rescuers can set up two emergency centers where residents can find temporary shelter and warmth, charge their devices and receive psychological first aid.

A second delivery reached rescuers in Rivne oblast in southeastern Ukraine, including an off-road vehicle, a generator, battery power stations, lighting towers and heaters. The generator was donated by a private donor who decided to give their equipment to those who need it most.

Since the start of the invasion in February 2022, with support from donors and partners, the Rescue Association has delivered nearly €7 million worth of rescue equipment and vehicles to Ukrainian rescuers.

World.title: Estonian unicorn Pipedrive announces 'major' restructuring, office closures
World.content:
ERR has obtained a letter to employees from Pipedrive CEO Paulo Cunha , in which he writes that the company is significantly reducing its size in all its locations — which means fewer teams, management layers and locations. Cunha said the changes affect most of Pipedrive's current jobs and roles, adding the company will be speaking to every employee individually over the next two days, to explain whether their job is at risk and what will happen next.

Äripäev also reported Pipedrive is to make structural changes which will significantly reduce its size both in Estonia and in other countries it has a presence in.

Pipedrive marketing chief Mariliis Beger would not confirm to Äripäev whether the Tallinn and Tartu offices will remain open, stating: "We can't say at the moment, because different employment laws apply in different countries."

The group currently employs nearly 800 people, around half of them in Estonia.

In his letter, Cunha said the aim is to turn into a company which brings new solutions to market faster, understands its customers more deeply and succeeds through product strength. He said the goal is more time for work requiring depth and fewer obstacles to doing it — "in many ways a company that operates like the startup we started out as."

Pipedrive says it intends to remain product-focused and continue investing in its core CRM aspects, with a sharper focus on quality and reliability. Alongside that, it says it is building an AI-driven sales system for teams which records sales conversations, keeps data current, recommends next steps and handles routine tasks so salespeople can spend more time selling.

The company states it also wants to reduce its dependence on paid search advertising, cut management layers and meeting frequencies, and consolidate into fewer locations, so that most core teams are located in the same office.

"Small businesses' habits and expectations around buying software are evolving quickly," Cunha continued, adding that continuing to deliver value to customers requires changing how software is built and sold, and how the company operates.

He said more small businesses are asking artificial intelligence (AI) for software recommendations, that free web traffic driving the company's growth has fallen sharply, and that paid traffic to replace it costs more.

Cunha wrote that recent product updates had taught the company it needs to move faster: "We invested more in product and marketing, reorganized product development, changed our ways of working and significantly reduced operating costs." But he said those steps alone were not enough: "To build a company that matches our vision, we need a smaller and simpler organisation, focused on fewer priorities and more strongly product-centered."

He added that the layoffs do not mean AI is being used to cut costs or to replace people — AI has simply changed what customers want and how they find the product.

According to Äripäev, Pipedrive is closing its Portuguese office. It still operates in Tallinn, Tartu, New York, Prague, Florida, London, Berlin and Dublin.

Founded in 2010 by Ragnar Sass, Timo Rein, Martin Henk, Urmas Purde and Martin Tajur, Pipedrive became one of Estonia's 10 unicorn firms (a privately held startup valued at US$1 billion or more) around a decade later.

World.title: Iraq’s Development Road to provide million job opportunities
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The designs for the Development Road project have reached their final stages and will be fully completed before the end of 2026, according to the Iraqi Ministry of Transport.

The spokesperson for the Ministry of Transport, Ali al-Khalidi, said that the Development Road project is expected to generate approximately 100,000 job opportunities during its first phase.

Plans include the construction of modern stations, industrial zones, and residential areas along the route, developments that could potentially create over a million jobs as the project and its associated facilities expand, according to al-Khalidi.

The Iraqi official explained that 95 percent of the project’s railway designs have been completed, with 92 percent of the highway designs finished, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

Extending from the al-Faw Grand Port in the southern province of Basra to the Turkish border, with both the highway and railway being parallel lines, the first phase of the project is expected to be completed in 2033.

The Development Road’s primary objective is to transport goods from al-Faw Grans Port to Turkey—and onward to Europe—and vice versa.

Work is currently underway to finalize an agreement with Turkey to establish a fund that would finance the project’s implementation by Turkish companies through an oil-for-financing arrangement, according to INA.

The $17 billion project, which will connect the al-Faw Grand Port in southern Iraq to the Turkish border by constructing a railway and road network, is anticipated to transform Iraq into a transit center by cutting the time it takes to travel from Asia to Europe.

In addition to pipelines for energy transportation, the project’s railway will significantly assist in the transportation of commodities, with a first-phase capacity of 3.5 million tons and a second-phase capacity of 7.5 million tons.

By connecting the port city of Basra to Turkey via an overland route, the logistics project will compete with Egypt’s Suez Canal and establish Basra as a gateway to Europe.

World.title: Norway’s DNO considers exporting Iraqi Kurdistan oil via Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Norwegian oil producer DNO is actively exploring routes through Syria to export its Iraqi Kurdistan crude oil to the Mediterranean.

According to Reuters, the initiative aims to bypass local market constraints and fetch significantly higher international benchmark prices.

DNO has been selling oil from its Tawke and Peshkabir fields to the local market at low prices. Although its domestic sales price increased somewhat to $45 per barrel in October 2026 compared to an average of $38.50 in the third quarter, it is still significantly below global benchmarks.

Due to the Syrian civil war, transport to the Mediterranean through Syria was previously impossible. However, regional logistics are shifting. Significant volumes of southern Iraqi fuel oil and crude are already being transported by tanker trucks directly through Syria for export.

Reflecting past delays in payments from the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG), DNO requires international buyers to deposit US dollars into its offshore accounts before any oil is collected.

While trucks would be necessary for short-term movements, long-term solutions would encounter infrastructural obstacles.

Despite prior political support from the United States to study the route, rebuilding a key Iraq-Syria oil pipeline may cost around $15 billion and take years to become fully operational.

DNO is stepping up its drilling operations to increase the gross output from its important Kurdish licenses, which averaged 77,621 barrels of oil per day in the third quarter of 2026.

World.title: Iraq, Syria discuss exporting two million bpd of oil via Baniyas
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa discussed on Wednesday the development of economic and security cooperation, particularly the export of Iraqi oil through Baniyas with a capacity up to two million barrels per day.

The discussions took place during the first visit by an Iraqi prime minister to Syria since the fall of Bashar al-Assad’s regime in late 2024. The visit marks a step toward strengthening relations between the two countries, which share a border stretching over 600 kilometers.

The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said in a statement that the meeting addressed increasing trade exchange and developing the agricultural sector to achieve food and economic integration, in addition to discussing oil exports via Syria’s Baniyas port.

However, the statement did not mention when the route will start operating at the specified capacity.

Al-Zaidi highlighted initiatives to develop partnerships in the social and economic domains, boost security cooperation, and coordinate stances on regional and global concerns.

The Syrian Presidency said that the extended discussions in Damascus covered approaches to promote security, economic, and commercial cooperation, as well as regional and international developments.

Iraq started earlier exporting limited quantities of oil through the Syrian port of Baniyas—a move prompted by disruptions of maritime shipping in the Strait of Hormuz amid the conflict in the Middle East.

In July, the two countries signed a memorandum of understanding to revive the Haditha–Baniyas pipeline. A deal was signed with a consortium of three companies, including US-based Chevron, to carry out the project.

The pipeline was built in 1952, but it was abandoned in 2003 due to damage sustained during the invasion of Iraq by the United States. Its reactivation would provide an outlet for Iraqi oil exports via the Mediterranean Sea.

World.title: Christine Lagarde: unifying ECB chief in turbulent times
World.content:
Frankfurt – Christine Lagarde, who will step down in February 2027 as president of the European Central Bank, has been seen as a unifying leader who headed the institution in turbulent geopolitical times and sought to strengthen it for a more uncertain world.

The veteran French politician’s tenure was also rocky at times; she was criticised for policy missteps, notably failing to lift interest rates fast enough during the post-pandemic inflation surge.

Lagarde, 70, was the first woman to head the ECB when she was nominated in 2019, having previously been the first woman to head the International Monetary Fund.

She had a hard act to follow after Mario Draghi, the Italian economist credited with steering the eurozone through the sovereign debt crisis that began in 2009 with his vow to do “whatever it takes” to preserve the single currency.

Nevertheless, most observers agree that Lagarde’s consensual leadership style unified the central bank’s governing council, which sets interest rates for the 21-nation euro area, and that it has been less riven by disputes than during the Draghi era.

Lagarde “made everyone feel they were part of the same team”, a council member told AFP, speaking on condition of anonymity. “Seven years later, that spirit is still there.”

Highlighting her desire to find a middle ground between the ECB’s “hawks” — who favour rate increases — and “doves” who prefer looser policy, she described herself as an “owl”.

“My ambition is to be this owl that’s often associated with a little bit of wisdom,” she said in 2019. Afterwards she was often seen wearing an owl brooch.

Lagarde did not have an easy start, however.

Just months into her tenure, she faced criticism after saying the ECB was “not here to close spreads” between member states’ borrowing costs, as Italy’s government bond yields surged as the economy was battered by the coronavirus lockdowns.

Following fury in Italy and further sharp rises in borrowing costs, the ECB quickly changed course, announcing a massive pandemic emergency bond-buying programme.

– ‘Madam Inflation’ –

But the central bank’s biggest misstep during her tenure was perhaps its flat-footed response to the inflation surge triggered by the easing of Covid lockdowns and the Ukraine war energy shock, which pushed prices to a record above 10 percent in 2022.

“The ECB was slow to raise rates — probably six months slow,” Andrew Kenningham of Capital Economics told AFP, while acknowledging that other central banks had also not acted quickly enough.

The failure to get to grips with surging prices earned Lagarde the unflattering moniker “Madam Inflation” from Germany’s top-selling tabloid Bild, which also criticised her taste in luxury fashion.

When the ECB did decide to move, however, it moved rapidly.

Policymakers began a historic tightening campaign, lifting its benchmark rate from negative territory in mid-2022 to a record four percent in late 2023.

On the positive side of the ledger, analysts say the central bank has introduced a raft of innovations under Lagarde’s leadership that could help it cope with a more uncertain world.

She has warned that upheavals — like Covid, US tariffs and energy shocks — may be the new normal, and that policymakers must be prepared.

In 2021 she led the ECB’s first strategy review for two decades, which aimed to make policymaking clearer by setting out how it would respond to changes in inflation and the broader economy.

And in 2022 the bank created a crisis-fighting tool, the Transmission Protection Instrument (TPI), that allows the ECB to buy bonds of a eurozone member if yields rise uncontrollably and there is a risk of financial stress spreading.

The tool has never been used, though recently there has been speculation the ECB could step in to help France as its borrowing costs soar amid debt worries.

“The ECB has equipped itself with increasingly flexible tools,” Frederik Ducrozet, head of strategy and macroeconomic research at Pictet Wealth Management, told AFP.

– ‘Rebellious little girl’ –

Away from policy, Lagarde’s time heading the ECB was marked by simmering discontent among some of the central bank’s roughly 5,000 employees in Frankfurt.

A study commissioned by staff representatives in 2024 found that cases of burnout were on the rise, with unions pointing to concerns about favouritism. The ECB responded by saying it took the health and well-being of staff seriously.

Lagarde, a lawyer by training and the daughter of teachers, had a modest upbringing spent mostly in the French port city of Le Havre.

In her autobiography, to be published in early 2027, she says she was a “rebellious little girl”, determined to show that people did not need “the right name” to succeed.

“I have broken a few glass ceilings along the way,” she told Elle magazine this year. “I hope that, thanks to that, other women understand they can too.”

World.title: Iraqi court sentences Azm Alliance leader to 6 years in prison
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Central Anti-Corruption Criminal Court sentenced on Thursday Azm Alliance leader Muthanna al-Samarrai to six years in prison over corruption.

The verdict is part of a sweeping, high-profile anti-corruption campaign known as the “Operation Dawn,” which was initiated by Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi.

Al-Samarrai was found guilty of profiting from contracts and public works projects, particularly by using his power to mediate illegal deals with significant state-owned refining companies under Iraq’s Ministry of Oil.

Al-Samarrai was sentenced by the court to refund 30 billion Iraqi dinars, or around $20 million, that he had obtained from his dishonest activities.

In late June, Al-Samarrai, a well-known politician and businessman whose Azm Alliance has 15 seats in the Iraqi parliament, was arrested. Additionally, several politicians, oil ministry officials, and political elites were arrested in a police raid on Baghdad’s strongly protected Green Zone.

After former deputy oil minister Adnan al-Jumaili made comprehensive confessions that revealed a widespread network of illicit refinery contracts, the investigations gained momentum.

The case carries considerable political implications, as al-Samarrai leads the second-largest Sunni faction in parliament and is a candidate for the upcoming parliamentary elections.

According to the Iraqi law, al-Samarrai now has 30 days to appeal his verdict before the Court of Cassation.

World.title: Israel piles pressure on Arab parties as Netanyahu seeks government
World.content:
Jerusalem – Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc on Thursday piled pressure on Israeli Arab leaders over unproven accusations of foreign funding, in a push to neuter parties that made strong gains after an otherwise indecisive election.

National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir, a far-right firebrand with a history of attacks on Palestinians, went so far as to encourage Israel “immediately” to order the arrests of Arab party leaders.

Israel was nearing the completion of ballot-counting from Tuesday’s election in which neither Netanyahu nor the opposition bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot looked able to secure a majority in the parliament known as the Knesset.

A looming threat on the horizon, meanwhile, was the prospect of a return to war with Iran, alongside Israel’s ally the United States, which is holding its own crucial midterms next week.

Israel’s election saw a soaring performance by Israeli Arabs, descendants of Palestinians who stayed after the country’s creation in 1948, as outrage boiled at calls by ministers such as Ben Gvir to treat the Israeli minority group much as Israel has dealt with Palestinians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank.

The Arab parties together have enough votes to take the opposition bloc over the finish line, but Eisenkot has baulked, after relentless attacks by Netanyahu who warned his right-wing Jewish base that voting for the opposition would put Arabs in power.

Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, a conservative who heads the Central Election Commission, requested an investigation by the Shin Bet security service into allegations that key Arab party Raam received money from Qatar, the energy-rich Gulf powerbroker that has channels for Hamas.

“The Raamgate scandal is a political earthquake. Israel’s elections have been stolen!” Netanyahu’s Likud party said.

Government officials did not offer evidence to back the allegations.

Netanyahu himself has long been under the cloud of allegations related to Qatar after the arrests last year of two of his aides for allegedly receiving payments from the Gulf power.

Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, for years tacitly supported Qatar funding to Hamas-ruled Gaza, hoping to preserve stability.

That paradigm collapsed on October 7, 2023 when Hamas carried out the deadliest single attack ever on Israel, under Netanyahu’s watch.

– Kingmakers under pressure –

With nearly 93 percent of the vote counted, Netanyahu’s bloc was at 53 seats and the opposition forces led by Eisenkot had 48 — both well under the 61 needed to form a government.

The two main Arab formations were on track for an unprecedented 19 seats.

Some observers quickly said that the allegations would help Netanyahu by making the Arab lawmakers even more toxic to Eisenkot.

Yousef Jabareen, the head of one of them, the leftist Arab-majority Joint List, told AFP on Wednesday that he was willing to cooperate with the opposition to bring down Netanyahu but without joining it in a government.

He said the priority was to end “Netanyahu’s blood-soaked government” but noted that the Arab lawmakers disagreed on plenty with Eisenkot, who has largely backed the destruction of Gaza ordered by Netanyahu after the October 7 attack.

In response to the new allegations, Eisenkot said he was receiving updates and promised “utmost vigilance” against election interference.

“On the other hand, we cannot allow political actors to exploit the situation and influence the timing of the inauguration of the 26th Knesset,” he said.

One of Eisenkot’s right-leaning allies, Avigdor Lieberman, called the allegations “dramatic and unprecedented” and urged a swift investigation.

An Israeli police statement said that they would investigate every complaint about election integrity.

– The great survivor –

Netanyahu, who has led Israel on and off for more than 19 years, is known as a wily political operator.

He also tried on Tuesday to raise allegations of fraud, saying that Arab parties were caught with envelopes of cash and encouraging his base to come out in response.

Police said they arrested three suspects but the election commission called it an isolated local case.

Another factor that could play into the formation is an attack on Iran.

Netanyahu has repeatedly threatened to strike Iran, with his ally, US President Donald Trump, signalling he is ready to attack after next Tuesday’s US midterm elections, in which his Republican Party is forecast to lose ground.

Eisenkot has warned the military that Netanyahu has no mandate and that officers must not respond to his “political needs”.

But an attack could raise pressure on Eisenkot to join an emergency unity government, an option he has publicly ruled out, or keep the clock running until Israel can call new elections.

President Isaac Herzog will decide after the publication of the official results which person to task with a first chance of forming a government.

World.title: US dollar rates hold steady near 168,000 across major Iraqi exchanges
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar maintained relative stability across parallel markets in major commercial hubs on Thursday morning, October 29, 2026, with purchase rates hovering near the 168,000 dinar threshold per $100.

According to morning trading data, Baghdad exchange bureaus posted retail selling rates at 168,500 dinars against purchase bids of 168,000 dinars per $100.

In Erbil, trading counters quoted selling prices at 168,000 dinars and buying bids at 167,500 dinars. Across the southern port city of Basra, foreign currency desks registered selling prices at 168,000 dinars alongside purchase offers of 167,500 dinars per $100.

The parallel market spreads remain firmly elevated above the Central Bank of Iraq’s statutory official peg, which remains set at 152,000 dinars per $100 (1,520 dinars per dollar), as traders monitor ongoing cash liquidity consignments and executive measures aimed at curbing currency premiums.

World.title: TotalEnergies profit hits record on high oil prices
World.content:
Paris – French oil and gas giant TotalEnergies said Thursday that its net profit hit a new record in the third quarter as the war in the Middle East pushed up hydrocarbon prices.

Net profit reached $8.3 billion in the period from July to September, up from $5.4 billion in the preceding three months.

“In a high-price environment characterised by historic refining margin levels and a bull gas market, TotalEnergies is once again fully leveraging its integrated business model and its geographic diversification,” chief executive Patrick Pouyanne said in a statement.

The company had already reported a strong rise in its bottom line in the preceding two quarters, similarly driven by soaring oil and gas prices as well as its trading activities.

TotalEnergies said the surge in profits would be reflected in a higher dividend for shareholders.

“The board of directors commended the very good operational performance of all business segments which enabled the company to capture higher market prices,” the company said in its earnings statement.

The group will undertake a new capital increase reserved for employees, “who will benefit from a 20 percent discount on the share price”.

The board confirmed a third interim dividend of 0.90 euros per share for 2026, up 5.9 percent compared to 2025.

TotalEnergies will also proceed with share buybacks for cancellation of $2.5 billion “for the fourth quarter as well as for the first quarter 2027”.

World.title: 'Keeping a list of names': Abhishek Banerjee warns cops trying to 'please' Suvendu
World.content:
NEW DELHi: Trinamool Congress (TMC) national general secretary

on Thursday warned police officers allegedly targeting party workers to please West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari.

He added that those responsible would face consequences when his party returned to power.

âI am keeping a list of names. None will be spared once the government changes,â Banerjee said, accusing police officers of implicating thousands of TMC workers in false cases at the behest of the chief minister.

âI will identify the names of the police officers who are acting at his (Adhikari's) behest. I will record their names.

Those who are trying to please the chief minister and secure good postings will see the consequences in two years,â he said.

Banerjee alleged that several police officers had been targeting TMC workers to secure favourable postings and warned that their actions would be scrutinised if the party returned to power. He also accused an IPS officer in Paschim Medinipur of targeting TMC workers despite having earlier congratulated him on the party's expected electoral victory.





The remarks come amid a political confrontation between the ruling BJP and the TMC following the arrest of former West Bengal minister Indranil Sen over alleged financial irregularities linked to Durga Puja preview shows and the sale of passes.

World.title: 'Don't push us': SC warns of harsh stand on firecrackers if orders go unenforced
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday said it was not inclined to impose a complete ban on firecrackers in Delhi-NCR, but warned authorities against pushing it to take a "very harsh stand" by failing to enforce its orders on the ground.

A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale said repeated judicial directions would serve little purpose unless authorities ensured compliance, stressing that air pollution affected "every living being".

"We are not inclined to completely ban but donât push us to take a very harsh stand," the bench said as reported by news agency PTI. The Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati outlined measures taken by the Delhi government and the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) to tackle pollution.

âThere is no point in passing orders and directions unless you give effect to them on the ground, otherwise, it becomes a mockery,â the bench observed.

The court said the matter was not adversarial and called for serious action and cooperation from all stakeholders to regulate the use of firecrackers.

âEvery year we are trying to balance it out but unless there is cooperation from everyone, it canât be done,â the bench said, adding that the concerned officers must be present on the ground to monitor implementation.





The bench also suggested roping in prominent personalities, including sportspersons, to spread public awareness about the harmful effects of firecrackers.

Bhati told the court that the Delhi government had drawn up an extensive plan to tackle the pollution season. Measures scheduled to come into effect from November include curbs on older vehicles and construction and demolition activities, along with staggered office timings.

The Centre informed the court that internal consultations on the use of barium in firecrackers were still under way. Bhati sought three weeks to complete the process, and the bench said it would consider the issue after that period.

World.title: India-EU landmark FTA likely rollout in mid-2027, says top EU lawmaker
World.content:
The European Parliamentâs Foreign Affairs Committee Chair, David McAllister, has said that the India-EU Free Trade Agreement (FTA) is expected to be signed by mid-December 2026, with PM Narendra Modi anticipated to travel to Brussels for the official signing ceremony.

The "mother of all deals" will still undergo rigorous scrutiny by the European Parliament, but McAllister told TOI in an interview he's confident about smooth ratification, given the benefits it will bring to both sides. The EU lawmaker said that a consent vote is expected by spring next year, paving the way for the trade agreement to officially enter into force mid-2027.

"We expect the FTA to be signed by mid-December. Hopefully, PM Modi will manage to visit Brussels and attend the official signing ceremony," said McAllister, who led an EU Parliamentary delegation to India this week.

"Though Parliament cannot amend the text of the agreement, our consent is required before it enters into force. I followed the debate in the European Parliament over the past months, and I can say there seems to be a broad majority support for this landmark FTA. The benefits for both sides are so huge that I'm sure the European Parliament will give its support in the consent vote," added McAllister, who heads the Parliamentary committee that shapes and monitors the EU's common foreign and security policy.





McAllister also said the EU would particularly welcome progress on the investment protection agreement as it would strengthen the confidence of European investors in the Indian market, encouraging greater European investments and contributing to job creation in India. He said the FTA would allow India and the EU to work more closely on de-risking supply chains and reducing dependencies.

If the FTA indeed is ready for signing by mid-December, Modi is likely to stop over in Brussels to ink the deal on his way back to India from the US G20 summit.

The PM will also travel to Canada and possibly to Germany during that trip.

Asked about the prospects of defence-industrial collaboration and technology sharing under the new India-EU defence and security partnership, McAllister backed closer cooperation between India and the European defence industry, saying it is in the interest of both sides. He also spoke about the convergence of interest in keeping the Indo-Pacific free and open and the need to reduce reliance on any one country

"There are many fields of cooperation in this matter. I would definitely mention information sharing, research cooperation and cybersecurity.

One element would be that we also invite India to participate in a closer cooperation with our European defense industry, because here we also have a joint interest," said the lawmaker.

"We in Europe, as part of our strategic sovereignty, want to reduce the dependence on one particular country, and I understand that the debate in India is very similar. You also want to step-by-step reduce your dependence, and I think this is a very good win-win situation for both sides," said McAllister.
