"Any peace agreement must be just, sustainable and acceptable to both sides. It must also include absolute, concrete security guarantees for Ukraine that Putin (Russian president) is not able to repeat this unbelievable act of aggression and violation of international law. So, if India with its special relationship with Russia - and also India with its constructive relationship with Ukraine - can play any kind of role constructively, it would be welcome," he said, while praising Jaishankar's "constructive" role for peace.

World.title: It only takes one rumour: How a small trigger can lead to a deadly stampede
World.content:
Stampede at Kolkata pandal during Durga Puja claimed 19 lives.

The anatomy of a stampede

Psychology of the crowd

How should police act and react?

Preparing for the unexpected

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: It begins with a rumour, feeds on panic and ends in tragedy. A stampede can turn a celebration into chaos within minutes, leaving thousands gathered in joy struggling to find a way out. In a tightly packed crowd, even a small disturbance can have deadly consequences.A similar script played out in Kolkata on October 17. On the night of Maha Saptami during Durga Puja, pandal-hoppers gathered in large numbers at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin pandal. The crowd swelled further after a sudden spell of rain prompted people waiting outside to seek shelter, while visitors near the exit stopped moving.An announcement over the public address system warning that the pandal was about to collapse added to the panic. Investigators believe several factors contributed to the stampede, including overcrowding, narrow entry and exit points, inadequate crowd management and the misleading announcement.The crowd crush, which police said lasted around three minutes, claimed 19 lives and left at least 25 people injured.India is a country of festivals, and its massive religious gatherings also make it prone to stampedes. This year, it was Kolkata.Last year, it was Karur in Tamil Nadu and the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj. The locations change, the crowds differ, but the tragedy keeps repeating itself.This raises an important question: despite elaborate planning and dedicated crowd management teams, why do stampedes keep happening? And what can authorities do to prevent a small disturbance from turning into a disaster?Public excitement soars during religious gatherings. Actual turnout often exceeds what authorities anticipate, resulting in more people entering an area than it can safely accommodate.As the crowd swells, even a small disturbance, a rumour, someone tripping and falling, a sudden power outage or even a broken barricade can lead to a situation in which people lose control of their movement.According to a 2014 report by the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), titled Managing Crowd at Events and Venues of Mass Gathering: A Guide for State Government, Local Authorities, Administrators and Organizers, crowd disasters can be triggered by several factors.Structural problems such as weak temporary structures, collapsed barricades, poorly lit stairways, slippery roads and narrow entrances and exits can lead to a crowd crush.Fires, electrical failures and security scares can also turn an otherwise manageable gathering into a dangerous crush.The report explains the causes of stampedes through the "FIST" model which is an acronym for Force, Information, Space and Time. According to the model, the four factors that can contribute to a crowd disaster are the force exerted by the crowd, the information that triggers its reaction, the physical space available and the duration of the incident."The FIST circumstances namely crowd force, the information upon which the crowd acts, the physical space involved, and the time duration of the incident play a very important role resulting in either overcrowding or high desired velocity," the report says.In simple terms, when too many people are packed into a limited space, pressure builds as those behind continue moving forward while those in front are unable to move. At extreme crowd densities, people can be pushed against one another with such force that they lose control of their movements. Even those who remain standing can struggle to breathe.Deaths in such situations do not necessarily occur because someone has literally been "trampled" under the feet of others. The NDMA says compressive asphyxia, which occurs when pressure on the chest prevents a person from breathing, has historically been the most common cause of death in crowd disasters."On occasions, this has led to deaths because of crushing, suffocation, and trampling. Historically, compressive asphyxia has been the most common reason for deaths in crowd disasters," the report says.Crowd psychology is also a factor that can contribute to a stampede-like situation. According to the NDMA report, individuals often conform their thoughts and behaviour to those of a larger group rather than acting independently."Individual behaviour in a crowd is sometimes influenced by the behaviour of others. The individuals within a crowd may act differently than if they were on their own," it says."The unlawful actions of a few people can result in larger numbers following them. Research has shown that understanding of crowd behaviour has led to community based approach to crowd control instead of force based control," the report adds.For instance, long queues at places of worship may lead some devotees to climb over fences, prompting others to follow and causing overcrowding in another area.However, crowd behaviour is not always irrational. People react to incomplete information, the movement of others and the fear of danger. In dense crowds, they may also lose the ability to control their own movement.This is why rumours and misleading announcements can be particularly dangerous. People may begin moving towards an exit without knowing what is happening elsewhere in the venue. If the exit is already congested, the sudden movement can increase pressure on those trapped in the crowd.Talking to The Times of India, former Bihar director general of police Abhayanand, who handled several such gatherings during his long service, said police should refrain from using force when a crowd is already panicked during a stampede-like situation."There is always a trigger, however small. It is followed immediately thereafter by a rumour which spreads like wildfire," Abhayanand said."I haven't followed any SOP in my days. I followed two basics: The crowd has panicked. Don't increase the panic by lathi charge. If there is an individual in whom the crowd has trust and if he can be made to communicate with the crowd, its effect is magical," he added."Crowds where there is some common binding force experience stampede. Such stampedes are easier to manage," he further said.Abhayanand also recalled handling a similar situation during the funeral procession of Ranvir Sena chief Brahmeshwar Mukhiya in Patna in 2012. He said police refrained from using force against a particularly unruly gathering of supporters."The crowd was itching for a trigger, and a police lathi charge could have set things off. We restrained ourselves because the repercussions would not have been limited to the capital but could have spread across the entire state," he told TOI."Those indulging in arson wanted the police to react and resort to a lathi charge. That was precisely what they were trying to provoke, but we did not allow that trigger to be pulled," he added.His account points to the importance of police response when a crowd is already on edge. An attempt to disperse people by force can worsen the situation if it causes them to rush towards a narrow exit or move against an incoming crowd.The NDMA has also laid down guidelines on how authorities should manage crowds and respond when a stampede-like situation develops.According to the agency, the guiding principle should be to bridge the gap between demand and supply. This requires controlling the number of people entering a venue, regulating the crowd within it and managing the outflow when necessary.The NDMA recommends designated staging points through which visitors should pass, along with effective systems to count and monitor people moving through them. Multiple routes should be encouraged to prevent bottlenecks and facilitate the movement of vulnerable groups.Crowd management also requires authorities to anticipate disturbances without allowing their response to trigger a larger crisis."Such miscreants should be immediately quarantined and removed. Action should be taken immediately with tact and firmness, without inviting undue attention from the general public, which may be there if force is used," it says."Inappropriate or poorly managed control procedures may precipitate crowd incidents rather than preventing them. For example, police reacting to a group of unruly people may chase them in a direction opposite to the incoming crowd, which may create a collision, and hence a disaster. Special attention should also be given to the border of the venue and the floating crowd moving there because the mischief is usually caused at such places," it adds.The agency also recommends "input control" by restricting or staggering entry to prevent overcrowding. Authorities must be able to regulate, slow or temporarily stop the inflow when a venue reaches its safe capacity.This also means keeping entry and exit routes clear, ensuring that people leaving a venue do not collide with those entering, and monitoring areas where crowds tend to gather or stop moving.Communication is another important part of crowd management. The NDMA says a lack of reliable information can cause people to panic or change direction, leading to dangerous crowd movements."Communicating with visitors and providing them with the correct information is a very critical factor in all situations," the report says, stressing that communication is essential during normal operations, emergencies and recovery.The Kolkata tragedy showed how quickly things can go wrong when these safeguards fail. Police said the crowd had become congested near the exit during the rain, even as the entry point remained open. The misleading announcement about the pandal collapsing is believed to have added to the pressure, although investigators are still examining the exact sequence of events.Ultimately, effective crowd management lies in anticipating pressure, regulating movement and ensuring that a small trigger does not turn into an uncontrollable chain of events. The challenge is not just to prepare for the thousands expected to attend an event, but also to recognise when a gathering is becoming unsafe and act before it is too late.

World.title: 'What is wrong with victims': CJI on digital arrest cases; calls for compensation from banks
World.content:
SC questioned the Centre over pharma companies pricing medicines at over 1,000% of cost, saying the industry can't "run amok" in the name of free market.

'Banks must act as a protective umbrella'

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday fumed over rising digital arrest cases and expressed shock over how educated people were getting "arrested on mobile phones" despite public awareness campaigns, news reports and court orders.While hearing a suo motu case on digital arrests, CJI Surya Kant reportedly made an oral observation: "What is wrong with these victims? How are these victims being trapped like this? They can't understand this basic thing? What's the fear of arrest on mobile?""Hit the mobile on the wall and arrest goes. Something is wrong with people. God knows what is there. What kind of person are you in a democratic country if you think you are getting arrested on mobile?" a PTI report quoted the CJI.This comes after the amicus curiae in the case, NS Nappinai, said that she keeps receiving repeated inputs that while much was being done to stop digital arrests, the problem continues unabated.She told the court that a woman lost Rs 2.5 crore last week in such an incident."Something is wrong with people. God knows what is there. You are victimising yourself," the CJI retorted."We feel frustrated that all educated people are getting duped.What will you pass on to the next generation if you get digitally arrested at this age? People can go to the court's website to find if there's an order," the CJI added.During the hearing, the apex court also said that banks must be held accountable for compensating victims of digital arrest scams, stressing that they should act as a âprotective umbrellaâ for customers vulnerable to such fraud.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana questioned why unusually large withdrawals from a retired person's bank account could not trigger timely intervention to prevent the loss.The top court said it was considering directions requiring banks to compensate victims and face prosecution where digital arrest fraud occurred due to their failure to exercise due diligence."We are proposing to direct that wherever such fraud takes place, the bank will compensate the victim and suffer prosecution. It has to be done," the CJI said.Observing that banks must be made accountable to indemnify losses of victims of digital fraud, the bench said that victims of offences like digital arrests should receive compensation of at least the amount lost if the fraud is found to have resulted from a failure of due diligence by the financial institution.

World.title: Overwhelming response for Philately Passports in Madurai
World.content:
Philately Passports launched by the Tamil Nadu Postal Circle on October 28 received an overwhelming response in Madurai. All the 180 Philately Passports for Madurai Philatelic Bureau at the Head Post Office were sold out.

Philatelists and travel enthusiasts made a beeline for the Philatelic Bureau. People were on the office doorsteps as early as 9 a.m. to purchase the Philately Passport which was priced at ₹650 per copy. It features information about 58 permanent pictorial cancellations (PPCs) highlighting heritage sites and landmarks across Tamil Nadu.

Many people who had turned up at the Madurai Philatelic Bureau on Thursday were disappointed to learn that the Philately Passports had been sold out. However, taking into account the overwhelming response from the public, the officials asked them to leave their contact number on a register so that they could be alerted when the next batch was out.

Senior Post Master S. Mariappan said taking note of the overwhelming response they will be requesting more Philately Passports for Madurai.

Those interested can contact Madurai Philatelic Bureau contact number: 6380750541.

World.content:
The results of the Uttar Pradesh MLC (Members of Legislative Council) election for 11 seats, including both the Graduates’ and Teachers’ constituencies, has left much food for thought for the State BJP going into an Assembly election early next year, not least because the party may have to jettison more than half of its sitting MLAs going ahead.

World.title: Delhi government to strengthen food safety inspections, increase staff to curb adulteration
World.content:
Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Thursday (October 29) said the Delhi government plans to equip the Food Safety Department with modern equipment and additional staff to strengthen checks against food adulteration.

The announcement follows inspections across the city that detected adulterated and substandard food items.

The department seized 948.9 litres of ghee during inspections at Bhogal Market in south-east Delhi, Najafgarh Market in south-west Delhi and Shiv Vihar in north-east Delhi on Wednesday (October 28), the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) stated. It also collected 15 samples from two of the markets.

Of the seized stock, 389.9 litres came from Bhogal Market and 338 litres from Najafgarh Market. Another 221 litres of suspected adulterated ghee was seized during a joint operation with the Delhi Police in Shiv Vihar, officials said.

The samples have been sent to a laboratory for testing, and further action will be taken based on the results, the CMO stated.

In a post on X, Ms. Gupta stated, “Team Delhi is going all out against adulterated and unsafe food products, not just during the festive season, but throughout the year”.

The Chief Minister said she had issued instructions to blacklist offending brands, impose heavy fines, cancel licences, register FIRs and publicly disclose violators’ names through s. She also directed officials to make consumer helpline numbers available. “Delhiites’ health is non-negotiable,” she wrote.

Ms. Gupta urged people to report cases of adulteration, substandard food and the sale of expired products to the department’s helpline, 1800113921, during office hours.

Ms. Gupta said food safety is directly linked to public health and consumer confidence.

“The government’s responsibility is to ensure that people can purchase food products with confidence that their quality and safety have not been compromised,” she said.

World.title: Tail-end farmers of PAP Main Canal begin relay hunger fast at Bhagavathipalayam demanding equitable water distribution
World.content:
Tail-end farmers of PAP Main Canal began their relay hunger fast at Bhagavathipalayam Pirivu in Veeanampalayam village on Thursday (October 29), demanding equitable water distribution by the Water Resources Department.

Over 30 farmers sat on hunger fast on the first day, calling upon the authorities to act firmly against water theft incidences in the upstream of the Main Canal, and to increase the flow by 10 additional cusecs from the existing 131, and increasing water level to 4.8 feet from the existing 4.5 feet at the zero point.

Though the Police Department had denied permission, the farmers went ahead with the protest plan.

An official analysis had affirmed that the existing force is not enough to reach the tail-end of the Vellakoil Branch Canal that flows to a length of 39.65 km. The force of water flow, the study states, is obstructed by dilapidated concrete in the distributory canals.

Officials of Water Resource Department (WRD) held talks with the protesting farmers and gave an assurance for increasing the flow force by 10 cusecs. The farmers, however, sought the assurance in writing from the officials.

President of PAP Vellakovil Branch Canal (Kangayam-Vellakovil) Water Conservation Association P. Velusamy said that the protest would continue till the intended outcome is reached.

During late night hours, the WRD prevailed upon the farmers to withdraw their protest with an assurance in writing that the force of waterflow will be increased by 10 cusecs at the zero point, and that equitable distribution would be ensured in the future.

World.title: TDP leader promotes green campaigning in Tirupati by gifting saplings to voters
World.content:
While several novel methods are adopted to encourage voters to cast their vote and nudge them to support a candidate, here is a greener alternative chosen by a senior leader, who, actually, is not in the fray.

As part of his campaign for the party Mayor nominee J.B. Srinivas and other corporator candidates, senior TDP leader Ajay Pratap is presenting saplings to the public, with the twin requests to cast their vote in favour of his party candidate and to plant the sapling at their residential premises.

Mr. Pratap says presenting saplings is a moral responsibility of every individual, as planting a tree can never be treated as a ‘personal favour’ to the voter. According to him, exercising one’s right to vote is as important as planting a sapling, as ‘both makes our lives better’.

World.title: U.P. MLC poll results mark a defeat of BJP’s anti-education policies: Opposition leaders
World.content:
With the Samajwadi party winning five of the 11 Legislative Council seats that went to the polls in Uttar Pradesh, the Opposition INDIA bloc said on Thursday that the outcome was a defeat of the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party’s anti-teacher and anti-education policies. Despite massive administrative support for the BJP candidates, the results signify growing public discontent with the BJP government, Opposition leaders said.

“This is a double defeat of the double engine. The BJP’s defeat in the Legislative Council elections has set the stage for the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections to be held in 2027,” said SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, in a post on X. “On the one hand, this represents a defeat for the BJP’s anti-teacher, anti-learner, and anti-education policies, while on the other, educated unemployed graduates have also declared their verdict. The way the BJP has victimised and humiliated every community has brought all the oppressed together. The PDA’s support base has now grown to 95 percent, because those who suffer are the PDA,” he said.

‘BJP faces existential crisis’

The SP president claimed that the six seats won by the BJP in the Legislative Council polls came through fraud and manipulation. “The BJP has become a flop show. In Varanasi, the BJP lost first in the counting and then again in the re-counting, meaning the counting took place twice and both times the BJP and its allies lost. This has triggered an existential crisis within the BJP, as everyone within the party knows that even the seats it won were won through fraud,” he said.

“Internal divisions within the BJP have exacerbated the double-engine conflict. Consequently, BJP candidates have completely lost the courage to contest the Assembly elections. The BJP, which previously conducted candidate surveys, is now searching for candidates with binoculars, but no one is visible,” Mr. Yadav said, adding that the awareness and unity of voters will become the “decisive foundation” for forming an SP government in 2027.

The SP won five seats, through its candidates Kanti Singh (Lucknow Division Graduates’ seat), Lal Bihari Yadav (Varanasi division Teachers seat), Akash Agarwal (Agra Division Teachers’ seat), Asutosh Sinha (Varanasi Division Graduates’ seat) and Man Singh Yadav (Jhansi-Prayagraj Graduates’ seat). In the previous Council election held in 2020, the party had won only three seats.

‘Educated voters oppose BJP’

The Congress said the Opposition’s victory in five seats signals resentment against the BJP even among its core support base, despite the blatant misuse of State apparatus and officials.

“We saw how the administration delayed the counting on many seats including Varanasi and Gorakhpur. Since the start of the election campaign, the BJP was favoured by the administration. Despite this, the SP-Congress alliance won five seats. It signals how educated sections of society are fully opposed to the BJP and waiting for 2027 polls to defeat the BJP,” said Congress national secretary Shahnawaz Alam.

World.title: Sanitation workers toil without adequate restroom facilities at MGMGH
World.content:
Sanitation workers at the Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Government Hospital (MGMGH) in Tiruchi have urged the authorities to provide adequate toilets, changing and dining rooms for them on the premises.

Over 300 contractual sanitation workers are employed to clean wards, collect hospital waste and assist patients at the MGMGH. The absence of proper facilities for them to change their clothes at the start or end of their shift, use the restroom, or have their meal break, is a perennial problem, said activists.

“Since there is no designated place for us, we are often forced to change our clothes in the ramp areas between the wards, or in deserted corridors. Some mischievous members of the public have even secretly filmed sanitation workers while they are changing or re-adjusting their uniform. Ironically, we clean all the toilets in the GH, but we are not allowed to use them,” R. Rajendran, state organising secretary of the Tamil Nadu Government Hospital Auxiliary Workers Union, told The Hindu.

Mr. Rajendran said that the problem is prevalent throughout the public hospitals in Tamil Nadu. “We have been asking the authorities to provide separate facilities for sanitation workers for over a decade, but we still do not have a solution. This attitude hits our dignity of labour,” he said.

The workers earn between ₹14,000 and ₹20,000 per month and are employed on three-year contracts. “Most of the sanitation workers are women, and since there is no space in the hospital for us, we tend to wear our uniforms (a sari and jacket) from home. We handle bio-waste during our shift, but do not have adequate safety gear such as gloves provided. I usually have to re-drape my sari after a day’s work on the road before returning home. It is embarrassing and humiliating,” said a woman sanitation worker with over 10 years of service.

When contacted, a senior MGMGH official said that space would be allocated for the sanitation and other support staff after the new super-speciality block is inaugurated in the coming weeks. “This is a long-pending demand that we hope to fulfill soon,” the official said.

World.title: 'Not related to defence': Govt responds to Fazl's remarks about Makkah pact countries' meeting in Tehran
World.content:
Federal ministers on Thursday responded to Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s remarks regarding a recent huddle in Tehran comprising the Makkah defence pact countries and Iran.

Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the meeting was not related to defence. Hence, Asif said his presence was not required, while Naqvi explained the reasons for his participation.

The remarks came after the JUI-F chief questioned Asif’s absence and Naqvi’s presence at the meeting.

The meeting brought together top officials from Iran and member countries of the Makkah Defence Alliance — including Pakistan’s Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin.

On Iran’s side, President Masoud Pezeshkian, Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi were present. The huddle agreed to “continue their dialogue to bolster cooperation among the four regional nations, including in the areas of regional peace and security”.

On Wednesday, Fazl referred to the development during his address in the National Assembly (NA) and commented: “A defence pact is taking shape in Iran, a meeting is under way (there), and the defence minister is sitting here.”

Amid laughter and desk thumping in the Lower House, he referred to Naqvi’s presence at the Tehran huddle and questioned: “The interior minister is required there as well?”

Then, taking a jibe at Asif, he repeated the defence minister’s phrase that he had used against the PTI.

“There is your respect and stature — koi sharam hoti hai, koi haya hoti hai (have some shame, show some modesty),” he said, breaking into laughter.

Responding to him in the NA on Thursday, Asif said no defence pact was taking shape in Tehran, nor was the discussion focused on Pakistan’s defence or any related matter.

He said CDF Munir had “assumed a role for Pakistan” following last year’s military conflict with India. That role, he said, was of “peace and dialogue so that peace is established in our region”.

Since then, he noted, Pakistan has signed two defence pacts — the Makkah defence pact and the Badr Memorandum of Understanding.

“I was involved in those pacts as I am the defence minister,” he explained, adding that the meeting in Tehran was “not the defence ministry’s mandate”.

The CDF had gone there “as a messenger of peace and paved the ground” for the huddle, he said, ostensibly referring to Tehran last week.

During that visit, the CDF had proposed the Tehran meeting, according to Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei.

Asif said this was the situation and he was “not needed in Tehran”.

He added that the CDF had played a role in averting a confrontation. “The situation could have deteriorated as far as the Yemen issue is concerned […] There has been some talk and peace may emerge in the coming days or week as far as Saudi Arabia versus Yemen [sic] is concerned.”

Asif advised Fazl to be the bigger person and said his criticism was “misplaced”.

The defence minister further said Pakistan’s and the CDF’s role at the international level should be acknowledged, keeping political differences aside. He said one should at least show some dignity.

‘Not related to defence’

Meanwhile, in the Senate, Naqvi also responded to Fazl’s remarks on his participation in the Tehran meeting. The proceedings were marred by loud exchanges between the interior minister and JUI-F Senator Kamran Murtaza.

Naqvi clarified that he and CDF Munir undertook the visit to “handle the ongoing crisis in Iran”.

On Fazl’s query of why Asif had not gone there, he said, “He (Fazl) did not know that this [trip] was not related to defence.”

Defending his inclusion, the minister said: “I do not go out of my own volition. I have been especially tasked by the prime minister sahib; he has entrusted me with some matters regarding the current crisis of the [Iran] war, because of which I go.”

The independent senator noted that the JUI-F had been commenting on him for many days.

“I personally had heartfelt respect for Maulana Fazlur Rehman, but yesterday when he said I spit on the state, that respect ended,” Naqvi said.

Naqvi said he wanted to ask Fazl and his party’s senators present there just one question and then noted that JUI-F leaders had made very “disgusting statements about institutions” three to four months ago.

This prompted Senator Murtaza to object, saying he could not speak on a personal agenda in the House. Presiding Officer Shahadat Awan also immediately said he was expunging the word “disgusting” from Naqvi’s remarks.

As Murtaza continued shouting, Naqvi said, “You should listen here … You will have to listen.”

The presiding officer noted that Naqvi was a member of the Senate and urged the JUI-F leader to take his seat.

Resuming his remarks, Naqvi said, “Giving people the perception that this was a defence pact; this was not a defence agreement at all.

He added: “For them, the state is like a mother until the day they can squeeze it dry. The state is very good as long as they can extract wealth from the state, and when you do not get a share in the state and the government, then you spit on the state. This is not appropriate anywhere.”

Murtaza again interrupted, objecting to Naqvi’s language, at which the latter replied that the other side had also used similar language a day ago.

As the JUI-F senator continued speaking amid the presiding officer’s calls to halt cross-talk, Naqvi said, “If they criticise, they should garner and keep the courage to take the answer as well. This is no way [to behave] that you go and say whatever you want.”

The interior minister then went on to criticise the JUI-F, alleging that it “used Islam for business and for politics”.

Amid the ruckus, PML-N’s Abid Sher Ali also stood up and responded loudly, prompting State Minister of Interior Tallal Chaudhry and the presiding officer to urge him to take his seat.

Naqvi then addressed PTI’s Ali Zafar and said, “These very people (JUI-F) used to come to us before governor’s rule [was imposed] and say, ‘Impose governor’s rule, rid us of them!’ […] Those who come and sit with you and engage in opposition wanted governor’s rule imposed from their hearts. I will prove this to you.”

Addressing JUI-F, the interior minister said, “Now, you will not get jobs in the state. Now you will not get money from the state, nor will you get tickets from the state.”

He asserted that it was the JUI-F that was “continuously crossing the line” and that they would get a response if they kept doing so.

‘Full of contradictions’

In his remarks in the NA, Asif alleged that Fazl’s past “is full of contradictions”.

“You taunt me with ‘have some shame, show some modesty’, but you should also have some shame and show some modesty. How many perks have you enjoyed over the past 40 years? You have been violating the very principles that you have been highlighting,” the PML-N leader said.

He recalled that Fazl had also offered to mediate with Kabul. “Were you the foreign minister?” he questioned, alleging that the move was aimed at “value addition to his politics and leverage that to extract maximum advantage from the government”.

Asif said Fazl had been in the government with every political party, making an incomplete remark: “When you don’t get a share in the power —”

“When you delete the past from your memory and attack your rivals — at least I don’t have that courage. When I speak, my past is fresh in my mind; that if I say this, whether I would be taunted that we supported General Ziaul Haq’s government,” he went on to say.

The defence minister recalled that Fazl was part of the Musharraf government, had also been an opposition leader in the House and also served as the Kashmir Committee chairperson. He said a person serving as the head of such a committee that raises issues at an international forum should have “impeccable credentials”.

When some lawmakers opposed him in favour of Fazl, he remarked, “The Maulana now needs women’s support. He is unable to find a man.”

He also accused Fazl of “targeting our diplomatic efforts”, saying that the government’s achievement at the global stage had not received the commendation they deserved.

Asif said his advice to the JUI-F would be a line often seen on buses and trucks: “Mehnat kar, hasad na kar (work hard and don’t envy).”

He ended his address, alleging that had Fazl been given some share in the governance in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa following the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in the province, the JUI-F chief’s address the previous day would not have been delivered.

“This sideshow that they (JUI-F) are running, I feel that it is unfortunate that our sisters have been forced to defend the men [of JUI-F] while the men are nowhere to be seen,” Asif remarked.

Describing Fazl’s address as “blackmail”, Asif warned against coming into power based on “compromises”.

“Sitting in the opposition would be a more respectable approach, rather than sitting with people who will blackmail you,” he said.

“We as senior parliamentarians should convey to the nation that we will not do group-based politics but politics rooted in the constitution and [..] for the security of the country,” Asif urged, adding that lawmakers should chart a way forward together, rather than “grabbing each other by the collar”.

Electoral reforms committee

In his remarks, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas claimed KP had been “snatched from the people” and reiterated the opposition’s allegations of rigging in the 2024 general elections.

“If even one person’s vote is snatched, it is a crime. It is the responsibility of those conducting elections to protect the vote. Earlier also you laid a crooked brick, and Pakistan broke. On Feb 8, elections were stolen. While stealing elections, where have you reached — you have even stolen Khyber Pakhtunkhwa,” he claimed.

The opposition leader said no society could progress without law, or function if law existed but without its implementation.

The House also took up a motion moved by Minister of State for Law Barrister Aqeel Malik for the constitution of a parliamentary electoral reforms committee.

PTI’s Zafar said he could write down entire electoral reforms on paper in an hour. “The issue is implementation. Make such a committee and procedure that the electoral process is actually implemented. Whatever they want to do, only that is approved,” he said.

Barrister Aqeel said the issue could be resolved by sitting together and asked members to bring their proposals.

World.title: Rana Sanaullah says Imran's jailed sister Noreen 'fine' after being provided medical treatment
World.content:
Adviser to the prime minister on political affairs, Rana Sanaullah, on Thursday informed the Senate that Noreen Niazi, the sister of jailed PTI founder Imran Khan, was fine after being provided medical treatment in Lahore.

Imran’s three sisters — Noreen, Aleema Khan, and Uzma Khan — have been in detention since Sept 21 under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960 (MPO) on the Lahore deputy commissioner’s (DC) orders.

On Wednesday, Noreen’s lawyer said that she was moved from Lahore’s Kot Lakhpat jail to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology (PIC) due to high blood pressure. Her lawyer claimed that no family member had been informed about her deteriorating health condition.

Speaking on the floor of the Senate on Thursday, Sanaullah responded to the query by PTI parliamentary leader Barrister Ali Zafar, who sought information regarding Noreen’s health and her being taken to the hospital.

The PML-N senator said Noreen was “immediately provided with medical facilities”.

“As per the information available, she is fine and all her medical tests are normal,” he said.

On concerns about Noreen’s family allegedly not being allowed to meet her, the prime minister’s adviser said details would also be sought on the matter. He assured the PTI that if this was true, it would be addressed depending on the circumstances at the hospital.

During his address, PTI Senator Mashal Yousafzai continued to interrupt Sanaullah, questioning the need for Noreen’s detention.

The PML-N senator replied: “She is in jail because she wanted to spread turmoil in the country. She wanted to attack Islamabad by launching a long march and inciting the people.”

Addressing Zafar, Sanaullah said that as the PTI founder was in jail under judicial custody, any relief regarding his health and meeting should be sought from the courts.

Imran’s sisters are currently serving the second term of a 30-day detention under the MPO, which was extended on Oct 7. The detention came amid reports of a crackdown on the PTI ahead of its countrywide protest and march to Islamabad, which the party had called to demand Imran’s release from jail and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution.

‘Must never allow our humanity to fail’

In his remarks on the Senate floor, Zafar contended that Noreen had been detained despite not having committed any crime.

While Noreen’s lawyer had said she had faced high blood pressure, Zafar said she suffered a heart attack and claimed that her family was not being allowed to meet her.

Quoting Shakespeare’s phrase “milk of human kindness”, Senator Zafar said if even a little human kindness remained, the government must immediately stop grave human rights violations.

“If there is even a minimum of human kindness left in you, release her. At least allow her family to meet her and ensure proper medical care,” he said while speaking on a point of order.

He also condemned the detention of Imran’s nephews, asking why family members should suffer for their relationship with a political leader.

He alleged Imran had been kept in solitary confinement for a year and was being subjected to torture, claiming that the PTI founder’s wife Bushra Bibi was also facing inhumane treatment.

He demanded an immediate end to their mistreatment, which the government denies, saying both are being provided with the facilities they are entitled to.

Zafar claimed that the government believes the Constitution can be broken and suspended, as witnessed in the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which has rendered the elected provincial government non-functional.

“There is one thing that cannot be broken, suspended or compromised: the fundamental human rights of the people of Pakistan,” he asserted.

Senator Zafar stressed that even if governor’s rule was claimed to be justified, it could never be a licence to violate fundamental rights, detain the chief minister, speaker and elected representatives, or keep their whereabouts undisclosed.

He warned that violating the sanctity of home and family honour, which hold deepest importance in Pashtun society, would provoke strong resentment among people of KP.

He also referred to reports of attacks on homes of MNAs and alleged violence against their wives and sisters, calling for impartial investigation.

“These are not merely political issues. These are matters of human rights, human dignity, family honour and rule of law. Human rights stand above politics,” he said.

Concluding, he said: “The Constitution may be violated by those who wield power, democratic mandates may be undermined, and institutions may fail in their duty. But we must never allow our humanity to fail.”

PTI condemns Noreen’s hospital transfer ‘sans informing family’

Meanwhile, in a statement, the PTI condemned the transfer of 70-year-old Noreen to the PIC without informing her family, expressing grave concern over her health and the treatment of “political prisoners”.

PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram criticised the authorities for not informing Noreen’s family after she felt unwell while in custody at the Kot Lakhpat jail.

He described the handling of her medical emergency as “callous and inhumane”, arguing that denying family members timely information about the condition of an elderly heart patient raised serious questions about prisoners’ rights, legal safeguards and basic human dignity.

“Noreen Niazi’s transfer to the PIC without prior notification to her family is alarming,” Akram said, demanding an immediate explanation from the Punjab government and the relevant authorities.

He demanded that Noreen receive the best possible medical treatment under the supervision of senior cardiologists without any delay, that her necessary diagnostic tests be conducted, and that her family be allowed access in accordance with applicable law.

“The authorities must provide her family with complete, credible and timely information about her condition,” the PTI leader further stressed.

Warning the government against disregarding fundamental rights in the alleged pursuit of political objectives, he said the PTI would not compromise on the protection of human life, health or constitutional freedoms under any circumstances.

Additional input by Ikram Junaidi

World.title: Amid internal doubts, PTI affirms Sohail Afridi 'remains KP chief minister'
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The PTI on Thursday reaffirmed its support for Sohail Afridi, the ex-chief minister who was rendered nonfunctional after the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, ruling out any move within the party to consider an alternative candidate for the office.

Afridi has not been seen since the Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP on Oct 11. The very next day, a federal minister confirmed that he and some of his cabinet members were in preventive custody .

In the notification issued by the party’s central secretariat for the “purpose of clarity and emphasis”, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said that Afridi “remains and shall continue” to serve as the KP chief minister with the “confidence and support” of party founder and ex-premier Imran Khan.

“All PTI members, office-bearers, parliamentarians and party functionaries are hereby directed not to convene or participate in any meeting, introduce any agenda, initiate or entertain any proposal, or encourage or engage in any discussion concerning the nomination, replacement or consideration for the office of chief minister,” the notification said.

“It is categorically reiterated that no one other than the founding chairman has the authority to nominate an alternative candidate or alter this decision in any manner whatsoever. His decisions in this regard are final and binding upon all party members,” it said.

In a post on X, Barrister Gohar said that all party members part of the KP Assembly were a “source of pride for us” and that they had stayed loyal to Imran, complied with every decision and remained steadfast.

“However, in view of the unnecessary speculation and discussions circulating on social media and certain TV channels regarding the chief minister, this notification has been issued to provide further clarification and reassure party workers and supporters that decisions within our party are made solely in accordance with the directives of Imran Khan sahib,” he said.

The development comes after several PTI members expressed dissatisfaction with the party leadership’s handling of the prevailing challenges, questioning its decisions and overreliance on Afridi.

Heated arguments were witnessed during a joint parliamentary party meeting on Tuesday that lasted over seven hours, with some questioning why the top leadership had handed so much authority to Afridi, who, they said, held no position within the party hierarchy.

Some criticised the PTI chairman and Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, questioning why the party leadership appeared to be functioning under Afridi.

They alleged that the top leadership had left everything to Afridi, who had become non-functional after the imposition of governor’s rule in KP, because of its interest in transfers, postings and financial matters in the province.

World.title: Hesson hoping struggling Pakistan top order shows up on big occasion in tri-series final
World.content:
Pakistan head coach Mike Hesson is banking on his experienced top order to deliver when it matters most as the hosts prepare to face Sri Lanka in Saturday’s One-day International (ODI) tri-series final at Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore, with the opening batters’ inconsistent form remaining a major concern.

Pakistan qualified for the final with three consecutive victories before suffering an eight-wicket defeat against Sri Lanka in their last league match, when they were dismissed for just 110. The hosts will need a substantial improvement from their leading batters to avoid a repeat against the Islanders, who chased down the target with more than 30 overs to spare.

Speaking to PCB Digital in a video released on Thursday, Hesson said Pakistan had secured their wins despite some key players failing to make significant contributions, and expressed hope that the final would bring out their best.

“It’s been a pretty good couple of weeks. We have played some decent cricket without being perfect. To get three wins in a row without contributions from a few of our key players is a good sign,” he said.

“I still don’t think we have played our best game yet. Hopefully, we are saving that for the final.”

The numbers underline the challenge facing Pakistan’s top order. Fakhar Zaman has managed just 31 runs in four innings, while former captain Babar Azam has scored 118 in the same number of outings. Saim Ayub, who opened alongside Fakhar in the first three matches before being released from the squad at his own request, scored 21 runs in three innings.

Fakhar made 16 against Sri Lanka in the opening match, fell for a first-ball duck against England and scored 10 in the second England fixture before managing only five against Sri Lanka on Tuesday. Babar began with 45 against Sri Lanka, followed it with 34 against England and then made 10 before scoring 29 in the latest defeat.

Saim scored seven, eight and six in his three appearances. He was subsequently released to return to domestic cricket and work on his batting form, with Sahibzada Farhan named as his replacement, while opener Maaz Sadaqat was also called up earlier.

Hesson, however, remains confident that Pakistan’s senior batters Fakhar and Babar can rise to the occasion, describing the final as an ideal opportunity for them to produce a match-winning performance.

“You are talking about two of the greatest players in Pakistan’s history in the top three. I expect big players to stand up in big games,” he said.

“The fact that we have been able to achieve the wins that we have without the top order performing as well as we know they are capable of is a good sign. A couple of our key players are searching for that match-winning performance and there’s no better place to do it than in a final.”

While the top order has struggled, Pakistan’s middle order has provided important contributions. Salman Ali Agha struck a commanding 107 off 90 balls in the opening victory over Sri Lanka, while Hasan Nawaz scored 79 against England. Arafat Minhas also made 59 in that match.

Shadab Khan’s unbeaten 113 against England in Lahore proved decisive, as he and Haris Rauf put together an unbroken 89-run stand for the last wicket to secure a remarkable one-wicket win.

Hesson singled out Salman’s achievements and praised Hasan’s development, particularly his growing ability to manage pressure in the middle order.

“Salman Ali Agha has got the most hundreds of any Pakistan player batting at number five or below in an ODI,” he said. “His performance is often underrated.”

He added that Hasan was learning to “control the chase, understand risk and manage it”, describing his progress as encouraging.

Pakistan’s bowling, led by captain Shaheen Shah Afridi, has also offered positives, with Hesson praising the left-arm pacer’s ability to take early wickets and acknowledging contributions from Naseem Shah, Haris Rauf and young Arafat Minhas.

Pakistan, who have won 12 of their 19 ODIs since Hesson took charge as white-ball head coach last year, will hope their collective strength is complemented by a decisive contribution from the top order when the trophy is at stake.

World.title: US fires top military planner over alleged leaks: reports
World.content:
The United States has fired a top military planner, US media reported, with some outlets saying the dismissal was due to the officer allegedly leaking classified information.

Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia was removed from his role as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Staff, US media reported on Wednesday, citing unnamed sources.

CBS and Fox both reported that Sylvia’s dismissal was related to leaks, with the former citing a Pentagon official as saying the general failed three polygraphs about sharing classified information with the media.

A spokesperson for the Joint Staff, a top Pentagon body that handles planning and other issues, initially issued a statement that confirmed Sylvia’s departure and wished him well but later withdrew it, saying: “Upon further review, we determined that the statement did not appropriately reflect the full circumstances.”

Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell then said in a post on X that the Defense Department “has zero tolerance for the intentional, unauthorised disclosure of classified information” and took “necessary personnel action to protect sensitive information.”

Parnell did not identify Sylvia by name and said “no further comment will be made regarding the individual or the circumstances of this action”.

“This matter, along with others, have been referred to the Justice Department for potential further legal action,” he added.

The Justice Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Since returning to office early last year, Trump has overseen a purge of top military personnel, including the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, general Charles “CQ” Brown, whom he fired without explanation in February 2025.

Renewed Iran strikes?

Other senior officers pushed out include the heads of the US Army, Navy and Coast Guard, the general who headed the National Security Agency, the vice chief of staff of the US Air Force, a Navy admiral assigned to Nato, and three top military lawyers.

Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth has insisted the president is simply choosing the leaders he wants, but Democratic lawmakers have raised concerns about the potential politicisation of the traditionally neutral US military.

Hegseth said last month that the US had slashed the number of its generals and admirals by 20 per cent, in a move he said was aimed at “accountability”. He suggested the cuts targeted officers who failed to get on board with his efforts to ensure the military is focused on war-fighting rather than the “woke” policies of previous administrations, describing the reductions as an “accomplishment”.

The reported sacking of Sylvia comes as Trump is believed to be weighing fresh strikes against Iran after US midterm elections next Tuesday.

“We may do another little Epic Fury,” Trump said last week, referring to US-Israeli attacks on Tehran in February that triggered the war. He did not give any indication on timing.

Neither the US nor Iran has engaged in major attacks on land-based targets since early September, settling instead into a pattern of strikes on commercial ships.

No reason was given for Sylvia’s reported departure. His previous roles included leading the 101st Airborne Division — the US army’s air assault division — and heading a unit in Iraq.

World.title: ATC sentences Imaan, Hadi to 10 years in security breach case
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court on Thursday sentenced human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, to 10 years in prison each in the security breach case.

Imaan and Hadi were being tried in jail in the 2024 case pertaining to the alleged disruption of an international cricket team’s security route and incitement to public unrest. The couple, accused of removing barriers from the route, was indicted on Oct 7. A formal trial commenced after both lawyers pleaded not guilty. Both were on bail in this case prior to the verdict.

Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra announced the verdict in the case at Adiala jail on Thursday, where the trial was conducted.

The sentence was handed down under three separate legal provisions. According to the judgment, a copy of which is available with Dawn, the two were sentenced to ten years along with a fine of Rs100,000 each under Section 7 (h) of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, as defined under Section 6 (2) (m) — serious coercion or intimidation of a public servant in order to force him to discharge or to refrain from discharging his lawful duties.

The court further handed down a one-year sentence and fined Rs50,000 each under Section 186 (obstructing public servant in discharge of public functions) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC).

Imaan and Hadi were also sentenced to two years each under Section 353 (assault or criminal force to deter public servant from discharge of his duty) of the PPC.

All the sentences will run concurrently, the judgment stated.

Judge Sipra held that the two were “jointly responsible for the offence committed under joint object and common intention”. He stated that the objective of the accused was to “compromise the security arrangements through pressuring security officials”.

While the court acknowledged that the right of movement was a constitutional right, it held that the “same right is subject to observance of the law of the land, and nobody is allowed to attack/assault” law enforcement agencies.

The judgment, citing the attack on the Sri Lankan cricket team in Lahore in 2009, stated that the assault on police personnel and the attempt to “put the security of an international team visiting Pakistan at risk clearly shows the intentions and objective of the accused to create sense of terror”.

The court maintained that the two were well-educated persons “having the full knowledge of delicacy of the matter, but they assaulted upon the police officials deputed [there] for ensuring [..] security”.

Meanwhile, on charges under Section 506 ii (punishment for criminal intimidation), 120-B (punishment of criminal conspiracy), 148 (rioting, armed with deadly weapon), and 149 (every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object) of the PPC, both Imaan and Hadi were acquitted.

The court had appointed a state counsel for the defence in the case. State counsel Atif Mehmood conducted the cross-examination of the witnesses during the trial, while the prosecution presented a total of seven witnesses.

On Oct 27, both accused recorded their statements under Section 342 (power to examine the accused) of the Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC), while final arguments by the state counsel also concluded during the proceedings.

On Monday, the couple approached the SC to challenge the IHC’s Oct 19 order refusing to stay the trial in the case.

The IHC had heard their appeals last week against an Oct 10 ATC order dismissing petitions challenging the framing of charges and the inclusion of terrorism-related provisions. The high court issued notices and said it would decide how to proceed after receiving responses from the parties.

‘Prisoners of conscience’

In their statements recorded under Section 342 of the CrPC, Imaan and Hadi had denied the charges and alleged that they were being targeted for their human rights work and provision of pro bono legal assistance and services to the marginalised and oppressed communities.

“The evidence produced during this trial is not against us, but in fact a charge sheet against (prosecution witnesses)/police officials and the state,” Imaan and Hadi said in their separate similar recorded statements available with Dawn.

“I am a prisoner of conscience who has been at the receiving end of state persecution,” the statements read.

Imaan pointed out that the entire jail trial had been challenged by the couple in the IHC as well as the SC.

Further, the trial was conducted with Imaan and her husband being presented in a cage, preventing effective communication with their counsel or the court, she said.

“From day one, our constitutional rights to fair trial, due process and basic human dignity have been infringed,” she stated.

She also noted that the couple had been incarcerated for over nine months and handed 17-year sentences a day after their arrest on January 23.

“We are being made an example to further cement the chilling effect against those who stand (or want to stand) against tyranny, oppression and injustice,” Imaan stated.

The lawyer further highlighted that the two had spent the third year of their marriage in jail and thus “suffered painful separation from one another” very early on.

“We have not done so for any personal gain; in fact, we have endured only hardship for our work (and) activism,” she said. “But we surrender ourselves before the ultimate court where we all must return one day, where all will be held accountable for what they have done.”

The couple has been in jail since their arrest on Jan 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the IHC and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association president. The arrest prompted criticism by rights bodies, politicians and journalists, who stressed the couple’s right to a fair trial.

Just a day later, a sessions court sentenced them to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act in the controversial social media posts case. The convictions were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts .

On September 17, following months of litigation before the courts , the SC suspended their sentences in the case. The SC ordered their release pending the IHC’s final verdict on their appeals against the trial court’s decision.

However, the reprieve was short-lived as hours later, Islamabad police arrested the couple again in connection with the security breach case. The case was registered at the federal capital’s Kohsar police station on March 22 last year on the complaint of City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio.

World.title: 3 dead in rock spire collapse at tourist site in Turkiye's Cappadocia
World.content:
A landslide triggered by heavy rainfall caused a rock spire to collapse in Turkiye’s Unesco World Heritage-listed Cappadocia region on Thursday, bringing the death toll to three, officials said.

Turkiye’s Cappadocia region, a magnet for tourists from around the world, is home to cone-shaped rock formations known as “fairy chimneys”, created by ancient volcanic activity.

“According to initial findings, two people were killed and five others injured in the incident,” Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said on X.

Rescue teams pulled another body from the rubble, bringing the death toll to three, Nevsehir Governor Huseyin Kok said.

The nationalities of the dead were not immediately known.

“Search and rescue teams are continuing intensive, coordinated operations to locate any other victims who may be trapped under the debris,” the minister said.

Television footage showed heavy machinery digging through the rubble as rescue teams gathered at the site in an effort to recover people. Excavators and rescue workers worked into the night at the site, using powerful floodlights as the search operation continued.

This handout photograph taken and released on October 29, 2026 by Turkish news agency DHA (Demiroren News Agency) shows rescue teams searching for victims at the site of a rock formation that collapsed due to a landslide triggered by heavy rains in Cappadocia district of Nevsehir. — AFP

The incident occurred at 3:15pm local time (5:15pm PKT) when a landslide triggered a rockfall in the town of Goreme near the open-air museum, local governor Kok said.

The area was closed to the public following the collapse, according to reports.

Eyewitnesses described hearing a loud noise as the rock spire near a car park collapsed, sending up a huge cloud of dust.

Restoration

Turkiye’s culture and tourism ministry has launched restoration work in the region to help preserve the fragile rock formations from climate-related damage, natural erosion and human activity.

In 2024, another rockfall was reported in Cappadocia, although no deaths or injuries were recorded.

A Unesco heritage site since 1985, Goreme national park and the rock sites of Cappadocia are “a landscape of harmony combining human interaction and settlement with dramatic natural landforms,” according to the UN agency.

Some of the cones and pillars have experienced earthquake damage, but this is seen as a naturally occurring phenomenon.

“Overuse by tourists and some vandalism have been reported and some incompatible structures have been introduced,” it said on its website.

The Cappadocia region is also home to rock-carved underground cities and early Christian churches.

In 2025, some 4.5 million domestic and foreign tourists visited the region, according to tourism ministry figures.

Hot-air ballooning in Cappadocia is a thriving industry that sees dozens of balloons take to the skies on clear mornings. But concerns have been raised about safety following a series of accidents.

World.title: PM approves expansion of Jinnah and Allama Iqbal airports, eyes making Karachi 'air cargo hub'
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday approved the expansion of Allama Iqbal International Airport and Jinnah International Airport as outlined in their respective masterplans while seeking to turn Karachi into an “air cargo hub”.

According to a statement by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the directives came during a meeting held in Islamabad under the premier’s chairmanship. It was attended by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, federal ministers Khawaja Asif, Musadik Malik, Ahad Khan Cheema, Attaullah Tarar and other senior officials.

The statement said the meeting was briefed on a survey recently completed by an international firm assessing the quality of travel facilities at major airports.

During the meeting, the premier directed that no compromise be made on quality in the expansion projects, that they be aligned with international requirements and that third-party validation be ensured for reforms aimed at improving the expansion projects.

The meeting was informed that work on the installation of automated border management systems (e-gates) at major airports was underway. Furthermore, “work is also ongoing on the air cargo village to make Karachi an air cargo hub,” the statement said.

Per the statement, it was discussed that facilitating passengers at Pakistani airports should be made the “top priority”. PM Shehbaz directed that facilities be improved in line with international standards. To that effect, he directed to obtain the services of internationally renowned institutions.

He also emphasised the provision of regular training in high-quality service delivery to officers and staff facilitating passengers at airports, along with an improvement in the coordination among various entities present at airports.

“The services of the best caterers [should] be obtained for passengers at airports, and there will be no compromise on the quality of food and beverages,” the statement said.

The meeting was further briefed on the upgradation of various airports across the country and ongoing development work by the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA).

Furthermore, the meeting was informed that the expansion of the runway at Jinnah International Airport had been completed. According to the PMO, the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) had also increased the number of staff and counters, keeping in view passenger convenience.

A meet-and-greet service had been launched at Islamabad airport, the statement added. Similarly, the FIA had established pre-departure desks at major airports in the country for timely guidance to passengers.

“The meeting was informed that the existing aviation institution in Hyderabad is being further improved to establish an international standard aviation university, with work to commence by February 2028,” PMO’s statement said.

Earlier this month, PM Shehbaz had also ordered the installation of “smart scanners” at all international airports to facilitate travellers.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment. This should apply to Solar PV Module, Photovoltaic Cell, Solar Inverter, DC Cable, Data Logger, Aluminium Mounting Structure, Battery Pack, Battery Cell, BMS Circuit Board, PV DG Controller, Hybrid Controller, Solar Plant Safety Aluminium Walkway Mesh, Safety Accessories, and related components.

Current TTI rates are high. Solar PV Module carries 26.90 percent, Photovoltaic Cell 25.75 percent, Solar Inverter 28.73 percent, DC Cable 58.40 percent, Data Logger 37.25 percent, Aluminium Mounting Structure 58.40 percent, Battery Pack and Battery Cell 58.40 percent, BMS Circuit Board 31.50 percent, pack materials 37.25 percent, PV DG Controller or Hybrid Controller 89.08 percent, and Solar Plant Safety Aluminum Walkway Mesh 37.25 percent. These should be reduced to zero percent for renewable energy expansion.

The third reform is a tax holiday. Rooftop solar power producers and project companies should receive benefits comparable to those of utility-scale renewable energy producers. A practical structure could be a 100 percent tax holiday for the first 10 years, 50 percent for the next 3 years, and 25 percent for the next 2 years. This should apply to CAPEX, OPEX, IPP, and MPP models. A broader 10–20 year tax holiday for renewable energy projects should also be considered.

Bangladesh has a remarkable solar opportunity already waiting on its rooftops. About 7 percent of the country’s land is covered with concrete or other built structures. This means more than 10,000 square kilometres, or about 10 billion square meters of built surface. If only 30 percent is usable, that would give around 3 billion square meters. At 10 square meters per kW, this can create nearly 300 GW of solar potential. Bangladesh’s peak demand is only around 16–18 GW. The opportunity already exists on rooftops, factories, warehouses, schools, hospitals, government buildings, and commercial establishments.

Rooftop solar should therefore be relaunched nationwide with a clear business model. Utility-scale solar also needs support through unused khas land, transparent tendering, and grid readiness. Floating solar, river-based solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage should receive separate policy attention.

The suspended solar projects must also be revisited. A total of 31 solar power projects, with a combined capacity of more than 3,000 MW, were previously suspended or cancelled. Many were being developed by foreign investors, with more than USD 200 million reportedly already invested. If implemented, these projects could save around BDT 10,800 crore annually in energy import costs. They should be reassessed and revived quickly.

Energy storage is another missing pillar. Solar and wind need storage support to become more reliable. Duties on lithium-ion batteries, BESS, and other storage systems should be reduced to zero. This will help stabilise renewable power and support future grid flexibility.

Electric vehicles can also become part of the solution. In China, Japan, and the United States, EVs are increasingly seen as mobile energy storage systems. A typical EV battery has a capacity of 40–70 kWh, enough to power an average household for 1–2 days. If Bangladesh had 1 million EVs, the country would have 40–70 GWh of distributed storage. This is several times higher than the daily peak demand gap. Solar-powered EV charging, vehicle-to-home, and vehicle-to-grid systems should be included in future energy planning.

If Bangladesh had 30–40 percent of the grid powered by solar, along with solar-powered EVs, the country would be far less exposed to global fuel market shocks.
